knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Reduction Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space representation of a feasible equality-constrained Newton step under linear independence of the constraint gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), where \(m<n\), be twice continuously differentiable. Fix \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(c(x)=0\), and define \(A=Dc(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)\). Suppose that \(A\) has full row rank and that the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\operatorname{null}(A)\). For every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), the condition \(Ad=0\) holds if and only if there is a unique \(p\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\) such that \(d=Zp\). Moreover, the KKT Newton system for \((d,\delta\lambda)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\),
\[
\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}d\\\delta\lambda\end{bmatrix}
=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\\0\end{bmatrix},
\]
is equivalent in its primal component to
\[
Z^{\mathsf T}HZp=-Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x),\qquad d=Zp.
\]
If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular, the reduced equation uniquely determines \(p\) and hence the tangent Newton step \(d\); the unique multiplier correction \(\delta\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) is then determined by the first KKT block equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point where the constraint Jacobian has full row rank, every tangent step has unique null-space coordinates. Projecting the KKT Newton system onto this null space produces the reduced-Hessian equation. If the reduced Hessian is nonsingular, it uniquely determines the primal Newton step, after which the multiplier correction is uniquely recovered.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable, with \(m<n\).
\(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c(x)=0\), and \(A=Dc(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank, \(AZ=0\), and \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique primal KKT Newton step is \(d=Zp\), where \(p\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\) uniquely solves \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZp=-Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the current feasible point, represented as an m-by-n matrix.
Full-column-rank basis matrix for the tangent space, which is the null space of the constraint Jacobian.
Hessian of the Lagrangian with respect to the primal variable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality-constraint geometric regularity at a feasible point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[c:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is }C^1,\qquad \mathcal M=\{x\in U:c(x)=0\},\qquad \bar x\in\mathcal M,\qquad J(x)=Dc(x).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality systems. Regularity is attached to the specified constraint representation at \(\bar x\), not solely to the underlying feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\bar x\text{ is geometrically regular for }c(x)=0\iff \operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)=m.\] Equivalently, \(J(\bar x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is surjective. In this regime the linearized tangent and normal spaces are \[\mathcal T_{\bar x}=\ker J(\bar x),\qquad \mathcal N_{\bar x}=\operatorname{range}J(\bar x)^T,\qquad \mathbb R^n=\mathcal T_{\bar x}\oplus\mathcal N_{\bar x}.\] The equality representation has regularity defect \[\delta_c(\bar x):=m-\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x),\] so regularity is precisely \(\delta_c(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable equality map \(c:U\to\mathbb R^m\) and a feasible point \(\bar x\), the equality representation is geometrically regular at \(\bar x\) when its Jacobian \(J(\bar x)\) has full row rank \(m\). Its linearized tangent space is \(\ker J(\bar x)\), its normal space is \(\operatorname{range}J(\bar x)^T\), and these spaces form an orthogonal direct sum of \(\mathbb R^n\). The rank defect \(m-\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)\) is then zero.
assumptions_latex: \[U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open and }c\in C^1(U;\mathbb R^m).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}Dc(\bar x)=m,\qquad T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)=\ker Dc(\bar x),\qquad N_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)=\operatorname{range}Dc(\bar x)^T.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)=m\iff J(\bar x)J(\bar x)^T\succ0\iff \ker J(\bar x)^T=\{0\}.\]
\[\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)=m\iff \{\nabla c_i(\bar x)\}_{i=1}^m\text{ is linearly independent}.\]
special_cases_latex: \[m=0:\quad \mathcal T_{\bar x}=\mathbb R^n,\quad \mathcal N_{\bar x}=\{0\}.\]
\[m=n\text{ and }J(\bar x)\text{ nonsingular}:\quad \mathcal T_{\bar x}=\{0\}.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\dim\mathcal T_{\bar x}=n-m,\qquad \dim\mathcal N_{\bar x}=m.\]
\[J(\bar x)^T\lambda_1=J(\bar x)^T\lambda_2\Longrightarrow \lambda_1=\lambda_2.\]
boundary_notes: Full row rank requires \(m\le n\).
A geometrically smooth feasible set can possess a singular redundant representation; regularity here is representation-dependent.
At rank-deficient points, \(\ker J(\bar x)\) remains a linearized space but need not equal the geometric tangent cone.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality map, with constraint gradients as rows.
Row-rank defect of the equality representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry induced by an affine equality system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\qquad b\in\mathbb R^m,\qquad \mathcal F(A,b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine equalities with arbitrary rank. The definition separates the fixed direction spaces from the question of consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\text{The affine equality geometry of }(A,b)\text{ is the triple }\bigl(\mathcal F(A,b),\ker A,\operatorname{range}A^T\bigr).\] If \(\mathcal F(A,b)\ne\varnothing\), then for every \(x\in\mathcal F(A,b)\), \[T_{\mathcal F}(x)=\ker A,\qquad N_{\mathcal F}(x)=\operatorname{range}A^T,\qquad \mathbb R^n=\ker A\oplus\operatorname{range}A^T.\] Thus tangent and normal spaces are independent of the feasible point. For any particular solution \(x_p\), \[\mathcal F(A,b)=x_p+\ker A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine equality geometry of \(Ax=b\) consists of its feasible set, the null space of \(A\), and the range of \(A^T\). Whenever the system is consistent, every feasible point has the same tangent space \(\ker A\) and normal space \(\operatorname{range}A^T\), and the feasible set is a translate \(x_p+\ker A\) of the null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal F(A,b)\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow \mathcal F(A,b)=x_p+\ker A,\quad T_{\mathcal F}(x)=\ker A,\quad N_{\mathcal F}(x)=\operatorname{range}A^T.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[x,y\in\mathcal F(A,b)\Longrightarrow x-y\in\ker A.\]
\[d\in T_{\mathcal F}(x)\iff A d=0,\qquad v\in N_{\mathcal F}(x)\iff v=A^T\lambda\text{ for some }\lambda.\]
special_cases_latex: \[A=0:\quad \mathcal F(A,b)=\mathbb R^n\text{ if }b=0,\text{ and }\varnothing\text{ otherwise}.\]
\[\operatorname{rank}A=n\text{ and the system is consistent}:\quad \mathcal F(A,b)\text{ is a singleton}.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\dim T_{\mathcal F}(x)=n-\operatorname{rank}A.\]
\[\dim N_{\mathcal F}(x)=\operatorname{rank}A.\]
boundary_notes: When \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent, it has no feasible-point tangent or normal space, although \(\ker A\) and \(\operatorname{range}A^T\) remain defined.
The orthogonal decomposition is Euclidean; other metrics produce different complementary projectors but the same tangent subspace.

notation.meaning: Any particular solution of the consistent system.

children.title: Consistent Affine Feasible Sets
children.top_down_role: Nonempty affine feasible sets and their fixed feasible-direction structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistent Affine Feasible Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a nonempty real affine equality set and its invariant feasible-direction space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:Ax=b\}\). The system is consistent exactly when \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). If \(x_p\in F\), then
\[
F=x_p+\ker(A)=\{x_p+z:z\in\ker(A)\}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(x,y\in F\), the displacement \(y-x\) belongs to \(\ker(A)\), and every direction in \(\ker(A)\) preserves feasibility. Moreover, \(F\) is an affine subspace of dimension \(n-\operatorname{rank}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent system Ax=b has feasible set equal to any particular solution plus the null space of A; its feasible directions are fixed and its dimension is n−rank(A).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=x_p+\ker(A)\) and \(\dim F=n-\operatorname{rank}(A)\).

notation.meaning: affine feasible set defined by Ax=b
null space and feasible-direction space of A

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent, Normal, and Projector Structure of an Affine Feasible Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order geometry of a nonempty affine equality set, including rank-deficient representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\). At every \(x\in F\), \[T_F(x)=\ker(A),\qquad N_F(x)=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})=\ker(A)^\perp.\] These spaces are independent of \(x\). Their orthogonal projectors are \[P_T=I-A^\dagger A,\qquad P_N=A^\dagger A,\] and every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) has the unique orthogonal decomposition \(d=P_Td+P_Nd\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty affine equality set has constant tangent space ker(A), constant normal space range(Aᵀ), and pseudoinverse formulas for their orthogonal projectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(x)=\ker(A)\), \(N_F(x)=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\), \(P_T=I-A^\dagger A\), and \(P_N=A^\dagger A\) for every \(x\in F\).

notation.meaning: tangent space of F at x
normal space of F at x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Consistency and parametrization of affine feasible sets
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \[A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb R^m,\quad r=\operatorname{rank}A,\quad \mathcal F=\{x:Ax=b\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional linear equalities. Numerical tolerance-based consistency is outside this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathcal F\text{ is a consistent affine feasible set}\iff \mathcal F\ne\varnothing\iff b\in\operatorname{range}A\iff \operatorname{rank}[A\ b]=\operatorname{rank}A.\] For any \(x_p\) satisfying \(Ax_p=b\), and any full-column-rank \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) with \(\operatorname{range}Z=\ker A\), \[\mathcal F=\{x_p+Zz:z\in\mathbb R^{n-r}\}.\] The vector \(z\) is unique for a fixed basis \(Z\), while the particular solution \(x_p\) is not unique unless \(r=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine system \(Ax=b\) is consistent exactly when \(b\) belongs to the range of \(A\), equivalently when adjoining \(b\) does not increase the matrix rank. If \(x_p\) is one solution and the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), every feasible point has the unique reduced-coordinate representation \(x=x_p+Zz\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[b\in\operatorname{range}A\Longrightarrow \mathcal F=x_p+\ker A=\{x_p+Zz:z\in\mathbb R^{n-r}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\iff AA^{\dagger}b=b.\]
\[\mathcal F\ne\varnothing\iff y^Tb=0\quad\forall y\in\ker A^T.\]
special_cases_latex: \[r=n:\quad \ker A=\{0\},\text{ so a consistent system has exactly one solution}.\]
\[r=0:\quad \mathcal F=\mathbb R^n\text{ precisely when }b=0.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\dim\mathcal F:=\dim(\mathcal F-x_p)=n-r.\]
\[x_1,x_2\in\mathcal F\iff A(x_1-x_2)=0.\]
boundary_notes: Consistency does not imply that the rows of \(A\) are independent.
The pseudoinverse characterization uses the Euclidean Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse.
For floating-point data, numerical rank and residual tolerances must be specified separately.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the constraint matrix.

children.title: Affine Degrees-of-Freedom Regimes
children.top_down_role: Degree-of-freedom regimes governing elimination and reduced-system dimensions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\operatorname{range}A,\quad r=\operatorname{rank}A,
\quad d=n-r.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent exact affine equalities. Degrees of freedom refer to the intrinsic dimension of the feasible affine set, not to the displayed number of variables minus the displayed number of rows unless the rows are independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[d(A,b):=\dim\ker A=n-\operatorname{rank}A\] is the affine degree-of-freedom count. The regimes are \[d>0\text{ (underdetermined)},\qquad d=0\text{ (fully determined)},\] while the regular full-row-rank subregime satisfies \(r=m\) and hence \(d=n-m\). A null-space reduction therefore uses exactly \(d\) reduced coordinates: \[x=x_p+Zz,\\ z\in\mathbb R^d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a consistent affine system \(Ax=b\), the number of feasible degrees of freedom is \(d=n-\operatorname{rank}A\). If \(d>0\), the feasible set has free directions and is underdetermined; if \(d=0\), it is a singleton. Only when \(A\) has full row rank does the familiar count \(d=n-m\) apply. A null-space elimination uses one reduced coordinate for each degree of freedom.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[d=n-r,
\qquad \mathcal F=x_p+\ker A,
\qquad \dim(\mathcal F-x_p)=d.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[d=\operatorname{nullity}A=n-r.\]
\[d=0\iff \ker A=\{0\}\iff A\text{ has full column rank}.\]
special_cases_latex: \[r=m<n:\quad d=n-m>0.\]
\[r=n\le m:\quad d=0\text{ and consistency gives a unique feasible point}.\]
\[r<m:\quad m-r\text{ displayed equalities are linearly redundant}.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\text{ for every null-space basis matrix}.\]
\[d_1<d_2\text{ corresponds to a smaller reduced optimization space, independently of the number of redundant rows}.\]
boundary_notes: The label “overdetermined” based only on \(m>n\) does not determine consistency or intrinsic dimension.
A rank-deficient system may still have zero degrees of freedom when \(r=n<m\).
Near-rank deficiency requires a numerical rank threshold and is not classified by exact rank alone.

children.title: Determined Affine Systems
children.top_down_role: Square or fully determined constraint structures with no free affine coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Determined Affine Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses rank, rather than equation count alone, to define zero affine degrees of freedom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), a consistent affine system \(Ax=b\) is determined when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=n\). Equivalently, \(A\) has trivial null space, so for any feasible point \(x_p\),
\[
\{x:Ax=b\}=x_p+\ker(A)=\{x_p\}.
\]
Thus the feasible set has dimension zero and contains exactly one point. This definition permits \(m>n\), provided any extra equations are compatible and do not reduce consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent affine system is determined when A has full column rank; its null space is zero and its feasible point is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=n\), equivalently \(\ker(A)=\{0\}\), and the solution is unique.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Solution of a Determined Affine System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact solution formulas are canonically owned by affine feasible-point construction rather than this degree-of-freedom regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=n\), and suppose \(Ax=b\) is consistent. Then \(A^{\mathsf T}A\) is positive definite and the unique feasible point is \(x_*=(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b=A^\dagger b\). Every left inverse \(L\) of \(A\) also satisfies \(x_*=Lb\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent full-column-rank system can be solved using its pseudoinverse, normal equations, or any left inverse.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_*=(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b=A^\dagger b\) is the unique solution.

children.title: Underdetermined Affine Systems
children.top_down_role: Constraint structures retaining free coordinates for reduced optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Underdetermined Affine Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the positive-degrees-of-freedom regime for a consistent affine equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), a consistent affine system \(Ax=b\) is underdetermined when \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A)<n\). For any particular solution \(x_p\),
\[
\{x:Ax=b\}=x_p+\ker(A),\qquad \dim\ker(A)=n-r>0.
\]
Hence infinitely many feasible points exist, parameterized as \(x=x_p+Zp\), where the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-r)}\) form a basis of \(\ker(A)\) and \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-r}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent affine system is underdetermined when rank(A)<n; it has n−rank(A) free coordinates and infinitely many solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=x_p+Zp\) with \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-r}\), and the feasible dimension is \(n-r>0\).

notation.meaning: matrix whose columns form a null-space basis

children.title: Degrees-of-Freedom Transition
children.top_down_role: Changes in reduced dimension as the relationship between variables and independent equalities changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Degrees-of-Freedom Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates rank changes to discrete changes in affine feasible dimension under maintained consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\) be a parameter set, let \(A(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\) for every \(t\in T\), and suppose \(F(t)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A(t)x=b(t)\}\) is nonempty for every parameter under consideration. Then
\[
\dim F(t)=n-\operatorname{rank}(A(t)).
\]
On any subset of \(T\) where the rank is constant, the number of affine degrees of freedom is constant. If \(t_1,t_2\in T\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A(t_1))=r\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(A(t_2))=r+k\), then the corresponding feasible dimensions are \(n-r\) and \(n-r-k\). The transition from underdetermined to determined occurs precisely at parameters \(t\) for which \(\operatorname{rank}(A(t))=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a consistent parameterized affine system, feasible dimension equals the number of variables minus the rank. An increase of k in rank decreases feasible dimension by k, and the system is determined when rank reaches the number of variables.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a parameter set, and \(A(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and \(F(t)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(t\in T\) under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F(t)=n-\operatorname{rank}(A(t))\), with the determined transition at \(\operatorname{rank}(A(t))=n\).

notation.meaning: parameter set indexing the affine systems
parameter in T indexing an affine system

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Continuity of Affine Degrees of Freedom
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local behavior of feasible dimension near a rank-deficient parameter under maintained consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) depend continuously on \(t\), and suppose \(A(t)x=b(t)\) is consistent for the parameters considered. If \(r=\operatorname{rank}A(t_0)\), then some \(r\times r\) minor remains nonzero near \(t_0\), so \[\operatorname{rank}A(t)\ge r\quad\text{and}\quad \dim F(t)\le\dim F(t_0)\] for all sufficiently near \(t\). Thus degrees of freedom may increase at a rank-loss parameter but cannot be smaller there than at all sufficiently nearby parameters. For \(A(t)=[t]\) and \(b(t)=0\), \(\dim F(t)=0\) for \(t\ne0\) and \(\dim F(0)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under continuous data and consistency, nullity is upper semicontinuous: extra degrees of freedom can appear at rank loss but cannot disappear abruptly there.
assumptions_latex: The affine systems are consistent at the parameters being compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \limsup_{t\to t_0}\dim F(t)\le\dim F(t_0).
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Continuity of Affine Degrees of Freedom

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Taxonomy of affine rank and feasibility failures
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb R^m,
\quad r=\operatorname{rank}A,
\quad \widehat r=\operatorname{rank}[A\ b].\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic classification of affine equality systems. Several labels can coexist, except that consistency and inconsistency are mutually exclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine system \(Ax=b\) is classified by \[(i)\ \text{inconsistent}\iff \widehat r>r;\qquad (ii)\ \text{row-redundant}\iff r<m;\qquad (iii)\ \text{rank-deficient relative to full column rank}\iff r<n.\] A consistent row-redundant system satisfies \(\widehat r=r<m\): dependent equations do not reduce the feasible set beyond an independent subsystem. An inconsistent system satisfies \(b\notin\operatorname{range}A\) and has no feasible point. A numerically rank-ambiguous system is not an exact algebraic class; it is declared only after choosing a tolerance for singular values or a rank-revealing factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The system \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent when adjoining \(b\) increases rank. It has redundant rows when \(\operatorname{rank}A<m\), and it lacks full column rank when \(\operatorname{rank}A<n\). Consistent redundancy leaves a nonempty feasible geometry describable by an independent row subsystem, whereas inconsistency leaves no feasible set. Numerical near-dependence is a separate tolerance-dependent diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\widehat r>r\iff \mathcal F(A,b)=\varnothing,
\qquad r<m\iff \ker A^T\ne\{0\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal F(A,b)=\varnothing\iff b\notin\operatorname{range}A\iff \exists y\in\ker A^T:\ y^Tb\ne0.\]
\[r<m\iff \exists y\ne0:\ A^Ty=0.\]
special_cases_latex: \[r=m\text{ and }m\le n:\quad \text{no row redundancy and }Ax=b\text{ is consistent for every }b.\]
\[r=n<m:\quad \text{a consistent system has a unique solution despite redundant rows}.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[r<m\Longrightarrow AA^T\text{ is singular}.\]
\[\widehat r>r\Longrightarrow \text{feasible-point reduction methods require an infeasibility phase or reformulation}.\]
boundary_notes: Row redundancy does not itself imply inconsistency.
The phrase “rank deficient” must identify whether full row rank or full column rank is the reference.
Small singular values indicate conditioning, not exact rank failure, until a tolerance is fixed.

children.title: Redundant Affine Systems
children.top_down_role: Dependent affine constraints whose removal preserves the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Affine Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines redundancy through row dependence and invariance of the solution set after equation removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An affine system \(Ax=b\), with augmented matrix \([A\mid b]\), is redundant when at least one equation may be deleted without changing its solution set. Equivalently, for some row index \(i\), the augmented row \([a_i^{\mathsf T},b_i]\) lies in the span of the remaining augmented rows. If the system is consistent, redundancy occurs whenever \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\): exactly \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\) independent equations suffice to define the same feasible set, and the remaining \(m-r\) equations add no restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine system is redundant when an equation follows from the others and can be removed without changing the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and rows represent affine equations.
For the rank-count conclusion, \(Ax=b\) is consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A redundant row is removable without changing \(\{x:Ax=b\}\); a consistent system has \(m-r\) redundant equations relative to an independent row subsystem.

notation.meaning: rank of A for a consistent system

source_refs.locator: 6.1 Over-determined Systems p. 110

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 Over-determined Systems p. 110

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp qualification needed when redundancy is defined by invariance of a possibly empty solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an equation index \(i\), and let \(F_{-i}\) be the solution set of the remaining affine equations. If \(F_{-i}\neq\varnothing\), then deleting equation \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\) preserves the solution set if and only if the augmented row \([a_i^{\mathsf T},b_i]\) lies in the span of the remaining augmented rows. If \(F_{-i}=\varnothing\), deletion automatically preserves the empty solution set, and augmented-row dependence is not necessary. For example, the equations \(x=0\), \(x=1\), and \(y=0\) have empty solution set before and after deleting \(y=0\), although \([0,1,0]\) is not in the span of \([1,0,0]\) and \([1,0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented-row dependence is equivalent to removability when the remaining subsystem is consistent; if it is already inconsistent, a row may be removable without being dependent.
assumptions_latex: For the equivalence, the subsystem remaining after deletion is consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(F_{-i}\neq\varnothing\), removability is equivalent to augmented-row dependence; without that assumption only the dependence-to-removability implication is generally valid.

notation.meaning: solution set after deleting equation i

children.title: Inconsistent Affine Systems
children.top_down_role: Affine constraints lacking a common feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Affine Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives equivalent rank, range, and left-null-space certificates for affine infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), the affine system \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent exactly when
\[
b\notin\operatorname{range}(A),
\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
\operatorname{rank}([A\mid b])>\operatorname{rank}(A).
\]
Equivalently, there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\) satisfying
\[
A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y\neq0.
\]
Such a vector \(y\) is a directly checkable infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ax=b is infeasible exactly when the augmented rank rises; a left-null vector y with bᵀy≠0 certifies inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}([A\mid b])>\operatorname{rank}(A)\), equivalently such a certificate \(y\) exists.

source_refs.locator: 6.1 Over-determined Systems p. 110

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 Over-determined Systems p. 110

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized left-null certificate and exact Euclidean distance from the right-hand side to compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(r=(I-AA^\dagger)b\) and \(\delta=\|r\|_2=\operatorname{dist}(b,\operatorname{range}(A))\). Then \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent if and only if \(\delta>0\). In that case \(y=r/\|r\|_2\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), \(\|y\|_2=1\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\delta>0\). Moreover, \[\delta=\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ \|y\|_2\le1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distance from b to the range of A is an exact inconsistency margin attained by the normalized orthogonal residual as a left-null certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) is inconsistent exactly when \(\delta=\|(I-AA^\dagger)b\|_2>0\), with the displayed normalized certificate and maximization formula.

notation.meaning: component of b orthogonal to the range of A

children.title: Rank-Revealed Affine Classification
children.top_down_role: Structural classification of dependent rows, effective rank, and incompatible constraint components.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealed Affine Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies affine systems by coefficient and augmented ranks, then reports feasible dimension and redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and a stated numerical rank tolerance \(\tau\), compute rank-revealing factorizations of \(A\) and \([A\mid b]\), obtaining \(r=\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(A)\) and \(r_a=\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}([A\mid b])\). If \(r_a>r\), output inconsistent. Otherwise output consistent with feasible dimension \(n-r\); additionally output determined if \(r=n\), underdetermined if \(r<n\), and row-redundant if \(r<m\). When consistent, recover a particular solution and a null-space basis from the same factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare numerical ranks of A and [A|b] to detect inconsistency; otherwise classify uniqueness, degrees of freedom, and redundant equations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and a rank tolerance \(\tau\) are supplied.
The chosen rank-revealing factorization applies the same tolerance to both matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the rank-based affine classification, with feasible dimension \(n-r\) whenever \(r_a=r\).

notation.meaning: numerical rank of the augmented matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local geometry of a nonlinear equality level set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[c:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is }C^1,
\quad \mathcal M=c^{-1}(0),
\quad x\in\mathcal M,
\quad J(x)=Dc(x).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional equality systems, including both regular and singular level-set points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The nonlinear equality geometry at \(x\) consists of the geometric tangent cone \[T_{\mathcal M}(x)=\left\{d:\exists x_k\in\mathcal M,\ t_k\downarrow0,
\ x_k\to x,
\ \frac{x_k-x}{t_k}\to d\right\},\] the linearized feasible space \[L_c(x)=\ker J(x)=\{d:J(x)d=0\},\] and the linearized normal space \[N_c^{\mathrm{lin}}(x)=\operatorname{range}J(x)^T.\] At a regular point these satisfy \(T_{\mathcal M}(x)=L_c(x)\); at a singular representation the inclusion or equality must be assessed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the nonlinear level set \(\mathcal M=\{x:c(x)=0\}\), the geometric tangent cone is formed from limits of scaled feasible displacements. The linearized feasible space is the Jacobian null space \(\ker J(x)\), and the linearized normal space is \(\operatorname{range}J(x)^T\). At regular points the geometric and linearized tangent objects agree; at singular points they need not.
assumptions_latex: \[U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open},\qquad c\in C^1(U;\mathbb R^m).\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal G_c(x):=\bigl(T_{\mathcal M}(x),\ker J(x),\operatorname{range}J(x)^T\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex:
\[d\in T_{\mathcal M}(x)\iff \exists x_k\in\mathcal M,
\alpha_k>0:\ x_k\to x,
\alpha_k(x_k-x)\to d.\]
\[d\in L_c(x)\iff \nabla c_i(x)^Td=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\]
special_cases_latex: \[c(x)=Ax-b:\quad T_{\mathcal M}(x)=\ker A\text{ at every feasible }x.\]
\[J(x)\text{ has full row rank}:\quad T_{\mathcal M}(x)=\ker J(x).\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\ker J(x)\perp\operatorname{range}J(x)^T.\]
\[\dim\ker J(x)=n-\operatorname{rank}J(x),\text{ although the local feasible-set dimension need not equal this at a singular point}.\]
boundary_notes: The tangent cone is representation-independent, while \(L_c(x)\) depends on the chosen equations.
A first-order linearized direction need not be the derivative of an exactly feasible curve at a singular point.
No convexity of the level set is assumed.

children.title: Regular Embedded-Manifold Regime
children.top_down_role: Locally smooth equality geometry supporting tangent coordinates and feasible corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Embedded-Manifold Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local regular-level-set theorem for continuously differentiable equality constraints of constant full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x_*\in U\) satisfy \(c(x_*)=0\), and suppose \(J_c(x_*)\) has rank \(m\le n\). Then there is a neighborhood \(V\) of \(x_*\) such that
\[
M\cap V=\{x\in V:c(x)=0\}
\]
is a \(C^1\) embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb{R}^{n}\) of dimension \(n-m\). Its tangent space at every sufficiently nearby feasible \(x\) is
\[
T_xM=\ker J_c(x),
\]
and its normal space is \(\operatorname{range}(J_c(x)^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full row rank of the equality Jacobian makes the nearby feasible set a smooth manifold whose tangent space is the Jacobian null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Locally, \(M=c^{-1}(0)\) is an embedded \(C^1\) manifold of dimension \(n-m\), with \(T_xM=\ker J_c(x)\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the equality map c at x
tangent space of M at x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular level set as a locally embedded manifold
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[c:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is }C^p,
\quad p\ge1,
\quad \mathcal M=c^{-1}(0),
\quad \bar x\in\mathcal M.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-dimensional smooth geometry under full row rank. The definition does not assert global connectedness or a single global chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality level set is in the regular embedded-manifold regime at \(\bar x\) when \[\operatorname{rank}Dc(\bar x)=m.\] Then there is a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) in which \(\mathcal M\cap V\) is a \(C^p\) embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb R^n\) of dimension \(n-m\), with \[T_x\mathcal M=\ker Dc(x),
\qquad N_x\mathcal M=box{\(\operatorname{range}Dc(x)^T\)},
\qquad x\in\mathcal M\cap V.\] Here the boxed expression denotes the normal space; equivalently, omit the box and read \(N_x\mathcal M=\operatorname{range}Dc(x)^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point \(\bar x\) is in the regular embedded-manifold regime when \(Dc(\bar x)\) has full row rank. Locally, the level set is then a smooth embedded manifold of dimension \(n-m\). At nearby feasible points its tangent space is the Jacobian null space and its normal space is the range of the transposed Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists V\ni\bar x:\quad \mathcal M\cap V\text{ is a }C^p\text{ embedded manifold of dimension }n-m.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[Dc(\bar x)\text{ is surjective}.\]
\[Dc(\bar x)Dc(\bar x)^T\succ0.\]
special_cases_latex: \[m=1:\quad \nabla c(\bar x)\ne0\text{ defines a regular hypersurface}.\]
\[m=n:\quad \mathcal M\cap V=\{\bar x\}\text{ after shrinking }V.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\mathbb R^n=T_x\mathcal M\oplus N_x\mathcal M.\]
\[\dim T_x\mathcal M=n-m\text{ is locally constant}.\]
boundary_notes: Full row rank is sufficient for this regular level-set formulation; lower constant rank requires removal or reparametrization of redundant equations.
The conclusion is local and does not provide a global feasible parametrization.
A manifold may admit a rank-deficient redundant equation representation, which this representation-level regime excludes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependent-variable local chart for nonlinear equalities
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[x=(u,v)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^{n-m},
\quad c:U\to\mathbb R^m,
\quad c(\bar u,\bar v)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth elimination using a chosen nonsingular Jacobian block. The chart can fail away from its neighborhood and can depend strongly on the variable partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A local-chart variable-partition representation at \(\bar x=(\bar u,\bar v)\) is a partition for which \[D_uc(\bar u,\bar v)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\text{ is nonsingular}.\] It consists of neighborhoods \(V\ni\bar v\), \(W\ni\bar u\), and a unique \(C^p\) map \(\phi:V\to W\) such that \[c(\phi(v),v)=0,
\qquad \phi(\bar v)=\bar u,
\qquad \mathcal M\cap(W\times V)=\{(\phi(v),v):v\in V\}.\] Its derivative is \[D\phi(v)=-[D_uc(\phi(v),v)]^{-1}D_vc(\phi(v),v).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose \(m\) dependent variables \(u\) and \(n-m\) free variables \(v\). If the Jacobian block with respect to \(u\) is nonsingular at a feasible point, the nearby feasible set is uniquely represented as \(u=\phi(v)\). The derivative of this chart is \(-D_uc^{-1}D_vc\), so reduced optimization can be performed in the free variable \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\exists!\,\phi:V\to W:\quad c(\phi(v),v)=0,
\quad D\phi(v)=-D_uc^{-1}D_vc.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[v\longmapsto (\phi(v),v)\text{ is a local coordinate chart for }\mathcal M.\]

\[Z(v)=\begin{bmatrix}D\phi(v)\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}
\quad\text{satisfies}\quad Dc(\phi(v),v)Z(v)=0.\]
special_cases_latex: \[c(u,v)=A_u u+A_vv-b:\quad \phi(v)=A_u^{-1}(b-A_vv).\]
\[n=m:\quad V\subseteq\mathbb R^0\text{ and the local feasible point is isolated}.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[\psi(v):=f(\phi(v),v)\text{ is the locally reduced objective}.\]
\[\dim\mathcal M=n-m\text{ in the chart neighborhood}.\]
boundary_notes: Nonsingularity of the selected block is stronger than mere consistency and may require pivoting or repartitioning.
The chart is local; folds can prevent a single dependent-variable representation globally.
Ill-conditioning of \(D_uc\) can make an algebraically valid chart numerically unreliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Feasible Charts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit-function representation of a regular equality-feasible set by local Euclidean coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\) be \(C^1\), let \(x_*=(u_*,v_*)\) satisfy \(c(x_*)=0\), and suppose the square partial Jacobian \(J_vc(x_*)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Then neighborhoods \(U_0\) of \(u_*\) and \(V_0\) of \(v_*\) and a unique \(C^1\) map \(\phi:U_0\to V_0\) exist such that
\[
c(u,v)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad v=\phi(u)
\]
within \(U_0\times V_0\). The map \(\psi(u)=(u,\phi(u))\) is a local feasible chart with \(n-m\) coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular dependent-variable Jacobian lets nearby feasible points be written uniquely as (u,φ(u)), with u supplying n−m local coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Locally, \(c(u,v)=0\) if and only if \(v=\phi(u)\), and \(\psi(u)=(u,\phi(u))\) parameterizes the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent-Variable Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies when a selected variable block can be solved locally from the equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}\) be \(C^1\) and let \(x_*\) be feasible with \(\operatorname{rank}J_c(x_*)=m\). A set \(D\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) of \(m\) indices is a valid dependent-variable partition at \(x_*\) when
\[
\det J_{c,D}(x_*)\neq0,
\]
where \(J_{c,D}(x_*)\) is the submatrix formed by the columns indexed by \(D\). With complementary index set \(F\), the variables \(x_D\) are then uniquely expressible locally as a \(C^1\) function of the free variables \(x_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose m dependent variables whose Jacobian columns form a nonsingular square block; the remaining variables then serve as local free variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is valid exactly when \(\det J_{c,D}(x_*)\neq0\), in which case \(x_D=\phi(x_F)\) locally.

More than one such set may exist; each valid set supplies a different coordinate partition for the same local feasible set.

children.title: Free-Variable Coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Free-Variable Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses feasible tangents and chart derivatives in coordinates associated with the free-variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under a valid partition \(x=(u,v)\) with \(v=\phi(u)\), differentiation of \(c(u,\phi(u))=0\) gives
\[
D\phi(u)=-J_vc(u,\phi(u))^{-1}J_uc(u,\phi(u)).
\]
Therefore an infinitesimal free-coordinate displacement \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\) induces the feasible tangent displacement
\[
d=Z(u)p,\qquad Z(u)=\begin{bmatrix}I_{n-m}\\D\phi(u)\end{bmatrix},
\]
and \(J_c(u,\phi(u))Z(u)=0\). Since \(Z(u)\) has \(n-m\) independent columns, those columns form a basis of the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Free-coordinate changes p map to feasible tangent directions Zp, where Z is obtained by differentiating the implicit dependent-variable function.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is \(C^1\) and \(c(u,\phi(u))=0\) on a local chart.
\(J_vc(u,\phi(u))\) is nonsingular throughout the chart neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\phi=-J_vc^{-1}J_uc\), and the columns of \(Z=[I;D\phi]\) form a basis of \(\ker J_c\).

notation.meaning: derivative of the implicit dependent-variable map

knowledge_statements.title: Chart Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies loss of the selected Jacobian minor as the boundary of a fixed variable-partition chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed dependent index set \(D\), the implicit chart based on solving \(x_D=\phi(x_F)\) is guaranteed only on a neighborhood where
\[
\det J_{c,D}(x)\neq0.
\]
The selected block approaches singularity when \(\sigma_{\min}(J_{c,D}(x))\to0\). Its inverse then becomes unbounded in norm, and at singularity the derivative formula containing \(J_{c,D}(x)^{-1}\) is undefined; consequently, the implicit-function guarantee for expressing the selected variables as a single-valued function of \(x_F\) is lost. The feasible set may nevertheless admit a regular chart if another \(m\)-column Jacobian minor is nonsingular. If \(\operatorname{rank}J_c(x)<m\), the full-row-rank regular-level-set guarantee is lost, although rank loss alone does not determine the intrinsic geometry of the zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed chart loses its guarantee when its selected Jacobian block becomes singular. Another partition may still work, while loss of full Jacobian row rank removes the regular-level-set guarantee without by itself determining the feasible set's intrinsic geometry.
assumptions_latex: A chart uses a fixed dependent index set \(D\) with \(|D|=m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fixed chart loses its implicit-function guarantee at \(\det J_{c,D}(x)=0\); the full-row-rank regular-level-set guarantee is lost when \(\operatorname{rank}J_c(x)<m\).

children.title: Singular Feasible Geometry
children.top_down_role: Rank-changing or nonmanifold feasible geometry outside classical smooth reduction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-branch singular feasible set that is not a smooth embedded curve at its cusp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x,y)=y^2-x^3\), the feasible set near the origin is the cusp \[F=\{(t^2,t^3):t\in\mathbb{R}\}.\] Since \(J_c(0,0)=0\), the linearized set is \(\ker J_c(0,0)=\mathbb{R}^2\). Its Bouligand tangent cone is instead \[T_F(0,0)=\{(a,0):a\ge 0\},\] a ray rather than a vector space. Thus a singular equality may produce a nonmanifold cusp without intersecting branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality y²=x³ has a cusp: its zero Jacobian predicts the whole plane, but the true tangent cone is a single ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_F(0,0)=\{(a,0):a\ge0\}\subsetneq\mathbb{R}^2=\ker J_c(0,0).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone at the cusp

knowledge_statements.title: Cuspidal Singular Feasible Branch

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Crossing Feasible Branches at a Singular Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A singular equality whose feasible set has intersecting branches and no tangent space at the intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x,y)=xy\), \[F=c^{-1}(0)=(\mathbb{R}\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}).\] At the origin, \(J_c(0,0)=0\), hence \(\ker J_c(0,0)=\mathbb{R}^2\), whereas \[T_F(0,0)=(\mathbb{R}\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb{R}).\] The tangent cone is nonconvex and not a vector space, so the crossing is not an embedded one-dimensional manifold and the Jacobian kernel strictly overestimates feasible tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For xy=0, two axes cross at the origin; the zero Jacobian predicts every direction, while the true tangent cone contains only the axes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_F(0,0)\subsetneq\ker J_c(0,0)=\mathbb{R}^2,\qquad T_F(0,0)\text{ is not a vector space}.

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone at the crossing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-Rank Deficient Representations Can Still Define Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes deficient equation rank from intrinsic nonmanifold geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be \(C^1\), let \(c(\bar x)=0\), and suppose \(\operatorname{rank}J_c(x)=r<m\) throughout a neighborhood of \(\bar x\). The constant-rank theorem supplies local domain and codomain coordinates in which \[c(y)=(y_1,\ldots,y_r,0,\ldots,0).\] Consequently, \(c^{-1}(0)\) is locally a \(C^1\) embedded manifold of dimension \(n-r\). Thus deficient row rank alone does not imply nonmanifold feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally constant but deficient constraint rank can represent a smooth feasible manifold whose codimension is the actual rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^{-1}(0)\text{ is locally an embedded manifold of dimension }n-r.

notation.meaning: local constant rank of the constraint Jacobian

knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Rank Deficient Representations Can Still Define Manifolds
Singular Feasible Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A rank-deficient equality whose linearization strictly overestimates feasible first-order motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be given by \(c(x)=x^2\), and let \(F=\{x:c(x)=0\}=\{0\}\). At the feasible point \(\bar x=0\), the Jacobian satisfies \(J(\bar x)=c'(0)=0\). Consequently, the linearized feasible-direction set is \(\ker J(\bar x)=\mathbb{R}\), whereas the Bouligand tangent cone is \(T_F(\bar x)=\{0\}\). Thus the equality linearization need not equal the actual tangent cone when constraint rank degenerates, and the feasible set cannot locally be represented as a codimension-one regular level-set manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the constraint x²=0, every direction satisfies the zero Jacobian equation, but the isolated feasible point has only the zero tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq\ker J(0)=\mathbb{R}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular point of an equality-defined feasible set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[c:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is }C^1,
\quad \mathcal M=c^{-1}(0),
\quad \bar x\in\mathcal M,
\quad J(x)=Dc(x).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-level singularity for smooth equality systems. The definition includes redundant smooth representations as well as genuinely nonmanifold feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality representation is singular at \(\bar x\) when \[\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)<m.\] It is rank-changing singular at \(\bar x\) when, in addition, every neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) contains points \(x,y\in V\) with \(\operatorname{rank}J(x)\ne\operatorname{rank}J(y)\). The first-order geometric discrepancy is measured by \[\Delta_c(\bar x):=\ker J(\bar x)\setminus T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x).\] A nonempty \(\Delta_c(\bar x)\) means the linearized equality system admits directions not realized as geometric tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality representation is singular at a feasible point when its Jacobian lacks full row rank. It is rank-changing singular if the Jacobian rank is not locally constant. The set difference between the Jacobian null space and the geometric tangent cone records spurious linearized directions. Singularity of the representation does not by itself prove that the feasible set is nonmanifold, because redundant equations can describe a smooth set singularly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\operatorname{rank}Dc(\bar x)<m,
\qquad \Delta_c(\bar x)=\ker Dc(\bar x)\setminus T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)<m\iff \exists\lambda\ne0:\ J(\bar x)^T\lambda=0.\]
\[\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)<m\iff \{\nabla c_i(\bar x)\}_{i=1}^m\text{ is linearly dependent}.\]
special_cases_latex:
\[c(x)=g(x)^2,
\quad g(\bar x)=0:\quad Dc(\bar x)=0\text{ even when }\{g=0\}\text{ is a smooth hypersurface}.\]

\[c(x)=x^2\text{ on }\mathbb R:\quad \mathcal M=\{0\},
\ker Dc(0)=\mathbb R,
T_{\mathcal M}(0)=\{0\}.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[J(\bar x)J(\bar x)^T\text{ is singular}.\]
\[\dim\ker J(\bar x)>n-m.\]
boundary_notes: Rank deficiency can arise solely from redundant equations and need not destroy manifold geometry.
The set difference \(\Delta_c(\bar x)\) is not generally a vector space.
Classical implicit elimination based on an \(m\times m\) nonsingular Jacobian block is unavailable at such a point.

notation.meaning: Spurious portion of the linearized space relative to the tangent cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-Rank Singular Representations Can Still Define Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes failure of full row rank from failure of manifold geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be \(C^1\), let \(c(\bar x)=0\), and suppose \(\operatorname{rank}J_c(x)=r<m\) throughout a neighborhood of \(\bar x\). Then the constant-rank theorem gives local diffeomorphisms of domain and codomain in which
\[
c(y)=(y_1,\ldots,y_r,0,\ldots,0).
\]
Consequently, \(c^{-1}(0)\) is locally a \(C^1\) embedded manifold of dimension \(n-r\), even though the equality representation is row-rank deficient. Thus deficient rank alone does not imply nonmanifold feasible geometry; rank variation or higher-order degeneracy must be examined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally constant but deficient constraint rank may represent a perfectly smooth feasible manifold, with codimension equal to the actual rank rather than the number of equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Locally, \(c^{-1}(0)\) is an embedded manifold of dimension \(n-r\).

notation.meaning: local constant rank of the constraint Jacobian

children.title: Tangent–Normal Decomposition
children.top_down_role: The geometric separation of feasibility-preserving motion from constraint-correcting motion.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},
\quad \mathcal T=\ker J,
\quad \mathcal N=unction{range}(J^T).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean finite-dimensional decomposition for a constraint Jacobian of arbitrary rank. The subspaces exist even when the equality representation is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The tangent–normal decomposition induced by \(J\) is the unique orthogonal splitting \[\mathbb R^n=\mathcal T\oplus\mathcal N,
\qquad \mathcal T=\ker J,
\qquad \mathcal N=\operatorname{range}J^T.\] Thus every \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) has unique components \[p=p_T+p_N,
\qquad p_T\in\ker J,
\qquad p_N\in\operatorname{range}J^T,
\qquad p_T^Tp_N=0.\] With the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, \[p_N=J^{\dagger}Jp,
\qquad p_T=(I-J^{\dagger}J)p.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint Jacobian \(J\) splits the primal space orthogonally into the tangent subspace \(\ker J\) and the normal subspace \(\operatorname{range}J^T\). Every vector has one unique tangent component and one unique normal component. The pseudoinverse projectors are \(I-J^{\dagger}J\) and \(J^{\dagger}J\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\mathbb R^n=\ker J\oplus\operatorname{range}J^T,
\qquad P_T=I-J^{\dagger}J,
\qquad P_N=J^{\dagger}J.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal N=\mathcal T^{\perp}.\]

\[P_T^2=P_T=P_T^T,
\quad P_N^2=P_N=P_N^T,
\quad P_TP_N=0,
\quad P_T+P_N=I.\]
special_cases_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}J=m:\quad P_N=J^T(JJ^T)^{-1}J.\]

\[J=0:\quad P_T=I,
\quad P_N=0.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[p_N\text{ is the minimum-distance Euclidean correction from }p\text{ to }\ker J.\]
boundary_notes: For nonlinear constraints the decomposition varies with the evaluation point through \(J(x)\).
A non-Euclidean metric changes orthogonality and projector formulas but not \(\ker J\).
The normal component need not by itself satisfy a prescribed constraint residual equation.

notation.meaning: Euclidean tangent and normal orthogonal projectors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correspondence between tangent vectors and linearized feasible directions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[c:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m,
\quad \mathcal M=c^{-1}(0),
\quad \bar x\in\mathcal M,
\quad J=Dc(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order local correspondence for continuously differentiable equalities at a full-row-rank feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The tangent-space feasible-direction correspondence holds at \(\bar x\) when \[T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Jd=0\}=\ker J.\] Equivalently, every derivative \(d=\gamma'(0)\) of a differentiable feasible curve \(\gamma\) with \(\gamma(0)=\bar x\) satisfies \(Jd=0\), and, under full row rank, every \(d\in\ker J\) is realized by a local differentiable feasible curve. A null-space basis \(Z\) therefore gives reduced directions bijectively: \[q\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\longmapsto d=Zq\in T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular equality-feasible point, geometric tangent vectors are exactly the solutions of the linearized equality equation \(Jd=0\). Every differentiable feasible curve has such a derivative, and every null-space direction can be realized by a local feasible curve. If \(Z\) is a null-space basis, reduced-coordinate vectors \(q\) correspond one-to-one with tangent directions \(Zq\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)=\ker Dc(\bar x)=\{Zq:q\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[d\in T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)\iff Dc(\bar x)d=0.\]

\[Z^TDc(\bar x)^T=0,
\qquad \dim T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)=n-m.\]
special_cases_latex: \[c(x)=Ax-b:\quad \bar x+td\text{ is feasible for every }t\in\mathbb R\iff Ad=0.\]
\[n=m:\quad T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)=\{0\}.\]
immediate_consequences_latex:
\[\nabla f(\bar x)^Td=0\quad\forall d\in T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)
\iff Z^T\nabla f(\bar x)=0.\]
\[\text{First-order reduced optimization occurs in }\mathbb R^{n-m}.\]
boundary_notes: Without a constraint qualification, \(Jd=0\) may admit directions not belonging to the geometric tangent cone.
For inequalities, the linearized feasible object is generally a cone rather than a subspace.
The correspondence is first-order and does not make the straight line \(\bar x+td\) exactly feasible for nonlinear constraints.

notation.meaning: A local differentiable curve lying in the feasible set.

children.title: Tangent Spaces
children.top_down_role: Local linear spaces supporting reduced optimization at regular feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent space of a regular nonlinear equality level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(F=c^{-1}(0)\), and let \(\bar x\in F\). If the Jacobian \(J(\bar x)=Dc(\bar x)\) has full row rank \(m\), then \(F\) is locally an embedded manifold of dimension \(n-m\). Its tangent space at \(\bar x\) is the kernel of the constraint Jacobian:
\[
T_{\bar x}F=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:J(\bar x)d=0\}=\ker J(\bar x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular feasible point, the tangent space consists exactly of directions annihilated by the equality-constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\bar x}F=\ker J(\bar x)\) and \(\dim T_{\bar x}F=n-m\).

notation.meaning: Tangent space to the regular feasible manifold at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curve-Velocity Characterization of the Tangent Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent intrinsic characterization at a regular equality-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal M=c^{-1}(0)\) be a \(C^1\) embedded manifold near \(\bar x\). Then
\[
T_{\bar x}\mathcal M=\{\gamma'(0):\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\to\mathcal M\text{ is }C^1,\ \gamma(0)=\bar x\}.
\]
Under full row rank of \(Dc(\bar x)\), this set equals \(\ker Dc(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent vectors are exactly velocities of differentiable feasible curves and, at a regular equality point, exactly the Jacobian-null directions.
assumptions_latex: \(c(\bar x)=0\) and \(Dc(\bar x)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\bar x}\mathcal M=\{\gamma'(0):\gamma(0)=\bar x,\gamma(t)\in\mathcal M\}=\ker Dc(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Curve-Velocity Characterization of the Tangent Space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the source's algebraic tangent-space convention without adding regularity. At a nonregular point, this Jacobian nullspace is a linearized space and need not coincide with the velocities of feasible curves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S=\{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n:\mathbf{h}(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{0}\}\) and \(\mathbf{x}^*\in S\), the tangent space is defined by \(T(\mathbf{x}^*)=\{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^n:D\mathbf{h}(\mathbf{x}^*)\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{0}\}=\ker D\mathbf{h}(\mathbf{x}^*)\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T(\mathbf{x}^*)=\{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^n:D\mathbf{h}(\mathbf{x}^*)\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{0}\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nullspace representation of the tangent space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the curve-based tangent space of a continuously differentiable equality-constraint surface at a regular feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(x)=0\}\), where \(h_i\in C^1\) in a neighborhood of \(x^*\). If \(x^*\in S\) is regular, meaning \(\{\nabla h_i(x^*)\}_{i=1}^m\) is linearly independent, then
\[
T_S(x^*)=\ker \nabla h(x^*)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\nabla h(x^*)y=0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular feasible point of a continuously differentiable equality-constraint surface, the tangent space equals the nullspace of the constraint Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: h_i\in C^1\text{ in a neighborhood of }x^*
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_S(x^*)=\ker\nabla h(x^*)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:\nabla h(x^*)y=0\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearized tangent space for smooth equality constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the Jacobian-null-space linearization from the geometric tangent space and states the regularity condition under which they coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i(x)=0,\ i=1,\ldots,p\}\), where the \(a_i\) are continuously differentiable near \(x^*\in S\), and let \(J_e(x^*)\) have rows \(\nabla a_i(x^*)^T\). The linearized tangent direction space and affine tangent linearization are
\[
T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=\ker J_e(x^*)=\{d:J_e(x^*)d=0\},
\qquad x^*+T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*).
\]
Moreover, \(\dim T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=n-\operatorname{rank}J_e(x^*)\). If \(\operatorname{rank}J_e(x^*)=p\), then \(S\) is locally a regular level-set manifold, its geometric tangent space equals \(T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)\), and its dimension is \(n-p\). At a rank-deficient point, the Jacobian kernel is only a linearized tangent space and need not describe the full tangent geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Jacobian null space gives the linearized tangent directions of an equality-constrained set. Its dimension is n minus the Jacobian rank. Under full row rank it is the actual tangent space of the regular constraint manifold and has dimension n−p; without regularity that identification can fail.
assumptions_latex: a_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is continuously differentiable near }x^*\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=\ker J_e(x^*),\quad \dim T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=n-\operatorname{rank}J_e(x^*);\quad \operatorname{rank}J_e(x^*)=p\Rightarrow T_S(x^*)=T_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)\text{ and }\dim T_S(x^*)=n-p

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curve-based tangent plane of an equality-constraint surface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines tangent vectors through velocities of feasible differentiable curves. The manifold-dimension and linear-subspace conclusions require constraint regularity; continuous differentiability alone does not exclude singular level sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:h(x)=0\}\), where \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_m)\) and \(h_i\in C^1\). For \(x^*\in S\), define
\[
T_S(x^*)=\{\dot x(t^*):x:[a,b]\to S\text{ is differentiable and }x(t^*)=x^*\}.
\]
This is the tangent plane defined through feasible curves. If \(\operatorname{rank}\nabla h(x)=m\) at every \(x\in S\), then \(S\) is a smooth set of dimension \(n-m\), and its tangent planes are linear subspaces of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent plane at a feasible point is defined as the set of velocities of all differentiable curves on the equality-constraint surface that pass through that point. Under full-rank constraint regularity, the surface has dimension n minus m and its tangent planes are linear subspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_S(x^*)=\{\dot x(t^*):x(t)\in S,\ x(t^*)=x^*\};\quad \operatorname{rank}\nabla h(x)=m\ \forall x\in S\Longrightarrow \dim S=n-m.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Feasible Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order feasible directions defined solely by the equality linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a continuously differentiable equality mapping \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and a feasible point \(\bar x\) satisfying \(c(\bar x)=0\), the linearized feasible-direction space is
\[
L_F(\bar x):=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:J(\bar x)d=0\}=\ker J(\bar x).
\]
This definition is meaningful without a rank assumption. If \(J(\bar x)\) has full row rank, then \(L_F(\bar x)\) equals the tangent space of the regular level set. At a singular point it may strictly contain the Bouligand tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized feasible directions solve the homogeneous Jacobian equation; they equal true tangent directions under regularity but may overestimate them at singular points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_F(\bar x)=\ker J(\bar x)\), with \(T_F(\bar x)=L_F(\bar x)\) under full row rank.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension and Orthogonal Characterization of Linearized Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-algebraic structure of the equality linearization at an arbitrary feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(r\), then \(L=\ker J\) is a closed linear subspace and
\[
\dim L=n-r,\qquad L^\perp=\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T}).
\]
Equivalently, \(d\in L\) exactly when it is orthogonal to every row of \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Jacobian kernel has dimension n minus the Jacobian rank and is orthogonal to the transposed-Jacobian range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim\ker J=n-r\) and \((\ker J)^\perp=\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Singular Gap Between Tangent and Linearized Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable-equality inclusion and a canonical family witnessing strictness at rank-deficient points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(c\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\in F=c^{-1}(0)\), then
\[
T_F(\bar x)\subseteq\ker Dc(\bar x).
\]
The inclusion can be strict. For \(c_q(x)=x^q\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(q\ge2\), the feasible set is \(F=\{0\}\), so
\[
T_F(0)=\{0\},\qquad Dc_q(0)=0,
\qquad \ker Dc_q(0)=\mathbb R.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every true tangent direction satisfies the linearized equality, but singular equalities such as x to an integer power at least two can make every direction appear linearly feasible although the feasible point is isolated.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is differentiable at the feasible point for the inclusion.
\(q\) is an integer with \(q\ge2\) for the counterexample family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(\bar x)\subseteq\ker Dc(\bar x)\), with strict inclusion for \(c_q(x)=x^q\) at zero.

notation.meaning: Singular scalar equality map x ↦ x^q.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance Characterization of the Bouligand Tangent Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent metric characterization of feasible first-order motion at a singular equality-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=c^{-1}(0)\) with continuous \(c\), and let \(\bar x\in F\). The Bouligand tangent cone admits the equivalent characterization
\[
T_F(\bar x)=\left\{d:\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\operatorname{dist}(\bar x+td,F)}{t}=0\right\}.
\]
It is a closed cone but need not be convex or a linear space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction is Bouligand tangent exactly when first-order trial points in that direction approach feasibility at sublinear distance; the resulting cone may be nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(\bar x)=\{d:\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\operatorname{dist}(\bar x+td,F)/t=0\}\), a closed, not necessarily convex cone.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from y to F.

Tangent Cones at Singular Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Bouligand tangent cone, applicable without constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c(x)=0\}\) and \(\bar x\in F\). The Bouligand tangent cone to \(F\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
T_F(\bar x):=\left\{d:\exists\,x_k\in F,\ t_k>0,\ x_k\to\bar x,\ t_k\downarrow0,\frac{x_k-\bar x}{t_k}\to d\right\}.
\]
If \(c\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\), then every such tangent direction satisfies \(J(\bar x)d=0\), so \(T_F(\bar x)\subseteq\ker J(\bar x)\). Equality can fail when \(J(\bar x)\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent cone contains limits of scaled feasible displacements. It lies in the Jacobian kernel, but singularity can make the inclusion strict.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is differentiable at \(\bar x\) for the stated inclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_F(\bar x)\subseteq\ker J(\bar x)\), without guaranteed equality at singular points.

notation.meaning: Positive scaling sequence converging to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-norm normal correction for linearized equalities
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
\[J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},
\quad r\in\mathbb R^m,
\quad \mathcal N=unction{range}(J^T).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized feasibility correction in the Euclidean metric. Exact nonlinear feasibility generally requires repeated correction or a nonlinear projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A normal-space correction for residual \(r\) is a vector \(n\in\mathcal N\) satisfying \[Jn=-r.\] If \(J\) has full row rank, the interface is single-valued and equals \[\mathcal C_J(r):=-J^T(JJ^T)^{-1}r.\] It is the unique solution of \[\min_{n\in\mathbb R^n}\frac12\|n\|_2^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Jn=-r.\] For a nonlinear equality map at \(x\), taking \(J=Dc(x)\) and \(r=c(x)\) produces the minimum-norm step satisfying the linearized constraint equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal correction associated with \(J\) and residual \(r\) is the normal-space vector solving \(Jn=-r\). Under full row rank it is uniquely \(-J^T(JJ^T)^{-1}r\), which is also the minimum-Euclidean-norm solution of the linearized feasibility equation. With \(J=Dc(x)\) and \(r=c(x)\), this is the standard linearized correction for nonlinear equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\mathcal C_J(r)=-J^T(JJ^T)^{-1}r,
\qquad J\mathcal C_J(r)=-r,
\qquad \mathcal C_J(r)\in\operatorname{range}J^T.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal C_J(r)=-J^{\dagger}r\quad\text{for full-row-rank }J.\]
special_cases_latex: \[r=0:\quad \mathcal C_J(0)=0.\]
\[m=n\text{ and }J\text{ nonsingular}:\quad \mathcal C_J(r)=-J^{-1}r.\]
immediate_consequences_latex: \[n\perp\ker J.\]
\[p=n+Zq\text{ satisfies }Jp=-r\text{ for every }q\text{ when }JZ=0.\]
boundary_notes: If \(J\) is rank deficient, a correction exists only when \(-r\in\operatorname{range}J\), and multiplier coordinates may be nonunique.
The correction satisfies only the linearized nonlinear constraints; \(c(x+n)\) need not vanish.
Other metrics replace the Euclidean minimum-norm formula by a weighted one.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean normal space of a regular equality-feasible manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=c^{-1}(0)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable, and let \(\bar x\in F\) satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}J(\bar x)=m\). The Euclidean normal space is the orthogonal complement of the tangent space:
\[
N_{\bar x}F:=(T_{\bar x}F)^\perp.
\]
Because \(T_{\bar x}F=\ker J(\bar x)\), finite-dimensional orthogonal-complement identities give
\[
N_{\bar x}F=\operatorname{range}J(\bar x)^\mathsf{T}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular feasible point, the normal space is the orthogonal complement of the tangent space and the range of the transposed Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\bar x}F=(\ker J(\bar x))^\perp=\operatorname{range}J(\bar x)^\mathsf{T}\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean normal space to the feasible manifold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension and unique Euclidean decomposition induced by a full-row-rank equality Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Then \[\mathbb{R}^n=\ker J\oplus\operatorname{range}J^{\mathsf T},\qquad \dim\ker J=n-m,\quad \dim\operatorname{range}J^{\mathsf T}=m.\] Every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) therefore has a unique decomposition \[d=d_T+d_N,\qquad d_T\in\ker J,\quad d_N\in\operatorname{range}J^{\mathsf T},\quad d_T^{\mathsf T}d_N=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every ambient direction decomposes uniquely into orthogonal tangent and normal components of dimensions n−m and m.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-generated normal space for smooth equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the range-of-transposed-Jacobian normal space, its rank-dependent dimension, its orthogonality to the linearized tangent space, and the regularity boundary for interpreting it geometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i(x)=0,\ i=1,\ldots,p\}\), where the \(a_i\) are continuously differentiable near \(x^*\in S\), and let \(J_e(x^*)\) have rows \(\nabla a_i(x^*)^T\). The constraint-generated normal direction space and corresponding affine normal plane are
\[
N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=\operatorname{range}J_e(x^*)^T
=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p\alpha_i\nabla a_i(x^*):\alpha_i\in\mathbb{R}\right\},
\qquad x^*+N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*).
\]
It satisfies
\[
N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=(\ker J_e(x^*))^\perp,
\qquad \dim N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=\operatorname{rank}J_e(x^*).
\]
If \(J_e(x^*)\) has full row rank \(p\), this is the geometric normal space of the regular constraint manifold and has dimension \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraint-generated normal directions are the linear combinations of the equality-constraint gradients, equivalently the range of the transposed Jacobian. They form the orthogonal complement of the Jacobian null space and have dimension equal to the Jacobian rank, hence p only under full row rank.
assumptions_latex: a_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is continuously differentiable near }x^*\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=\operatorname{range}J_e(x^*)^T=(\ker J_e(x^*))^\perp,\quad \dim N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=\operatorname{rank}J_e(x^*),\quad \operatorname{rank}J_e(x^*)=p\Rightarrow \dim N_{\mathrm{lin}}(x^*)=p

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Feasibility Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-metric-norm correction for the linearized equality residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a differentiable equality mapping \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(M\), set \(J=J(x)\). If \(J\) has full row rank, compute
\[
d_N:=\underset{d}{\operatorname{argmin}}\ \tfrac12 d^\mathsf{T}Md\quad\text{subject to}\quad Jd=-c(x).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
d_N=-M^{-1}J^\mathsf{T}(JM^{-1}J^\mathsf{T})^{-1}c(x).
\]
The correction satisfies \(Jd_N=-c(x)\), belongs to the \(M\)-normal subspace \(M^{-1}\operatorname{range}J^\mathsf{T}\), and is the unique feasible linearized correction of minimum \(M\)-norm. Output \(x+d_N\) or combine \(d_N\) with a tangent step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the linearized constraints with the unique minimum-metric-norm step; the resulting correction lies in the metric-normal subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Jd_N=-c(x)\) and \(d_N=-M^{-1}J^\mathsf{T}(JM^{-1}J^\mathsf{T})^{-1}c(x)\).

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the current point.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Based Normal Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of regular normal vectors by equality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=c^{-1}(0)\) and suppose \(J(\bar x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank at \(\bar x\in F\). Every normal vector \(v\in N_{\bar x}F\) has the representation
\[
v=J(\bar x)^\mathsf{T}\lambda
\]
for some \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Full row rank makes \(J(\bar x)^\mathsf{T}\) injective, so this multiplier coordinate is unique and equals
\[
\lambda=(J(\bar x)J(\bar x)^\mathsf{T})^{-1}J(\bar x)v.
\]
If row rank is deficient, the same normal vector may have multiple multiplier representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-gradient combinations represent all regular normal vectors, and full row rank makes their multiplier coefficients unique.
assumptions_latex: \(c\in C^1\) near the feasible point \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\bar x}F=\{J(\bar x)^\mathsf{T}\lambda:\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\}\), with a unique \(\lambda\) for every normal vector.

notation.meaning: Equality-multiplier coordinates of the normal vector.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Dependent Projectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent and normal projectors induced by a positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(M=M^\mathsf{T}\succ0\). The \(M\)-orthogonal tangent and normal projectors are
\[
P_T^M=I-M^{-1}J^\mathsf{T}(JM^{-1}J^\mathsf{T})^{-1}J,\qquad P_N^M=I-P_T^M.
\]
They satisfy \((P_T^M)^2=P_T^M\), \((P_N^M)^2=P_N^M\), \(JP_T^M=0\), and
\[
\operatorname{range}P_T^M=\ker J,\qquad \operatorname{range}P_N^M=M^{-1}\operatorname{range}J^\mathsf{T}.
\]
Moreover, the two ranges are orthogonal under \(\langle u,v\rangle_M=u^\mathsf{T}Mv\). Taking \(M=I\) recovers Euclidean orthogonal projectors; other metrics generally yield Euclidean-oblique decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric determines complementary tangent and metric-normal projectors; Euclidean projectors arise when the metric is the identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I=P_T^M+P_N^M\), with tangent and metric-normal ranges orthogonal in the \(M\)-inner product.

notation.meaning: Metric-orthogonal projector onto the Jacobian kernel.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis Formula for the Metric Tangent Projector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent null-space-basis representation of the metric-orthogonal tangent projector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(M=M^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and let the full-column-rank matrix \(Z\) satisfy \(JZ=0\). Then \[P_T^M=Z(Z^{\mathsf T}MZ)^{-1}Z^{\mathsf T}M=I-M^{-1}J^{\mathsf T}(JM^{-1}J^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J.\] Moreover, \((P_T^M)^{\mathsf T}M=MP_T^M\), and the basis formula is unchanged when \(Z\) is replaced by \(ZR\) for any nonsingular \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metric tangent projector has equivalent tangent-basis and constraint-space formulas, is metric-self-adjoint, and is independent of the chosen tangent basis.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is a full-column-rank basis of \(\ker J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_T^M=Z(Z^{\mathsf T}MZ)^{-1}Z^{\mathsf T}M,\qquad(P_T^M)^{\mathsf T}M=MP_T^M.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the tangent null space

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a positive-definite metric \(W\), the weighted tangent projector is \(I-W^{-1}J^T(JW^{-1}J^T)^{-1}J\), and the complementary normal projector is the remaining term. They are idempotent, complementary, and orthogonal with respect to the \(W\)-inner product. The tangent projection is the closest vector in \(\ker J\) measured in the \(W\)-norm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local classification of smooth equality representations by Jacobian rank. It distinguishes full-row regularity, constant lower rank, and rank-changing singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint regularity regime at \(\bar x\) is classified as follows: \[(i)\ \text{full-row regular if }r(\bar x)=m;\] \[(ii)\ \text{constant-rank redundant if }r(\bar x)=r<m\text{ and }r(x)=r\text{ on some neighborhood of }\bar x;\] \[(iii)\ \text{rank-changing singular if no neighborhood of }\bar x\text{ has constant }r(x).\] In regime (i), \(\dim\ker Dc(x)=n-m\) locally and Jacobian-generated multiplier coordinates are unique.
