knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise state elimination retaining selected boundary states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the horizon by \(0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_J=N\). For \(x_{k+1}=F_kx_k+G_ku_k+b_k\), eliminate only the interior states of each block. Then \[x_{\tau_{j+1}}=\Phi_jx_{\tau_j}+\sum_{k=\tau_j}^{\tau_{j+1}-1}\Gamma_{j,k}u_k+d_j.\] Substitution gives an exactly equivalent problem in the controls and retained boundary states, and every eliminated state is uniquely recovered by forward recursion within its block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial condensing eliminates interior states blockwise while retaining boundary states, interpolating exactly between the original staged system and full condensing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary equations are equivalent to the original staged equalities, and all interior states are uniquely recoverable.

notation.meaning: propagation of control k to the next boundary state

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Condensing of Staged Equalities

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporal sparsity loss under state substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If full elimination gives \(x=Su+s\) and a quadratic model has Hessian blocks \(H_{xx}=H_{xx}^\top\), \(H_{xu}\), and \(H_{uu}=H_{uu}^\top\), then its condensed control Hessian is \[H_c=S^\top H_{xx}S+S^\top H_{xu}+H_{xu}^\top S+H_{uu}.\] Since a control generally affects many later states, \(H_c\) may be block dense even when the original staged model is sparse. Retaining boundary states through partial condensing limits this fill-in.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact state substitution can turn a sparse staged quadratic model into a dense control-space model; partial condensing trades dimension against fill-in.
assumptions_latex: The objective model is quadratic with conformable Hessian blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_c=S^\top H_{xx}S+S^\top H_{xu}+H_{xu}^\top S+H_{uu}\), which may be dense despite stagewise sparsity.
knowledge_statements.title: Condensing Fill-In

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elimination of states in a structured equality system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Partition variables as \(x=(y,u)\), where \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) are states and \(u\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\) are controls or design variables. Let the state equations be \(c(y,u)=0\), with \(D_yc(y,u)\) nonsingular on the domain of interest.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-equation and staged systems for which the state Jacobian can be solved efficiently; nonlinear elimination is local unless global solvability is separately known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Structured state elimination is the reduction obtained by defining a state solution operator \(S\) with \[c(S(u),u)=0\] and replacing the full problem by the reduced objective \(F(u)=f(S(u),u)\), together with any transformed side constraints on \((S(u),u)\). At a regular point, the state sensitivity and tangent lift are \[DS(u)=-D_yc(S(u),u)^{-1}D_uc(S(u),u),\qquad d(u;w)=\binom{DS(u)w}{w}.\] The elimination is called structured when applications of \(D_yc^{-1}\) exploit the block-triangular, banded, staged, or state-propagation structure of the equations rather than forming a generic dense inverse. In a linearized calculation, state increments are condensed as \(\delta y=-D_yc^{-1}(c+D_uc\,\delta u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured state elimination solves the state equations for the state variables as functions of controls or design variables and substitutes that solution into the objective and side constraints. Its defining tangent operation solves the state Jacobian against a control perturbation. The representation is structured when those solves exploit staged, banded, triangular, or propagation structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x(u)=(S(u),u),\qquad c(x(u))=0,\qquad DS(u)=-D_yc(x(u))^{-1}D_uc(x(u)).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tangent lift is the partition-based null-space action \(w\mapsto(-D_yc^{-1}D_uc\,w,w)\).
Linearized elimination is block Gaussian condensation of the state increments.
special_cases_latex: For discrete-time dynamics, forward state propagation is the state solution operator.
For affine state equations, the condensed map is affine and global whenever the state block is nonsingular.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced calculation has the dimension of the control or design variables.
Full-space feasible states can be reconstructed from a reduced variable by applying \(S\).
boundary_notes: The notation \(D_yc^{-1}\) denotes a linear solve, not a requirement to form a dense inverse.
If the state Jacobian becomes singular, a single-valued differentiable state operator need not exist.

notation.meaning: State solution operator determined by the equality equations.

children.title: Null-Space Representations
children.top_down_role: Explicit and implicit descriptions of the tangent degrees of freedom.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) satisfy \(AZ=0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)=n-m\), and let \(p_F\) be any particular solution of \(Ap=r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linearized equality corrections in finite dimensions, using explicit tangent coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A null-space representation of \(Ap=r\) is the parameterization \[p=p_F+Zz,\qquad z\in\mathbb R^{n-m}.\] Its defining properties are \(Ap_F=r\), \(AZ=0\), and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\); hence it represents every solution of the equality equation exactly once. For the quadratic model \(g^Tp+\tfrac12p^THp\), stationarity over the feasible affine set is represented by the reduced system \[(Z^THZ)z=-Z^T(g+Hp_F).\] The matrix \(Z^THZ\) is the reduced Hessian. A multiplier may subsequently be recovered from \(A^T\lambda=-g-Hp\) when the right-hand side belongs to \(\operatorname{range}(A^T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space representation writes every equality-feasible correction as one particular feasible correction plus a linear combination of tangent basis vectors. Substitution into a quadratic model produces a reduced system whose dimension is the number of unconstrained degrees of freedom and whose coefficient matrix is the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\{p:Ap=r\}=\{p_F+Zz:z\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(r=0\), every tangent correction is \(p=Zz\).
Changing basis to \(ZT\) with invertible \(T\) changes coordinates but not the represented tangent space.
special_cases_latex: If \(Z\) has orthonormal columns, then \(z=Z^T(p-p_F)\).
If \(n-m\) is small, the reduced system can be substantially smaller than the full KKT system.
immediate_consequences_latex: The equality equations are satisfied identically after parameterization.
Positive definiteness of \(Z^THZ\) gives a unique reduced correction.
boundary_notes: Forming an explicit dense \(Z\) can destroy sparsity.
A rank-deficient \(A\) requires a null-space dimension based on \(\operatorname{rank}(A)\), not the nominal number of equalities.

notation.meaning: Particular solution of the linear equality equation.

children.title: Orthogonal-Factorization Bases
children.top_down_role: Stable tangent bases obtained from QR- or LQ-type factorizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal-Factorization Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthonormal null-space bases extracted from a full QR factorization of the transposed Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), with \(m\le n\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\). In a full QR factorization \(A^{T}=Q\begin{bmatrix}R\\0\end{bmatrix}\), let \(Q=[Y\ Z]\), where \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular, \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\), and \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\). Orthogonality of \(Q\) gives \(Z^{T}Z=I\), while the factorization gives \(AZ=0\). Hence \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker(A)\), and every tangent step has the unique representation \(d=Zp\). An LQ factorization of \(A\) yields the same construction without explicitly factoring \(A^{T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full QR or LQ factorization separates range and null-space factors, furnishing an orthonormal tangent basis and unique reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AZ=0\), \(Z^{T}Z=I\), and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker(A)\).

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal null-space bases obtained from a rank-revealing QR or LQ factorization when constraint rows may be dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\). A rank-revealing orthogonal factorization of \(A^T\) may be written
\[A^T\Pi=Q\begin{bmatrix}R_{11}&R_{12}\\0&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad Q=[Q_1\ Z],\]
where \(R_{11}\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) is nonsingular, \(Q_1\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\). Then \(Z^TZ=I\), \(AZ=0\), and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker(A)\). Thus the nullity is \(n-r\), rather than \(n-m\), when the constraint rows are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-revealing QR or LQ factorization yields an orthonormal null-space basis whose dimension is the number of variables minus the identified rank.
assumptions_latex: The rank-revealing factorization identifies the intended rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^TZ=I\), \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker(A)\), and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\).

notation.meaning: rank identified for the constraint matrix
permutation used by the rank-revealing factorization

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Orthogonal Null-Space Factorization

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank with \(m\le n\). Let a complete QR factorization of \(A^T\) be \(A^T=Q_1R\), where \(Q=[Q_1\ Q_2]\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is orthogonal and \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular upper triangular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean orthonormal range and null-space bases obtained by complete QR, LQ, or an equivalent complete orthogonal factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The orthogonal-factorization null-space basis associated with the complete factorization is \(Z=Q_2\). It satisfies \[AZ=0,\qquad Z^TZ=I_{n-m},\qquad Q_1^TZ=0,\] and its columns form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker A\), while the columns of \(Q_1\) span \(\operatorname{range}(A^T)\). Consequently, every vector has the orthogonal decomposition \(v=Q_1Q_1^Tv+ZZ^Tv\), and \(ZZ^T\) is the Euclidean projector onto the tangent null space. An LQ factorization of \(A\) gives the same construction by partitioning the orthogonal right factor into row-space and null-space columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete orthogonal factorization separates an orthonormal basis for the range of the transposed constraint matrix from an orthonormal basis for its null space. The latter block is the orthogonal-factorization null-space basis. It yields orthogonal normal and tangent components and represents the tangent projector as the basis times its transpose.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Z=Q_2,\qquad AZ=0,\qquad Z^TZ=I,\qquad \operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(ZZ^T=I-Q_1Q_1^T\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\).
A complete LQ factorization of \(A\) produces the same row-space/null-space split.
special_cases_latex: When \(m=n\), the null-space block has zero columns.
Rank-revealing orthogonal factorizations can extend the construction when numerical rank must be determined.
immediate_consequences_latex: For any tangent vector \(p\), its reduced coordinates are \(z=Z^Tp\) and \(\|p\|_2=\|z\|_2\).
boundary_notes: A dense orthogonal factor can be expensive or unsuitable for large sparse systems.
Ordinary QR without the complementary orthogonal block does not explicitly supply \(Z\).

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for the normal range space.
Orthonormal basis for the tangent null space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-space basis induced by a dependent/free column partition
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Choose a permutation matrix \(P\) such that \(AP=[B\ N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular and \(N\in\mathbb R^{m\times(n-m)}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit, generally nonorthogonal null-space bases tied to a chosen partition of dependent and independent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The partition-based null-space basis associated with \((B,N,P)\) is \[Z=P\binom{-B^{-1}N}{I_{n-m}}.\] It has full column rank and satisfies \(AZ=0\). For a free-coordinate vector \(z\), the permuted tangent step has dependent component \(-B^{-1}Nz\) and independent component \(z\). Thus the basis encodes exactly the linear response of the dependent variables required to preserve the equality equation. Different admissible pivot blocks produce different bases of the same null space, and these bases need not be orthogonal or equally well conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a nonsingular square block of constraint columns as dependent variables and treat the remaining columns as free variables. A unit change in the free coordinates determines the dependent change by solving with the selected block. Stacking these changes yields an explicit null-space basis, adjusted by the column permutation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Z=P\binom{-B^{-1}N}{I},\qquad AZ=0,\qquad\operatorname{rank}(Z)=n-m.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In permuted coordinates, every tangent vector is \((-B^{-1}Nz,z)\).
The same matrix is the derivative of affine dependent-variable elimination with respect to free variables.
special_cases_latex: If \(N=0\), then the free variables themselves span the null space.
A sparse or well-conditioned pivot block may make applications of \(Z\) inexpensive.
immediate_consequences_latex: No complete orthogonal factorization is required.
The reduced Hessian is \(Z^THZ\) in the selected free coordinates.
boundary_notes: Nonsingularity of \(B\) does not guarantee good conditioning.
The basis is generally nonorthogonal, so reduced-coordinate Euclidean norms need not equal full-space norms.

notation.meaning: Remaining free-variable columns of the constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Fundamental Null-Space Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity-normalized null-space basis associated with a nonsingular column partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and choose a column permutation \(\Pi\) such that \(A\Pi=[B\ N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Define \(Z_f=\Pi\begin{bmatrix}-B^{-1}N\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}\). Then \(AZ_f=0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(Z_f)=n-m\), and therefore \(\operatorname{range}(Z_f)=\ker(A)\). For each vector of free coordinates \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\), the tangent vector \(d=Z_fp\) has permuted basic block \(-B^{-1}Np\) and nonbasic block \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular constraint-column block yields an identity-normalized null-space basis whose coordinates equal the selected free-variable components.
assumptions_latex: The selected square block \(B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_f=\Pi[-B^{-1}N;I_{n-m}]\) has full column rank and spans \(\ker(A)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Reduction Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent and particular steps obtained by solving for selected dependent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), and choose a permutation matrix \(\Pi\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) such that \(A\Pi=[A_D\ A_I]\), where \(A_D\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular and \(A_I\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(n-m)}\). For a step \(d\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), define its permuted blocks by \(\Pi^{T}d=(d_D,d_I)\). The equality \(Ad=-c\) is then \(A_Dd_D+A_Id_I=-c\). Setting \(d_I=p\), where \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\), gives the complete affine solution representation \[d=\Pi\left(\begin{bmatrix}-A_D^{-1}c\\0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-A_D^{-1}A_I\\I_{n-m}\end{bmatrix}p\right).\] The first term is a particular equality-correction step, and the second matrix is a null-space basis. Thus optimization over equality-compatible steps reduces to optimization over the independent-variable increment \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After permuting variables into dependent and independent blocks, solving the linearized equalities for the dependent increments separates a particular correction from a null-space mapping of the independent increments.
assumptions_latex: The permutation \(\Pi\) satisfies \(A\Pi=[A_D\ A_I]\), where \(A_D\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solution of \(Ad=-c\) equals \(\Pi([-A_D^{-1}c;0]+[-A_D^{-1}A_I;I_{n-m}]p)\) for a unique \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\).

children.title: Basis Partition Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for choosing dependent and free coordinate blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Partition Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-revealing selection of a nonsingular and acceptably conditioned basic column block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a full-row-rank matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and a reciprocal-condition threshold \(\tau\in(0,1]\). Compute a column-pivoted rank-revealing factorization of \(A\), producing a permutation \(\Pi\) and a partition \(A\Pi=[B\ N]\) with \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\). Accept the partition if \(B\) is nonsingular and \(\operatorname{rcond}(B)\ge\tau\). Otherwise, apply stronger pivoting or examine another column partition. If an admissible partition is found, form basis actions by triangular or factored solves with \(B\), without explicitly computing \(B^{-1}\), and output \((\Pi,B,N)\). If no examined nonsingular column partition meets the threshold, report failure for the prescribed \(\tau\) rather than returning an unqualified accepted basis. When the Jacobian changes, repeat the conditioning test and reselection if necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pivoting searches for a nonsingular basic block meeting a prescribed conditioning threshold and reports failure if the requested threshold cannot be attained.
assumptions_latex: The reciprocal-condition estimator uses a fixed matrix norm and a consistent estimation procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On success, the output satisfies \(A\Pi=[B\ N]\), \(B\) is nonsingular, and \(\operatorname{rcond}(B)\ge\tau\); otherwise the algorithm reports that no accepted partition was found.

children.title: Partition-Basis Stability
children.top_down_role: Conditioning limits of bases induced by coordinate partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Basis Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning and perturbation sensitivity of an identity-normalized partition basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition \(A\Pi=[B\ N]\) with nonsingular \(B\), put \(M=B^{-1}N\) and \(Z=\Pi\begin{bmatrix}-M\\I\end{bmatrix}\). Then \(Z^{T}Z=I+M^{T}M\), so \(\lVert Z\rVert_2=\sqrt{1+\lVert M\rVert_2^2}\). Under perturbations \(B+\Delta B\) and \(N+\Delta N\), with \(B+\Delta B\) nonsingular, the first-order basis-factor change satisfies \[\Delta M=B^{-1}(\Delta N-\Delta B M)+O(\lVert(\Delta B,\Delta N)\rVert^2).\] Thus a large \(\lVert B^{-1}\rVert_2\) or \(\lVert B^{-1}N\rVert_2\) amplifies basis magnitude and sensitivity; stable partitions keep both controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The size and sensitivity of a partition basis are governed by the inverse basic block and the coupling factor between basic and free columns.
assumptions_latex: Perturbations are small enough that \(B+\Delta B\) remains nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert Z\rVert_2=\sqrt{1+\lVert B^{-1}N\rVert_2^2}\), with first-order sensitivity scaled by \(\lVert B^{-1}\rVert_2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse basis representation of a constraint null space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m\), and let \(s\) be a prescribed sparsity budget. Write \(\operatorname{nnz}(Z)\) for the number of structurally nonzero entries in \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional explicit null-space bases; sparsity is measured relative to an application-dependent budget or ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse null-space basis under budget \(s\) is a matrix \[Z\in\mathcal Z_s(A):=\{W\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}:AW=0,\ \operatorname{rank}(W)=n-m,\ \operatorname{nnz}(W)\le s\}.\] More generally, the term denotes a basis selected to limit storage and the fill generated when applying \(Z\), \(Z^T\), or forming reduced operators such as \(Z^THZ\). A common construction chooses a column partition \(AP=[B\ N]\) and uses \(Z=P(-B^{-1}N,I)^T\), selecting the pivot block and ordering so that solves with \(B\) and the product \(B^{-1}N\) remain sparse. Sparsity is a representation property: two bases can span the same null space while having very different nonzero patterns and conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse null-space basis is a full-rank basis of the constraint null space whose nonzero pattern meets a stated storage or fill objective. Partition-based constructions select dependent columns and an ordering so that the required solves and resulting basis remain sparse. Sparsity belongs to the chosen basis, not to the null space alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[AZ=0,\qquad\operatorname{rank}(Z)=n-m,\qquad\operatorname{nnz}(Z)\le s.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A basis may be selected by minimizing a stated structural cost \(\psi(Z)\), such as \(\operatorname{nnz}(Z)\) or predicted fill in \(Z^THZ\), over all bases of \(\ker A\).
special_cases_latex: A partition basis is sparse when the chosen factorization of \(B\) and the matrix \(B^{-1}N\) have acceptable fill.
An orthonormal basis is not generally sparse.
immediate_consequences_latex: Sparse applications of \(Z\) and \(Z^T\) can reduce storage and arithmetic in reduced-space methods.
boundary_notes: There is no universal numerical threshold defining sparse; the budget or structural objective must be specified by the application.
Minimizing basis nonzeros alone need not minimize fill in \(Z^THZ\) or provide good conditioning.

notation.meaning: Number of structurally nonzero entries in the basis matrix.
Family of null-space bases satisfying the prescribed sparsity budget.

children.title: Implicit Null-Space Projectors
children.top_down_role: Tangent actions performed without forming a null-space basis.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Null-Space Projectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean tangent projection computed through constraint-space solves without forming a basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. The Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\ker(A)\) is \[P=I-A^{T}(AA^{T})^{-1}A.\] It satisfies \(P^{T}=P\), \(P^{2}=P\), \(AP=0\), and \(Pv=v\) for every \(v\in\ker(A)\). Consequently, the tangent projection of \(v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\) can be evaluated without constructing a null-space basis: solve \((AA^{T})w=Av\) and return \(v-A^{T}w\). The complementary component \(A^{T}w\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}(A^{T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent projection can be applied by solving a constraint-space normal equation and subtracting the resulting range-space component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=I-A^{T}(AA^{T})^{-1}A\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker(A)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudoinverse Form of the Implicit Tangent Projector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-independent Euclidean null-space projection without constructing an explicit basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), including a rank-deficient matrix, the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\ker(A)\) is
\[P_{\ker A}=I-A^{\dagger}A=I-A^T(AA^T)^{\dagger}A,\]
where \(A^{\dagger}\) is the Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse. It is symmetric and idempotent, satisfies \(AP_{\ker A}=0\), and acts as the identity on \(\ker(A)\). When \(A\) has full row rank, this reduces to \(I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pseudoinverse formula extends the basis-free orthogonal tangent projector to rank-deficient matrices and reduces to the normal-equation formula under full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\ker A}=I-A^{\dagger}A\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\ker(A)\).

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the null space of A

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit weighted projector onto equality-tangent directions
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\). Define \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\), which is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear equality tangent spaces with Euclidean or symmetric positive-definite weighted inner products; no explicit null-space basis is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implicit \(H\)-orthogonal null-space projector is \[P_H=I-H^{-1}A^TS^{-1}A,\qquad S=AH^{-1}A^T.\] It is characterized by \(P_H^2=P_H\), \(AP_H=0\), \(\operatorname{range}(P_H)=\ker A\), and \(P_H^TH=HP_H\). For every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P_Hv\) is the unique minimizer of \(\tfrac12\|p-v\|_H^2\) subject to \(Ap=0\). The projector is implicit when its action is computed by solving \(Sy=Av\) and returning \(v-H^{-1}A^Ty\), without constructing either \(P_H\) or a basis \(Z\). For \(H=I\), this becomes the Euclidean projector \(I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit null-space projector maps any vector to its weighted orthogonal tangent component. Its action is computed through a constraint-space solve and a back-projection, so neither a dense projector matrix nor an explicit null-space basis is required. The map is idempotent, annihilates the constraint Jacobian, and is self-adjoint in the weighted inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_H=I-H^{-1}A^T(AH^{-1}A^T)^{-1}A,\quad P_H^2=P_H,\quad AP_H=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(P_Hv=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ap=0}\tfrac12\|p-v\|_H^2\).
If \(Z\) spans \(\ker A\), then \(P_H=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^TH\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H=I\), \(P_H\) is the ordinary Euclidean orthogonal projector.
If an orthonormal null-space basis is available and \(H=I\), then \(P_H=ZZ^T\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Projected gradients and tangent matrix-vector products can be computed without storing a null-space basis.
boundary_notes: The displayed inverse requires full row rank of \(A\) and positive definiteness of \(H\).
Normal-equation solves may be poorly conditioned even when the projector is mathematically well defined.

notation.meaning: Weighted orthogonal projector onto the constraint null space.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Range-space representation of an equality-constrained correction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and consider \(Hp+A^T\lambda=-g\), \(Ap=r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact multiplier-space reduction for a positive-definite primal metric or Hessian; the reduced system dimension is the number of equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The range-space representation eliminates the primal correction through \[p=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda)\] and determines the multiplier from the constraint-space system \[(AH^{-1}A^T)\lambda=-r-AH^{-1}g.\] The matrix \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\) is symmetric positive definite, and its vectors lie in the multiplier space \(\mathbb R^m\). After solving for \(\lambda\), the primal correction is reconstructed by one additional solve with \(H\). The term range-space reflects that the normal component of the correction is generated by \(H^{-1}A^T\lambda\), the weighted image of constraint normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A range-space representation first solves an equation whose unknown is the equality multiplier and whose dimension is the number of constraints. It is obtained by eliminating the primal correction with the positive-definite primal matrix. The primal correction is then reconstructed from the multiplier through the weighted constraint normals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(AH^{-1}A^T)\lambda=-r-AH^{-1}g,\qquad p=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: It is the Schur-complement reduction of the full KKT system with \(H\) as the pivot block.
The normal correction belongs to \(\operatorname{range}(H^{-1}A^T)\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H=I\), the reduced matrix is \(AA^T\).
When \(m\ll n\) and solves with \(H\) are inexpensive, the multiplier system can be much smaller than the KKT system.
immediate_consequences_latex: Full row rank of \(A\) and positive definiteness of \(H\) imply that the range-space system has a unique solution.
boundary_notes: The representation requires usable solves with \(H\); it is not directly applicable when \(H\) is singular.
Forming \(AH^{-1}A^T\) can increase density and square conditioning effects.

children.title: Schur-Complement Multiplier Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduction to a system whose dimension follows the number of equality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Multiplier Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT reduction to a constraint-dimensional system for multiplier increments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), consider the KKT equations \(Hd+A^{T}\lambda=-g\) and \(Ad=-c\). Assume \(H\) is nonsingular and \(S=AH^{-1}A^{T}\) is nonsingular. Use solves with \(H\) to apply \(S\), solve \[S\lambda=c-AH^{-1}g,\] and recover \(d=-H^{-1}(g+A^{T}\lambda)\). With exact solves, the resulting pair \((d,\lambda)\) solves both KKT equations, and the reduced system has dimension \(m\). For an inexact multiplier solve, define \(r_{\lambda}=S\lambda-(c-AH^{-1}g)\); if the recovery solve with \(H\) is exact, the stationarity residual is zero and the equality residual satisfies \(Ad+c=-r_{\lambda}\). Stop when \(\lVert r_{\lambda}\rVert\) meets the prescribed linear-solve tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal step gives a constraint-sized Schur-complement system; exact reduced solves recover an exact KKT solution, while the reduced-system residual controls the equality residual for an inexact solve.
assumptions_latex: The KKT equations use the stated signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(r_{\lambda}=0\), then \(d=-H^{-1}(g+A^{T}\lambda)\) and \(S\lambda=c-AH^{-1}g\) solve the KKT system; with exact recovery and nonzero \(r_{\lambda}\), \(Ad+c=-r_{\lambda}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definiteness and nonsingularity of the multiplier reduction under positive-definite primal curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H^T\succ0\) and let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Then \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\) is symmetric positive definite. Consequently, the multiplier Schur system has a unique solution and is eligible for symmetric positive-definite solvers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier reduction by the primal Schur complement
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and consider the KKT system \(Gp+A^T\lambda=-g\), \(Ap=r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block elimination using an invertible positive-definite primal block; this slot identifies the specific Schur-complement construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Schur-complement multiplier reduction is block Gaussian elimination of \(p\) from the KKT system using \(G\) as the pivot. Its Schur complement is \[-S=-AG^{-1}A^T,\qquad S=AG^{-1}A^T,\] and the reduced multiplier equation and primal recovery are \[S\lambda=-r-AG^{-1}g,\qquad Gp=-g-A^T\lambda.\] Because \(G\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, \(S\succ0\). The defining reduction therefore replaces the \((n+m)\)-dimensional indefinite system by factorizations or solves with \(G\) and an \(m\)-dimensional positive-definite multiplier system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Schur-complement multiplier reduction eliminates the primal unknown from the block KKT equations. It forms a positive-definite constraint-space matrix from the constraint Jacobian and the inverse action of the primal block, solves the smaller multiplier equation, and then recovers the primal correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[S=AG^{-1}A^T\succ0,\qquad S\lambda=-r-AG^{-1}g,\qquad p=-G^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Block elimination transforms the KKT coefficient matrix to \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}G&A^T\\0&-S\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).
The lower-right block of the KKT inverse is \(-S^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(G\) is diagonal or block diagonal, applications of \(G^{-1}\) may be inexpensive.
If \(m\) is small, the principal reduced factorization is only \(m\times m\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier and primal correction are unique under the stated hypotheses.
boundary_notes: The construction is unavailable with \(G\) singular unless a different pivot, regularization, or generalized inverse is specified.
Explicit formation of \(G^{-1}\) is unnecessary; the notation denotes solves with \(G\).

notation.meaning: Positive-definite primal Schur complement in multiplier space.

children.title: Normal-Equation Projection
children.top_down_role: Constraint-space projection through normal-equation systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-Euclidean-norm equality correction obtained from a normal-equation solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\). The unique minimum-Euclidean-norm solution of \(Ad=-c\) is \[d_N=-A^{T}(AA^{T})^{-1}c.\] Equivalently, solve the normal equation \((AA^{T})w=c\) and set \(d_N=-A^{T}w\). Every solution of \(Ad=-c\) is \(d=d_N+z\) with \(z\in\ker(A)\), and \(d_N\) is orthogonal to \(z\). Thus the normal-equation solve supplies the range-space correction, while the remaining freedom is tangent to the equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving the constraint normal equations gives the unique minimum-norm correction; all other feasible corrections add a null-space vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_N=-A^{T}(AA^{T})^{-1}c\) uniquely minimizes \(\lVert d\rVert_2\) subject to \(Ad=-c\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection onto an affine equality set by normal equations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), and assume the affine set \(\mathcal L=\{p:Ap=r\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted least-distance projection onto linear equality constraints, computed through a constraint-space normal equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The normal-equation projection of \(v\) onto \(\mathcal L\) in the \(H\)-norm is the unique minimizer \[p_H=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ap=r}\tfrac12(p-v)^TH(p-v).\] It is represented by the multiplier normal equation \[(AH^{-1}A^T)y=Av-r\] and the reconstruction \[p_H=v-H^{-1}A^Ty.\] The displacement \(p_H-v\) is a weighted normal vector, while \(p_H\) satisfies the affine equality exactly. For \(r=0\), the mapping is linear and equals \(P_Hv\), where \(P_H=I-H^{-1}A^T(AH^{-1}A^T)^{-1}A\) is the weighted tangent projector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal-equation projection finds the closest point, in a positive-definite weighted norm, satisfying the affine equalities. The multiplier is obtained from a positive-definite system in constraint space, and the projected point is reconstructed by subtracting a weighted normal correction from the original vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(AH^{-1}A^T)y=Av-r,\qquad p_H=v-H^{-1}A^Ty,\qquad Ap_H=r.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(H(p_H-v)+A^Ty=0\) and \(Ap_H=r\) are the KKT equations of the least-distance problem.
For \(r=0\), \(p_H=P_Hv\) is the \(H\)-orthogonal projection onto \(\ker A\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H=I\), the normal equation is \((AA^T)y=Av-r\).
For \(v=0\), the result is the minimum-\(H\)-norm solution of \(Ap=r\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The projection is unique because the objective is strictly convex and the affine set is nonempty.
The residual displacement is orthogonal, in the \(H\)-inner product, to every tangent direction.
boundary_notes: Normal equations can amplify conditioning difficulties; orthogonal or augmented-system methods may be preferable numerically.
If \(A\) is rank deficient, the displayed inverse must be replaced by a rank-revealing or generalized-inverse formulation.

notation.meaning: Weighted projection of the given vector onto the affine equality set.
Multiplier solving the constraint-space normal equation.
Affine equality set onto which the vector is projected.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Range-Space Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-metric correction and tangent projection induced by a positive-definite weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. For \(c\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\), the unique minimizer of \(\tfrac12d^{T}Wd\) subject to \(Ad=-c\) is \[d_W=-W^{-1}A^{T}(AW^{-1}A^{T})^{-1}c.\] The associated \(W\)-orthogonal projector onto \(\ker(A)\) is \[P_W=I-W^{-1}A^{T}(AW^{-1}A^{T})^{-1}A.\] It satisfies \(AP_W=0\), \(P_W^2=P_W\), and \(P_W^{T}W=WP_W\). Both operations require only solves with \(W\) and the constraint-space matrix \(AW^{-1}A^{T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric induces a weighted minimum-norm equality correction and a corresponding metric-orthogonal tangent projector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_W=-W^{-1}A^{T}(AW^{-1}A^{T})^{-1}c\) is the minimum-\(W\)-norm correction, and \(P_W\) is the \(W\)-orthogonal tangent projector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniqueness or boundedness when the weighting matrix is not positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[1\ 0]\) and \(c=0\). For \(W=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\), every feasible vector \(d=(0,t)\) has \(\tfrac12d^TWd=0\), so the minimizer is nonunique. For \(W=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\), the same feasible family has objective \(-t^2/2\), which is unbounded below. Thus symmetry, or symmetry and invertibility, does not replace positive definiteness in the weighted projection result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite weight can destroy uniqueness, while an indefinite weight can make the correction problem unbounded.
assumptions_latex: The displayed weights replace the positive-definite metric assumed by weighted range-space reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without \(W\succ0\), a unique minimum-\(W\)-norm correction and a \(W\)-orthogonal projector are not guaranteed.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(W=W^T\succ0\), and let \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\). The correction space is \(\mathbb{R}^n\), equipped with the metric \(\langle u,v\rangle_W=u^TWv\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact linear algebra with independent equality constraints and a symmetric positive-definite weighting or preconditioning metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The weighted range-space reduction of \(Ap=r\) is the multiplier equation \[S_Wy=r,\qquad S_W:=AW^{-1}A^T,\] followed by reconstruction \(p=W^{-1}A^Ty\). Equivalently, \[p_W(r):=W^{-1}A^T(AW^{-1}A^T)^{-1}r\] is the unique solution of \[\min_{p\in\mathbb{R}^n}\tfrac12p^TWp\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=r.\] The induced weighted null-space projector is \[P_W:=I-W^{-1}A^T(AW^{-1}A^T)^{-1}A.\] It satisfies \(AP_W=0\), \(P_W^2=P_W\), and \(P_W^TW=WP_W\); hence its range is \(\ker A\), while \(I-P_W\) maps a vector to its \(W\)-orthogonal range-space component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-row-rank constraint matrix and a positive-definite metric, weighted range-space reduction solves an m-dimensional system with coefficient A W inverse A transpose and reconstructs the minimum-W-norm correction. It also defines the W-orthogonal projector onto the null space of A.
assumptions_latex: \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\), so the equation \(Ap=r\) is consistent under full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_W(r)=W^{-1}A^T(AW^{-1}A^T)^{-1}r\) is the unique minimum-\(W\)-norm correction satisfying \(Ap=r\), and \(P_W=I-W^{-1}A^T(AW^{-1}A^T)^{-1}A\) is the associated \(W\)-orthogonal null-space projector.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The pair \((p,y)\) satisfies \(Wp-A^Ty=0\) and \(Ap=r\).
For every \(z\in\ker A\), the correction satisfies \(z^TWp_W(r)=0\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(W=H\) gives the constraint-preconditioned projection associated with a positive-definite preconditioner \(H\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \(S_W=AW^{-1}A^T\) is symmetric positive definite.
Every \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) decomposes uniquely as \(v=P_Wv+(I-P_W)v\), with the two components \(W\)-orthogonal.
boundary_notes: If the constraint rows are dependent, the displayed inverse must be replaced by a compatible generalized inverse and uniqueness requires separate qualifications.
An indefinite weight does not define a norm and is outside this definition.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=G^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and right-hand sides \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic corrections; both primal and multiplier variables are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A full-space primal–dual representation is a coupled system for a primal correction \(p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) of the form \[Gp+A^T\lambda=s,	frac{}{}\qquad Ap=t,\] or, equivalently, \[\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}s\\t\end{bmatrix}.\] For the quadratic program \(\min_x\tfrac12x^TGx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), the solution representation is obtained with \(s=-c\) and \(t=b\). For a correction from a current point \(x\), sign conventions may instead use \(p=x^*-x\), \(g=c+Gx\), and \(h=Ax-b\); these conventions define the same coupled stationarity and feasibility equations after the corresponding sign change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space primal–dual representation retains the n primal variables and m equality multipliers in one coupled saddle-point system. Its block rows impose stationarity and equality feasibility simultaneously, without eliminating either variable block.
assumptions_latex: The dimensions of \(G\), \(A\), and the right-hand sides are conformable.
Existence or uniqueness is not part of the representation itself; it depends on the constraint rank and reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented solution set is \(\{(p,\lambda):Gp+A^T\lambda=s,\ Ap=t\}\), equivalently the solution set of the displayed \((n+m)\)-dimensional saddle-point system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The two block equations are the stationarity and primal-feasibility conditions of an equality-constrained quadratic model.
When a unique solution exists, eliminating \(p\) or parameterizing feasible \(p\) produces range-space or null-space representations of the same correction.
special_cases_latex: For \(t=0\), the primal correction is tangent to the equality constraints.
For \(G=I\), the system represents an orthogonal projection correction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The representation preserves the original sparsity and block structure of \(G\) and \(A\).
No inverse of \(G\) and no explicit null-space basis is required merely to state the system.
boundary_notes: The KKT matrix may be singular when constraint rows are dependent or reduced curvature is singular.
This definition does not prescribe a direct or iterative linear solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric KKT Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized equality correction with a symmetric Hessian model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\). A full-space primal–dual correction \((p,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) is represented by
\[
\begin{bmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\y\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}g\\c\end{bmatrix},
\]
equivalently, \(Bp+A^\top y=-g\) and \(Ap=-c\). If \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), then nonsingularity of \(Z^\top BZ\) implies that the KKT matrix is nonsingular and the correction \((p,y)\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal feasibility and dual stationarity corrections form one symmetric saddle-point system. With independent equality rows, the system is uniquely solvable when the reduced Hessian on the constraint null space is nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\), \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and \(Z^\top BZ\) is nonsingular
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{bmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) is nonsingular and determines a unique \((p,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-Program Interpretation of the Symmetric KKT System
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality interpretation of the full-space correction equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_p\ \tfrac12p^\top Bp+g^\top p\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=-c,\] where \(B=B^\top\) and \(A\) has full row rank. A pair \((p,y)\) satisfies its first-order conditions exactly when \[\begin{bmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\y\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}g\\c\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(Z\) spans \(\ker A\) and \(Z^\top BZ\succ0\), the pair is unique and \(p\) is the unique global minimizer, even if \(B\) is indefinite outside \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric KKT equations are the first-order conditions of an equality-constrained quadratic model; positive curvature on feasible directions yields its unique global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed system is the quadratic program's KKT system, and \(Z^\top BZ\succ0\) makes \(p\) its unique global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=G^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(t\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric equality-constrained quadratic models, with no requirement that the full Hessian be positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The symmetric KKT form is \[K\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}s\\t\end{bmatrix},\qquad K:=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}=K^T.\] Its first block row, \(Gp+A^T\lambda=s\), is the stationarity equation, and its second block row, \(Ap=t\), is the linear equality equation. If \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z\) has columns spanning \(\ker A\), then \(K\) is nonsingular whenever \(Z^TGZ\succ0\). For \(m>0\), the matrix is generally symmetric indefinite rather than positive definite; under positive reduced curvature its inertia is \((n,m,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric KKT form is the saddle-point matrix with Hessian block G, transposed constraint blocks, and a zero multiplier block. It simultaneously represents stationarity and feasibility and is nonsingular under independent constraints and positive reduced curvature.
assumptions_latex: For the stated nonsingularity qualification, \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\) and \(Z^TGZ\succ0\), where \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) is the canonical symmetric KKT coefficient matrix; under full row rank and positive reduced curvature it is nonsingular and has inertia \((n,m,0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Changing \(\lambda\) to \(-\lambda\) gives the alternative sign convention \(\begin{bmatrix}G&-A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) without changing the represented primal solution.
The system is the first-order system for the Lagrangian of an equality-constrained quadratic problem.
special_cases_latex: When \(G\succ0\), block elimination yields a positive-definite range-space Schur complement.
When \(t=0\), the correction lies in \(\ker A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Ordinary Cholesky factorization is not applicable to \(K\) when \(m>0\).
A symmetric-indefinite factorization can preserve the symmetry of the system.
boundary_notes: Symmetry does not imply nonsingularity.
Dependent constraint rows force singularity of the unregularized multiplier block representation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symmetric KKT form of the primal–dual barrier Newton equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior-point specialization of the symmetric full-space KKT representation after inequality constraints are expressed with slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\nabla_{xx}^{2}\mathcal L(x,y,z)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(Z=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\), and \(\Sigma=S^{-1}Z\). Then the primal--dual Newton equations can be written as
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
H&0&A_E(x)^T&A_I(x)^T\\
0&\Sigma&0&-I\\
A_E(x)&0&0&0\\
A_I(x)&-I&0&0
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}p_x\\p_s\\-p_y\\-p_z\end{bmatrix}
=-\begin{bmatrix}
\nabla f(x)-A_E(x)^Ty-A_I(x)^Tz\\
z-\mu S^{-1}e\\
c_E(x)\\
c_I(x)-s
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive slack variables and Σ = S⁻¹Z, the primal–dual barrier Newton equations have the displayed symmetric KKT form. This permits a symmetric linear-equation solver and can reduce the work per interior-point iteration.
assumptions_latex: f,c_E,c_I\text{ are sufficiently differentiable for the displayed derivatives to exist}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The primal--dual Newton equations admit the displayed symmetric KKT representation.}

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-augmented form algebraically equivalent to the symmetric KKT correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(\rho\in\mathbb R\), define \(B_\rho=B+\rho A^\top A\). The augmented system
\[
\begin{bmatrix}B_\rho&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\y\end{bmatrix}=-\begin{bmatrix}g+\rho A^\top c\\c\end{bmatrix}
\]
has exactly the same solutions as the symmetric KKT system with first block row \(Bp+A^\top y=-g\) and second block row \(Ap=-c\). Thus augmentation may alter numerical factorization properties without altering the exact primal–dual correction. When \(B\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), sufficiently large positive \(\rho\) can make \(B_\rho\) positive definite if \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a quadratic constraint term and the matching right-hand-side term preserves the exact KKT correction while potentially improving the primal block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Sol}(B_\rho,A,g+\rho A^\top c,c)=\operatorname{Sol}(B,A,g,c)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence between original and constraint-augmented saddle-point matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[K_0=\begin{bmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad K_\rho=\begin{bmatrix}B+\rho A^\top A&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad T_\rho=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\(\rho/2)A&I\end{bmatrix}.\] Then \(K_\rho=T_\rho^\top K_0T_\rho\). Hence the two matrices have identical inertia and nullity for every finite \(\rho\); augmentation cannot make a singular full KKT matrix nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint augmentation is a congruence transformation of the full saddle-point matrix, so it preserves inertia and singularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Inertia}(K_\rho)=\operatorname{Inertia}(K_0)\) and \(\dim\ker K_\rho=\dim\ker K_0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Augmented-system representation of a constrained projection
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and let \(r\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projection-oriented saddle-point systems; the usual stable regime has positive-definite reduced metric \(Z^THZ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The augmented-system form of the constrained projection of \(r\) is \[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}r\\0\end{bmatrix}.\] Thus \(Hu+A^Tv=r\) and \(Au=0\). When \(H\) is nonsingular and \(AH^{-1}A^T\) is nonsingular, the primal component is \[u=H^{-1}\bigl(I-A^T(AH^{-1}A^T)^{-1}AH^{-1}\bigr)r.\] More generally, the augmented system remains the defining representation whenever \(z^THz\ne0\) for every nonzero \(z\in\ker A\). It computes the constrained, metric-weighted component without explicitly constructing a null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An augmented-system form computes a projected primal vector and an auxiliary multiplier together in a symmetric saddle-point system. The zero second right-hand side forces the primal vector into the constraint null space, while the first equation imposes the chosen metric relation to the input.
assumptions_latex: For the explicit inverse formula, \(H\) and \(AH^{-1}A^T\) are nonsingular; positive definiteness of \(H\) is a standard sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented-system primal solution is the \(H\)-weighted projection of \(r\) into \(\ker A\), represented jointly with its multiplier by the displayed symmetric system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(H\succ0\), \(u\) uniquely minimizes \(\tfrac12u^THu-r^Tu\) subject to \(Au=0\).
Eliminating \(u\) yields the normal equation \((AH^{-1}A^T)v=AH^{-1}r\).
special_cases_latex: Using \(H\) as a preconditioner gives the constraint-preconditioner augmented system.
immediate_consequences_latex: No explicit matrix \(Z\) spanning \(\ker A\) is required.
The same factorization can be reused for multiple projection right-hand sides.
boundary_notes: This is a projection-oriented augmented system, not an augmented-Lagrangian penalty function.
If reduced nonsingularity fails, the system may have nonunique or nonexistent solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized correction representations for dependent equality constraints
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r<m\), let \(G=G^T\), and consider \(Gp+A^T\lambda=s\), \(Ap=t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact arithmetic with dependent constraint rows; feasibility and nonuniqueness are treated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The rank-deficient correction representation family is the collection of generalized full-, range-, and null-space descriptions of the solution set \[\mathcal C(s,t):=\{(p,\lambda):Gp+A^T\lambda=s,\ Ap=t\}\] when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\). Feasibility requires \(t\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). If \((p_0,\lambda_0)\in\mathcal C(s,t)\), every multiplier \(\lambda_0+\eta\) with \(\eta\in\ker A^T\) represents the same primal correction. A minimum-norm constraint correction may be selected as \(p_c=A^\dagger t\), with all solutions of \(Ap=t\) given by \[p=A^\dagger t+(I-A^\dagger A)w,\qquad w\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Stationarity then restricts the free null-space component and determines multipliers only modulo \(\ker A^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For dependent equality constraints, a correction representation denotes a solution set rather than automatically a unique primal–dual pair. Feasibility requires the equality residual to lie in the range of A; generalized inverses select canonical corrections, and redundant rows make multipliers nonunique.
assumptions_latex: The Moore–Penrose inverse \(A^\dagger\) is used for the canonical minimum-Euclidean-norm constraint correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(t\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), all equality corrections are \(A^\dagger t+(I-A^\dagger A)w\); compatible KKT multipliers, when they exist, are determined only up to addition of elements of \(\ker A^T\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Removing redundant rows produces a full-row-rank matrix with the same primal feasible affine set.
An orthonormal basis of \(\ker A\) parameterizes the free primal component independently of redundant constraints.
special_cases_latex: If \(t\notin\operatorname{range}(A)\), the exact correction set is empty.
If reduced curvature is positive definite on \(\ker A\), the primal correction can be unique even though the multiplier is not.
immediate_consequences_latex: The unregularized full KKT matrix has a null vector \((0,\eta)\) for every \(\eta\in\ker A^T\).
A unique multiplier requires a convention such as minimum norm or removal of redundant rows.
boundary_notes: Least-squares corrections for inconsistent right-hand sides are nearby inexact variants, not members of the exact set defined here.
No supplied locator was found that supports the complete pseudoinverse-based family with this exact scope.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Inverse Correction Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moore–Penrose parameterization of corrections for a possibly rank-deficient Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and let \(A^\dagger\) be its Moore–Penrose inverse. The linearized feasibility equation \(Ap=-c\) is solvable exactly if and only if \(c\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), equivalently \(AA^\dagger c=c\). Under this compatibility condition, every primal correction has the form
\[
p=-A^\dagger c+(I-A^\dagger A)w,
\]
where \(w\in\mathbb R^n\) is arbitrary. The first term lies in \(\operatorname{range}(A^\top)\), while the second ranges over \(\ker A\). Without compatibility, \(-A^\dagger c\) instead minimizes \(\lVert Ap+c\rVert_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pseudoinverse supplies a particular correction, and an arbitrary null-space component supplies every other correction; exact feasibility requires range compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ap=-c\iff c\in\operatorname{range}(A)\) and \(p=-A^\dagger c+(I-A^\dagger A)w\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic Moore–Penrose identities and projector structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(A^\dagger\) is characterized by \(AA^\dagger A=A\), \(A^\dagger AA^\dagger=A^\dagger\), \((AA^\dagger)^\top=AA^\dagger\), and \((A^\dagger A)^\top=A^\dagger A\). Thus \(AA^\dagger\), \(A^\dagger A\), and \(I-A^\dagger A\) project orthogonally onto \(\operatorname{range}(A)\), \(\operatorname{range}(A^\top)\), and \(\ker A\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Moore–Penrose identities and associated projectors are generic linear-algebra facts rather than a locally owned equality-correction statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AA^\dagger=P_{\operatorname{range}(A)}\), \(A^\dagger A=P_{\operatorname{range}(A^\top)}\), and \(I-A^\dagger A=P_{\ker A}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Moore–Penrose Inverse and Correction Projectors

children.title: Least-Norm Primal Corrections
children.top_down_role: Canonical primal representatives selected from nonunique correction sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Norm Primal Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean least-norm solution of the linearized equality correction equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(c\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), the problem
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert p\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=-c
\]
has the unique solution \(p_{\min}=-A^\dagger c\). It is characterized by \(Ap_{\min}=-c\) and \(p_{\min}\in\operatorname{range}(A^\top)=(\ker A)^\perp\). Every feasible correction is \(p_{\min}+z\) with \(z\in\ker A\), and therefore satisfies \(\lVert p_{\min}+z\rVert_2^2=\lVert p_{\min}\rVert_2^2+\lVert z\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among all exact primal feasibility corrections, the negative pseudoinverse correction is the unique one of minimum Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\min}=-A^\dagger c=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ap=-c}\lVert p\rVert_2\).

children.title: Least-Norm Dual Corrections
children.top_down_role: Canonical multiplier representatives selected under dual nonuniqueness.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Norm Dual Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean least-norm multiplier correction for a compatible stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a primal correction \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) and set \(r=g+Bp\). If \(r\in\operatorname{range}(A^\top)\), then the dual equation \(A^\top y=-r\) is consistent. Its unique minimum-Euclidean-norm solution is
\[
y_{\min}=-(A^\top)^\dagger r=-(A^\dagger)^\top(g+Bp).
\]
Every dual solution equals \(y_{\min}+q\) for some \(q\in\ker(A^\top)\), and \(y_{\min}\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). If compatibility fails, the same formula uniquely minimizes \(\lVert y\rVert_2\) among all least-squares minimizers of \(\lVert A^\top y+r\rVert_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed primal correction, the pseudoinverse gives the unique minimum-norm multiplier satisfying stationarity, or the minimum-norm least-squares multiplier if incompatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{\min}=-(A^\top)^\dagger(g+Bp)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{A^\top y=-(g+Bp)}\lVert y\rVert_2\).

children.title: Rank-Deficient Correction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity and interpretive limits of generalized correction forms near rank changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar example of lost correction sensitivity across a rank change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_\varepsilon=[\varepsilon]\) and \(c=[1]\). For \(\varepsilon\ne0\), the unique correction satisfying \(A_\varepsilon p=-c\) is \(p_\varepsilon=-A_\varepsilon^\dagger c=-1/\varepsilon\). Hence \(|p_\varepsilon|\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\to0\), whereas at \(\varepsilon=0\) the equation is inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar Jacobian approaching zero makes its exact pseudoinverse correction diverge and becomes inconsistent at rank loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_\varepsilon=-1/\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon\ne0\), while no exact correction exists at \(\varepsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudoinverse Blow-Up at Rank Loss

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity within, but not generally across, constant-rank regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(t)\) be continuous near \(t_0\). If \(\operatorname{rank}A(t)=r\) throughout a neighborhood, then \(A(t)^\dagger\) is continuous there, as is \(-A(t)^\dagger c(t)\) for continuous \(c(t)\). Across a rank change, continuity and local boundedness need not hold; if the smallest nonzero singular value satisfies \(\sigma_r(A(t))\downarrow0\), then \(\lVert A(t)^\dagger\rVert_2=1/\sigma_r(A(t))\uparrow\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pseudoinverse corrections are continuous on a constant-rank stratum, but may become unbounded when a nonzero singular value vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}A(t)\equiv r\Rightarrow A(t)^\dagger\text{ is continuous};\quad \sigma_r(A(t))\downarrow0\Rightarrow\lVert A(t)^\dagger\rVert_2\uparrow\infty.\)

notation.meaning: smallest nonzero singular value for rank r

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Continuity Boundary
Rank-Deficient Correction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness boundaries caused by dependent equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is rank deficient, the feasibility equation \(Ap=-c\) has no solution whenever \(c\notin\operatorname{range}(A)\). When it is consistent, primal corrections are nonunique whenever \(\ker A\neq\{0\}\). For the KKT equations, a nonzero \(q\in\ker(A^\top)\) implies that \((0,q)\) lies in the null space of the KKT matrix, so multipliers cannot be unique. Consequently, pseudoinverse corrections remain well defined, but they represent selected least-norm solutions rather than an inverse of the singular KKT operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency can destroy feasibility and always permits multiplier nonuniqueness through dependent constraint rows; pseudoinverses select representatives but do not restore invertibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\notin\operatorname{range}(A)\Rightarrow Ap=-c\text{ is inconsistent}\), and \(0\neq q\in\ker(A^\top)\Rightarrow (0,q)\in\ker\begin{bmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\).

children.title: Equivalent Correction Representations
children.top_down_role: Equivalence of full-, null-, and range-space corrections together with their distinct computational regimes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, \(G=G^T\), and suppose the KKT correction is uniquely defined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional corrections under independent constraints and nonsingular reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two correction representations are equivalent when, for every admissible right-hand side, they produce the same primal correction \(p\) and, where represented, the same multiplier \(\lambda\). The canonical taxonomy consists of: the full-space system \[\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}s\\t\end{bmatrix};\] a null-space representation \(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\), with \(AZ=0\), obtained from systems in dimensions \(m\) and \(n-m\); and, when \(G\) is nonsingular, a range-space representation based on the \(m\)-dimensional Schur complement \(AG^{-1}A^T\). These are algebraically equivalent representations but distinct computational regimes because they factor matrices of different dimensions, definiteness, conditioning, and sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy groups full-space, null-space, and range-space descriptions as equivalent when they return the same equality correction. They differ computationally because they expose different matrix dimensions, sparsity patterns, definiteness properties, and operator requirements.
assumptions_latex: The reduced KKT problem is nonsingular; a sufficient condition is \(Z^TGZ\succ0\).
The range-space member additionally requires nonsingularity of \(G\) and of \(AG^{-1}A^T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full-space, null-space, and admissible range-space systems form one equivalence class under equality of their reconstructed \((p,\lambda)\), while retaining distinct reduced dimensions and matrix structures.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Equivalence may be expressed by equality of the linear solution operators mapping \((s,t)\) to \((p,\lambda)\).
The null-space and Schur-complement systems are block eliminations or coordinate parameterizations of the full KKT equations.
special_cases_latex: When \(m\ll n\) and \(G^{-1}\) is inexpensive, the range-space member has small reduced dimension.
When \(n-m\ll n\), the null-space reduced Hessian has small dimension.
immediate_consequences_latex: Choosing a representation changes numerical work but not the exact correction.
Failure of a representation-specific assumption does not necessarily imply failure of the full KKT problem.
boundary_notes: Equivalence in exact arithmetic does not imply equal numerical stability in floating-point arithmetic.
Rank-deficient constraints require a generalized taxonomy.

notation.meaning: Complementary range and null-space basis matrices.

children.title: Full-Reduced Correction Correspondence
children.top_down_role: The equivalence family connecting coupled and eliminated equality corrections.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correspondence between coupled and null-space corrections
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker A\), and choose \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) so \([Y\ Z]\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact null-space reduction of a nonsingular equality-constrained quadratic KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The full-reduced correction correspondence maps a full KKT solution \((p,\lambda)\) to unique coordinates \((p_Y,p_Z)\) through \[p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z.\] For \[Gp+A^T\lambda=s,\qquad Ap=t,\] the coordinates are characterized by \[(AY)p_Y=t,\] \[(Z^TGZ)p_Z=Z^T(s-GYp_Y),\] and the multiplier is recovered from \[(AY)^T\lambda=Y^T(s-Gp).\] If \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z^TGZ\) is nonsingular, these operations define a bijection between solutions of the full KKT system and solutions of the two reduced coordinate systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correspondence decomposes every primal correction uniquely into a constraint-restoring component and a tangent component. Solving the small feasibility and reduced-curvature systems and then recovering the multiplier gives exactly the same pair as the coupled KKT system.
assumptions_latex: \(Z^TGZ\) is nonsingular; positive definiteness is a standard sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maps \((p,\lambda)\mapsto(p_Y,p_Z)\) and \((p_Y,p_Z)\mapsto(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z,\lambda)\) establish a one-to-one correspondence between full and reduced corrections.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The correspondence is a change of primal coordinates followed by elimination of the multiplier from the tangent equation.
Using a particular solution \(p_c\) of \(Ap=t\), one may write \(p=p_c+Zz\) and solve only for \(z\).
special_cases_latex: If \(t=0\), then \(p_Y=0\) for a complementary basis with nonsingular \(AY\), so \(p=Zp_Z\).
If \(AY=I\), the feasibility coordinate is directly \(p_Y=t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced system has dimension \(n-m\).
The exact reconstructed correction is independent of the particular valid basis \(Y,Z\), although conditioning is basis dependent.
boundary_notes: A poorly conditioned basis can degrade numerical accuracy without invalidating exact equivalence.
Rank-deficient constraints destroy the stated bijection unless redundant coordinates are removed.

children.title: Full-Space Corrections
children.top_down_role: Coupled primal-dual corrections represented in the original variable space.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction of a feasible full-space correction from range- and null-space components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Choose \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Av=-c\). Every \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ap=-c\) has a unique representation
\[
p=v+Zu,
\]
with \(u\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\). For the quadratic correction model \(\tfrac12p^\top Bp+g^\top p\), stationarity along all feasible directions is equivalent to
\[
Z^\top BZ\,u=-Z^\top(g+Bv).
\]
After computing \(u\), the corresponding full-space correction is \(p=v+Zu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible full-space correction is uniquely a particular feasibility correction plus a null-space component. For a symmetric quadratic model, projected stationarity gives the reduced linear system for that component.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible correction has the unique form \(p=v+Zu\), and projected stationarity is equivalent to \(Z^\top BZ\,u=-Z^\top(g+Bv)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Recovery from a Full-Space Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of the multiplier after a feasible primal correction satisfies projected stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and suppose \(Ap=-c\) and \(Z^\top(Bp+g)=0\). Then \(Bp+g\in\operatorname{range}(A^\top)\), and the unique \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(Bp+g+A^\top\lambda=0\) is \[\lambda=-(AA^\top)^{-1}A(Bp+g).\] Thus \((p,\lambda)\) solves the coupled correction equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under full row rank, a feasible correction satisfying projected stationarity has a unique multiplier, obtained from the normal equations.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda=-(AA^\top)^{-1}A(Bp+g)\) uniquely satisfies \(Bp+g+A^\top\lambda=0\).

notation.meaning: multiplier associated with the primal correction

children.title: Reduced-Space Corrections
children.top_down_role: Corrections represented through feasible degrees of freedom.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space coordinate system for equality-feasible correction directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), and let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Choose \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Av=-c\), and define
\[
H_R=Z^\top BZ,\qquad r_R=Z^\top(g+Bv).
\]
A reduced correction \(u\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\) satisfies \(H_Ru=-r_R\). If \(H_R\) is nonsingular, then \(u=-H_R^{-1}r_R\) is unique, and \(p=v+Zu\) satisfies \(Ap=-c\) and \(Z^\top(Bp+g)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null-space coordinates reduce the projected correction equation to the remaining degrees of freedom. If the reduced Hessian is nonsingular, the reduced correction and its reconstructed feasible full-space correction are unique.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(H_R=Z^\top BZ\) is nonsingular, then \(u=-H_R^{-1}r_R\) is unique and \(p=v+Zu\) satisfies \(Ap=-c\) and \(Z^\top(Bp+g)=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of reduced quantities under a change of null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) be bases of \(\ker A\). Then \(\widehat Z=ZT\) for a unique nonsingular \(T\). If \(H_R=Z^\top BZ\), \(r_R=Z^\top(g+Bv)\), \(\widehat H_R=\widehat Z^\top B\widehat Z\), and \(\widehat r_R=\widehat Z^\top(g+Bv)\), then \[\widehat H_R=T^\top H_RT,\qquad \widehat r_R=T^\top r_R.\] The equations correspond under \(u=T\widehat u\), and \(v+Zu=v+\widehat Z\widehat u\). Hence nonsingularity and inertia of the reduced Hessian are basis independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a null-space basis congruently transforms the reduced Hessian and changes coordinates but not the reconstructed correction or inertia.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) have full column rank
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat H_R=T^\top H_RT\), \(\widehat r_R=T^\top r_R\), and corresponding coordinates reconstruct the same correction.

notation.meaning: reduced Hessian in the alternative basis

children.title: Correction-Space Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural mapping between coupled corrections and eliminated corrections.

knowledge_statements.title: Correction-Space Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bijection between reduced coordinates and affine equality-feasible corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Fix \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Av=-c\). Then
\[
\Phi:\mathbb R^{n-m}\to\{p\in\mathbb R^n:Ap=-c\},\qquad \Phi(u)=v+Zu,
\]
is bijective. Moreover, for every \(u\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\), the equation \(Z^\top BZ\,u=-Z^\top(g+Bv)\) holds if and only if \(p=\Phi(u)\) satisfies \(Ap=-c\) and \(Z^\top(Bp+g)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space basis gives a one-to-one correspondence between reduced coordinates and feasible full-space corrections, and the correspondence preserves the reduced and projected stationarity equations.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi(u)=v+Zu\) is a bijection from \(\mathbb R^{n-m}\) to \(\{p\in\mathbb R^n:Ap=-c\}\) and preserves the reduced and projected correction equations.

notation.meaning: reconstruction map from reduced coordinates to feasible full-space corrections
