children.top_down_role: Block and staged elimination exploiting recurring equality structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Schur Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Staged Schur elimination for recurring block-structured equality systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(H_i=H_i^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n_i}\), \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\), and \(r_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,k\), and let \(s\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Set \(H=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\ldots,H_k)\) and \(A=(A_1,\ldots,A_k)\). Factor each nonsingular \(H_i\), form or apply \(S_i=A_iH_i^{-1}A_i^T\), and form or represent \(S=\sum_{i=1}^kS_i\). Solve \(S\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^kA_iH_i^{-1}r_i-s\) for \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and recover \(u_i=H_i^{-1}(r_i-A_i^T\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\). Unchanged block factors may be reused across repeated systems. Accept a computed solution only after checking every primal-block residual and the coupled constraint residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate independent nonsingular primal blocks separately, combine their Schur contributions, solve the coupled constraint equation, recover every primal block, and check all original residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The staged elimination and recovery produce \((u_1,\ldots,u_k,\lambda)\) satisfying the original structured KKT equations in exact arithmetic.

notation.meaning: primal diagonal block and its constraint coupling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Work of Additive Schur Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric sequential setup cost for explicitly assembling a dense structured Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one solve with available factors of \(H_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times n_i}\) cost \(T_i\). Explicitly forming \(W_i=H_i^{-1}A_i^T\) and \(S_i=A_iW_i\) for all blocks, summing the dense \(m\times m\) contributions, and factoring an SPD assembled complement requires \[O\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^k(mT_i+n_im^2)+km^2+m^3\right)\] sequential arithmetic. Storing only the assembled complement costs \(O(m^2)\); retaining all \(W_i\) additionally costs \(O(m\sum_i n_i)\). Reusable unchanged block factors remove their refactorization costs from later systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured formation costs the sum of the local solve and product costs plus dense assembly and factorization, while unchanged local factors can be reused.
assumptions_latex: Local and assembled Schur matrices are treated as dense.
The assembled complement is SPD when Cholesky work is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{work}=O\!\left(\sum_i(mT_i+n_im^2)+km^2+m^3\right).

notation.meaning: Cost of one solve using the available factors of H_i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cancellation of Indefinite Local Schur Contributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of local nonsingularity to imply nonsingularity after additive assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(m=1\), \(H_1=[1]\), \(H_2=[-1]\), and \(A_1=A_2=[1]\). Then \[S_1=[1],\qquad S_2=[-1],\qquad S_1+S_2=[0].\] Every primal block and local Schur contribution is nonsingular, but the assembled multiplier system is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular indefinite local contributions can cancel and produce a singular assembled Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_1\text{ and }S_2\text{ are nonsingular, but }S_1+S_2\text{ is singular}.
knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation of Indefinite Local Schur Contributions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Definiteness of an Additive Structured Schur Complement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definiteness criterion for a Schur complement assembled from independent SPD primal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_i\succ0\), \(A=(A_1,\ldots,A_k)\), and \[S=\sum_{i=1}^kA_iH_i^{-1}A_i^T.\] Then \(S\succeq0\) and \[y^TSy=0\iff A_i^Ty=0\ \text{for every }i\iff A^Ty=0.\] Consequently, \(S\succ0\) if and only if \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The additive Schur complement is positive semidefinite and is positive definite exactly when the aggregate constraint rows are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\succ0\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=m.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Definiteness of an Additive Structured Schur Complement

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\) be a block matrix whose variables are partitioned into ordered groups \(I_1,\ldots,I_q\), and suppose the pivot block selected at every elimination stage is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional block elimination that preserves and exploits a prescribed partition, sparsity graph, or repeated constraint structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Structured Schur elimination is recursive block Gaussian elimination in a prescribed block order. At stage \(j\), write the current matrix as \[K^{(j)}=\begin{pmatrix}E_j&F_j\\F_j^T&H_j\end{pmatrix},\qquad E_j\text{ nonsingular},\] eliminate the variables associated with \(E_j\), and define the next remaining operator by \[K^{(j+1)}:=H_j-F_j^TE_j^{-1}F_j.\] The recursion terminates with a final reduced block, which is solved directly or iteratively; eliminated variables are recovered in reverse order by block back-substitution. The elimination is structured when the partition and order are chosen so that the solves with \(E_j\), the products involving \(F_j\), and the nonzero pattern of \(K^{(j+1)}\) exploit recurring problem structure rather than treating \(K\) as an undifferentiated matrix. For a KKT matrix, the one-stage choice \(E_1=G\) produces the constraint Schur complement \(-AG^{-1}A^T\); multiple stages produce nested Schur complements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured Schur elimination recursively partitions the current system, eliminates a nonsingular block \(E_j\), and replaces the remaining block by \(H_j-F_j^TE_j^{-1}F_j\). A prescribed block ordering exploits repeated, sparse, or hierarchical equality structure, and reverse block substitution recovers all eliminated variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining recursion is \(K^{(j+1)}=H_j-F_j^TE_j^{-1}F_j\), followed by reverse recovery of eliminated blocks.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Each stage has the exact block factorization \(K^{(j)}=\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\F_j^TE_j^{-1}&I\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}E_j&0\\0&K^{(j+1)}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}I&E_j^{-1}F_j\\0&I\end{pmatrix}\).
special_cases_latex: A single primal-block elimination of \(\begin{pmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\) yields \(-AG^{-1}A^T\).
Block-diagonal \(E_j\) permits independent local eliminations before a smaller coupling system is solved.
immediate_consequences_latex: The final reduced system represents all eliminated blocks exactly.
The chosen order determines intermediate fill and computational cost, though not the exact solution.
boundary_notes: If a required pivot block is singular, this recursion needs permutation, regularization, or generalized elimination.
Dropping fill or approximating a Schur block produces an approximate, not exact, structured elimination.

notation.meaning: The remaining block operator before elimination stage \(j\).
The nonsingular pivot block eliminated at stage \(j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Definiteness of the Additive Structured Schur Complement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definiteness and singularity characterization for a Schur complement assembled from independent SPD primal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_i\succ0\), \(A=(A_1,\ldots,A_k)\), and
\[S=\sum_{i=1}^k A_iH_i^{-1}A_i^T.\]
Then \(S\succeq0\) and
\[y^TSy=0\iff A_i^Ty=0\ \text{for every }i\iff A^Ty=0.\]
Consequently, \(S\succ0\) if and only if the aggregate constraint matrix \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of local Schur contributions is positive semidefinite and is positive definite exactly when the combined constraint rows are independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\succ0\iff\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block elimination for a positive-definite KKT system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range-space Schur-complement solution of an equality-constrained KKT system. No full-row-rank assumption on A is stated, so solvability and uniqueness of the reduced equation are not automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the KKT system \(Hv+A^Tw=-g\), \(Av=-h\), with \(H\succ0\), form \(H^{-1}A^T\) and \(H^{-1}g\), set \(S=-AH^{-1}A^T\), solve \(Sw=AH^{-1}g-h\), and recover \(v\) by solving \(Hv=-A^Tw-g\). If the reduced equation is solvable, the resulting pair \((v,w)\) satisfies the original KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a KKT system with a positive-definite primal block, form the negative Schur complement, solve the reduced equation for the dual variable, and recover the primal variable with a solve involving H. Whenever the reduced equation is solvable, the recovered pair solves the original system. Without an additional rank assumption on A, uniqueness is not guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: AH^{-1}A^T\text{ and the displayed products are conformable}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Hv+A^Tw=-g,\qquad Av=-h

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(AZ=0\), and consider \(Gx+A^T\lambda=r\), \(Ax=s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality systems with an explicit or implicit basis of feasible directions and a nonsingular reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A null-space reduced solve decomposes the primal variable as \[x=x_F+Zp,\qquad Ax_F=s,\qquad AZ=0.\] Premultiplication of the stationarity equation by \(Z^T\) removes the multiplier and defines the reduced system \[(Z^TGZ)p=Z^T(r-Gx_F).\] After solving it, the primal solution is \(x=x_F+Zp\). A multiplier may then be recovered from \[A^T\lambda=r-Gx\] by any full-rank range-space solve. The method is well defined when the reduced matrix \(Z^TGZ\) is nonsingular; if it is positive definite, the reduced quadratic is strictly convex. The vector \(x_F\) is a particular feasibility correction, whereas \(Zp\) is a tangent-space optimization correction. Different bases \(Z\) and different feasible representatives \(x_F\) yield coordinate systems for the same affine feasible space and therefore the same exact primal solution when the KKT solution is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space reduced solve writes every feasible primal vector as \(x=x_F+Zp\), where \(Ax_F=s\) and \(AZ=0\). It solves \((Z^TGZ)p=Z^T(r-Gx_F)\), reconstructs \(x\), and optionally recovers the multiplier from \(A^T\lambda=r-Gx\). This separates feasibility from optimization along tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled KKT equations reduce to the tangent-space system \((Z^TGZ)p=Z^T(r-Gx_F)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using complementary matrices \(Y,Z\), one may write \(x=Yx_Y+Zx_Z\), determine \(x_Y\) from the constraints, and solve for \(x_Z\).
special_cases_latex: For homogeneous constraints \(s=0\), one may choose \(x_F=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced system has dimension \(n-m\).
The multiplier does not appear in the reduced equation because \(Z^TA^T=0\).
boundary_notes: A poorly conditioned basis can make \(Z^TGZ\) numerically difficult even when the underlying restricted quadratic form is well conditioned.
Rank-deficient \(A\) requires a rank-revealing basis construction and a revised dimension count.

notation.meaning: Any particular vector satisfying the equality constraints.
Coordinates of the tangent-space correction in basis \(Z\).

children.title: Orthogonal-Basis Null-Space Solves
children.top_down_role: Reduced solves constructed from stable orthogonal factorizations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric and spectral properties specific to an orthonormal null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) satisfy \(Z^TZ=I\) and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Then \(\|Zz\|_2=\|z\|_2\) and \(z^TZ^THZz=(Zz)^TH(Zz)\). If \(H=H^T\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), the extreme eigenvalues of \(Z^THZ\) are the extreme Rayleigh quotients of \(H\) on \(\ker A\); orthonormal coordinates introduce no Euclidean basis-conditioning factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal null-space basis preserves lengths and tangent-space curvature without coordinate amplification.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\) for the spectral conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Zz\|_2=\|z\|_2\), and \(Z^THZ\) represents the restriction of \(H\) to \(\ker A\) isometrically.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the constraint null space.

knowledge_statements.title: Orthonormal-Coordinate Conditioning
Orthogonal-Basis Null-Space Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense equality-quadratic solve using an orthonormal basis of the constraint null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given the equality-constrained quadratic problem 
\[\min_p \tfrac12 p^T H p+g^T p\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=b,\]
compute an orthogonal matrix \(Q=[Y\ Z]\) such that \(AZ=0\) and \(AY\) is nonsingular. Set \(p_Y=Y(AY)^{-1}b\), solve
\[(Z^T H Z)z=-Z^T(Hp_Y+g),\]
and return \(p=p_Y+Zz\). If \(Z^T HZ\) is positive definite, this reduced system has a unique solution and the returned vector is the unique constrained minimizer. Recover the multiplier from \((AA^T)\lambda=-A(Hp+g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal factorization supplies feasible and null-space coordinates; solving the reduced Hessian system gives the constrained minimizer and then the multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=p_Y+Zz\) uniquely minimizes the quadratic subject to \(Ap=b\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal range-space and null-space basis blocks.
Particular feasible vector in the range-space coordinates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank with \(m\le n\), and let a complete orthogonal factorization of \(A^T\) produce \(Q=[Y\ Z]\), where \(Q^TQ=I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense or sparse finite-dimensional null-space reduction in an orthonormal coordinate basis obtained from QR or SVD-type factorizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An orthogonal-basis null-space solve is a null-space reduction in which \[Z^TZ=I_{n-m},\qquad AZ=0,\] and the complementary columns \(Y\) satisfy \([Y\ Z]^T[Y\ Z]=I_n\). A particular feasible component \(Yp_Y\) is chosen to satisfy \(AYp_Y=s\), and the tangent coordinates solve \[(Z^TGZ)p_Z=Z^T(r-GYp_Y).\] The primal variable is then \[x=Yp_Y+Zp_Z.\] The basis is normally obtained from a complete QR factorization of \(A^T\), in which the last \(n-m\) columns of the orthogonal factor span \(\ker A\), or from an SVD. Orthogonality is the defining distinction: it makes \(\|Zp_Z\|_2=\|p_Z\|_2\), avoids amplification caused solely by the basis, and provides orthogonal range and null components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal-basis null-space solve uses an orthonormal matrix \(Z\) spanning \(\ker A\), usually from a complete QR factorization of \(A^T\) or an SVD. It determines a feasible range component, solves the reduced equation in coordinates \(p_Z\), and reconstructs \(x=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced solve uses an orthonormal null-space basis satisfying \(AZ=0\) and \(Z^TZ=I\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(A^TP=QR=[Q_1\ Q_2]R\), one may take \(Z=Q_2\).
special_cases_latex: An SVD supplies orthonormal range and null-space bases and additionally reveals numerical rank.
immediate_consequences_latex: Euclidean norms of tangent vectors and their reduced coordinates coincide.
The two components \(Yp_Y\) and \(Zp_Z\) are orthogonal.
boundary_notes: A complete orthogonal factorization can introduce substantial fill for sparse \(A\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Reduction Null-Space Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction induced by a nonsingular partition of the constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition the variables as \(p=(p_B,p_N)\) and write \(A=[B\ N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Define
\[p_0=\begin{bmatrix}B^{-1}b\\0\end{bmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{bmatrix}-B^{-1}N\\I\end{bmatrix}.\]
Then every feasible vector is uniquely expressible as \(p=p_0+Zz\). Compute \(z\) from
\[(Z^THZ)z=-Z^T(Hp_0+g),\]
and return \(p_B=B^{-1}(b-Np_N)\) with \(p_N=z\). When \(Z^THZ\succ0\), the returned vector is the unique constrained minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose dependent variables through a nonsingular constraint block, eliminate them, solve in the independent variables, and reconstruct the feasible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=p_0+Zz\) is feasible and uniquely minimizes \(\tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\).

notation.meaning: Constraint columns associated with dependent and independent variables.
Fundamental null-space basis induced by the partition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partition-based null-space construction and reduced solve fit the exact leaf and are mathematically standard, but the record supplies no source or locator supporting the construction and minimizer claim.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Choose a column permutation \(P\) such that \(AP=[A_D\ A_I]\) with \(A_D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based null-space reduction using dependent variables determined by independent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable-reduction null-space solve partitions \(P^Tx=(x_D,x_I)\) into dependent and independent variables. Feasibility \[A_Dx_D+A_Ix_I=s\] gives \[x_D=A_D^{-1}s-A_D^{-1}A_Ix_I.\] Hence every feasible vector has the form \[x=x_F+Zx_I,\qquad x_F=P\begin{pmatrix}A_D^{-1}s\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=P\begin{pmatrix}-A_D^{-1}A_I\\I_{n-m}\end{pmatrix}.\] By construction \(Ax_F=s\) and \(AZ=0\). The reduced coordinates are obtained from \[(Z^TGZ)x_I=Z^T(r-Gx_F),\] followed by reconstruction of the dependent variables. The defining feature is that the null-space basis is induced by a nonsingular square submatrix of the constraint Jacobian rather than by an orthogonal factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable-reduction solve chooses \(m\) dependent variables whose constraint block \(A_D\) is nonsingular. It expresses them as \(x_D=A_D^{-1}s-A_D^{-1}A_Ix_I\), thereby obtaining the null-space basis \(Z=P(-A_D^{-1}A_I,I)^T\), and solves the reduced system in the independent variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition defines \(x=x_F+Zx_I\) with \(Ax_F=s\) and \(AZ=0\), reducing the KKT system to independent-variable coordinates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The construction is the fundamental null-space basis associated with the column basis \(A_D\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A_D\) is triangular after permutation, feasibility and basis applications use triangular solves.
immediate_consequences_latex: No complete orthogonal matrix is required.
Changing the selected dependent columns changes conditioning and sparsity but not the exact feasible affine space.
boundary_notes: A nonsingular but ill-conditioned \(A_D\) can produce an unstable or dense basis.
Rank-revealing pivoting is needed when the numerical rank or a safe dependent-variable set is uncertain.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Basis Null-Space Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction using a sparse basis selected to limit storage and reduced-Hessian fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[\min_p \tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=b,\]
construct a full-column-rank sparse matrix \(Z\) satisfying \(AZ=0\), together with any particular feasible vector \(p_0\). Form or apply the reduced operator \(R=Z^THZ\), solve
\[Rz=-Z^T(Hp_0+g),\]
and return \(p=p_0+Zz\). Sparsity of \(Z\) alone does not guarantee sparsity of \(R\); the basis ordering and column supports must therefore be chosen to control fill in products or factorizations involving \(R\). If \(R\succ0\), the result is the unique constrained minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse null-space basis reduces the KKT equations, but its supports and ordering must also control fill in the reduced Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(Ap_0=b\).
\(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has full column rank and satisfies \(AZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=p_0+Zz\) is the unique constrained minimizer; reduced-system sparsity depends on both \(H\) and the support pattern of \(Z\).

notation.meaning: Sparse basis for the null space of the constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sparse-basis algorithm fits the leaf, but no source supports the fill-control assertion. The hypotheses should also state that H is symmetric so that the positive-definite reduced-Hessian condition is unambiguous.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Basis with Dense Reduced Operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of the implication that a sparse basis produces a sparse reduced matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\ge2\), let \(A=[1,-1,\ldots,-1]\in\mathbb R^{1\times(k+1)}\), \(z_j=e_1+e_{j+1}\), and \(Z=[z_1\ \cdots\ z_k]\). Then \(AZ=0\), while for \(H=I\), \(Z^THZ=I+\mathbf1\mathbf1^T\) is dense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse null-space basis can yield a dense reduced Hessian even when the full Hessian is the identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z\) and \(H\) sparse does not imply \(Z^THZ\) sparse.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) satisfy \(AZ=0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)=n-m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact null-space reduction whose basis is selected for sparse representation and controlled fill in basis application or reduced-Hessian formation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse-basis null-space solve is a null-space reduced solve in which the basis \(Z\) is selected subject to a sparsity objective, such as minimizing or bounding \(\operatorname{nnz}(Z)\), the fill in a factorization of \(Z^TGZ\), or the work required to apply \(Z\) and \(Z^T\). It solves \[(Z^TGZ)p=Z^T(r-Gx_F),\qquad x=x_F+Zp,\qquad Ax_F=s.\] A standard construction chooses a permutation with \(AP=[A_D\ A_I]\), \(A_D\) nonsingular, and \[Z=P\begin{pmatrix}-A_D^{-1}A_I\\I\end{pmatrix},\] selecting \(A_D\) so that its factorization and the computed block \(A_D^{-1}A_I\) remain acceptably sparse. Sparsity, rather than orthonormality, is the defining basis criterion; the algebraic requirements \(AZ=0\) and full column rank remain mandatory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse-basis null-space solve uses a full-rank basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\) chosen to limit nonzeros, factorization fill, or basis-application cost. It solves the usual reduced equation and reconstructs the primal vector. A common construction chooses dependent columns so that both the factorization of \(A_D\) and \(A_D^{-1}A_I\) remain sparse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solve is a null-space reduction whose admissible basis additionally satisfies an explicit sparsity or fill-control criterion.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A sparse fundamental basis has the form \(P(-A_D^{-1}A_I,I)^T\) for a sparsity-aware choice of \(A_D\).
special_cases_latex: For graph-structured constraints, a basis induced by a suitable spanning structure can have few nonzeros per column.
immediate_consequences_latex: Sparse applications of \(Z\) and \(Z^T\) can reduce memory and arithmetic.
The reduced matrix may still be dense even when \(Z\) is sparse.
boundary_notes: The sparsest basis need not be numerically well conditioned.
Sparsity of \(Z\) and sparsity of \(Z^TGZ\) are distinct objectives and may conflict.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Iterative Solution of Equality Saddle-Point Systems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=\begin{pmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), with \(A\) full row rank, and suppose the restricted operator \(Z^TGZ\) is positive definite for a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale finite-dimensional iterative methods that solve either the coupled KKT system or its tangent-space projection without forming a dense inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A projected saddle-point iterative solver is an iterative method for the KKT equations whose primal iterates or search directions are constrained by a projector \(\Pi\) with \[A\Pi=0,\qquad \operatorname{range}(\Pi)=\ker A.\] Starting from a feasible \(x_0\), it constructs corrections \(d_k\in\ker A\) and hence \(Ax_k=s\) for all \(k\), while reducing the projected stationarity residual \(\Pi^T(Gx_k-r)\). The projection may be explicit, for example \[\Pi=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A,\] or implicit through an augmented solve \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}v\\w\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}q\\0\end{pmatrix},\] which returns \(v\in\ker A\). The family includes conjugate gradients on the positive-definite reduced operator, basis-free projected conjugate gradient, and Krylov methods applied to the full indefinite matrix with compatible block preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected saddle-point iterative solver repeatedly removes constraint-normal components so that primal corrections lie in \(\ker A\), while reducing the projected stationarity residual. Projection can use an explicit formula or an augmented KKT solve. The family covers reduced CG, basis-free projected CG, and suitable Krylov methods for the full coupled system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining invariants are \(d_k\in\ker A\) and, from feasible initialization, \(Ax_k=s\), together with iterative reduction of the projected or coupled residual.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method may operate in coordinates with \(Z^TGZ\), or in the original space with a projector whose range equals \(\ker A\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H=I\), the orthogonal projector is \(I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: No explicit null-space basis is needed when projection is implemented through an augmented system.
boundary_notes: Ordinary CG applied directly to the indefinite full KKT matrix is not included unless a formulation restores its definiteness requirements.
In finite precision, inaccurate projection can cause loss of feasibility.

notation.meaning: A projector or projection operator onto the constraint null space.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate Gradients on Reduced Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic conjugate gradients applied to a positive-definite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(m\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Let \(p_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfy \(Ap_0=b\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\), where \(d=n-m\), have columns spanning \(\ker A\). Define \(R=Z^THZ\succ0\) and \(h=Z^T(Hp_0+g)\). Given \(z_0\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), set \(r_0=-h-Rz_0\) and \(d_0=r_0\). If \(\lVert r_0\rVert\le\varepsilon\), return \(p=p_0+Zz_0\). Otherwise, while the stopping test is not satisfied, compute
\[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{d_k^TRd_k},\qquad z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kRd_k.\]
If \(\lVert r_{k+1}\rVert\le\varepsilon\), return \(p=p_0+Zz_{k+1}\); otherwise set
\[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.\]
In exact arithmetic with \(\varepsilon=0\), conjugate gradients reaches the solution of \(Rz=-h\) in at most \(d=n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate gradients solves the symmetric positive-definite reduced Hessian system from a feasible null-space parameterization. It handles an already converged initial guess and, in exact arithmetic with a zero tolerance, terminates within the reduced dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(Ap_0=b\), \(AZ=0\), and the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker A\).
\(R=Z^THZ\) is symmetric positive definite, \(z_0\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=p_0+Zz\) remains feasible, and an exact reduced solve yields the unique constrained minimizer; in exact arithmetic, conjugate gradients reaches that reduced solution in at most \(n-m\) iterations.

notation.meaning: Residual of the reduced linear system.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\succ0\), let \(z_*\) solve \(Rz=-h\), and let \(z_k\) be the \(k\)-th conjugate-gradient iterate. If \(\kappa=\lambda_{\max}(R)/\lambda_{\min}(R)\), then \[\|z_k-z_*\|_R\le 2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|z_0-z_*\|_R.\] Moreover, \(z_k\) minimizes the reduced quadratic over \(z_0+\mathcal K_k(R,r_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced CG minimizes over successive Krylov spaces and converges geometrically in the reduced-Hessian energy norm according to its condition number.
assumptions_latex: The recurrences are performed in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z_k-z_*\|_R\le2((\sqrt\kappa-1)/(\sqrt\kappa+1))^k\|z_0-z_*\|_R\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-CG Energy-Norm Convergence Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Breakdown boundary for the unmodified reduced-CG recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard reduced-CG recurrence requires \(d_k^TRd_k>0\) for every nonzero generated direction. If \(R\) is singular or indefinite, a nonzero direction can satisfy \(d_k^TRd_k\le0\), so the step length may be undefined or cease to minimize the reduced quadratic. Unmodified CG therefore has no general minimization or convergence guarantee outside the positive-definite regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard reduced CG is justified only for a positive-definite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\not\succ0\) removes the denominator-positivity and minimization guarantees of standard CG.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate Gradients on the Reduced Hessian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(R=Z^TGZ\succ0\) and \(d=Z^T(r-Gx_F)\), where \(AZ=0\), \(Z\) has full column rank, and \(Ax_F=s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic linear conjugate gradients applied in explicit tangent coordinates to a symmetric positive-definite reduced system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conjugate gradients on the reduced system is the linear CG method applied to \[Rp=d,\qquad R=Z^TGZ\succ0.\] From an initial \(p_0\), define \(r_0=d-Rp_0\) and \(q_0=r_0\). For \(k\ge0\), \[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{q_k^TRq_k},\quad p_{k+1}=p_k+\alpha_kq_k,\quad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kRq_k,\] \[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\quad q_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kq_k.\] The corresponding primal iterates are \(x_k=x_F+Zp_k\), so they remain feasible. The method may use matrix-free products \(Ru=Z^TG(Zu)\); explicit storage of \(R\) is not required. A preconditioned version replaces residuals by solutions with a symmetric positive-definite reduced preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This method applies ordinary linear CG to the positive-definite reduced Hessian system \((Z^TGZ)p=d\). Each coordinate iterate gives a feasible primal iterate \(x=x_F+Zp\), and reduced matrix-vector products can be evaluated as \(Z^TG(Zu)\) without storing the reduced matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The CG recurrence is applied to the symmetric positive-definite operator \(R=Z^TGZ\), with primal reconstruction \(x_k=x_F+Zp_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The iterates minimize the reduced quadratic over increasing Krylov spaces \(p_0+\mathcal K_k(R,r_0)\).
special_cases_latex: With orthonormal \(Z\), reduced and primal tangent coordinate norms coincide.
immediate_consequences_latex: In exact arithmetic, termination occurs in at most \(n-m\) iterations.
Every reconstructed primal iterate satisfies \(Ax_k=s\).
boundary_notes: The recurrence requires positive definiteness of \(Z^TGZ\); indefinite reduced curvature calls for a different Krylov method or truncation rule.
Finite-precision loss of conjugacy can delay termination.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned conjugate-gradient recurrence in reduced null-space coordinates for the referenced equality-constrained quadratic system; no convergence guarantee is asserted by this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a reduced-coordinate initial vector $x_0^{\mathrm N}$, set $g_0^{\mathrm N}=N^THNx_0^{\mathrm N}+N^Tc$, $v_0^{\mathrm N}=(M^{\mathrm N})^{-1}g_0^{\mathrm N}$, and $p_0^{\mathrm N}=-v_0^{\mathrm N}$. For $k=0,1,\ldots$ until termination, compute
\[
\alpha_k=\frac{\langle g_k^{\mathrm N},v_k^{\mathrm N}\rangle}{\langle p_k^{\mathrm N},N^THNp_k^{\mathrm N}\rangle},\qquad x_{k+1}^{\mathrm N}=x_k^{\mathrm N}+\alpha_kp_k^{\mathrm N},
\]
\[
g_{k+1}^{\mathrm N}=g_k^{\mathrm N}+\alpha_kN^THNp_k^{\mathrm N},\qquad v_{k+1}^{\mathrm N}=(M^{\mathrm N})^{-1}g_{k+1}^{\mathrm N},
\]
\[
\beta_k=\frac{\langle g_{k+1}^{\mathrm N},v_{k+1}^{\mathrm N}\rangle}{\langle g_k^{\mathrm N},v_k^{\mathrm N}\rangle},\qquad p_{k+1}^{\mathrm N}=-v_{k+1}^{\mathrm N}+\beta_kp_k^{\mathrm N}.
\]
Recover the corresponding full-space vector from the terminal reduced iterate by $x=Nx_{k+1}^{\mathrm N}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply preconditioned conjugate gradients to the reduced matrix NᵀHN, updating the reduced iterate, gradient, preconditioned gradient, and search direction. At termination, map the reduced iterate into full space with N.
assumptions_latex: \langle p_k^{\mathrm N},N^THNp_k^{\mathrm N}\rangle\ne0\quad\text{and}\quad\langle g_k^{\mathrm N},v_k^{\mathrm N}\rangle\ne0\text{ whenever the corresponding quotients are evaluated}

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-free conjugate gradients on the tangent space of full-row-rank linear equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Assume \(v^THv>0\) for every nonzero \(v\in\ker A\). Define the orthogonal projector \(P=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\), choose \(p_0\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Ap_0=b\), and initialize \(q_0=0\), \(r_0=-P(Hp_0+g)\), and \(d_0=r_0\). Given \(\varepsilon\ge0\), return \(p=p_0\) if \(\lVert r_0\rVert\le\varepsilon\). Otherwise, while the stopping test is not satisfied, compute
\[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Tr_k}{d_k^THd_k},\qquad q_{k+1}=q_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kPHd_k.\]
If \(\lVert r_{k+1}\rVert\le\varepsilon\), return \(p=p_0+q_{k+1}\); otherwise set
\[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1}}{r_k^Tr_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.\]
In exact arithmetic, every \(q_k\), \(r_k\), and \(d_k\) belongs to \(\ker A\), so every returned primal iterate is feasible without an explicit null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected conjugate gradients applies conjugate gradients to the symmetric positive-definite Hessian restricted to the constraint null space. Repeated orthogonal projection keeps the corrections in that null space, preserves feasibility, and avoids constructing explicit tangent coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\), and the invariance statements are interpreted in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every exact-arithmetic iterate \(p_0+q_k\) is feasible, and the iteration is conjugate gradients applied to the positive-definite restriction of \(H\) to \(\ker A\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the null space of the constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a computed projector application satisfies \(\widehat Pv=Pv+e\) with \(Ae\ne0\), then a correction assembled from such vectors need not lie in \(\ker A\). For \(p=p_0+q\) with \(Ap_0=b\), the feasibility residual is \(Ap-b=Aq\). Exact-arithmetic feasibility invariance is therefore lost unless projection errors are controlled or iterates are reprojected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection error outside the null space can cause equality-feasibility drift.
assumptions_latex: Computed projection errors need not lie in \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ap-b=Aq\), so inexact tangent projections do not automatically preserve feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic equivalence between projector-based and orthonormal-coordinate CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z^TZ=I\), \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and \(P=ZZ^T\). Starting from the same feasible \(p_0\), projected CG and reduced CG for \(R=Z^THZ\) generate corresponding corrections \(q_k=Zz_k\), residuals \(r_k=Z\rho_k\), and directions \(d_k=Z\delta_k\). They therefore have identical scalar coefficients, objective values, and exact-arithmetic termination indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an orthonormal null-space basis, projected CG is reduced CG expressed in full-space tangent vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric and positive definite on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k=Zz_k\), and projected and reduced CG have identical scalar recurrences.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\) have full row rank, let \(Z^TGZ\succ0\), and let \(H=H^T\) satisfy \(Z^THZ\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear projected preconditioned CG in original variables, with projections computed without explicitly storing a null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Projected conjugate gradient is the original-space realization of CG on the reduced system. Define the scaled null-space projection \[P_H=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^T.\] Starting from \(Ax_0=s\), form the stationarity residual \(r_k=Gx_k-r\), the projected preconditioned residual \(g_k=P_Hr_k\), and search directions recursively from \(d_0=-g_0\) and \[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^Tg_k}{d_k^TGd_k},\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\quad r_{k+1}=r_k+\alpha_kGd_k,\] \[g_{k+1}=P_Hr_{k+1},\quad \beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^Tg_{k+1}}{r_k^Tg_k},\quad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.\] The action \(g=P_Hr\) may be computed without \(Z\) by solving \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}g\\v\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r\\0\end{pmatrix}.\] Thus \(Ag_k=Ad_k=0\) and all primal iterates remain feasible in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected CG performs reduced-space conjugate gradients directly in the original variables. Each residual is projected into \(\ker A\), possibly by an augmented solve with \(H\) and \(A\), and the CG directions remain tangent to the constraints. Starting from a feasible point, every exact-arithmetic iterate is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented projection produces \(g_k,d_k\in\ker A\), and the stated CG recurrence preserves \(Ax_k=s\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The iteration is algebraically equivalent to preconditioned CG on \(Z^TGZ\) with preconditioner \(Z^THZ\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H=I\), the projection is the Euclidean null-space projection.
Taking \(H=G\) gives the ideal constraint preconditioner when the required restricted definiteness holds.
immediate_consequences_latex: An explicit basis \(Z\) is unnecessary.
Feasibility follows from \(Ad_k=0\) at every update.
boundary_notes: Projection solves must be sufficiently accurate; otherwise tangent invariance can be lost.
The full matrix \(H\) need not be positive definite, but its restriction \(Z^THZ\) must be positive definite.

\[

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u_k=(p_k,\lambda_k)\), \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), and \(f=(-g,b)\), the residual \(r_k=f-Ku_k\) has blocks \[r_k^{\rm d}=-g-Hp_k-A^T\lambda_k,\qquad r_k^{\rm p}=b-Ap_k.\] Thus the blocks vanish exactly when stationarity and equality feasibility hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Krylov residual separates into stationarity and feasibility residuals.
assumptions_latex: The KKT matrix and right-hand side use the displayed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k=0\iff r_k^{\rm d}=0\text{ and }r_k^{\rm p}=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for using MINRES with a preconditioned KKT operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: MINRES requires self-adjointness in the iteration inner product. An arbitrary one-sided matrix \(M^{-1}K\) need not be Euclidean symmetric even when \(K=K^T\). An SPD preconditioner permits an equivalent self-adjoint formulation in the \(M\)-inner product or by symmetric two-sided scaling; a nonsymmetric preconditioner generally removes standard MINRES guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES guarantees require symmetry-preserving preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Self-adjoint preconditioning is required by standard MINRES theory.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MINRES Residual Minimization and Finite Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core exact-arithmetic guarantee for a nonsingular symmetric KKT operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=K^T\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) be nonsingular. MINRES produces \(u_k\in u_0+\mathcal K_k(K,r_0)\) satisfying \[\|f-Ku_k\|_2=\min_{u\in u_0+\mathcal K_k(K,r_0)}\|f-Ku\|_2.\] In exact arithmetic it reaches the solution within the degree of the minimal polynomial of \(K\) relative to \(r_0\), hence within \(N\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MINRES minimizes the full KKT residual over each Krylov affine space and terminates finitely for a nonsingular symmetric KKT matrix.
assumptions_latex: The iteration is unpreconditioned and performed in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r_k\|_2\) is Krylov-minimal, and exact termination occurs in at most \(N\) steps.

Saddle-Point Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Krylov iteration on the symmetric indefinite KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad u=\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix},\qquad f=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\b\end{bmatrix}.\]
Given \(u_0\), apply a symmetric-indefinite Krylov method such as MINRES to \(Ku=f\), using only products \(v\mapsto Kv\). With a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner \(M\), apply MINRES in the \(M\)-inner product to the equivalent symmetrically preconditioned system. Stop when the computed residual \(r_k=f-Ku_k\) satisfies \(\lVert r_k\rVert\le\varepsilon(\lVert f\rVert+\lVert K\rVert\lVert u_k\rVert)\), and return the primal and multiplier blocks of \(u_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric-indefinite Krylov method attacks the coupled KKT system directly and may use an SPD preconditioner while monitoring the full residual.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^T\), \(A\) has full row rank, and \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\).
\(M\) is symmetric positive definite when preconditioning is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned blocks approximately satisfy both KKT equations to the stated residual tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Krylov Methods for the Full Saddle-Point System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=\begin{pmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{(n+m)\times(n+m)}\) be a nonsingular KKT matrix, and let \(Ku=b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional iterative solution applied directly to the coupled primal-multiplier representation, typically with a block or constraint preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A saddle-point Krylov method is an iterative method whose coupled iterates satisfy \[u_k\in u_0+\mathcal K_k(M^{-1}K,M^{-1}r_0),\qquad r_0=b-Ku_0,\] for a nonsingular preconditioner \(M\), with residuals selected according to the defining orthogonality or minimization condition of a Krylov method suitable for indefinite or general matrices. The operator action is \[K\begin{pmatrix}p\\q\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}Gp+A^Tq\\Ap\end{pmatrix},\] so neither a null-space basis nor a Schur complement need be formed. For symmetric \(K\) and compatible symmetric preconditioning, a symmetric-indefinite Krylov method may be used; methods for general systems such as GMRES or QMR apply under their respective assumptions. Ordinary positive-definite CG applied unmodified to \(K\) is excluded because a nontrivial KKT matrix is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A saddle-point Krylov method applies a Krylov iteration directly to the full coupled KKT operator. Its iterates lie in a preconditioned Krylov affine space generated by \(K\) and the initial residual, and one operator product evaluates both the primal and constraint blocks. It avoids explicit null-space or Schur-complement construction and must use a method compatible with indefinite or general systems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled iterate belongs to \(u_0+\mathcal K_k(M^{-1}K,M^{-1}r_0)\) and is generated using full KKT operator actions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With left preconditioning, the solved system is \(M^{-1}Ku=M^{-1}b\); right and split preconditioning give equivalent Krylov formulations with different residual measures.
special_cases_latex: Without preconditioning, \(M=I\).
A symmetric constraint preconditioner preserves a structure suitable for symmetric-indefinite Krylov methods when applied compatibly.
immediate_consequences_latex: Primal and multiplier variables are approximated simultaneously.
The method requires only products with \(G\), \(A\), and \(A^T\), plus preconditioner applications.
boundary_notes: Feasibility of intermediate primal iterates is not generally preserved.
CG for symmetric positive-definite matrices is not a valid direct full-KKT method because \(K\) is indefinite when constraints are present.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=\begin{pmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), and let \(\widehat G\) approximate \(G\) while \(\widehat S\) approximates the Schur complement \(A\widehat G^{-1}A^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingular block preconditioners whose application approximates the null-space, Schur-complement, or block-factorization structure of an equality KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured KKT preconditioner is a nonsingular operator \(M\) for which applying \(M^{-1}\) is organized according to a block reduction of \(K\). Canonical members include the block-diagonal form \[M_D=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat G&0\\0&-\widehat S\end{pmatrix},\] the block-triangular form \[M_T=\begin{pmatrix}\widehat G&A^T\\0&-\widehat S\end{pmatrix},\] and the constraint preconditioner \[M_C=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z^THZ\succ0.\] An application of \(M_D^{-1}\) or \(M_T^{-1}\) uses approximate primal and Schur solves; an application of \(M_C^{-1}\) performs a coupled projection whose primal component lies in \(\ker A\) for a homogeneous constraint right-hand side. The family is structured because it retains the primal, multiplier, and constraint couplings rather than approximating \(K\) by an unrelated matrix. The exact choice is a preconditioner only when the displayed operator is nonsingular and its inverse action is cheaper than solving with \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured KKT preconditioner is a nonsingular approximation whose inverse is applied through primal-block, Schur-complement, null-space, or coupled constraint solves. Standard forms are block diagonal, block triangular, and the constraint preconditioner \((H,A^T;A,0)\). They preserve the saddle-point partition and are intended to make the preconditioned Krylov system easier to solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family consists of nonsingular preconditioners whose inverse actions approximate a recognized block factorization or constrained projection of \(K\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constraint preconditioner implements the projector \(Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^T\) through an augmented solve.
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(H=G\) gives an ideal constraint preconditioner on the reduced space.
Taking exact \(\widehat G=G\) and \(\widehat S=AG^{-1}A^T\) reproduces exact block elimination.
immediate_consequences_latex: A preconditioner may be applied without forming an explicit null-space basis.
Block approximations permit independent use of solvers specialized for primal and multiplier blocks.
boundary_notes: Nonsingularity and symmetry of a block formula do not alone guarantee effective spectral clustering.
Sign conventions for the Schur block must match the chosen KKT matrix and Krylov implementation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, \(G=G^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Then \[M_C=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular if and only if \(Z^TGZ\) is nonsingular. Definiteness of \(Z^TGZ\) is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner is nonsingular exactly when its surrogate Hessian is nonsingular on the constraint null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_C\text{ is nonsingular}\iff Z^TGZ\text{ is nonsingular}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to treating positive reduced curvature as necessary for preconditioner nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(G=-I\) and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(Z^TGZ=-Z^TZ\prec0\), so \(M_C\) is nonsingular although \(G\) is not positive definite on \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-definite surrogate Hessian still gives a nonsingular constraint preconditioner, so null-space positivity is not necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_C\text{ is nonsingular while }z^TGz<0\text{ for every }0\ne z\in\ker A.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Positivity Is Not Necessary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized spectrum when only the primal block of a KKT matrix is replaced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad M_C=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\] where \(H=H^T\), \(G=G^T\), \(A\) has full row rank, and \(Z^TGZ\) is nonsingular. Up to a nonzero constant factor, \[\det(K-\lambda M_C)=(1-\lambda)^{2m}\det\!\left(Z^T(H-\lambda G)Z\right).\] Thus \(M_C^{-1}K\) has \(2m\) unit eigenvalues before multiplicities contributed by the reduced pencil are combined, and its other \(n-m\) eigenvalues are those of \((Z^THZ,Z^TGZ)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint preconditioning fixes 2m unit eigenvalues, while the remaining spectrum is the reduced Hessian pencil on the constraint null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma(M_C^{-1}K)=\{1\}^{2m}\uplus\sigma(Z^THZ,Z^TGZ),\text{ with coincident multiplicities combined}.

notation.meaning: Generalized spectrum of the pencil B-lambda C.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectrum of Constraint-Preconditioned KKT Systems
Constraint Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingularity condition for a constraint preconditioner sharing the KKT constraint blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the KKT matrix \(K\), a constraint preconditioner has the form
\[M_C=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\]
where \(G=G^T\) approximates \(H\). If \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, then \(M_C\) is nonsingular whenever
\[z^TGz>0\quad\text{for every nonzero }z\in\ker A.\]
Application of \(M_C^{-1}\) requires solving a surrogate equality-constrained system. Because the constraint blocks are retained exactly, each preconditioner solve couples primal and multiplier corrections and respects the same linearized constraint geometry as the original KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner replaces the Hessian block but retains both constraint blocks; positivity on the constraint null space guarantees nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_C\) is nonsingular if \(G\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sufficient null-space positivity condition is mathematically appropriate and the condition content kind matches the record's role, but the constraint-preconditioner characterization and nonsingularity claim have no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Nonsingularity Criterion for a Constraint Preconditioner
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient reduced-space condition for nonsingularity of the constraint-preconditioner matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(G=G^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Then
\[M_C=\begin{bmatrix}G&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\]
is nonsingular if and only if \(Z^TGZ\) is nonsingular. Positive definiteness of \(Z^TGZ\) is sufficient but not necessary; for example, \(G=-I\) gives \(Z^TGZ=-Z^TZ\prec0\) and still yields a nonsingular \(M_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint preconditioner is nonsingular exactly when its surrogate Hessian is nonsingular on the constraint null space; null-space positivity is sufficient but not necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_C\text{ is nonsingular}\iff Z^TGZ\text{ is nonsingular}.\)

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for the null space of the constraint Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widetilde H\succ0\) and \(\widetilde S\succ0\), then \(M_D=\operatorname{diag}(\widetilde H,\widetilde S)\succ0\). For symmetric \(K\), \(M_D^{-1}K\) is self-adjoint in the \(M_D\)-inner product, so a symmetry-preserving preconditioned MINRES formulation is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite block-diagonal preconditioners preserve the self-adjoint structure required by MINRES.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_D\succ0\), and \(M_D^{-1}K\) is self-adjoint in \(\langle x,y\rangle_{M_D}=x^TM_Dy\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectrum of the exactly preconditioned SPD-Hessian saddle-point system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, set \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\), and define \(M_D=\operatorname{diag}(H,S)\). For \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), the generalized eigenvalues of \(Kx=\lambda M_Dx\) are \(1\) with multiplicity \(n-m\) and \((1\pm\sqrt5)/2\), each with multiplicity \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact primal and Schur blocks, block-diagonal preconditioning places the KKT spectrum at three dimension-independent values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(M_D^{-1}K)=\{1,(1-\sqrt5)/2,(1+\sqrt5)/2\}\) with the stated multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.title: Ideal Block-Diagonal Spectrum
Block-Diagonal Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric positive-definite block approximation for Krylov solution of saddle-point systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\]
a block-diagonal preconditioner is
\[M_D=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&0\\0&\widetilde S\end{bmatrix},\qquad \widetilde S\approx A\widetilde H^{-1}A^T,\]
where \(\widetilde H\succ0\) and \(\widetilde S\succ0\). Its application separates into solves with \(\widetilde H\) and \(\widetilde S\). If positive constants \(c_H,C_H,c_S,C_S\) bound the corresponding Rayleigh quotients of \(\widetilde H^{-1}H\) on \(\ker A\) and \(\widetilde S^{-1}A\widetilde H^{-1}A^T\), then preconditioner quality is governed by these spectral-equivalence bounds rather than by the unscaled block magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-diagonal preconditioner independently approximates the primal block and its Schur complement, giving separable SPD solves suitable for symmetric Krylov methods.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde H\) and \(\widetilde S\) are symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_D\succ0\), and applying \(M_D^{-1}\) requires one primal-block solve and one Schur-block solve.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-diagonal representation fits the leaf, but the constants and corresponding Rayleigh quotients are not explicitly defined, and the quality claim lacks a supporting source. A saddle-point preconditioning reference with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Block-Triangular Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Coupled block approximations reflecting saddle-point factorization structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krylov-method compatibility boundary for triangular preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nontrivial block-triangular preconditioner is generally nonsymmetric, and one-sided application generally makes \(M_T^{-1}K\) or \(KM_T^{-1}\) nonsymmetric even when \(K=K^T\). Standard MINRES therefore does not apply to the resulting Euclidean operator; a nonsymmetric Krylov method or a separately constructed symmetry-preserving formulation is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangular preconditioning usually sacrifices the Euclidean symmetry needed by standard MINRES.
assumptions_latex: \(M_T\) is a genuinely coupled block-triangular preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_T^{-1}K\) is generally nonsymmetric, so standard MINRES guarantees do not apply.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Euclidean Symmetry

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise exact-block meaning of triangular factorization preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be nonsingular, let \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\) be nonsingular, and write \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}=LU,\quad L=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\AH^{-1}&I\end{bmatrix},\quad U=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\0&-S\end{bmatrix}.\] With exact upper-triangular right preconditioning, \(KU^{-1}=L=I+N\), where \(N^2=0\). Hence every eigenvalue is \(1\), the minimal polynomial has degree at most two, and unrestarted GMRES terminates within two iterations in exact arithmetic. The triangular factor alone is not \(K^{-1}\); an exact direct solve also applies the complementary factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact triangular right preconditioning leaves a unit triangular operator with a square-zero off-diagonal part, yielding at most two GMRES iterations.
assumptions_latex: Right-preconditioned unrestarted GMRES is performed in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(KU^{-1}=I+N\), \(N^2=0\), so GMRES terminates in at most two iterations.

notation.meaning: Exact lower and upper factors of the KKT matrix.
Strictly lower block of the preconditioned operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Triangular Preconditioned Operator
Block-Triangular Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Triangular approximations derived from block factorization of the KKT operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(H\) is nonsingular and define the positive Schur complement \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\). The KKT matrix admits
\[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}I&0\\AH^{-1}&I\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\0&-S\end{bmatrix}.\]
Replacing \(H\) and \(S\) by invertible approximations gives the lower-triangular preconditioner
\[M_L=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&0\\A&-\widetilde S\end{bmatrix}\]
or the upper-triangular analogue \(M_U=\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde H&A^T\\0&-\widetilde S\end{bmatrix}\). Application consists of sequential block solves. With exact blocks, the associated factorization reproduces the exact KKT solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-triangular preconditioners approximate an exact KKT factorization, using sequential primal and Schur-complement solves while retaining one coupling block.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank and \(\widetilde S\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The triangular forms approximate the exact block factorization and become exact when \(\widetilde H=H\) and \(\widetilde S=AH^{-1}A^T\).

notation.meaning: Positive Schur complement associated with the multiplier block.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed block factorization is correct and the representation kind fits the leaf. However, the statement that the triangular preconditioner becomes an exact solve is ambiguous unless the omitted complementary factor and preconditioned operator are specified, and no source supports the intended formulation.

children.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioners
children.top_down_role: Preconditioners based on approximations to the multiplier-space complement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral-Equivalence Bound for SPD Schur Preconditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PCG convergence when an SPD Schur complement has an SPD spectrally equivalent preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\succ0\), \(\widetilde S\succ0\), and suppose \[\alpha v^T\widetilde Sv\le v^TSv\le\beta v^T\widetilde Sv\qquad(v\ne0),\] with \(0<\alpha\le\beta\). Then \(\sigma(\widetilde S^{-1}S)\subset[\alpha,\beta]\), and PCG satisfies \[\|e_k\|_S\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt{\beta/\alpha}-1}{\sqrt{\beta/\alpha}+1}\right)^k\|e_0\|_S.\] This PCG guarantee does not apply if the required symmetry or positive definiteness is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral equivalence controls the preconditioned Schur spectrum and gives the standard PCG error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa(\widetilde S^{-1}S)\le\beta/\alpha\text{ and PCG obeys the displayed bound}.

notation.meaning: Multiplier error after k PCG iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Equivalence Bound for SPD Schur Preconditioning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space preconditioning after elimination of an invertible primal KKT block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Hp+A^T\lambda=-g\) and \(Ap=b\), with nonsingular \(H\), elimination gives \[S\lambda=-b-AH^{-1}g,\qquad S=AH^{-1}A^T,\] followed by \(p=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda)\). A Schur-complement preconditioner applies an efficiently invertible approximation \(\widetilde S\) to this multiplier equation. If \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Schur preconditioner approximates the multiplier-space operator obtained by eliminating the primal variables.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(\widetilde S\) are nonsingular for the respective exact and preconditioned solves.
For \(S\succ0\), \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\text{ is solved in multiplier space and }p=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda);\quad H\succ0,\ \operatorname{rank}(A)=m\Rightarrow S\succ0.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Preconditioning
Schur-Complement Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space preconditioning obtained by eliminating the primal KKT block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(H\) is nonsingular, eliminating \(p\) from
\[Hp+A^T\lambda=-g,\qquad Ap=b\]
gives the multiplier equation
\[S\lambda=-b-AH^{-1}g,\qquad S=AH^{-1}A^T.\]
A Schur-complement preconditioner replaces \(S
eq0\) by an efficiently invertible \(\widetilde S\) and applies a Krylov method to the multiplier equation using products with \(A\), \(A^T\), and solves with \(H\) or an approximation \(\widetilde H\). After computing \(\lambda\), recover \(p=-H^{-1}(g+A^T\lambda)\). If \(H\succ0\) and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal variables produces a multiplier-space Schur system; an approximation to this operator preconditions the multiplier solve before primal recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT solution is recovered from the Schur equation and primal back-substitution; moreover, \(S\succ0\) when \(H\succ0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur equation, back-substitution, and positive-definiteness claim are mathematically consistent, and the representation kind fits the leaf. The phrase replacing S not equal to zero is imprecise, however, and no source with a locator supports the preconditioning formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence guarantee for an SPD multiplier Schur system preconditioned by an SPD approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\succ0\) and let \(\widetilde S\succ0\). If constants \(0<\alpha\le\beta\) satisfy
\[\alpha\,v^T\widetilde S v\le v^TSv\le\beta\,v^T\widetilde S v\qquad\text{for all }v\ne0,\]
then every eigenvalue of \(\widetilde S^{-1}S\) lies in \([\alpha,\beta]\). Preconditioned conjugate gradients therefore satisfies
\[\|e_k\|_S\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt{\beta/\alpha}-1}{\sqrt{\beta/\alpha}+1}\right)^k\|e_0\|_S.\]
For \(\widetilde S=S\), exact arithmetic terminates after one preconditioned iteration. If symmetry or positive definiteness of either operator is lost, this PCG guarantee does not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform spectral equivalence between the exact and approximate Schur complements bounds the preconditioned spectrum and gives the standard PCG geometric error estimate.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(\widetilde S\) satisfy the displayed spectral-equivalence inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(\widetilde S^{-1}S)\le\beta/\alpha\) and PCG has the stated energy-norm convergence bound.

notation.meaning: SPD approximation used to precondition the exact Schur complement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Controlled Reliability Mechanisms for KKT Solves
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Kz=b\) be a KKT, projection, or reduced linear system, and let \(\widehat z\) denote a computed approximation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision safeguards expressed through residual correction, feasibility monitoring, and stable factorization reuse; no particular floating-point error model is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A linear-solve reliability mechanism is an auxiliary rule that accepts or corrects a computed solution using explicit residual conditions. Its canonical refinement form is \[r=b-K\widehat z,\qquad K\Delta z=r,\qquad \widehat z\leftarrow\widehat z+\Delta z,\] repeated until a prescribed scaled residual test such as \[\frac{\|b-K\widehat z\|}{\|K\|\,\|\widehat z\|+\|b\|}\le\tau\] is met or a declared failure condition occurs. For projected methods, reliability additionally monitors the constraint residual \(\|Av\|\) of every nominally tangent vector and may recompute the vector by a stable augmented solve. For a factored KKT matrix, the same factors may be reused for correction equations, while residuals are recomputed from the original matrix and right-hand side. A mechanism belongs to this class only if it exposes a measurable acceptance condition or corrective relation; pivoting, scaling, or regularization without an associated accuracy check is a solver design choice rather than a complete reliability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear-solve reliability mechanism checks a computed KKT or projection solve through its residual and corrects it when necessary. Iterative refinement solves \(K\Delta z=b-K\widehat z\) and updates \(\widehat z\). Projected methods also monitor \(Av\) so that supposedly tangent vectors remain close to the null space. Acceptance is tied to an explicit scaled residual tolerance or a declared failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reliability is defined by residual evaluation, an explicit acceptance threshold, and, when needed, the correction equation \(K\Delta z=b-K\widehat z\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Componentwise or normwise backward-error tests may replace the displayed normwise scaled residual when their scaling is stated explicitly.
special_cases_latex: For a fixed factorization, iterative refinement reuses the factors to solve each correction equation.
For projected CG, monitoring \(\|Av_k\|\) detects loss of the null-space invariant.
immediate_consequences_latex: Residual recomputation can reveal errors hidden by triangular-solve recurrences.
Refinement may improve the computed solution without refactorizing the coefficient matrix.
boundary_notes: A small residual does not imply a small forward error when \(K\) is severely ill conditioned.
The tolerance \(\tau\), norm, and scaling must be specified by the surrounding solver.
Refinement can stagnate; a reliability mechanism must then report failure or trigger a different factorization or regularization.

notation.meaning: Residual of the current computed linear-system solution.

children.title: Residual-Driven Solve Refinement
children.top_down_role: Post-solve correction for inaccurate projections and saddle-point solutions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Driven Refinement of a KKT or Projection Solve
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^N\), and let \(z^{(0)}\) be a computed approximation to a solution of \(Kz=b\). In an equality-constrained quadratic model, \(K\) may be the saddle-point matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), and \(z\) then collects a primal step and multiplier vector.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic refinement with a fixed coefficient matrix and repeated correction solves; the definition covers direct KKT solves and linear systems used to compute null-space projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Residual-driven solve refinement is the iteration \[r^{(j)}=b-Kz^{(j)},\qquad Kd^{(j)}=r^{(j)},\qquad z^{(j+1)}=z^{(j)}+d^{(j)},\] where each correction equation is solved using the same stored factorization or linear-solve mechanism as the original system. A residual-based stopping rule terminates at the first \(j\) satisfying a prescribed scaled condition such as \[\|r^{(j)}\|\leq \tau\bigl(\|K\|\,\|z^{(j)}\|+\|b\|\bigr).\] For a KKT system, the residual decomposes into stationarity and constraint blocks, \[r^{(j)}=\begin{bmatrix}r_d^{(j)}\\r_p^{(j)}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}g-Hp^{(j)}-A^T\lambda^{(j)}\\h-Ap^{(j)}\end{bmatrix},\] so refinement corrects the primal and multiplier variables jointly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given an approximate solution of a linear KKT or projection system, compute its residual, solve the same coefficient system with that residual as the new right-hand side, and add the resulting correction. Repeat until a scaled residual test is met. For a saddle-point system, both the stationarity residual and the equality residual participate in the correction, so the refinement applies to the primal step and multiplier together.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) and \(b\) remain fixed throughout the refinement cycle.
Each correction equation \(Kd^{(j)}=r^{(j)}\) is solved by an available factorization or compatible linear solver.
The residual norm and tolerance \(\tau\geq0\) are specified consistently with the desired accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The refined approximation is \(z^{(j+1)}=z^{(j)}+d^{(j)}\), with termination controlled explicitly by the residual of the original linear system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing the linear-solve operator as \(\mathcal S\), the iteration is \(z^{(j+1)}=z^{(j)}+\mathcal S(b-Kz^{(j)})\).
special_cases_latex: For a projection computed from a saddle-point system, the primal block of \(z^{(j)}\) is the projected vector and its constraint residual measures loss of null-space membership.
immediate_consequences_latex: The coefficient factorization can be reused for every correction because only the right-hand side changes.
Separate monitoring of \(\|r_p^{(j)}\|\) and \(\|r_d^{(j)}\|\) distinguishes feasibility error from stationarity error.
boundary_notes: Refinement does not regularize a singular system or resolve inconsistent equations.
Residual reduction alone does not imply a small forward error when the system is extremely ill-conditioned.

notation.meaning: Residual of the original system at refinement index \(j\).
Correction obtained by solving with the residual right-hand side.
