children.title: Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Post-factorization improvement of computed saddle-point or projected solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical refinement of an approximate KKT linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular system Ku=f and approximation u_j, compute r_j=f-Ku_j, approximately solve K\delta u_j=r_j using the available factors or solver, and set u_{j+1}=u_j+\delta u_j. Stop when a declared residual or backward-error tolerance is met, or report stagnation when the chosen failure test is triggered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement repeatedly solves for the current residual and adds the resulting correction.
assumptions_latex: Residual and correction computations are defined in declared arithmetic and norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: u_{j+1}=u_j+\delta u_j,\qquad r_{j+1}=r_j-K\delta u_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Driven Iterative Refinement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic convergence for a fixed approximate correction operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every correction is \delta u_j=Mr_j for a fixed M. Then e_{j+1}=(I-MK)e_j and r_{j+1}=(I-KM)r_j. The iteration converges for every initial vector if and only if \rho(I-MK)<1, equivalently \rho(I-KM)<1. If \|I-KM\|\leq q<1 in a subordinate norm, then \|r_j\|\leq q^j\|r_0\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed approximate inverse, refinement converges exactly when its stationary iteration matrix has spectral radius below one.
assumptions_latex: The recurrence is evaluated in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(I-MK)<1\iff u_j\to K^{-1}f\ \text{for every }u_0.

notation.meaning: fixed approximate inverse used for corrections

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Refinement Contraction Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Refinement Iteration and Work Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration and work count under a uniform residual contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\|r_{j+1}\|\le q\|r_j\|\) with \(0<q<1\), then \(\|r_k\|\le\tau\) is guaranteed whenever \[k\ge\left\lceil\frac{\log(\|r_0\|/\tau)}{\log(1/q)}\right\rceil,\qquad 0<\tau<\|r_0\|.\] Each step performs one residual evaluation, one correction solve, and one vector update, so the counted work is at most \(k(C_{\rm res}+C_{\rm corr}+C_{\rm upd})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform residual contraction gives a logarithmic iteration bound, with one residual evaluation, correction solve, and update per step.
assumptions_latex: The contraction bound holds at every counted iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k=O\!\left(\log(\|r_0\|/\tau)/\log(1/q)\right).

notation.meaning: Work of one residual evaluation, correction solve, and update.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Refinement Iteration and Work Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract contraction condition separating residual-evaluation, correction, and update errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_j=f-Ku_j\), let \(\widehat r_j=r_j+d_j\), and suppose \(\|\widehat r_j-K\delta u_j\|\le\theta\|\widehat r_j\|\), \(\|d_j\|\le\alpha\|r_j\|\), and \(u_{j+1}=u_j+\delta u_j+w_j\) with \(\|Kw_j\|\le\beta\|r_j\|\). Then \[\|r_{j+1}\|\le q\|r_j\|,\qquad q=\theta(1+\alpha)+\alpha+\beta.\] Thus \(q<1\) gives geometric residual convergence. If the three bounds additionally contribute an aggregate absolute term \(\gamma\), then \(\|r_{j+1}\|\le q\|r_j\|+\gamma\) and \(\limsup_j\|r_j\|\le\gamma/(1-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement contracts when correction, residual-evaluation, and update errors have a combined relative coefficient below one; additive errors impose an accuracy floor.
assumptions_latex: All bounds use a declared compatible matrix and vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r_j\|\le q^j\|r_0\|\ \text{when }\gamma=0,\qquad \limsup_j\|r_j\|\le\gamma/(1-q)\ \text{when }\gamma>0.

notation.meaning: Error introduced while applying the correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbed Refinement Residual Recurrence
Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-driven correction of an approximate KKT linear-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonsingular KKT system \(Ku=f\), let \(u_0\) be an approximate solution. At iteration \(j\), evaluate the residual \(r_j=f-Ku_j\), preferably in precision at least as high as that used for the correction solve. Approximately solve
\[K\delta u_j=r_j\]
using the available KKT factorization or iterative solver, and set \(u_{j+1}=u_j+\delta u_j\). Stop when
\[\frac{\lVert r_{j+1}\rVert}{\lVert K\rVert\lVert u_{j+1}\rVert+\lVert f\rVert}\le\tau\]
or when residual reduction stagnates. Return the primal and multiplier blocks of the last iterate together with its normalized residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement repeatedly solves for the current KKT residual, updates the solution, and stops at a backward-error tolerance or stagnation.
assumptions_latex: The correction solver and residual evaluation are sufficiently accurate to reduce the residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On successful termination, \(u_{j+1}\) has normwise relative backward error at most \(\tau\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the iterative-refinement leaf, but the conclusion depends on a specified matrix norm, residual-rounding model, correction accuracy, and finite-precision conditions. Those details cannot be validated without an authoritative iterative-refinement source and locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic convergence criterion for stationary approximate correction solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Ku=f\) with nonsingular \(K\), and suppose every refinement correction is \(\delta u_j=Mr_j\), where \(r_j=f-Ku_j\) and \(M\) is fixed. Then the error and residual obey \(e_{j+1}=(I-MK)e_j\) and \(r_{j+1}=(I-KM)r_j\). The iteration converges for every initial vector if and only if \(\rho(I-MK)<1\), equivalently \(\rho(I-KM)<1\); if a subordinate norm satisfies \(\|I-KM\|\leq q<1\), then \(\|r_j\|\leq q^j\|r_0\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative refinement is a stationary residual iteration whose contraction is determined by the accuracy of the approximate inverse used for corrections.
assumptions_latex: The same linear correction operator \(M\) is used at every step.
Arithmetic is exact for the stated recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(I-MK)<1\Longleftrightarrow u_j\to K^{-1}f\ \text{for every}\ u_0.

notation.meaning: fixed approximate inverse implemented by the correction solve

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Error-Propagation Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient contraction condition accounting separately for residual error, inexact correction, and rounded updating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_j=f-Ku_j\), let the computed residual be \(\widehat r_j=r_j+d_j\), and suppose the computed correction and rounded update satisfy \(\|\widehat r_j-K\delta u_j\|\leq\theta\|\widehat r_j\|\), \(\|d_j\|\leq\alpha\|r_j\|\), and \(u_{j+1}=u_j+\delta u_j+w_j\) with \(\|Kw_j\|\leq\beta\|r_j\|\). Then \[\|r_{j+1}\|\leq q\|r_j\|,\qquad q=\theta(1+\alpha)+\alpha+\beta.\] Hence \(q<1\) implies geometric residual convergence. If instead the three error bounds contain additive floors whose resulting sum is \(\gamma\), then \(\|r_{j+1}\|\leq q\|r_j\|+\gamma\) and \(\limsup_j\|r_j\|\leq\gamma/(1-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement contracts when correction, residual-evaluation, and update errors have a combined relative coefficient below one; absolute rounding floors limit attainable accuracy.
assumptions_latex: All displayed bounds use one declared subordinate matrix/vector norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r_j\|\leq q^j\|r_0\|\) in the floor-free case, while additive arithmetic errors impose the floor \(\gamma/(1-q)\).

notation.meaning: rounding error in applying the correction

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Finite-Precision Refinement Contraction

children.title: Primal Residual Correction
children.top_down_role: Post-solve treatment of error in the primal optimality block.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correction of the primal KKT equation, also called the stationarity or dual residual block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r=b-K\widehat z=(r_d,r_c). Compute \delta z from K\delta z=(r_d,0) and set \widehat z^+=\widehat z+\delta z. For an exact correction, b-K\widehat z^+=(0,r_c). For correction defect q=(r_d,0)-K\delta z, the new residual is (0,r_c)+q.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationarity-only correction removes the primal optimality residual and preserves the previous equality residual, up to correction-solve error.
assumptions_latex: Nonsingularity of K is required for uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r^+=(0,r_c)\ \text{for an exact correction},\qquad r^+=(0,r_c)+q\ \text{otherwise}.

notation.meaning: stationarity residual in the primal KKT equation

review_flags: The leaf title is interpreted as residual in the primal KKT equation, conventionally called the stationarity or dual residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-Block KKT Correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space realization of stationarity correction when the current primal vector is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let AZ=0 with \operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A, assume Ap=b, and solve (Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)s=Z^{\mathsf T}r_d with \delta p=Zs. Then A\delta p=0 and Ap^+=b. If \delta\lambda is chosen so that A^{\mathsf T}\delta\lambda is the remaining range-space part of r_d-H\delta p, the corrected stationarity residual vanishes for exact compatible solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space solve corrects the tangent stationarity residual without disturbing an already satisfied equality equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ap^+=b,\qquad Z^{\mathsf T}r_d^+=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Preserving Tangent Realization
Primal Residual Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent correction targeting the primal stationarity block while preserving linearized feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the approximate KKT pair \((p,\lambda)\), define the stationarity residual \(r_d=-g-Hp-A^T\lambda\). Let \(Z\) span \(\ker A\). Compute a feasibility-preserving primal correction by solving
\[(Z^THZ)s=Z^Tr_d,\qquad \delta p=Zs.\]
Then \(A\delta p=0\), so an already satisfied constraint equation remains satisfied. Choose \(\delta\lambda\) to fit the remaining range-space residual, for example by solving
\[(AA^T)\delta\lambda=A(r_d-H\delta p).\]
Update \(p^+=p+\delta p\) and \(\lambda^+=\lambda+\delta\lambda\). The new stationarity residual is orthogonal to \(\ker A\) when the reduced solve is exact.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative correction of the equality-equation residual in a computed KKT solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the KKT system \(Kz=b\), with \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\), let \(\widehat z=(\widehat p,\widehat\lambda)\) be the current computed solution and form the constraint residual \(r_c=b_c-A\widehat p\). Repeat until \(\lVert r_c\rVert\leq \tau_c\), or terminate with a refinement-failure indication if the residual no longer decreases sufficiently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a KKT correction equation whose right-hand side is the current equality residual, update the primal and multiplier variables, and stop at tolerance or stagnation.

The residual \(r_c\) is evaluated with accuracy adequate for refinement.

children.title: Refinement Stagnation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditioning and arithmetic regimes where refinement no longer improves solve quality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual condition separating contracting refinement from stagnating or worsening steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r_j=f-Ku_j and q_j=r_j-K\delta u_j. Before rounding the update, the next exact residual is r_{j+1}=q_j. Thus \|q_j\|\leq\eta_j\|r_j\| with \eta_j<1 is a sufficient contraction condition. If \|q_j\|\geq\|r_j\|, the step gives no residual contraction; repeated occurrence prevents the unchanged procedure from establishing convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correction-solve defect becomes the next residual, so repeated noncontractive defects mark stagnation.
assumptions_latex: Residuals and defects are measured in one fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_{j+1}=q_j,\qquad \eta_j<1\Rightarrow\|r_{j+1}\|<\|r_j\|.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncontractive Correction Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stagnation caused by an update discarded by rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \operatorname{fl}(u_j+\delta u_j)=u_j while the recomputed residual is above tolerance, the stored iterate is unchanged. Repeating the same deterministic arithmetic, scaling, factors, and correction procedure from that state reproduces the same iterate and cannot reduce the residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When rounding discards the correction entirely, unchanged refinement is at a fixed point above tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The repeated procedure is deterministic and unchanged.
The residual is recomputed from the stored iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{fl}(u_j+\delta u_j)=u_j\Longrightarrow u_{j+1}=u_j\ \text{and}\ r_{j+1}=r_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Working-Precision Fixed-Point Boundary
Refinement Stagnation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary beyond which residual-driven KKT refinement should not be trusted to improve the solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r^{(j)}=b-K\widehat z^{(j)}\) be the recomputed residual after refinement step \(j\). Given \(0<\rho<1\), a maximum count \(j_{\max}\), and a target \(\tau\), refinement is declared stagnant if \(\lVert r^{(j)}\rVert>\tau\) and either \(j=j_{\max}\), \(\lVert r^{(j)}\rVert\geq\rho\lVert r^{(j-1)}\rVert\), or the computed correction is too small to change \(\widehat z^{(j)}\) at working precision. At this boundary, further solves with unchanged factors and precision provide no certified residual reduction; refactorization, rescaling, or higher-precision residual evaluation is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement has stagnated when the residual remains above tolerance but stops contracting, the iteration limit is reached, or corrections cannot change the computed solution.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are measured in one fixed norm.
Successive corrections use unchanged factors and working precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Further unchanged refinement does not certify reduction below \(\tau\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Management of redundant equality rows after rank-revealing selection.

If this holds, replacing Ax=b by A_Ix=b_I preserves the feasible set; if it fails, the full equality system is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:A_Ix=b_I\}\iff b_J=Cb_I.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of interpreting ordinary column-pivoted QR as a strong numerical-rank certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A small trailing diagonal or block in ordinary column-pivoted QR is a tolerance-dependent rank indicator. Without quantitative singular-value bounds, however, it is not by itself a strong rank-revealing certificate. When a singular value lies near the threshold or no gap separates \sigma_r from \sigma_{r+1}, perturbations comparable to the threshold may change the reported numerical rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary pivoted QR estimates rank, but a strong certificate needs singular-value bounds or a strong rank-revealing variant.
assumptions_latex: Numerical rank is defined relative to a declared positive tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_i|\sigma_i(A)-\tau|\ \text{small}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{rank}_\tau(A)\ \text{is perturbation-sensitive}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-dependent rank certificate and optimal low-rank approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T} have singular values \sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_q\geq0. If \sigma_r>\tau\geq\sigma_{r+1}, then thresholding at \tau reports numerical rank r. The truncated matrix A_r satisfies \|A-A_r\|_2=\sigma_{r+1}=\min_{\operatorname{rank}(B)\leq r}\|A-B\|_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular-value gap at the declared tolerance certifies numerical rank and the best rank-r approximation error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}_\tau(A)=r,\qquad \min_{\operatorname{rank}(B)\leq r}\|A-B\|_2=\sigma_{r+1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Numerical-Rank Certificate
Rank-Revealing Factorizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical-rank certificate for detecting redundant or nearly dependent equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), a column-pivoted factorization of \(A^{\mathsf T}\) has the form \[A^{\mathsf T}\Pi=QR,\qquad R=\begin{bmatrix}R_{11}&R_{12}\\0&R_{22}\end{bmatrix},\] where \(Q\) is orthogonal and \(\Pi\) is a permutation. For a chosen tolerance \(\tau>0\), if \(R_{11}\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) is well conditioned and \(\lVert R_{22}\rVert_2\leq\tau\), then the first \(r\) pivoted equality rows form a numerically independent set and the remaining rows are redundant to tolerance \(\tau\). The factorization therefore certifies numerical rank \(r\) relative to the stated threshold and conditioning test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pivoted QR factorization separates well-conditioned independent equality rows from a trailing block whose small norm identifies numerical redundancy at a chosen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The rank tolerance and acceptable conditioning threshold are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(A)=r\) under the stated block and conditioning tests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical Rank-Revealing Factorization of an Equality Jacobian
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be the matrix of linear equality gradients, and let \(0\leq r\leq\min\{m,n\}\). A numerical threshold \(\tau_{\rm rank}>0\) separates resolved from unresolved directions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional numerical linear algebra for detecting redundant or nearly dependent equalities; numerical rank is threshold-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-revealing factorization of \(A\) is an orthogonal or unitary factorization whose ordered diagonal or singular data expose an integer \(r\) and bases for the resolved range and null spaces. Canonical forms include \[A=U\Sigma V^T,\qquad \Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_q),\quad \sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_q\geq0,\] with \(q=\min\{m,n\}\), and a column-pivoted QR factorization \[A^T\Pi=Q\begin{bmatrix}R_{11}&R_{12}\\0&R_{22}\end{bmatrix}.\] At tolerance \(\tau_{\rm rank}\), the numerical rank is \[r=\#\{i:\sigma_i>\tau_{\rm rank}\}\] for the singular-value form, or the analogous accepted leading dimension in the pivoted QR form. The columns \(V_{:,r+1:n}\), or the corresponding trailing columns of \(Q\) when factoring \(A^T\), form a numerical null-space basis \(Z\); the accepted pivot rows identify an independent equality subsystem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-revealing factorization orders singular values or pivoted triangular data so that a tolerance determines the numerical rank. It supplies a basis for the effective range, a basis for the numerical null space, and an independent subset of equality constraints. Constraints associated with unresolved directions are treated as redundant or nearly dependent at the chosen threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a finite real matrix representing equality gradients.
A numerical rank threshold \(\tau_{\rm rank}>0\) and a matrix norm or scaling convention are fixed.
The factorization uses orthogonal transformations or an SVD so that its rank information is numerically interpretable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization defines a numerical rank \(r\), an effective independent constraint subsystem, and a matrix \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) satisfying \(AZ\approx0\) at the selected tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the SVD, \(r\) is equivalently the number of singular values exceeding \(\tau_{\rm rank}\), and \(\operatorname{span}(Z)\) is the span of the remaining right singular vectors.
Exact rank is recovered when \(\tau_{\rm rank}=0\) in exact arithmetic.
special_cases_latex: If \(r=m\leq n\), all equality rows are numerically independent and \(Z\) has \(n-m\) columns.
If \(r<m\), only \(r\) independent equality combinations should enter a nonsingular reduced or KKT representation.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced Hessian has dimension \(n-r\), not \(n-m\), after redundant equalities are removed.
A large gap between \(\sigma_r\) and \(\sigma_{r+1}\) makes the selected rank comparatively insensitive to the threshold.
boundary_notes: Numerical rank is not invariant under arbitrary row and column scaling unless the threshold is scaled accordingly.
A pivoted QR rank estimate need not coincide with an SVD threshold near a clustered singular spectrum.

notation.meaning: Selected numerical rank of the equality matrix.
Numerical basis for the null space of the resolved equality system.

children.top_down_role: Balancing primal, constraint, and multiplier blocks before solution.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-Diagonal Balancing of an Equality KKT System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) with \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) symmetric and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Let \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(D_\lambda\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular diagonal or block-diagonal scaling matrices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric scaling of primal and multiplier blocks before a KKT solve; no particular equilibration heuristic is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A KKT block balancing is a congruence transformation by \(D=\operatorname{diag}(D_x,D_\lambda)\) that replaces \[Kz=b\] with \[\widehat K\widehat z=\widehat b,\qquad \widehat K=D^TKD=\begin{bmatrix}D_x^THD_x&D_x^TA^TD_\lambda\\D_\lambda^TAD_x&0\end{bmatrix},\quad \widehat b=D^Tb,\quad z=D\widehat z.\] The scaling is called block-balanced relative to positive target levels \(\gamma_H,\gamma_A\) when its nonzero blocks satisfy prescribed comparability conditions, for example \[\|D_x^THD_x\|\asymp\gamma_H,\qquad \|D_\lambda^TAD_x\|\asymp\gamma_A,\] together with bounded row and column spreads within each block. The defining requirement is algebraic equivalence of the original and scaled systems plus explicit normalization of the primal-curvature and constraint-coupling blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT block balancing rescales primal variables and multipliers by nonsingular diagonal or block-diagonal matrices and applies the matching congruence transformation to the saddle-point matrix. The transformed system has the same solutions after unscaling, while its curvature and constraint blocks are normalized to comparable prescribed magnitudes.
assumptions_latex: The right-hand side and solution are transformed consistently as \(\widehat b=D^Tb\) and \(z=D\widehat z\).
A norm and target block scales are fixed before declaring the system balanced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solving the balanced system and setting \(z=D\widehat z\) yields a solution of the original KKT system, while the transformed nonzero blocks satisfy the selected scaling criteria.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Variable substitution \(p=D_x\widehat p\), \(\lambda=D_\lambda\widehat\lambda\) produces the same transformed equations.
For positive diagonal scalings, balancing may be expressed as equilibration of selected row and column norms of \(\widehat K\).
special_cases_latex: Scalar block scaling uses \(D_x=\alpha I\) and \(D_\lambda=\beta I\).
Symmetric equilibration is recovered when \(D_x\) and \(D_\lambda\) are diagonal and the same scaling is applied on both sides.
immediate_consequences_latex: Congruence preserves symmetry of the KKT matrix.
Nonsingular scaling preserves exact rank and maps exact null vectors bijectively.
boundary_notes: Balancing does not remove rank deficiency or guarantee a small condition number.
The source hints inspected do not provide a single canonical target rule for the block comparability relation.
review_flags: A precise scholarly locator supporting this full block-balancing definition and its normalization criterion was not found in the supplied source hints.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Block Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric variable scaling of the primal block in an equality-constrained KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_x\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular, and substitute \(p=D_x\widetilde p\) in \[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}g\\c\end{bmatrix}.\] Premultiplication by \(\operatorname{diag}(D_x^{\mathsf T},I)\) gives the equivalently scaled system \[\begin{bmatrix}D_x^{\mathsf T}HD_x&D_x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}\\AD_x&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\widetilde p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}D_x^{\mathsf T}g\\c\end{bmatrix}.\] Thus primal scaling changes the Hessian congruently and scales the columns of the constraint matrix while preserving the represented step through \(p=D_x\widetilde p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular change of primal variables congruently scales the Hessian and scales constraint columns without changing the physical primal step.
assumptions_latex: The original KKT system is dimensionally conformable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled and unscaled systems correspond bijectively through \(p=D_x\widetilde p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Block Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row scaling of equality equations and its symmetric embedding in the KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_c\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular. Replacing the equality equation \(Ap=c\) by \(D_cAp=D_cc\), and using the scaled multiplier coordinate \(\widetilde\lambda=D_c^{-\mathsf T}\lambda\), yields \[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}D_c^{\mathsf T}\\D_cA&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\widetilde\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}g\\D_cc\end{bmatrix}.\] This symmetric KKT representation scales constraint rows while preserving the primal equation and the physical multiplier through \(\lambda=D_c^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\lambda\). Consequently, any nonsingular constraint scaling leaves the underlying equality-constrained quadratic problem unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular row scaling of the equalities produces a symmetric scaled KKT system when multiplier coordinates are transformed contragrediently.
assumptions_latex: Multipliers are transformed consistently with the scaled equality equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled system represents the same primal solution, with \(\lambda=D_c^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\lambda\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary diagonal scaling based solely on equality-row magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonzero row \(a_i^T\) of \(A\), choose the positive scale \(d_i=1/\|a_i\|\) in a fixed vector norm and set \(D_c=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\). Then every scaled nonzero row has unit norm, and scaling the right-hand side and multiplier coordinates as in the seed preserves the equality-constrained problem. A zero row cannot be normalized by this rule: if its right-hand side is nonzero the equalities are infeasible, while if its right-hand side is zero the row is redundant and may be removed or assigned a separate conventional nonzero scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocal row norms normalize nonzero constraint rows without changing the problem; zero rows require explicit infeasibility or redundancy handling.
assumptions_latex: Every row assigned a reciprocal-norm scale is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|(D_cA)_{i,:}\|=1\) for each normalized row, with the primal problem preserved by consistent scaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Constraint-Row Normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of constraint-row scaling on a multiplier Schur complement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(H\) is symmetric and nonsingular and define \(S=AH^{-1}A^T\). Under the nonsingular row scaling \(\widetilde A=D_cA\), the scaled Schur matrix is \[\widetilde S=\widetilde A H^{-1}\widetilde A^T=D_cSD_c^T.\] Hence \(S\) and \(\widetilde S\) have the same inertia, rank, and nonsingularity, although their normwise condition numbers need not agree. Solving the consistently scaled Schur system and applying \(\lambda=D_c^T\widetilde\lambda\) recovers the same physical primal and multiplier solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint scaling congruently transforms the multiplier Schur complement, preserving rank and inertia while potentially changing conditioning.
assumptions_latex: The constraint equations and multiplier coordinates are scaled consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde S=D_cSD_c^T\), so rank, inertia, and nonsingularity are invariant while conditioning may change.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of errors and stopping tolerances after multiplier scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda, corresponding multiplier errors satisfy e_\lambda=D_\lambda e_{\widetilde\lambda}. Therefore raw normwise errors or step tolerances in scaled coordinates are not physical-coordinate invariants; they obey \|e_\lambda\|\leq\|D_\lambda\|\|e_{\widetilde\lambda}\| and \|e_{\widetilde\lambda}\|\leq\|D_\lambda^{-1}\|\|e_\lambda\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled multiplier errors and tolerances must be mapped through the scaling before physical interpretation.
assumptions_latex: Both errors represent the same physical multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_\lambda=D_\lambda e_{\widetilde\lambda}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate scaling of KKT multipliers with the matching constraint-equation transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D_\lambda\in\mathbb R^{m\times m} be nonsingular and write \lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda. Premultiplying the constraint equation by D_\lambda^{\mathsf T} gives the equivalent symmetric system \[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}D_\lambda\\D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\widetilde\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}g\\D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}c\end{bmatrix}.\] The physical variables are recovered by p=p and \lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier-coordinate scaling preserves symmetric KKT form when the constraint equation receives the matching transpose scaling.
assumptions_latex: The constraint equation is transformed together with the multiplier coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda,\qquad D_c=D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}.

Multiplier-Block Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate scaling of KKT multipliers with the corresponding constraint-row transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_\lambda\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular and write \(\lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda\). To retain a symmetric coefficient matrix, premultiply the constraint equation by \(D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}\). The KKT equations become \[\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}D_\lambda\\D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\widetilde\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}g\\D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}c\end{bmatrix}.\] The physical multiplier is recovered as \(\lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda\), and the primal step is unchanged. Multiplier-block scaling is therefore algebraically equivalent to the matching constraint-row scaling \(D_c=D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling multiplier coordinates requires the matching transpose scaling of constraint equations to preserve symmetric KKT form and the original primal solution.
assumptions_latex: The constraint block is transformed together with the multiplier coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiplier scaling is equivalent to constraint scaling with \(D_c=D_\lambda^{\mathsf T}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of multiplier error and stationarity residual under multiplier-coordinate scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(\lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda\), the multiplier error satisfies \(e_\lambda=D_\lambda e_{\widetilde\lambda}\), while the physical stationarity residual is \(r_d=g-Hp-A^{\mathsf T}D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda\). Thus a normwise stopping test in scaled multiplier coordinates is not invariant unless it is mapped through \(D_\lambda\); in particular, \(\|e_\lambda\|\leq\|D_\lambda\|\,\|e_{\widetilde\lambda}\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier errors and stopping tolerances must be mapped back through the multiplier scaling before they are interpreted physically.
assumptions_latex: The same physical multiplier is represented by \(\lambda=D_\lambda\widetilde\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: e_\lambda=D_\lambda e_{\widetilde\lambda},\qquad \|e_\lambda\|\leq\|D_\lambda\|\|e_{\widetilde\lambda}\|.

children.title: KKT Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Joint balancing of coupled saddle-point blocks before numerical solution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties that nonsingular diagonal equilibration cannot repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonsingular diagonal D, \ker(DKD)=D^{-1}\ker(K). Thus diagonal equilibration cannot change nullity or remove singularity, and a structurally zero row and corresponding column remain zero after scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equilibration cannot repair singularity or structural zeros.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim\ker(DKD)=\dim\ker(K).
knowledge_statements.title: Singularity and Structural-Zero Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic effects of nonsingular diagonal symmetric scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K=K^{\mathsf T}, let D be nonsingular diagonal, and set \widetilde K=DKD and \widetilde b=Db. Then Kz=b if and only if \widetilde K\widetilde z=\widetilde b with z=D\widetilde z. Moreover, \operatorname{rank}(\widetilde K)=\operatorname{rank}(K) and \operatorname{In}(\widetilde K)=\operatorname{In}(K).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric diagonal scaling preserves the represented solution, rank, and inertia.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Kz=b\iff(DKD)D^{-1}z=Db,\quad \operatorname{rank}(DKD)=\operatorname{rank}(K),\quad \operatorname{In}(DKD)=\operatorname{In}(K).
knowledge_statements.title: Congruence Invariants and Solution Mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite safeguarded diagonal equilibration for a symmetric, possibly indefinite KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D=I\). At each sweep form or access \(B=DKD\), compute \(s_i=\|B_{i,:}\|_\infty\), and fail with a structural-zero status if some required row has \(s_i=0\). Otherwise set \(E_{ii}=s_i^{-1/2}\), optionally clip each positive entry to declared scaling bounds, and update \(D\leftarrow DE\). Stop when the nonzero row-norm spread is at most \(\gamma\), or after \(N_{\max}\) sweeps. Solve \((DKD)\widetilde z=Db\), recover \(z=D\widetilde z\), and test the original KKT residual. This is a balancing heuristic; absent additional hypotheses, reaching the spread target before the cap is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply safeguarded positive diagonal congruence sweeps, stop at a norm-spread target or iteration cap, solve the scaled system, and certify the unscaled residual.
assumptions_latex: Scaling bounds, if used, are positive and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ remains nonsingular and the procedure terminates by the cap; successful balancing before the cap is not guaranteed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Capped Symmetric Norm Equilibration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual transformation under symmetric diagonal KKT scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde K=DKD\), \(\widetilde b=Db\), and \(z=D\widetilde z\). Then \[r=b-Kz,\qquad \widetilde r=\widetilde b-\widetilde K\widetilde z=Dr.\] Hence an original-system residual tolerance must be checked after unscaling or translated using the declared norm and bounds on \(D\); a small unweighted scaled residual alone is not an invariant certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled residual is the diagonal scaling of the original residual, so the final KKT equations must be checked in original coordinates or with a rigorously translated tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde r=Dr,\qquad r=D^{-1}\widetilde r.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled and Original Residual Correspondence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equilibration Sweep Cost and Termination Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bound for capped diagonal norm-equilibration sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Diagonal scaling preserves the sparsity pattern of \(K\). If row norms and diagonal updates are computed from the stored nonzeros, one equilibration sweep costs \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(K))\) arithmetic and \(O(n+m)\) auxiliary storage. With a cap of \(N_{\max}\) sweeps, preprocessing costs \(O(N_{\max}\operatorname{nnz}(K))\) and terminates after at most \(N_{\max}\) sweeps, independently of whether the requested norm spread is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each diagonal equilibration sweep is linear in the stored nonzeros, and the prescribed sweep cap gives finite termination without implying convergence to the target balance.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ is stored sparsely or scanned by its nonzeros}.
Only diagonal scaling and row-norm accumulation are performed during a sweep.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{equil}}=O(N_{\max}\operatorname{nnz}(K)),\qquad M_{\mathrm{aux}}=O(n+m).

notation.meaning: number of stored nonzero entries of K

KKT Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal symmetric equilibration intended to reduce coefficient-scale disparities in a KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric KKT matrix \(K\in\mathbb R^{(n+m)\times(n+m)}\), choose a positive diagonal matrix \(D=\operatorname{diag}(D_x,D_\lambda)\). Starting from \(D=I\), repeatedly estimate each row norm \(s_i=\lVert(DKD)_{i,:}\rVert\) and update \(D_{ii}\leftarrow D_{ii}/\sqrt{s_i}\) for rows with \(s_i>0\). Stop when the ratio of the largest to smallest nonzero row norm is at most \(\gamma\), or after a prescribed iteration limit. Solve \((DKD)\widetilde z=Db\) and recover \(z=D\widetilde z\). Symmetric scaling preserves inertia while seeking balanced row and column magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteratively apply positive diagonal symmetric scaling until nonzero KKT row norms are balanced, solve the scaled system, and map the solution back.
assumptions_latex: Every structurally nonzero row has positive norm during scaling.
\(\gamma\geq1\) and an iteration limit are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(Kz=b\) whenever the scaled solve is exact, and \(DKD\) has the same inertia as \(K\).

notation.meaning: current norm of scaled row i

children.title: Factorization Maintenance Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of bases, numeric factors, and symbolic structure across related equality systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k\) be a sequence of related equality matrices, \(Z_k\) a null-space basis, and \(R_k\) or \(L_k\) stored factors of \(A_k\) or \(Z_k^TH_kZ_k\). Changes between consecutive systems may add or delete constraints or modify numerical values without changing all sparsity data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional direct linear algebra across a sequence of related equality-constrained subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A factorization-maintenance lifecycle is a state sequence \(\mathcal F_k=(\mathcal S_k,\mathcal N_k,\mathcal B_k)\), where \(\mathcal S_k\) is symbolic structure, \(\mathcal N_k\) is a numerical factorization, and \(\mathcal B_k\) is an associated range/null-space basis, together with the transition rule \[\mathcal F_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\operatorname{reuse}(\mathcal F_k),&M_{k+1}=M_k,\\\operatorname{update}(\mathcal F_k,\Delta M_k),&M_{k+1}=M_k+\Delta M_k\text{ and a stable update is accepted},\\\operatorname{refactor}(M_{k+1}),&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] An update is accepted only if its factors represent the new matrix to a prescribed residual tolerance and retain required rank, inertia, or definiteness information. For an added or deleted equality, orthogonal transformations update the QR factors and hence \(Z_k\); a compatible update may then transform a factor of \(Z_k^TH_kZ_k\) into one for \(Z_{k+1}^TH_{k+1}Z_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifecycle stores symbolic structure, numerical factors, and range or null-space bases for a sequence of related equality systems. An unchanged system reuses its factors; a limited change triggers an accepted stable update; and any failed accuracy, rank, inertia, or stability test triggers fresh factorization.
assumptions_latex: Consecutive matrices are explicitly related by no change, a structured modification, or general replacement.
Every maintained factor has a computable representation-residual test.
Any definiteness, rank, or inertia property required by the downstream solve is included in the acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every accepted lifecycle state, the stored factors and bases represent the current equality system within the prescribed tolerance; otherwise they are discarded and recomputed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For active-set changes, the lifecycle is equivalently a sequence of QR updates and downdates followed by reduced-Hessian factor updates when applicable.
special_cases_latex: Adding one independent equality removes one column from the null-space dimension.
Deleting one equality augments the null-space basis and may require enlarging a Cholesky factor of the reduced Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: Symbolic analysis may be reused when only numerical values change and the sparsity pattern is fixed.
A refactorization is a defined lifecycle transition rather than an exceptional mathematical state.
boundary_notes: An update cheaper than refactorization can still be rejected for numerical instability.
Cholesky maintenance requires the updated reduced matrix to remain positive definite.

notation.meaning: Symbolic, numerical-factor, and basis components of the state.

children.title: Numeric Factorization Updates

knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Factorization Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of a fixed sparse elimination structure while recomputing numerical KKT factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_k\) and \(K_{k+1}\) be symmetric KKT matrices with the same sparsity pattern, and let \(P\) be a permutation obtained from a prior symbolic analysis. Retain \(P\), the elimination tree, and allocated factor structure; replace the stored matrix values by those of \(K_{k+1}\), then recompute numerical factors satisfying \[P^{\mathsf T}K_{k+1}P=L_{k+1}D_{k+1}L_{k+1}^{\mathsf T},\] including any permitted numerical pivoting. Accept the update only if pivot tests and solve-residual tests pass. Otherwise discard the numeric update and initiate renewed symbolic analysis or a full factorization under a revised ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When KKT sparsity is unchanged, reuse symbolic analysis but recompute numeric factors, accepting them only after pivot and residual checks.
assumptions_latex: \(K_{k+1}\) is symmetric and has the anticipated sparsity pattern.
The factorization supports the required stability-preserving pivoting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted factors solve systems with \(K_{k+1}\) to the prescribed residual tolerance.

children.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of elimination structure across systems sharing a sparsity pattern.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Factorization Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for retaining sparse ordering and elimination structure across KKT factorizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_k\) and \(K_{k+1}\) be symmetric matrices with identical structural nonzero patterns, and fix a permutation \(P\). In an elimination scheme whose symbolic fill depends only on that pattern and \(P\), the elimination tree and predicted storage pattern computed for \(P^{\mathsf T}K_kP\) are also valid for \(P^{\mathsf T}K_{k+1}P\). Only numerical factor values need recomputation. If numerical pivoting introduces permutations not represented by the stored symbolic structure, or if the structural pattern changes, this reuse guarantee no longer applies and symbolic analysis must be revised.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged structural sparsity pattern and ordering permit reuse of the elimination tree and predicted fill, unless dynamic pivoting or pattern changes invalidate them.
assumptions_latex: The two matrices have identical structural sparsity patterns.
The same permutation and compatible pivoting policy are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The prior symbolic elimination structure remains valid for the new numerical factorization.

children.title: Null-Space Basis Updates
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of reduced-space bases under related constraint changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Basis Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal maintenance of a null-space basis after a small equality-matrix modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m_k\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(Z_k\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker(A_k)\). After adding one equality row \(a^{\mathsf T}\), compute \(w=Z_k^{\mathsf T}a\). If \(\lVert w\rVert\leq\tau\lVert a\rVert\), declare the new row numerically redundant and retain \(Z_k\). Otherwise construct an orthogonal matrix \(Q\) with \(Q^{\mathsf T}w=\lVert w\rVert e_1\), and set \(Z_{k+1}=Z_kQ_{:,2:}\). Reorthogonalize when necessary and accept only if \(\lVert A_{k+1}Z_{k+1}\rVert\) and \(\lVert Z_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}Z_{k+1}-I\rVert\) meet prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an added equality, rotate the old null-space basis so one direction captures the new restriction, then drop that direction and verify feasibility and orthogonality.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one candidate equality row is added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon acceptance, the columns of \(Z_{k+1}\) numerically span \(\ker(A_{k+1})\).

notation.meaning: new equality row represented in current null-space coordinates

children.title: Update-Rebuild Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes determining when incremental maintenance should give way to complete reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Update-Rebuild Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance boundary separating inexpensive factor updates from complete factorization reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an updated factorization produce a computed solution \(\widehat z\) of \(Kz=b\). Define the scaled backward error \[\eta=\frac{\lVert b-K\widehat z\rVert}{\lVert K\rVert\lVert\widehat z\rVert+\lVert b\rVert}.\] Continue update-based maintenance only while \(\eta\leq\tau_b\), all required pivots exceed the stability threshold \(\tau_p\), the structural pattern remains compatible with stored symbolic data, and accumulated update count does not exceed \(u_{\max}\). Violation of any condition is an update-rebuild boundary: discard the maintained numeric factors and rebuild from the current matrix, including renewed symbolic analysis when structural compatibility has failed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rebuild factors when backward error, pivot quality, sparsity compatibility, or accumulated-update limits fail their prescribed acceptance tests.
assumptions_latex: Matrix and residual norms are mutually compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An update is retained only if every stated reliability test passes.
review_flags: Specific update rejection and rebuild criteria require a sparse-factorization implementation source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the combined backward-error, pivot, structural-compatibility, and update-count policy is implementation-specific and uncited. The backward-error formula also needs a convention for a zero denominator, and the pivot-quality test requires a precise definition suitable for block pivots.

children.title: Linear-Equality Optimization Methods
children.top_down_role: Optimization methods specialized to fixed affine feasible spaces and their reduced search-direction models.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduction Method for Optimization on a Fixed Affine Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(r\), the feasible set is nonempty, \(x_p\) satisfies \(Ax_p=b\), and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) has full column rank with \(AZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth optimization with fixed linear equalities; global convergence properties depend on the chosen unconstrained method and are not part of this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A linear-equality optimization method is a reduction method that parameterizes every feasible point as \[x=x_p+Zy,\ y\in\mathbb R^{n-r},\] defines the reduced objective \[\phi(y)=f(x_p+Zy),\] and applies an unconstrained optimization step to \(\phi\). If \(f\) is differentiable, its reduced gradient is \[
abla\phi(y)=Z^T
abla f(x_p+Zy).\] If \(f\) is twice differentiable, its reduced Hessian is \[
abla^2\phi(y)=Z^T
abla^2f(x_p+Zy)Z.\] A reduced step \(s_y\) induces the feasible full-space step \(s=Zs_y\), for which \(A(x+s)=b\). The method is specified by the feasible representation, the reduced model, and a rule for selecting and accepting \(s_y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one feasible point and a basis for the null space of the fixed equality matrix. Express every feasible point through reduced coordinates, minimize the objective composed with this affine parameterization, and lift each reduced step through the null-space basis. Reduced gradients and Hessians are obtained by multiplying the full derivatives by the basis and its transpose.
assumptions_latex: The derivatives displayed exist on the affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained problem is represented exactly by the unconstrained reduced problem \(\min_{y\in\mathbb R^{n-r}}\phi(y)\), and every lifted reduced iterate is feasible.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The projected first-order stationarity condition is \(Z^T\nabla f(x)=0\).
With orthonormal \(Z\), the tangent-space projector is \(P=ZZ^T\) and stationarity is \(P\nabla f(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: When \(r=n\), the feasible set contains a single point and the reduced space has dimension zero.
When \(A=0\), one may take \(Z=I\), recovering unconstrained optimization.
immediate_consequences_latex: All trial displacements \(Zs_y\) preserve the equalities in exact arithmetic.
The reduced problem has \(n-r\) variables.
boundary_notes: This definition does not cover nonlinear equality manifolds, whose tangent basis changes with the iterate.
An ill-conditioned basis \(Z\) may degrade numerical behavior without changing the exact feasible set.

children.title: Projected Steepest-Descent Methods
children.top_down_role: First-order descent within a fixed affine tangent space.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Steepest-Descent Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order descent for a smooth objective restricted to a fixed affine equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(x_0\) is feasible. Define the orthogonal null-space projector \(P=I-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}A\). At iteration \(k\), set \(d_k=-P\nabla f(x_k)\). If \(\lVert P\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by a line search satisfying sufficient decrease along \(d_k\), and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Every iterate remains feasible, and any returned point satisfies the projected first-order stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the negative gradient into the equality null space, line-search along that feasible direction, and stop when the projected gradient is small.
assumptions_latex: The line search accepts a positive sufficient-decrease step when the projected gradient is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax_k=b\) for every iterate, and termination gives \(\lVert P\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Rate under Reduced Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-step rate on the affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be an orthonormal basis of \(\ker A\), and suppose \(\varphi(y)=f(x_0+Zy)\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and is \(\mu\)-strongly convex. Projected steepest descent with step \(1/L\) satisfies \[\varphi(y_k)-\varphi(y_*)\le\left(1-\frac\mu L\right)^k(\varphi(y_0)-\varphi(y_*)).\] Thus \(O((L/\mu)\log(1/\varepsilon))\) iterations reduce the objective gap by a factor \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced strong convexity and smoothness give projected gradient descent its standard linear rate.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) are orthonormal and span \(\ker A\).
The reduced objective is \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.

abla f(x_k)\). Then the accepted step lengths have a positive lower bound and \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|P
abla f(x_k)\|^2<\infty,\qquad \|P
abla f(x_k)\|	o0.\]

\(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz near the generated feasible level set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Steepest Descent on an Affine Feasible Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(Ax=b\) be consistent, and let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker(A)\). Define the orthogonal tangent projector \(P=ZZ^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order descent for fixed linear equalities in the Euclidean metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A projected steepest-descent iteration from a feasible point \(x_k\) is \[d_k=-P
abla f(x_k)=-ZZ^T
abla f(x_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\] where \(\alpha_k\geq0\) is selected by a line-search or prescribed step rule. Equivalently, in reduced coordinates \(x_k=x_p+Zy_k\), \[y_{k+1}=y_k-\alpha_k Z^T
abla f(x_p+Zy_k).\] The vector \(d_k\) is the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm tangent vector solving \[\min_{d:Ad=0}\ 
abla f(x_k)^Td+	frac12\|d\|^2.\] The method terminates at projected stationarity when \(P
abla f(x_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each feasible iterate, orthogonally project the negative gradient onto the null space of the equality matrix and move along that feasible direction. This is ordinary steepest descent applied to the affine reduced objective. The projected gradient vanishes exactly at first-order stationarity relative to the affine feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The step length \(\alpha_k\) is nonnegative and is chosen within the domain of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direction satisfies \(Ad_k=0\), every iterate remains feasible, and \(d_k=0\) precisely when the reduced gradient \(Z^T\nabla f(x_k)\) is zero.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The full-space iteration is identical to steepest descent on \(\phi(y)=f(x_p+Zy)\).
The direction is \(-P\nabla f(x_k)\), where \(P\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\ker(A)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A=0\), then \(P=I\) and the method is unconstrained steepest descent.
A weighted metric replaces \(P\) by the corresponding metric projector and is outside the Euclidean canonical form.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the projected gradient is nonzero, then \(\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k=-\|P\nabla f(x_k)\|^2<0\).
Exact line searches operate entirely along feasible affine lines.
boundary_notes: Projection with a nonorthonormal basis requires \(P=Z(Z^TZ)^{-1}Z^T\), not generally \(ZZ^T\).
Finite-precision projection may require residual refinement to maintain feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Derivative Method in Affine Reduced Coordinates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(Ax=b\) be consistent, choose \(Ax_p=b\), and let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) span \(\ker(A)\). Set \(\phi(y)=f(x_p+Zy)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional methods using exact or modified curvature on a fixed affine feasible space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduced second-derivative method forms at \(x_k=x_p+Zy_k\) the reduced gradient and curvature matrix \[g_k^R=Z^T\nabla f(x_k),\qquad B_k^R\approx Z^T\nabla^2f(x_k)Z,\] computes a reduced step from a second-order model, canonically \[B_k^Rs_k^R=-g_k^R,\] and lifts it as \(d_k=Zs_k^R\). The next iterate has the form \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k=x_p+Z(y_k+\alpha_ks_k^R),\] where globalization may use a line search or a reduced-space trust region. Exact reduced Newton uses equality in the curvature approximation; modified Newton replaces the reduced Hessian by a nonsingular matrix, commonly positive definite, that is suitable for the step rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form the gradient and Hessian of the objective restricted to the affine feasible space, solve a reduced second-order model, and lift the reduced step through the fixed null-space basis. Exact Newton and modified Newton differ only in whether the exact reduced Hessian or a safeguarded curvature matrix is used.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the relevant feasible iterates.
The chosen reduced curvature matrix is solvable, or the subproblem rule specifies how singular or indefinite curvature is handled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every lifted step lies in \(\ker(A)\), and the reduced model uses precisely the objective curvature restricted to feasible directions when \(B_k^R=Z^T\nabla^2f(x_k)Z\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The step minimizes \((g_k^R)^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_k^Rs\) when \(B_k^R\succ0\).
In full space, exact reduced Newton satisfies \(Z^T(\nabla f(x_k)+\nabla^2f(x_k)d_k)=0\) with \(Ad_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: For quadratic \(f\), the exact reduced model is the reduced objective itself.
With \(B_k^R=I\), the direction reduces to projected steepest descent in reduced coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only an \((n-r)\times(n-r)\) curvature system is solved.
Positive definiteness of \(B_k^R\) makes a nonzero reduced step a descent direction.
boundary_notes: For nonlinear equalities, derivatives of the Lagrangian and an iterate-dependent tangent basis replace the fixed affine formulas.
Indefinite reduced curvature requires a safeguard or a subproblem capable of exploiting negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Reduced-Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Newton iteration in the fixed null space of affine equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible iterate \(x_k\), form the reduced gradient and exact reduced Hessian \(g_k=Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(H_k=Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2 f(x_k)Z\). If \(H_k\) is nonsingular, compute \(p_k\) from \[H_kp_k=-g_k,\] choose a step length \(\alpha_k>0\) by an admissible Newton globalization rule, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\). Because \(AZ=0\), every iterate remains feasible. Stop when \(\lVert g_k\rVert\) is below the prescribed tolerance; with \(\alpha_k=1\), the update is the exact reduced-Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the Newton equation using the exact Hessian restricted to the equality-feasible null space, so every accepted iterate remains feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(Ax_k=b\), and the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
\(H_k=Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x_k)Z\) is nonsingular whenever the exact step is taken.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax_{k+1}=b\), and \(Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x_k)Zp_k=-Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Newton Step for a Linearly Equality-Constrained Objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(Ax=b\) be consistent, and let \(Z\) span \(\ker(A)\). At a feasible iterate \(x_k\), write \(g_k^R=Z^T\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(H_k^R=Z^T\nabla^2f(x_k)Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-derivative Newton iteration on a fixed affine space, with a nonsingular reduced Hessian at the step under consideration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The exact reduced-Newton direction is \[s_k^R=-(H_k^R)^{-1}g_k^R,\qquad d_k=Zs_k^R,\] equivalently the solution of \[Z^T
abla^2f(x_k)Zs_k^R=-Z^T
abla f(x_k).\] The iteration is \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\] with \(\alpha_k=1\) for the pure Newton iteration or a globalized step length otherwise. The adjective exact means that both \(
abla f(x_k)\) and the restricted Hessian \(Z^T
abla^2f(x_k)Z\) are evaluated from the exact derivatives of \(f\), rather than finite differences, secant updates, or regularized substitutes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict the exact Hessian and gradient to the null space of the fixed equality matrix, solve the resulting Newton equation, and lift the reduced correction to the original variables. The lifted direction is feasible and is the ordinary Newton direction for the reduced objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direction \(d_k\) satisfies \(Ad_k=0\) and the reduced Newton equation \(Z^T(\nabla f(x_k)+\nabla^2f(x_k)d_k)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The same direction is obtained by applying unconstrained Newton's method to \(\phi(y)=f(x_p+Zy)\).
It is the stationary point of the exact reduced quadratic Taylor model.
special_cases_latex: If \(H_k^R\succ0\) and \(g_k^R\neq0\), then \(d_k\) is a feasible descent direction.
For a strictly convex quadratic reduced objective, one full exact Newton step reaches its unique minimizer in exact arithmetic.
immediate_consequences_latex: No multiplier is required to compute the reduced step.
The linear system dimension equals the number of affine degrees of freedom.
boundary_notes: A singular or indefinite reduced Hessian may make the pure Newton direction undefined or non-descending.
Derivative approximation belongs to discrete or quasi-Newton variants, not this exact definition.

children.top_down_role: Reduced Newton variants accommodating indefinite or poorly conditioned curvature.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g_k^R=Z^T\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(H_k^R=Z^T\nabla^2f(x_k)Z\) for a feasible point of \(Ax=b\). Let \(\delta_k\geq0\), \(\Delta_k>0\), or another explicit safeguard parameter be available.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional reduced Newton variants designed for indefinite, singular, or poorly conditioned restricted curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A curvature-safeguarded reduced-Newton method replaces the unsafeguarded equation \(H_k^Rs=-g_k^R\) by a step rule that remains defined and supplies controlled model decrease when \(H_k^R\) is indefinite or ill-conditioned. Canonical members are the shifted system \[(H_k^R+\delta_kI)s_k^R=-g_k^R,\qquad H_k^R+\delta_kI\succeq\mu_k I\quad(\mu_k>0),\] and the reduced trust-region problem \[s_k^R\in\arg\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}\bigl((g_k^R)^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_k^Rs\bigr).\] The full step is \(d_k=Zs_k^R\). A negative-curvature variant may instead select \(v_k\) with \(v_k^TH_k^Rv_k<0\), orient it so \((g_k^R)^Tv_k\leq0\), and bound its length by the globalization rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the reduced Hessian is singular, indefinite, or poorly conditioned, replace the raw Newton solve by a positive shift, a reduced trust-region subproblem, or a bounded negative-curvature direction. Lift the resulting safeguarded reduced step through the null-space basis so feasibility is retained.
assumptions_latex: The reduced gradient and symmetric reduced Hessian are available.
The safeguard produces a finite step and imposes either positive-definite shifted curvature or an explicit radius bound.
\(Z\) spans the fixed equality null space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns a feasible direction \(d_k=Zs_k^R\) even when the pure reduced Newton equation is unsuitable, with curvature or step length controlled by the stated safeguard.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Modified Cholesky applied to \(H_k^R\) defines a positive-definite \(B_k^R\) and solves \(B_k^Rs=-g_k^R\).
Levenberg–Marquardt regularization is the scalar-shift specialization.
special_cases_latex: If \(H_k^R\succ0\) is sufficiently conditioned, one may set \(\delta_k=0\) and recover exact reduced Newton.
If negative curvature is encountered in a trust-region solve, the step may terminate on the reduced trust-region boundary.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive-definite shifted curvature makes every nonzero step a reduced descent direction.
All safeguards act only in the feasible degrees of freedom.
boundary_notes: A safeguard changes the pure Newton step and may change its local rate unless it becomes inactive near a regular minimizer.
Positive shifting suppresses rather than exploits negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Modified Reduced-Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral modification of reduced curvature before computing a feasible Newton-like step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible iterate \(x_k\), form \(g_k=Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\) and the symmetric reduced Hessian \(H_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\). For a safeguard \(\delta_k>0\), define \[B_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\max\{\lambda_{k,i},\delta_k\})Q_k^{\mathsf T}.\] Solve \(B_kp_k=-g_k\), select \(\alpha_k>0\) by a descent globalization rule, and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\). Stop when \(\lVert g_k\rVert\) meets the tolerance. The modification makes \(B_k\) positive definite and yields \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\) whenever \(g_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace unsafe reduced-Hessian eigenvalues by a positive floor, then compute and globalize the resulting feasible descent step.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(x_k\) satisfies \(Ax_k=b\).
\(AZ=0\), and \(H_k=Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x_k)Z\) is represented by a symmetric eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k\succeq\delta_k I\), \(Ax_{k+1}=b\), and \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k=-g_k^{\mathsf T}B_k^{-1}g_k<0\) for \(g_k\ne0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the full-step reduced iteration be \(T(y)=y-B(y)^{-1}
abla\varphi(y)\), where \(B\) is continuous and nonsingular near a stationary point \(y_*\). With \(H_*=
abla^2\varphi(y_*)\) and \(B_*=B(y_*)\), \[T'(y_*)=I-B_*^{-1}H_*.\] If \(B_*=H_*\), the derivative vanishes and quadratic Newton behavior is possible. If \(B_*
e H_*\), quadratic convergence is not generally available; when \(T\) is continuously differentiable and \(ho(I-B_*^{-1}H_*)<1\), the generic local rate is linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral modification that remains active at the solution generally sacrifices Newton's quadratic rate.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local rate matrix is \(I-B_*^{-1}H_*\); asymptotic exactness \(B_*=H_*\) is required for a zero derivative.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual Recovery of Exact Reduced Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic convergence once spectral flooring becomes inactive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_*\) be a stationary point of the reduced objective with \(H(y_*)\succ0\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(H(y_*))>\bar\delta>0\). If \(H\) is locally Lipschitz and \(0<\delta_k\le\bar\delta\), then sufficiently near \(y_*\), every eigenvalue of \(H_k\) exceeds \(\delta_k\), so the floor is inactive and \(B_k=H_k\). If unit steps are accepted, the iteration is exact reduced Newton and converges quadratically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a positive-definite solution, a sufficiently low eigenvalue floor becomes inactive and exact reduced-Newton convergence is recovered.
assumptions_latex: The reduced Hessian is locally Lipschitz.
\(0<\delta_k\le\bar\delta\), and unit steps are eventually accepted.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Newton's superlinear rate when scalar regularization remains bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the strongly convex quadratic \(\psi(z)=\tfrac12(z-z_*)^{\mathsf T}H(z-z_*)\), \(H\succ0\), a regularized full step with shift \(\lambda_k\ge0\) satisfies \[z_{k+1}-z_*=\lambda_k(H+\lambda_kI)^{-1}(z_k-z_*).\] If \(\lambda_k\to\bar\lambda>0\), the iteration is generally only linearly convergent and cannot have a superlinear rate for nonzero errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shift that approaches a positive constant generally leaves a nonzero linear error map and prevents recovery of Newton's superlinear rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{k+1}=\lambda_k(H+\lambda_kI)^{-1}e_k\), whose limiting iteration matrix is nonzero when \(\bar\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Shift Rate Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral and variational characterization of scalar regularization in reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(H\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^d\), and \(\delta>0\), the smallest nonnegative shift satisfying \(H+\lambda I\succeq\delta I\) is \[\lambda_*=\max\{0,\delta-\lambda_{\min}(H)\}.\] For every \(\lambda\ge\lambda_*\), \(p=-(H+\lambda I)^{-1}g\) is the unique minimizer of \[m_\lambda(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Hp+\tfrac\lambda2\lVert p\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal scalar shift raises the smallest eigenvalue to the prescribed floor, and the resulting step uniquely minimizes the regularized reduced quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+\lambda I\succeq\delta I\) for \(\lambda\ge\lambda_*\), and \(\operatorname*{argmin}m_\lambda=\{-(H+\lambda I)^{-1}g\}\).

notation.meaning: Smallest eigenvalue of the reduced Hessian.

abla\psi(z_*)=0\), \(

children.title: Indefinite-Curvature Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Structural responses to negative directions in the reduced model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorization-based branch for indefinite reduced Newton models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible iterate, form reduced gradient \(g_k\) and symmetric reduced Hessian \(H_k\). If a factorization certifies \(H_k\succeq\delta I\), use \(p_k=-H_k^{-1}g_k\). Otherwise extract \(d_k\ne0\) with \(d_k^{\mathsf T}H_kd_k<0\), orient it so that \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le0\), and set \(p_k=d_k\). Backtrack until the reduced objective satisfies a prescribed sufficient-decrease test compatible with the linear-plus-quadratic model, then update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the reduced Newton direction only after positive-curvature certification; otherwise use an oriented negative-curvature direction and safeguarded backtracking.
assumptions_latex: The reduced objective is twice continuously differentiable.
The indefinite factorization returns a verifiable negative-curvature direction.
The acceptance test permits sufficiently small steps certified by the local linear-plus-quadratic decrease model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected direction is either strict first-order descent or certified negative curvature with nonpositive first-order derivative, and \(Ax_{k+1}=b\).
knowledge_statements.title: Descent-or-Negative-Curvature Safeguard

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local feasible decrease certificate for indefinite reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\) and \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) be the reduced gradient and Hessian, and let \(d\ne0\) satisfy \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0\). Choose its sign so that \(g^{\mathsf T}d\le0\). For the recentered reduced objective \(\varphi\), \[\varphi(\alpha d)-\varphi(0)=\alpha g^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12\alpha^2d^{\mathsf T}Hd+o(\alpha^2).\] Hence every sufficiently small \(\alpha>0\) decreases \(\varphi\), including when \(g^{\mathsf T}d=0\). Mapping through a null-space basis preserves the affine equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oriented negative-curvature direction certifies local feasible decrease, even when its first-order derivative is zero.
assumptions_latex: The reduced objective is twice continuously differentiable.
\(d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0\), and the sign of \(d\) gives \(g^{\mathsf T}d\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all sufficiently small \(\alpha>0\), \(\varphi(\alpha d)<\varphi(0)\).

notation.meaning: recentered objective restricted to the affine null space

knowledge_statements.title: Oriented Negative-Curvature Descent Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent failure when indefinite reduced curvature is inverted without repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular symmetric \(H\), the Newton step \(p_N=-H^{-1}g\) satisfies \(g^{\mathsf T}p_N=-g^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}g\). This is negative for every \(g\ne0\) exactly when \(H\succ0\). If \(H\) is indefinite, some nonzero \(g\) gives \(g^{\mathsf T}p_N>0\), so the unmodified step can be ascending.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indefinite reduced curvature permits ascent Newton steps and therefore requires a safeguard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform descent of \(-H^{-1}g\) for all nonzero \(g\) holds exactly when \(H\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Unmodified Reduced-Newton Step
Indefinite-Curvature Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A descent-or-negative-curvature safeguard for indefinite reduced Hessians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible iterate, form the reduced gradient \(g_k\) and symmetric reduced Hessian \(H_k\). If a factorization certifies \(H_k\succeq\delta I\), use \(p_k=-H_k^{-1}g_k\). Otherwise choose either a modified positive-definite matrix \(B_k\succeq\delta I\) and set \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k\), or find \(d_k\ne0\) with \(d_k^{\mathsf T}H_kd_k<0\) and orient it so that \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le0\). Globalize the selected reduced direction and update through \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\), taking \(p_k=d_k\) in the negative-curvature case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When reduced curvature is indefinite, replace it by safe positive curvature or follow an oriented negative-curvature direction while preserving feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The globalization rule accepts only steps satisfying its prescribed sufficient-decrease criterion.
