children.title: Poor-Conditioning Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Structural responses to nearly singular reduced curvature.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue clipping imposing a prescribed reduced-system condition bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\) and choose \(0<\delta_k\le\Delta_k\). Define \[\widehat\lambda_{k,i}=\min\{\Delta_k,\max\{\lambda_{k,i},\delta_k\}\},\qquad B_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T}.\] Compute \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k\), globalize the direction, and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\). Then \(\delta_kI\preceq B_k\preceq\Delta_kI\), \(\kappa_2(B_k)\le\Delta_k/\delta_k\), and \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\) whenever \(g_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip reduced-Hessian eigenvalues to a positive bounded interval to control conditioning while retaining a feasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_kI\preceq B_k\preceq\Delta_kI\), \(\kappa_2(B_k)\le\Delta_k/\delta_k\), and \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\) for \(g_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Spectral Conditioning Repair

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-aware test for an inexact reduced-Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\succ0\), let \(Bp_*=-g\), and let \(r=B\widehat p+g\). Then \[\widehat p-p_*=B^{-1}r,\qquad \|\widehat p-p_*\|_2\le\frac{\|r\|_2}{\lambda_{\min}(B)}.\] If \(g\ne0\), then \[\frac{\|\widehat p-p_*\|_2}{\|p_*\|_2}\le\kappa_2(B)\frac{\|r\|_2}{\|g\|_2}.\] Thus a small residual alone does not certify a small relative step error when \(B\) is poorly conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced residual becomes a reliable step-error certificate only after accounting for conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat p-p_*\|_2\le\|r\|_2/\lambda_{\min}(B)\), with relative error amplified by \(\kappa_2(B)\).

notation.meaning: spectral condition number of the reduced matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Residual and Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Test for accepting reduced curvature without conditioning repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric reduced curvature \(B\) and prescribed \(0<\delta\le\Delta<\infty\), accept \(B\) as uniformly positive and adequately conditioned only when certified bounds give \[\delta I\preceq B\preceq\Delta I.\] Then \(\|B^{-1}\|_2\le1/\delta\), \(\|B\|_2\le\Delta\), and \(\kappa_2(B)\le\Delta/\delta\). Failure triggers the designated repair, scaling, regularization, or fallback.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided certified spectral bounds are the canonical acceptance test for well-conditioned reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance implies \(B\succ0\), \(\|B^{-1}\|_2\le1/\delta\), and \(\kappa_2(B)\le\Delta/\delta\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral clipping of reduced curvature to impose a prescribed condition-number bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the symmetric reduced Hessian have decomposition \(H_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\). Choose constants \(0<\delta_k\le\Delta_k\), define \(\widehat\lambda_{k,i}=\min\{\Delta_k,\max\{\lambda_{k,i},\delta_k\}\}\), and set \[B_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\widehat\lambda_{k,i})Q_k^{\mathsf T}.\] Compute \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k\), globalize it, and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\). Then \(B_k\) has no eigenvalue below \(\delta_k\) or above \(\Delta_k\), so its spectral condition number is at most \(\Delta_k/\delta_k\). Stop when the reduced-gradient tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip reduced-Hessian eigenvalues to a positive bounded interval, limiting the linear system's condition number while retaining a feasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_kI\preceq B_k\preceq\Delta_kI\), \(\kappa_2(B_k)\le\Delta_k/\delta_k\), and \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k<0\) for \(g_k\ne0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Reduced-Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-difference approximation of reduced curvature using reduced-gradient samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_j\) denote column \(j\) of a fixed null-space basis \(Z\). At feasible \(x_k\), compute \(g_k=Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\) and, for \(h_k>0\), form columns \[(D_k)_{:j}=\frac{Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k+h_kz_j)-g_k}{h_k}.\] Symmetrize by \(B_k=(D_k+D_k^{\mathsf T})/2\), safeguard \(B_k\) if it is singular or not positive definite, solve \(B_kp_k=-g_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\) with a globalization step length. Stop at the prescribed reduced-gradient tolerance. Every difference sample and iterate remains equality feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate reduced Hessian columns by feasible finite differences of reduced gradients, safeguard the approximation, and solve the resulting reduced Newton system.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable near all sampled points.
\(Ax_k=b\), \(AZ=0\), and the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\).
\(h_k>0\), and the final safeguarded matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x_k+h_kz_j)=b\), \(Ax_{k+1}=b\), and \(B_kp_k=-Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x_k)\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(y)=f(x_p+Zy)\) be the affine reduced objective. Assume reduced gradients \(g^R(y)=Z^T\nabla f(x_p+Zy)\) can be evaluated, or that function values can be used to approximate them.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic reduced Newton iteration whose required derivative or Hessian information is generated by finite differences rather than exact second derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A discrete reduced-Newton method constructs a finite-difference approximation \(\widetilde H_k^R\) to the Jacobian of the reduced gradient and solves \[\widetilde H_k^Rs_k^R=-\widetilde g_k^R,\qquad d_k=Zs_k^R.\] For coordinate increments \(h_{k,j}\neq0\), a forward-difference reduced Hessian is defined columnwise by \[\widetilde H_k^Re_j=\frac{g^R(y_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-g^R(y_k)}{h_{k,j}}.\] If only objective values are available, \(\widetilde g_k^R\) may itself be formed by finite differences of \(\phi\). Symmetrization, regularization, or a trust-region bound must be stated when the discrete matrix is nonsymmetric, singular, or indefinite. The lifted step remains tangent because it is in \(\operatorname{range}(Z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate the reduced gradient or its Jacobian from finite differences in reduced coordinates, solve the resulting approximate Newton equation, and lift the step through the fixed null-space basis. The derivative approximation is discrete, but feasibility of the lifted direction remains exact in the affine model.
assumptions_latex: The perturbed reduced points \(y_k+h_{k,j}e_j\) lie in the domain of \(\phi\).
Every increment \(h_{k,j}\) is nonzero and is chosen relative to truncation and evaluation errors.
The approximate linear system is solvable or is equipped with an explicit safeguard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method defines a derivative-approximate Newton step \(d_k=Zs_k^R\) satisfying \(Ad_k=0\), without evaluating the exact reduced Hessian.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Directional differences may replace coordinate differences: \(\widetilde H_k^Rv\approx[g^R(y_k+hv)-g^R(y_k)]/h\).
Central differences replace the forward quotient when two perturbed evaluations are permitted.
special_cases_latex: Exact reduced Newton is recovered when \(\widetilde g_k^R=g_k^R\) and \(\widetilde H_k^R=H_k^R\).
Finite-difference Hessian-vector products permit matrix-free reduced Krylov solves.
immediate_consequences_latex: All perturbations occur in the reduced coordinates and therefore correspond to affine-feasible full-space points.
The choice of differencing increments directly affects the computed curvature.
boundary_notes: Finite differences are not quasi-Newton secant updates accumulated across optimization iterations.
The supplied sources separately support finite-difference Newton systems and reduced Newton equations, but do not name this combined affine variant as a canonical family.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Null-Space Quasi-Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced BFGS iteration in a constant null-space coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(Z\) with \(AZ=0\), take feasible \(x_0\), and choose \(B_0\succ0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(g_k=Z^{\mathsf T}
abla f(x_k)\), solve \(B_kp_k=-g_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kZp_k\) using a line search. Define \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\) and \(y_k=Z^{\mathsf T}(
abla f(x_{k+1})-
abla f(x_k))\). If \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), update \[B_{k+1}=B_k- rac{B_ks_ks_k^{\mathsf T}B_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k}+ rac{y_ky_k^{\mathsf T}}{s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k};\] otherwise retain or damp \(B_k\). Stop when \(\lVert g_kVert\) meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a BFGS curvature approximation entirely in fixed null-space coordinates, producing feasible iterates and preserving positive definiteness under the curvature condition.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable, \(Ax_0=b\), and \(AZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax_k=b\) for every \(k\), and an undamped BFGS update satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).

If \(|v_k^{\mathsf T}s_k|\ge r\|v_k\|\|s_k\|\), set \[B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{v_kv_k^{\mathsf T}}{v_k^{\mathsf T}s_k};\] otherwise retain \(B_k\). An accepted update is symmetric and satisfies the reduced secant equation, but need not preserve positive definiteness, so its step requires an indefinite-system or globalization safeguard.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Superlinear Convergence of Reduced BFGS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local BFGS convergence inherited from the fixed reduced objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi(y)=f(x_0+Zy)\). Suppose \(\varphi\in C^2\) near a minimizer \(y_*\), \(\nabla^2\varphi(y_*)\succ0\), and \(\nabla^2\varphi\) is locally Lipschitz. If reduced BFGS iterates converge to \(y_*\), use a Wolfe line search, and eventually accept unit steps, then \[\frac{\|y_{k+1}-y_*\|}{\|y_k-y_*\|}\to0.\] Consequently, \(x_k=x_0+Zy_k\) converges superlinearly to \(x_*=x_0+Zy_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard local BFGS superlinear convergence transfers to a fixed affine null-space problem under its usual hypotheses.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) is fixed, has full column rank, and satisfies \(AZ=0\).
The reduced Hessian at the solution is positive definite and locally Lipschitz.
The iterates converge, Wolfe conditions hold, and unit steps are eventually accepted.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Newton Updating in a Fixed Equality Null Space
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Ax=b\) be fixed, let \(Z\) be a fixed basis of \(\ker(A)\), and let \(\phi(y)=f(x_p+Zy)\). Write \(g_k^R=Z^T\nabla f(x_k)\) and maintain \(B_k^R\in\mathbb R^{(n-r)\times(n-r)}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional affine equality optimization with reduced secant updates; the null-space basis is constant across iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-null-space quasi-Newton method computes \[B_k^Rs_k^R=-g_k^R,\qquad d_k=Zs_k^R,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\] and updates \(B_k^R\) from reduced secant pairs \[s_k=y_{k+1}-y_k,\qquad q_k=g_{k+1}^R-g_k^R,\qquad B_{k+1}^Rs_k=q_k.\] For BFGS, provided \(s_k^Tq_k>0\), \[B_{k+1}^R=B_k^R-\frac{B_k^Rs_ks_k^TB_k^R}{s_k^TB_k^Rs_k}+\frac{q_kq_k^T}{s_k^Tq_k}.\] Because \(Z\) is fixed, reduced gradients at successive iterates belong to the same coordinate space and their ordinary difference is well-defined without transporting bases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a Hessian approximation only in the constant null space of the linear equalities. Compute a reduced quasi-Newton step, lift it to a feasible full-space direction, and update the reduced matrix from changes in reduced coordinates and projected gradients. A fixed basis makes successive reduced secant pairs directly comparable.
assumptions_latex: The equality matrix and selected null-space basis \(Z\) do not change with \(k\).
Reduced gradients are available at successive iterates.
The selected update's denominator and curvature conditions hold, or a stated damping or skipping rule is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained matrix satisfies a reduced secant relation and produces lifted directions in \(\ker(A)\); BFGS preserves positive definiteness when \(B_k^R\succ0\) and \(s_k^Tq_k>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The procedure is ordinary quasi-Newton optimization applied to \(\phi(y)\).
An inverse approximation \(M_k^R\approx(H_k^R)^{-1}\) may be updated instead and used as \(s_k^R=-M_k^Rg_k^R\).
special_cases_latex: With \(Z=I\), the method is unconstrained quasi-Newton optimization.
Damped BFGS modifies \(q_k\) to preserve positive definiteness when curvature is insufficient.
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage scales with the reduced dimension.
All lifted trial steps preserve the fixed linear equalities in exact arithmetic.
boundary_notes: For nonlinear equalities, changing tangent bases require a transport or specially defined secant pair.
SR1 may retain indefinite curvature and does not require the BFGS positivity condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Reduced Conjugate-Direction Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate-gradient iteration for a quadratic objective restricted to a fixed feasible affine space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For a feasible point \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and a matrix \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) whose columns form a basis of \(\ker A\), write \(x=x_0+Zy\), set \(H=Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\) and \(q=Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx_0+c)\), and initialize \(y_0=0\), \(r_0=-(Hy_0+q)\), and \(p_0=r_0\). While \(r_k\ne0\), compute \[\alpha_k=\frac{r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k}{p_k^{\mathsf T}Hp_k},\quad y_{k+1}=y_k+\alpha_kp_k,\quad r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kHp_k,\] and, if \(r_{k+1}\ne0\), compute \[\beta_k=\frac{r_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}r_{k+1}}{r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k},\quad p_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kp_k.\] Output \(x_k=x_0+Zy_k\) when the residual is zero or meets the prescribed tolerance. If \(H\succ0\), exact-arithmetic termination occurs within at most \(n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply conjugate gradients to the positive-definite quadratic obtained by restricting the equality-constrained quadratic objective to fixed null-space coordinates, then map every reduced iterate back to the feasible affine space.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(Ax_0=b\), and the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
Arithmetic is exact for the finite-termination assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(x_k=x_0+Zy_k\) satisfies \(Ax_k=b\), the nonzero search directions are \(H\)-conjugate, and the exact minimizer is reached in at most \(n-m\) iterations in exact arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition-number convergence rate for preconditioned reduced CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_*\) solve \(Hy_*=-q\), and let \(\kappa=\kappa_2(M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2})\). Preconditioned CG satisfies \[\|y_k-y_*\|_H\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k\|y_0-y_*\|_H.\] Hence \(O(\sqrt\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon))\) iterations suffice for relative \(H\)-norm error \(\varepsilon\), subject to the exact-arithmetic cap \(n-m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced PCG has the standard square-root condition-number rate and a nullity-dimensional exact-arithmetic cap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|y_k-y_*\|_H\le2((\sqrt\kappa-1)/(\sqrt\kappa+1))^k\|y_0-y_*\|_H\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of standard minimization guarantees outside positive reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Standard reduced CG requires \(p_k^{\mathsf T}Hp_k>0\) for each nonzero direction. If \(H\) is indefinite, a generated denominator can be nonpositive, and any negative-curvature direction makes the unrestricted reduced quadratic unbounded below. If \(H\succeq0\) is singular, a minimizer exists only when \(q\in\operatorname{range}(H)\); uniqueness and the SPD convergence bound are then lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard reduced CG is a minimization method only under positive-definite reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The standard CG minimization and rate guarantees require \(H\succ0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conjugate-Direction Iteration in a Fixed Feasible Subspace
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Ax=b\), let \(Z\) span \(\ker(A)\), and consider the reduced quadratic model \(m(s)=g_R^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_Rs\), where \(H_R=Z^THZ\) is symmetric positive definite. Optionally let \(M_R\succ0\) be a reduced preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conjugate-gradient or preconditioned conjugate-direction solution of a positive-definite reduced quadratic system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An affine reduced conjugate-direction method applies conjugate gradients to \[H_Rs=-g_R\] in reduced coordinates and lifts every reduced iterate through \(Z\). In the unpreconditioned form, with \(s_0=0\), \(r_0=-g_R-H_Rs_0\), and \(p_0=r_0\), \[\alpha_j=\frac{r_j^Tr_j}{p_j^TH_Rp_j},\quad s_{j+1}=s_j+\alpha_jp_j,\quad r_{j+1}=r_j-\alpha_jH_Rp_j,\] \[\beta_{j+1}=\frac{r_{j+1}^Tr_{j+1}}{r_j^Tr_j},\quad p_{j+1}=r_{j+1}+\beta_{j+1}p_j.\] The full-space displacement is \(d_j=Zs_j\). In the preconditioned form, residuals are mapped by \(M_R^{-1}\), and the search directions are mutually \(H_R\)-conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the positive-definite reduced Newton or quadratic system by conjugate gradients, optionally with a reduced preconditioner, and lift each reduced approximation through the null-space basis. All full-space iterates remain in the fixed affine feasible subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(H_R\) is symmetric positive definite on the reduced space.
For the preconditioned variant, \(M_R\) is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted displacements satisfy \(Ad_j=0\), while the reduced search directions are \(H_R\)-conjugate and solve the reduced system in at most \(n-r\) exact-arithmetic iterations.

The method minimizes the quadratic model over successively expanding reduced Krylov subspaces.

Termination after one iteration gives a scaled reduced steepest-descent step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structure-Preserving Affine Reduction of an Objective
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Ax=b\) be consistent, write \(x=x_p+Zy\), and suppose the objective belongs to a declared structural class, such as linear, quadratic, nonlinear least squares, or block-separable functions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An umbrella definition for fixed-affine reductions that retain exploitable algebraic structure of the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A special objective structure under equalities is a representation \[f(x)=\mathcal F(\mathcal R(x))\quad\text{or}\quad f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(E_ix)\] whose affine reduction \[\phi(y)=f(x_p+Zy)\] remains in a corresponding structured class with explicitly transformed data. For example, \[f(x)=c^Tx\Rightarrow\phi(y)=c^Tx_p+(Z^Tc)^Ty,\] \[f(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx\Rightarrow\nabla^2\phi=Z^THZ,\] and \[f(x)=\tfrac12\|R(x)\|^2\Rightarrow\phi(y)=\tfrac12\|R(x_p+Zy)\|^2.\] For a separable representation, \[\phi(y)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(E_ix_p+E_iZy).\] A method is structure-preserving when it computes reduced models, products, or factorizations from these transformed components rather than treating \(\phi\) as an unstructured black box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterize the affine feasible set and substitute that parameterization into a structured objective. Linear and quadratic objectives remain linear and quadratic; least-squares objectives retain their residual form; and separable objectives retain a sum of transformed component functions. A specialized method uses this reduced structure explicitly.
assumptions_latex: The affine system is consistent and \(Z\) spans its null space.
The objective has an explicitly supplied structural representation.
All component maps are defined at the reduced points under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Affine substitution produces a reduced objective with transformed linear, quadratic, residual, or component data, enabling algorithms specialized to that retained structure.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Structure preservation may be expressed through reduced operators such as \(HZ\), \(J_R(x)Z\), or \(E_iZ\) without forming dense reduced matrices.
special_cases_latex: A linear objective yields a constant reduced gradient.
A quadratic objective yields a constant reduced Hessian.
A linear residual map yields a linearly constrained linear least-squares problem in reduced coordinates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Affine reduction cannot increase the number of optimization variables.
Sparsity or separability may be altered by multiplication with a dense null-space basis.
boundary_notes: This umbrella definition does not assert that every structural advantage survives an arbitrary choice of \(Z\).
The supplied sources discuss the component families, but no single locator was found that states this exact umbrella classification.

notation.meaning: Residual or other structured objective map.

children.title: Linear-Quadratic Objective Family

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Reduction of Linear and Quadratic Objectives
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and assume \(Ax=b\) is consistent. Choose \(Ax_p=b\) and a full-column-rank \(Z\) spanning \(\ker(A)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear or quadratic optimization over a fixed affine equality set; convexity is determined on the null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear-quadratic objective family under affine equalities consists of problems \[\min_x\ q(x)=\tfrac12x^THx+c^Tx+c_0\quad\text{subject to }Ax=b,\] where \(H=H^T\); the linear case is \(H=0\). Under \(x=x_p+Zy\), the reduced problem is \[\min_y\ \widehat q(y)=\tfrac12y^TH_Ry+c_R^Ty+\widehat c_0,\] with \[H_R=Z^THZ,\qquad c_R=Z^T(Hx_p+c),\qquad \widehat c_0=\tfrac12x_p^THx_p+c^Tx_p+c_0.\] Its reduced stationarity equation is \[H_Ry=-c_R.\] For \(H_R\succ0\), this equation has a unique solution and determines the unique minimizer on the affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric quadratic objective subject to fixed linear equalities becomes a lower-dimensional quadratic after substituting a particular feasible point plus a null-space basis. The reduced Hessian is the original Hessian restricted to feasible directions. Linear objectives are the zero-Hessian special case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality-constrained problem is exactly equivalent to the reduced quadratic with data \(H_R\), \(c_R\), and \(\widehat c_0\); positive definiteness of \(H_R\) gives a unique affine-feasible minimizer.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The KKT equations are \(Hx+c-A^T\lambda=0\) and \(Ax=b\).
The null-space stationarity equation is \(Z^T(Hx+c)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(H=0\), the reduced objective is affine and is bounded below only if \(Z^Tc=0\), unless the reduced domain is otherwise restricted.
For \(H_R\succeq0\), the reduced quadratic is convex; uniqueness additionally requires \(H_R\succ0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Only curvature along feasible directions affects affine-constrained convexity.
The reduced system has dimension \(n-\operatorname{rank}(A)\).
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness of \(H\) is sufficient but not necessary for \(H_R\succ0\).
If \(H_R\) has a negative eigenvalue, the unrestricted affine quadratic is unbounded below along the associated feasible direction unless higher-order or domain restrictions intervene.

notation.meaning: Quadratic curvature restricted to the equality null space.
Linear coefficient of the reduced quadratic.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian dual and bounded-case optimality certificate for a linear objective over a nonempty affine equality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\inf_x\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d:Ax=b\},\] with \(L(x,y)=c^{\mathsf T}x+d+y^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\), the dual is \[\sup_y\{d-b^{\mathsf T}y:c+A^{\mathsf T}y=0\}.\] If \(x\) is primal feasible and \(y\) satisfies \(c+A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), then \(c^{\mathsf T}x+d=d-b^{\mathsf T}y\), so every feasible \(x\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier satisfying linear stationarity certifies that the objective is constant and globally minimal on the feasible affine set.
assumptions_latex: The primal equality system is feasible.
The Lagrangian sign convention is \(L=f+y^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax=b\ \land\ c+A^{\mathsf T}y=0\Rightarrow c^{\mathsf T}x+d=d-b^{\mathsf T}y=\inf_{Au=b}(c^{\mathsf T}u+d).

notation.meaning: Dual objective under the stated sign convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2}x_2\) subject to \(x_1=0\). Every \((0,t)\) is feasible, and the feasible sequence \(x^{(k)}=(0,-k)\) satisfies \(f(x^{(k)})=-k\to-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality system \(Ax=b\) is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \[A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine equality system is infeasible exactly when a left-null-space vector is not orthogonal to its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\iff\exists y:\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Equality Infeasibility Certificate
Linear Objectives under Equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete boundedness and optimality classification for an affine equality-constrained linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) subject to \(Ax=b\), and suppose the feasible set is nonempty. Choose a feasible point \(x_0\) and a matrix \(Z\) whose columns span \(\ker A\). If \(Z^{\mathsf T}c=0\), the objective is constant on the feasible affine space, so every feasible point is a global minimizer. If \(Z^{\mathsf T}c\ne0\), the feasible ray \(x(t)=x_0-tZ(Z^{\mathsf T}c)\) satisfies \[c^{\mathsf T}x(t)+d=c^{\mathsf T}x_0+d-t\lVert Z^{\mathsf T}c\rVert^2,\] and the problem is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear objective is constant on the feasible affine space exactly when its reduced gradient vanishes; otherwise the problem is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^{\mathsf T}c=0\) implies every feasible point is optimal, whereas \(Z^{\mathsf T}c\ne0\) implies \(\inf_{Ax=b}(c^{\mathsf T}x+d)=-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Optimality Certificate for an Equality-Constrained Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient global-minimization certificate over a nonempty affine equality set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(x_*\) satisfy \(Ax_*=b\). Then \(x_*\) globally minimizes \(f\) over \(\{x:Ax=b\}\) if and only if there is a multiplier \(\lambda_*\) such that \(Qx_*+c+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda_*=0\) and \(v^{\mathsf T}Qv\ge0\) for every \(v\in\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point globally minimizes the quadratic exactly when multiplier stationarity holds and curvature is nonnegative along every feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}f(x)\iff\left(\exists\lambda_*:Qx_*+c+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda_*=0\right)\land\left(v^{\mathsf T}Qv\ge0\ \forall v\in\ker A\right).

Quadratic Objectives under Equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness conditions expressed through the quadratic restricted to feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\) and the feasible set is nonempty. For feasible \(x_0\) and null-space basis \(Z\), define \(H=Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\) and \(q=Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx_0+c)\). If \(H\succeq0\), a minimizer exists exactly when \(q\in\operatorname{range}(H)\); its reduced coordinates solve \(Hy=-q\). The minimizer is unique exactly when \(H\succ0\). If \(H\) has a negative eigenvalue, the objective is unbounded below along a feasible direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-constrained quadratic optimization is governed by the reduced Hessian: semidefiniteness and a range condition give existence, while positive definiteness gives uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax_0=b\), and the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(H\succeq0\), minimizers exist if and only if \(q\in\operatorname{range}(H)\), and uniqueness holds if and only if \(H\succ0\); if \(H\not\succeq0\), the infimum is \(-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Linear Objective Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space-coordinate representation of a linear objective on an affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0\) satisfy \(Ax_0=b\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Every feasible point has a unique representation \(x=x_0+Zy\) when \(Z\) has linearly independent columns. For the linear objective \(f(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), restriction to the feasible affine space gives \[\phi(y)=f(x_0+Zy)=c^{\mathsf T}x_0+d+(Z^{\mathsf T}c)^{\mathsf T}y.\] Thus the reduced objective remains linear, its reduced gradient is the constant vector \(Z^{\mathsf T}c\), and its reduced Hessian is the zero matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting a null-space parameterization into a linear objective produces another linear objective whose coefficient is the projected vector.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) are linearly independent and span \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_0+Zy)=c^{\mathsf T}x_0+d+(Z^{\mathsf T}c)^{\mathsf T}y\), with \(\nabla\phi(y)=Z^{\mathsf T}c\) and \(\nabla^2\phi(y)=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Quadratic Objective Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space-coordinate representation of a quadratic objective on an affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), let \(x_0\) satisfy \(Ax_0=b\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Under the feasible parameterization \(x=x_0+Zy\), the quadratic objective \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+d\) becomes \[\phi(y)=\tfrac12y^{\mathsf T}(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ)y+\bigl(Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx_0+c)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}y+f(x_0).\] Consequently, \(\nabla\phi(y)=Z^{\mathsf T}QZy+Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx_0+c)\) and \(\nabla^2\phi(y)=Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a quadratic objective to null-space coordinates yields a quadratic whose Hessian and linear term are the corresponding reduced projections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced Hessian is \(Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\), and the reduced linear coefficient at \(y=0\) is \(Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx_0+c)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of reduced coefficients under a change of feasible origin with a fixed null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=Z^{\mathsf T}QZ\) and \(q_0=Z^{\mathsf T}(Qx_0+c)\). If \(x_1=x_0+Zs\) is another feasible origin, then the reduced objective based at \(x_1\) has Hessian \(H\), linear coefficient \(q_1=q_0+Hs\), and satisfies \(\phi_1(y)=\phi_0(s+y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the feasible origin translates reduced coordinates, leaves the reduced Hessian unchanged, and shifts the reduced linear coefficient by the Hessian times the translation.

children.title: Least-Squares-Separable Objective Family
children.top_down_role: Affine equality reductions preserving residual or block-separable structure.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x=x_p+Zy\) parameterize \(Ax=b\). Let residual blocks \(R_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{p_i}\) and component functions \(f_i\) be defined on the affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine reductions that preserve residual sums of squares or an explicit sum of component objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The least-squares-separable objective family consists of objectives of either or both forms \[f(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^q\|R_i(x)\|^2\] and \[f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(E_ix),\] subject to \(Ax=b\). Affine reduction defines \[\widehat R_i(y)=R_i(x_p+Zy),\qquad \phi(y)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^q\|\widehat R_i(y)\|^2,\] or \[\widehat f_i(y)=f_i(E_ix_p+E_iZy),\qquad \phi(y)=\sum_{i=1}^q\widehat f_i(y).\] For differentiable residuals, \[\nabla\phi(y)=\sum_i(J_i(x)Z)^TR_i(x),\] and the Gauss–Newton matrix is \[G_R(y)=\sum_i(J_i(x)Z)^T(J_i(x)Z),\qquad x=x_p+Zy.\] Thus the residual blocks or separable terms remain individually identifiable after reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute the affine null-space parameterization into each residual block or separable component. The reduced objective remains a sum of squares or a sum of component functions. Reduced residual Jacobians are the original Jacobians multiplied by the null-space basis, and their Gram matrix defines the reduced Gauss–Newton model.
assumptions_latex: The equality system is consistent and \(Z\) spans its null space.
Every residual or component function is defined at \(x_p+Zy\).
The Jacobians displayed exist when derivative formulas are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Affine reduction preserves the explicit sum-of-squares or component-sum representation, with reduced residual Jacobians \(J_i(x)Z\) and reduced component maps \(E_iZ\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Stacking residuals as \(R=(R_1^T,\ldots,R_q^T)^T\) gives \(G_R=(J_RZ)^T(J_RZ)\).
Weighted least squares is obtained by replacing each norm with \(\|W_i^{1/2}R_i(x)\|^2\) for \(W_i\succeq0\).
special_cases_latex: If every \(R_i\) is affine, the reduced problem is linear least squares.
If each \(E_i\) selects a disjoint variable block, a dense \(Z\) may couple the reduced blocks even though the component sum remains explicit.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced Gauss–Newton matrix is positive semidefinite.
Residual evaluation can remain blockwise after equality elimination.
boundary_notes: Affine reduction preserves the algebraic sum but may destroy sparsity or block independence.
General robust losses are separable residual objectives but are not ordinary least squares unless the loss is quadratic.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Objectives under Equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear equalities are eliminated through a null-space parameterization of a nonlinear least-squares objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), where \(A\) has full row rank. Let \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(Ax_p=b\), and choose \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) such that \(AZ=0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)=n-m\). The equality-constrained least-squares problem is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\] and its reduced form is \[\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}}\tfrac12\lVert r(x_p+Zz)\rVert_2^2.\] The map \(z\mapsto x_p+Zz\) is a bijection from \(\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\) onto \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\), and corresponding points have identical objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full null-space parameterization converts equality-constrained nonlinear least squares into an unconstrained least-squares problem in reduced coordinates while preserving all feasible points and their objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(r\) is defined at every parameterized point under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{\substack{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\\Ax=b}}\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2=\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}}\tfrac12\lVert r(x_p+Zz)\rVert_2^2.\]

A basis matrix for the null space of A.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality certificate for an equality-feasible zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2\) subject to \(Ax=b\), any \(\bar x\) satisfying \(A\bar x=b\) and \(r(\bar x)=0\) is a global minimizer with value zero. Conversely, an attained feasible optimum has value zero only if its residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-feasible exact fit certifies global optimality with value zero, and every attained zero optimum is an exact fit.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean least-squares objective is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\bar x=b\ \land\ r(\bar x)=0\iff A\bar x=b\ \land\ F(\bar x)=\min_{Ax=b}F=0.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Objectives under Equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additively separable objectives are restricted to an affine feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\), where \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), and let \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to\mathbb{R}\). For \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), the equality-constrained objective is additively separable with respect to this partition when the problem has the form \[\min_{x_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i},\ i=1,\ldots,p}\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^p A_i x_i=b.\] Each objective term depends only on its own block, although the equality may couple different blocks. If \(x=x^0+Zz\), with \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\), parameterizes the feasible set and \(Z_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times d}\) is the row block of \(Z\) associated with \(x_i\), then the reduced objective is \[\phi(z)=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i^0+Z_i z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained objective is additively separable when it is a sum of block-local functions, even though the equalities may couple the blocks. A feasible elimination can make each block depend on several reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\phi(z)=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i^0+Z_i z),\qquad z\in\mathbb{R}^d.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Residual Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residuals and their Jacobians are composed with the affine null-space chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^q\), \(x_p\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\), and define the feasible affine parameterization \(x(z)=x_p+Zz\) for \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Define the reduced residual by \(\rho:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^q\), \(\rho(z)=r(x(z))\). The reduced least-squares objective is \(\phi(z)=\tfrac12\lVert\rho(z)\rVert_2^2\). If \(r\) is differentiable at \(x(z)\), then \[J_\rho(z)=J_r(x(z))Z\] and \[\nabla\phi(z)=J_\rho(z)^\mathsf{T}\rho(z)=Z^\mathsf{T}J_r(x(z))^\mathsf{T}r(x(z)).\] Thus the affine reduction preserves the sum-of-squares form and right-multiplies the residual Jacobian by the feasible-direction basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composing a residual mapping with an affine feasible chart preserves the least-squares form. The reduced residual Jacobian equals the original residual Jacobian multiplied by the chart basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[J_\rho(z)=J_r(x(z))Z,\qquad \nabla\phi(z)=J_\rho(z)^\mathsf{T}\rho(z).\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regional criterion for additive separability in fixed reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=I_1	imes\cdots	imes I_d\) be a connected open box and let \(\phi\in C^2(U)\). Then \(\phi\) is additively separable in the displayed reduced coordinates, \[\phi(z)=c+\sum_{j=1}^d h_j(z_j),\] if and only if \[ rac{\partial^2\phi}{\partial z_j\partial z_\ell}(z)=0\qquad(j
e\ell,\ z\in U).\] For \(\phi(z)=\sum_i f_i(x_i^0+Z_i z)\), this condition is equivalently \[\sum_i e_j^{\mathsf T}Z_i^{\mathsf T}
abla^2f_i(x_i^0+Z_i z)Z_i e_\ell=0\qquad(j
e\ell,\ z\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a connected product region, reduced-coordinate separability is equivalent to the vanishing of every mixed second derivative, including all cancellations among block contributions.

For the block formula, every \(f_i\) is twice continuously differentiable on the relevant image.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupling Pattern Alone Does Not Decide Reduced Separability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation and destruction examples sharing the same null-space support pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[0\ 0\ 1]\), \(b=0\), and \[Z=2^{-1/2}\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\\0&0\end{bmatrix},\] so \(AZ=0\). For \(f(x)=\tfrac12(x_1^2+x_2^2)\), both active rows of \(Z\) involve both reduced coordinates, yet \(f(Zz)=\tfrac12(z_1^2+z_2^2)\) is separable. With the same equality and basis but \(f(x)=\tfrac12x_1^2\), \(f(Zz)=\tfrac14(z_1+z_2)^2\), which is not separable in \((z_1,z_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support pattern of the elimination basis neither guarantees nor precludes reduced separability; curvature and cancellation decide the result.
assumptions_latex: Separability is assessed in the displayed reduced coordinates.
Both examples use the same affine equality and null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same support pattern in \(Z\) can produce either a diagonal or a nondiagonal reduced Hessian.

notation.meaning: Null-space basis shared by both examples.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Pattern Alone Does Not Decide Reduced Separability
Reduced Separability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A null-space basis can introduce cross-coordinate dependence into an originally separable objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i)\) and \(x_i=x_{p,i}+Z_i z.\) Even when every \(f_i\) is block-local, \(\phi(z)=\sum_i f_i(x_{p,i}+Z_i z)\) is generally not separable by individual reduced coordinates. If the \(f_i\) are twice differentiable, then
\[\nabla^2\phi(z)=\sum_{i=1}^p Z_i^\mathsf{T}\nabla^2 f_i(x_i)Z_i.\]
Reduced-coordinate separability requires all cross-coordinate entries of this matrix to vanish throughout the region. It fails whenever some term has nonzero curvature and two reduced coordinates occur jointly in the corresponding rows of \(Z_i\), producing a nonzero cross entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination generally destroys coordinate separability because a single original block may depend on several reduced variables, creating cross terms in the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\) is coordinate-separable only if \(\sum_i Z_i^\mathsf{T}\nabla^2 f_i(x_i)Z_i\) has zero cross-coordinate entries throughout the region.

notation.meaning: Rows of the null-space basis associated with block i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, and the Hessian formula is standard. However, nonzero block curvature together with two reduced coordinates appearing in a block does not by itself guarantee a nonzero reduced cross entry: directional products can vanish and contributions from different blocks can cancel. An authoritative source and a corrected necessary or sufficient boundary statement are required.

children.title: Nonlinear Reduced-Space Methods
children.top_down_role: Feasibility-preserving methods for nonlinear equalities based on local elimination, reduced gradients, and projected feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Reduced-Space Method for Nonlinear Equalities
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(m<n\). At feasible \(x_k\), let \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\) have full row rank, and let \(Z_k\) span \(\ker(A_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth nonlinear equality reduction under full-rank constraint Jacobians; feasibility is maintained by nonlinear correction or elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear reduced-space algorithm chooses a reduced direction \(p_k\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\), forms the tangent predictor \[d_k^T=Z_kp_k,\qquad A_kd_k^T=0,\] and applies a nonlinear correction \(d_k^N(\alpha)\) so that the feasible arc \[x_k(\alpha)=x_k+\alpha d_k^T+d_k^N(\alpha)\] satisfies \[c(x_k(\alpha))=0.\] The reduced gradient is \[g_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k).\] A reduced-gradient member takes \(p_k=-g_k^R\); a second-order member solves \[Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_kp_k=-g_k^R,\] possibly with modified curvature. The correction may be computed by local elimination or Newton iterations in a complementary range-space basis. A line search selects \(\alpha\) along the feasible arc.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, compute a search direction in the tangent null space of the nonlinear constraint Jacobian. Correct the tangent predictor in a complementary direction until the nonlinear equalities are restored, producing a feasible arc. Choose the reduced direction from projected first-order or reduced second-order information and globalize along that arc.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) possess the derivatives required by the chosen first- or second-order reduced model.
The local correction or elimination equation has a solution for the trial step sizes considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted iterate lies on \(c(x)=0\); its initial arc tangent is \(Z_kp_k\), and stationarity in reduced coordinates is measured by \(Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Local variable elimination expresses dependent variables as smooth functions of \(n-m\) free variables.
A feasible-direction representation uses a tangent predictor followed by a range-space projection back to the constraint manifold.
special_cases_latex: For linear \(c(x)=Ax-b\), the nonlinear correction is zero and \(Z_k\) is constant.
Choosing \(p_k=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\) gives projected reduced steepest descent.
immediate_consequences_latex: The tangent basis and reduced curvature generally change with the iterate.
Exact correction separates nonlinear feasibility from tangential objective reduction.
boundary_notes: Full-rank failure invalidates the local smooth elimination model.
The inner feasibility correction need not converge for arbitrarily large predictor steps.
Methods that permit infeasible accepted iterates belong to a broader class than this feasibility-preserving definition.

notation.meaning: Equality Jacobian at the current feasible iterate.
Tangential predictor and nonlinear feasibility correction.
Lagrangian for the nonlinear equality problem.

children.title: Implicit-Function Reduction Principle
children.top_down_role: Local replacement of regular nonlinear equalities by independent reduced coordinates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:U\to\mathbb R^m\), with \(m<n\), be continuously differentiable. Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\). Write \(x=(x_B,x_N)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R^{n-m}\) after a coordinate permutation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, local reduction at a feasible point satisfying full row rank; it does not assert a global parameterization of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible point \(\bar x=(\bar x_B,\bar x_N)\), an implicit-function reduction is a choice of coordinate partition for which \(B(\bar x):=D_{x_B}c(\bar x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular, together with neighborhoods \(V_N\) of \(\bar x_N\), \(V_B\) of \(\bar x_B\), and a \(C^1\) map \(\phi:V_N\to V_B\) such that \(\phi(\bar x_N)=\bar x_B\) and \[c(\phi(z),z)=0\quad\text{for every }z\in V_N.\] Moreover, every \((y,z)\in V_B\times V_N\) satisfying \(c(y,z)=0\) obeys \(y=\phi(z)\). Thus \(z\mapsto(\phi(z),z)\) is a local feasible coordinate chart, and its derivative is \[D\phi(z)=-D_{x_B}c(\phi(z),z)^{-1}D_{x_N}c(\phi(z),z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular feasible point admits a local elimination of \(m\) dependent coordinates. Choose coordinates \(x_B\) so that their constraint Jacobian \(B(\bar x)\) is invertible. Then, near \(\bar x\), there is a unique continuously differentiable function \(x_B=\phi(x_N)\) whose graph is exactly the nearby feasible set. Its derivative is \(D\phi=-B^{-1}D_{x_N}c\), so variations of the free coordinates induce tangent feasible variations of all variables.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
\(\operatorname{rank}Dc(\bar x)=m\), and the selected square block \(D_{x_B}c(\bar x)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in V_B\times V_N:c(x)=0\}=\{(\phi(z),z):z\in V_N\}\), with \(D\phi(z)=-D_{x_B}c(\phi(z),z)^{-1}D_{x_N}c(\phi(z),z)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The map \(z\mapsto(\phi(z),z)\) is a local chart of the regular level set \(c^{-1}(0)\), whose tangent image equals \(\ker Dc(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints \(c(x)=Bx_B+Nx_N-b\) with nonsingular \(B\), the elimination is global and affine: \(\phi(z)=B^{-1}(b-Nz)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The equality-constrained problem is locally equivalent to the unconstrained reduced problem \(\min_{z\in V_N} f(\phi(z),z)\).
boundary_notes: The construction is local and can fail when the selected block becomes singular, even if another coordinate block remains usable.
If \(Dc(\bar x)\) is rank deficient, this regular implicit-function reduction is not available without removing redundant constraints or adopting a different local model.

children.title: Elimination Variable Partition Pair
children.top_down_role: Coordinate partitions supporting local nonlinear elimination.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x\) be feasible, and set \(A(x)=Dc(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), where \(m<n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-based local nonlinear elimination under full row rank; bounds and inequality-working-set changes are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An elimination variable partition pair at \(x\) is an ordered pair \((B,N)\) of disjoint index sets satisfying \(B\cup N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(|B|=m\), and \(|N|=n-m\), such that the column partition \[A(x)=[A_B(x)\;A_N(x)]\] has a nonsingular basis block \(A_B(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\). The variables \(x_B\) are dependent and \(x_N\) are independent. The associated coordinate null-space matrix and reduced gradient are \[Z_{B,N}(x)=\begin{pmatrix}-A_B(x)^{-1}A_N(x)\\ I_{n-m}\end{pmatrix},\qquad g_R(x)=Z_{B,N}(x)^T\nabla f(x),\] after ordering coordinates as \((x_B,x_N)\). Hence \(A(x)Z_{B,N}(x)=0\), and each reduced displacement \(p_N\) induces the tangent displacement \(p=Z_{B,N}(x)p_N\), with \(p_B=-A_B(x)^{-1}A_N(x)p_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elimination partition divides the coordinates into exactly \(m\) dependent variables and \(n-m\) independent variables. It is valid at \(x\) precisely when the constraint-Jacobian columns belonging to the dependent variables form an invertible square matrix \(A_B(x)\). The independent step \(p_N\) then uniquely determines the dependent tangent correction \(p_B=-A_B^{-1}A_Np_N\), and the corresponding reduced gradient is \(Z_{B,N}^T\nabla f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B,N)\) is a valid elimination partition exactly when \(|B|=m\), \(B\dot\cup N=\{1,[0mldots,n\}\), and \(\det A_B(x)\ne0\); it induces \(Z_{B,N}\), \(A Z_{B,N}=0\), and \(g_R=Z_{B,N}^T\nabla f\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Validity is equivalent to the selected dependent-variable differentials being locally solvable as functions of the independent-variable differentials.
special_cases_latex: If \(A_B\) is orthogonal, then the dependent tangent correction uses \(A_B^T\) in place of an explicit inverse.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced dimension is \(n-m\).
The conditioning of \(A_B\) directly influences the conditioning of the coordinate null-space basis.
boundary_notes: A full-row-rank Jacobian may admit many valid pairs; the definition does not prescribe a pivoting or conditioning criterion.
A partition can cease to be valid as \(x\) changes because \(A_B(x)\) may become singular.

notation.meaning: coordinate null-space basis induced by the partition

children.title: Dependent Variable Blocks
children.top_down_role: Coordinates locally determined through the nonlinear equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependent Variable Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependent variables are locally solved from nonlinear equalities as functions of free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(c(y,z)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\to\mathbb{R}^m.\) At a feasible point \((\bar y,\bar z)\), the block \(y\) is a dependent-variable block if \(c_y(\bar y,\bar z)\) is nonsingular. Then, locally, the equalities determine a unique mapping \(y=h(z)\) satisfying \(h(\bar z)=\bar y\) and \(c(h(z),z)=0.\) The dependent block therefore contains exactly as many scalar variables as there are locally independent equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dependent block contains variables locally determined by the equality constraints; its constraint Jacobian block must be square and nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable near \((\bar y,\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a local function \(h\) with \(y=h(z)\) and \(c(h(z),z)=0.\)

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the constraints with respect to y.

children.title: Independent Variable Blocks
children.top_down_role: Free coordinates parameterizing local feasible motion.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Variable Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent variables provide local coordinates on the equality-feasible manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equalities \(c(y,z)=0\) with \(c_y(\bar y,\bar z)\) nonsingular, the block \(z\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\) is the independent-variable block. Its values may vary in a neighborhood of \(\bar z\), while feasibility is restored by setting \(y=h(z)\), where \(c(h(z),z)=0.\) Hence \(z\) supplies local coordinates for the feasible set, and every nearby feasible point in the chart has the unique representation \((h(z),z).\)
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent variables are the free local coordinates; changing them determines the dependent variables through the equality-solving map.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable near a feasible point \((\bar y,\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every sufficiently near feasible point has the unique chart representation \((h(z),z).\)

children.title: Partition Admissibility
children.top_down_role: Rank and conditioning criteria governing valid coordinate partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Admissibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility is the nonsingularity condition required for implicit elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(\bar x\) satisfy \(c(\bar x)=0\), and partition \(x=(y,z)\) with \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m.\) The partition is locally admissible at \(\bar x=(\bar y,\bar z)\) precisely when
\[\det c_y(\bar y,\bar z)\ne0.\]
Equivalently, the columns of \(J_c(\bar x)\) selected for \(y\) form a basis of \(\mathbb{R}^m\). Under this condition the implicit-function reduction \(y=h(z)\) exists and is locally unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable partition is admissible when the constraint Jacobian columns assigned to dependent variables form a nonsingular square matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition is admissible if and only if \(c_y(\bar x)\) is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian block for the proposed dependent variables.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2 Structure of Methods p. 12

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2 Structure of Methods p. 12

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local persistence of the exact selected-minor condition, distinct from numerical conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\in C^1\) near \(\bar x\), and fix a partition \(x=(y,z)\) such that \(c_y(\bar x)\) is nonsingular. Then there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) for which \(c_y(x)\) is nonsingular for every \(x\in U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed admissible dependent-variable selection remains admissible throughout a sufficiently small neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists U\ni\bar x\;\forall x\in U:\det c_y(x)\ne0.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Persistence of an Admissible Partition

children.title: Partition Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of local elimination to the selected dependent-variable block.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaling Dependence of Raw Conditioning Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting singular-value or condition-number thresholds intrinsically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing the equality representation by \(\widetilde c=Sc\) and rescaling dependent coordinates by \(y=D\widetilde y\), with \(S,D\) nonsingular, replaces \(B\) by \(SBD\) without changing the feasible set or exact admissibility. In general, \(\sigma_{\min}(SBD)\) and \(\kappa_2(SBD)\) differ from those of \(B\). Therefore an unscaled absolute threshold is not an invariant partition-quality criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent equation and coordinate scalings preserve admissibility but can change raw singular values and condition numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact admissibility is invariant under \(B\mapsto SBD\), whereas raw spectral conditioning measures generally are not.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Dependence of Raw Conditioning Tests

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditioning and Sensitivity of an Admissible Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm- and scaling-qualified measures of local elimination sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix equation and variable scalings and use the spectral norm. For an admissible partition write \(J_c=[B\;N]\), where \(B=c_y\) is nonsingular. Its linear-solve conditioning is \(\kappa_2(B)=\|B\|_2\|B^{-1}\|_2=\sigma_{\max}(B)/\sigma_{\min}(B)\), while the chart derivative is \(Dh=-B^{-1}N\). Hence \(\|Dh\|_2=\|B^{-1}N\|_2\le \|N\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(B)\). A numerical acceptance bound is meaningful only relative to the fixed scaling and a stated tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block condition numbers govern the dependent solve, while the product of the inverse block with the free block gives the actual first-order chart sensitivity.
assumptions_latex: Equation and coordinate scalings are fixed.
The spectral operator norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(B)=\sigma_{\max}(B)/\sigma_{\min}(B)\) and \(\|Dh\|_2=\|B^{-1}N\|_2\le\|N\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(B).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning and Sensitivity of an Admissible Partition
Partition Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical suitability strengthens nonsingularity by requiring a well-conditioned dependent Jacobian block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an admissible partition \(x=(y,z)\), define its local conditioning by \(\kappa_2(c_y)=\|c_y\|_2\|c_y^{-1}\|_2.\) Given a prescribed tolerance \(\tau>0\), call the partition numerically acceptable when
\[\sigma_{\min}(c_y(\bar x))\ge \tau\quad\text{and hence}\quad \|c_y(\bar x)^{-1}\|_2\le \tau^{-1}.\]
Since \(h'(\bar z)=-c_y(\bar x)^{-1}c_z(\bar x)\), poor conditioning amplifies constraint derivatives and numerical errors in the eliminated variables even though the partition remains mathematically admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A useful partition requires more than nonsingularity: the dependent Jacobian block should have a safely bounded smallest singular value.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean operator norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\min}(c_y)\ge\tau\) bounds \(\|c_y^{-1}\|_2\) and limits amplification in \(h'=-c_y^{-1}c_z.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditioning topic fits the leaf and the inverse-norm identity is correct in the spectral norm. However, an absolute smallest-singular-value threshold is scaling dependent and its interpretation as numerical acceptability is algorithm dependent. A source must specify the scaling convention, threshold policy, and intended stability claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale Dependence of Raw Block Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explains why unscaled singular-value thresholds cannot define an intrinsic partition-quality criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=c_y(\bar x)\) be an admissible dependent block. Replacing the equality representation by \(\tilde c=Sc\), where \(S\) is nonsingular, replaces \(B\) by \(\tilde B=SB\) without changing the feasible set or admissibility. Likewise, rescaling dependent coordinates by \(y=D\tilde y\) replaces the block by \(BD\). Consequently, \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\) and \(\kappa_2(B)\) generally change under equivalent row or coordinate scalings. A numerical acceptance threshold is therefore meaningful only after specifying scaling and a norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent rescalings preserve admissibility but can change singular values and condition numbers, so numerical partition thresholds require a stated scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B,SB,\text{ and }BD\) define equivalent admissible representations but generally have different singular values and condition numbers.

notation.meaning: Nonsingular scaling of the equality equations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale Dependence of Raw Block Conditioning

children.title: Local Reduced-Objective Representation
children.top_down_role: The objective represented within a locally feasible coordinate chart.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Reduced-Objective Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The original objective is pulled back to a locally feasible implicit-function chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable. If \(c(\bar y,\bar z)=0\) and \(c_y(\bar y,\bar z)\) is nonsingular, let \(y=h(z)\) satisfy \(c(h(z),z)=0\) locally. The local reduced objective is
\[\phi(z)=f(h(z),z).\]
Its derivative is \(h'(z)=-c_y(h(z),z)^{-1}c_z(h(z),z)\), and
\[\nabla\phi(z)=f_z(h(z),z)-c_z(h(z),z)^\mathsf{T}c_y(h(z),z)^{-\mathsf{T}}f_y(h(z),z).\]
Local minimizers correspond under the chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Implicit elimination pulls the objective onto free coordinates; its gradient includes the sensitivity of dependent variables required to maintain feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near \((\bar y,\bar z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi=f\circ(h,\operatorname{id})\), with \(\nabla\phi=f_z-c_z^\mathsf{T}c_y^{-\mathsf{T}}f_y.\)

notation.meaning: Local implicit solution for dependent variables.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2 Structure of Methods p. 12

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2 Structure of Methods p. 12

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order pullback formula in an implicit feasible chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\chi(z)=(h(z),z)\) be a \(C^2\) feasible chart, \(Z(z)=D\chi(z)\), and \(\phi=f\circ\chi\). At a chart point choose the unique \(\lambda\) satisfying \(f_y(\chi(z))+c_y(\chi(z))^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\), and set \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). Then
\[\nabla^2\phi(z)=Z(z)^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(\chi(z),\lambda)Z(z).\]
At a constrained stationary point this \(\lambda\) is the KKT multiplier, so the reduced-objective Hessian is the tangent restriction of the Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the chart-consistent multiplier, the Hessian of the reduced objective equals the Lagrangian Hessian restricted to chart tangent coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2\phi(z)=Z(z)^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(\chi(z),\lambda)Z(z).\)
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Objective Hessian as Lagrangian Curvature

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Pulled Back to a Feasible Chart
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(c:U\to\mathbb R^m\), and suppose a local feasible chart is given by \(\chi(z)=(\phi(z),z)\) on an open set \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^{n-m}\), with \(c(\chi(z))=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth, finite-dimensional, local representation associated with a fixed valid elimination chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The local reduced-objective representation induced by \(\chi\) is the scalar function \[\psi:V	o\mathbb R,\qquad \psi(z):=(f\circ\chi)(z)=f(\phi(z),z).\] If \(f\) and \(\chi\) are \(C^1\), its gradient is \[
abla\psi(z)=D\chi(z)^T
abla f(\chi(z))=Z(z)^T
abla f(\chi(z)),\qquad Z(z):=D\chi(z).\] If they are \(C^2\), then \[
abla^2\psi(z)=Z(z)^T
abla_{xx}^2L(\chi(z),\lambda(z))Z(z),\] where \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\) and \(\lambda(z)\) is the multiplier determined by the chart differentiation convention. A point \(z_*\in V\) is a local minimizer of \(\psi\) if and only if \(x_*=[0mchi(z_*)\) is a local minimizer of \(f\) relative to the feasible points contained in the chart image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced objective is the original objective expressed in independent feasible coordinates: \(\psi(z)=f([0mchi(z))\). Its gradient is the original gradient restricted to chart-tangent directions, \(Z(z)^T\nabla f\). Under twice differentiability, its Hessian is the Lagrangian Hessian restricted to those directions. Local minimizers correspond exactly between the reduced domain and the feasible chart image.
assumptions_latex: \(\chi:V\to U\) is one-to-one onto a neighborhood of the feasible set and satisfies \(c(\chi(z))=0\).
For the gradient formula, \(f\) and \(\chi\) are continuously differentiable.
For the Hessian formula, \(f\), \(c\), and \(\chi\) are twice continuously differentiable and the constraint Jacobian has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\psi=f\circ\chi\), \(\nabla\psi=D\chi^T\nabla f\), and local minimizers of \(\psi\) correspond to local feasible minimizers of \(f\) within \(\chi(V)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an elimination chart \(\chi(z)=(\phi(z),z)\), the reduced objective is \(\psi(z)=f(\phi(z),z)\).
special_cases_latex: For affine equalities, \(\chi\) is affine and the chart-curvature terms vanish.
immediate_consequences_latex: First-order stationarity in the chart is \(Z(z)^T\nabla f(\chi(z))=0\).
A positive-definite reduced Hessian yields strict local minimality relative to the chart.
boundary_notes: The representation covers only the feasible component and neighborhood reached by the chosen chart.
Different charts give different coordinate formulas but represent the same intrinsic objective on their overlapping feasible images.

source_refs.locator: Section 7.2, equations (7.2.1)-(7.2.2), and Section 12.5, equations (12.5.5)-(12.5.7)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order pullback formula for the objective in an implicit feasible chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\chi(z)=(h(z),z)\) be a \(C^2\) feasible chart, let \(Z(z)=D\chi(z)\), and define \(\phi=f\circ\chi\). Choose \(\lambda(z)\) so that the dependent components satisfy \(f_y(\chi(z))+c_y(\chi(z))^{\mathsf T}\lambda(z)=0\). Then
\[
abla^2\phi(z)=Z(z)^{\mathsf T}
abla_{xx}^2L(\chi(z),\lambda(z))Z(z)+\sum_{i=1}^n \partial_iL(\chi(z),\lambda(z))\,
abla^2\chi_i(z).\]
At a constrained stationary point, \(
abla_xL=0\), so
\[
abla^2\phi( ar z)=Z( ar z)^{\mathsf T}
abla_{xx}^2L( ar x, ar\lambda)Z( ar z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced-objective Hessian is the pulled-back Lagrangian Hessian plus a chart-curvature term; at stationarity the extra term vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(c\), and the implicit chart \(\chi\) are twice continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At constrained stationarity, \(\nabla^2\phi=Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2LZ\).

children.title: Rank-Aware Chart Transition Calculus
children.top_down_role: Loss of dependent-variable validity and the need for rank-aware partition changes.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be \(C^1\) with \(\operatorname{rank}Dc(x)=m\) on a regular feasible neighborhood. Let \((B,N)\) and \((\widetilde B,\widetilde N)\) be two valid elimination partitions whose feasible charts \(\chi\) and \(\widetilde\chi\) overlap.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local, full-rank chart changes caused by loss of validity or poor conditioning of a selected dependent-variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-aware chart transition at a feasible point \(x\) is the replacement of \((B,N)\) by \((\widetilde B,\widetilde N)\) such that \(A_{\widetilde B}(x)\) is nonsingular and acceptably conditioned when \(A_B(x)\) is singular or rejected by a conditioning threshold. On an overlap, the coordinate transition is \[\tau:=\widetilde\chi^{-1}\circ\chi,\qquad D\tau(z)=\widetilde Z(\tau(z))^{\dagger}Z(z),\] where \(Z=D\chi\), \(\widetilde Z=D\widetilde\chi\), and \(\widetilde Z^{\dagger}\widetilde Z=I\). A reduced covector transforms by \[g_R^{\mathrm{new}}=D\tau(z)^{-T}g_R^{\mathrm{old}},\] while a reduced bilinear model \(M\) transforms by congruence, \[M^{\mathrm{new}}=D\tau(z)^{-T}M^{\mathrm{old}}D\tau(z)^{-1}.\] These rules preserve the represented ambient tangent vector, covector, and quadratic form across the partition change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-aware transition replaces a dependent-variable block that is singular or too ill-conditioned by another nonsingular block. Where the old and new feasible charts overlap, their reduced coordinates are connected by \([0mtau=\widetilde\chi^{-1}\circ\chi\). Reduced directions, gradients, and curvature models are transformed by the Jacobian of \([0mtau\), so the underlying ambient tangent quantities remain unchanged even though their coordinate arrays change.
assumptions_latex: Both selected basis blocks are nonsingular on the chart overlap.
The two charts describe the same local feasible points on their overlap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transition \([0mtau\) is locally invertible, with tangent coordinates related by \(p^{\mathrm{new}}=D\tau\,p^{\mathrm{old}}\), covectors by inverse transpose, and bilinear models by congruence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(Z\) and \(\widetilde Z\) are orthonormal bases of the same tangent space, then \(D\tau=\widetilde Z^TZ\) is orthogonal.
special_cases_latex: A pure permutation of independent coordinates gives a permutation matrix for \(D\tau\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Stationarity is chart invariant: \(g_R^{\mathrm{old}}=0\) if and only if \(g_R^{\mathrm{new}}=0\).
Positive definiteness of a reduced curvature model is preserved by an invertible congruence transformation.
boundary_notes: If the full Jacobian loses row rank, merely changing the dependent-variable block cannot restore a regular \((n-m)\)-dimensional chart.
Copying a reduced Hessian array unchanged across a discontinuous basis change generally represents a different quadratic form.

notation.meaning: coordinate transition between overlapping feasible charts
old and new chart tangent bases
left pseudoinverse for a full-column-rank matrix
