children.title: Local Chart Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Loss of validity or conditioning in a local dependent-variable representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample separating one singular selected minor from full constraint-rank loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2+x_2-1\) at \(\bar x=(0,1)\), \(J_c(\bar x)=[0\;1]\) has full row rank. Choosing \(x_1\) as dependent gives \(c_{x_1}(\bar x)=0\), so that selected chart lacks an implicit-function guarantee. Choosing \(x_2\) as dependent gives \(c_{x_2}(\bar x)=1\) and the valid chart \(x_2=1-x_1^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One dependent-variable choice can fail even though the feasible set is regular and another choice gives a valid chart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Singularity of one selected minor does not imply singularity of the feasible manifold.

notation.meaning: Scalar equality constraint in the example.

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Chart Failure Without Manifold Singularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact and Numerical Modes of Local Chart Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates loss of a fixed implicit-chart guarantee from poor conditioning and full Jacobian rank loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed partition with dependent block \(B=c_y\), the implicit-function guarantee applies only inside its chart neighborhood while \(B\) is nonsingular. If \(\sigma_{\min}(B(x_k))\to0\), then \(\|B(x_k)^{-1}\|_2\to\infty\), so the family loses a uniform inverse bound. This alone does not imply that \(Dh=-B^{-1}c_z\) diverges, that no local functional representation exists by other arguments, or that the full Jacobian loses row rank. At a point where \(B\) is singular, the implicit-function theorem no longer certifies this selected chart; another partition may remain regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near-singularity destroys uniform inverse control, while exact singularity removes the implicit-function guarantee for the selected chart without necessarily making the feasible manifold singular.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable along the considered feasible points.
The same dependent-variable block is tracked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\to0\Rightarrow\|B^{-1}\|_2\to\infty\), but selected-block failure need not imply full Jacobian rank loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact and Numerical Modes of Local Chart Breakdown
Local Chart Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An implicit reduction chart fails when its dependent Jacobian block loses invertibility or leaves its validity neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A chart defined by dependent variables \(y\) and the implicit relation \(y=h(z)\) is guaranteed only while \(c_y(h(z),z)\) remains nonsingular and the chart stays within its implicit-function neighborhood. Breakdown occurs at a limit point \(x_*\) when
\[\sigma_{\min}(c_y(x))\to0\quad\text{as}\quad x\to x_*.\]
Then \(\|c_y(x)^{-1}\|_2\to\infty\), so \(h'(z)=-c_y^{-1}c_z\) may become unbounded, uniqueness of the selected dependent-variable representation may be lost, and reduced derivatives become numerically unreliable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local chart breaks down as its dependent Jacobian approaches singularity, causing unbounded sensitivity and possible loss of a unique feasible representation.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable along the feasible sequence.
The current chart uses \(c_y\) as its dependent Jacobian block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma_{\min}(c_y)\to0\), the current implicit chart loses uniform regularity and may cease to represent nearby feasible points uniquely.

notation.meaning: Limit point at the chart boundary.
Smallest singular value of the dependent Jacobian block.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, and approaching singularity does imply loss of uniform inverse bounds. A source is still required to distinguish failure of the selected coordinate chart from loss of regularity of the feasible manifold itself and to support the stated numerical-reliability consequences.

children.title: Rank-Aware Repartitioning
children.top_down_role: Replacement of coordinate roles in response to rank or conditioning changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection procedure with correctly limited success and failure semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the current point form \(J=J_c(x)\). Use a rank-revealing column factorization to propose an \(m\)-column block \(B\), then verify directly that \(B\) is nonsingular and satisfies any stated scaled conditioning requirement. If the proposed block fails a conditioning requirement, continue the search or report only that this candidate failed; that event does not certify that every block fails. An exhaustive search over all \(\binom{n}{m}\) maximal column subsets gives a finite exact existence or nonexistence certificate, although it is generally impractical.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use rank-revealing factorization to propose a replacement and verify it; failure of one candidate is not global failure, while exhaustive search has exact but combinatorial semantics.
assumptions_latex: Any conditioning test specifies its scaling, norm, and tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted output is a verified admissible block; global nonexistence is certified by \(\operatorname{rank}J<m\) or by exhaustive failure of all maximal minors.
knowledge_statements.title: Verified Rank-Aware Block Replacement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a Replacement Partition Under Full Row Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp algebraic condition for availability of an alternative dependent-variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(m\le n\), there exists an index set \(I\) of \(m\) columns for which \(J_{:,I}\) is nonsingular if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}J=m\). Thus a singular current block can be replaced by some admissible block whenever the full constraint Jacobian retains full row rank; if \(\operatorname{rank}J<m\), no \(m\)-column dependent block is admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full row rank is exactly the condition that some admissible dependent-variable partition exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}J=m\iff\exists I,\ |I|=m:\det J_{:,I}\ne0.\)

notation.meaning: Submatrix formed from the columns indexed by \(I\).

knowledge_statements.title: Existence of a Replacement Partition Under Full Row Rank
Rank-Aware Repartitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A rank-revealing factorization selects a better-conditioned dependent-variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible iterate \(x_k\), constraint Jacobian \(J_k=J_c(x_k)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and threshold \(\tau>0\), compute a column-pivoted rank-revealing factorization \(J_kP=QR\).\) If the estimated numerical rank is \(m\), choose the first \(m\) pivot columns as the new dependent block \(B_k\) and the remaining columns as the independent block. Accept the partition only when \(\sigma_{\min}(B_k)\ge\tau\); otherwise report that no acceptable local chart was found. Re-express the current feasible point in the new partition before computing subsequent reduced derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the constraint Jacobian with column pivoting, choose independent columns as dependent variables, and accept them only if their smallest singular value is adequate.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k\) is available at a feasible iterate.
A rank-revealing column-pivoted factorization is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an accepted partition with \(\sigma_{\min}(B_k)\ge\tau\), or a failure report when none is identified.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the current iterate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but column-pivoted QR and the acceptance threshold define a method-dependent heuristic. Failure of the one block selected by the factorization does not establish that no acceptable block exists unless the search procedure provides that guarantee. A precise sourced algorithm and failure semantics are required.

children.title: Chart Transition Management
children.top_down_role: Continuity and compatibility issues when moving between local coordinate descriptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Transition Between Overlapping Feasible Charts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chart switching that preserves the represented feasible point and transforms reduced derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let regular charts \(\chi_o:U_o\to M\) and \(\chi_n:U_n\to M\) have overlapping images. For \(x=\chi_o(u)\) in the overlap, set \(v=\chi_n^{-1}(x)\) and \(T=\chi_n^{-1}\circ\chi_o\). Then \(\chi_n(v)=x\), the objective value and feasibility are unchanged, and for \(\phi_o=\phi_n\circ T\),
\[\nabla\phi_o(u)=T'(u)^{\mathsf T}\nabla\phi_n(T(u)).\]
A proposed transition is valid only if the new chart is regular at the point and reconstruction gives the same point; numerical tolerances are implementation policies rather than intrinsic mathematical thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switch charts by reconstructing the same feasible point in the new coordinates and transform reduced derivatives through the overlap map.
assumptions_latex: The old and new charts are continuously differentiable diffeomorphisms onto overlapping feasible neighborhoods.
The represented point lies in both chart images.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi_o(u)=\chi_n(T(u))\) and \(\nabla\phi_o=T'^{\mathsf T}\nabla\phi_n\circ T.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Transition Between Overlapping Feasible Charts

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of reduced curvature on a regular chart overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If the charts and \(T\) are \(C^2\), then
\[
abla^2\phi_o(u)=T'(u)^{\mathsf T}
abla^2\phi_n(T(u))T'(u)+\sum_j \partial_j\phi_n(T(u))
abla^2T_j(u).\]
At a reduced stationary point the second term vanishes, so the two reduced Hessians are congruent and have identical inertia.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced Hessians follow the second-order chain rule and are congruent at stationarity, making curvature classification chart-independent.
assumptions_latex: The overlapping charts are twice continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(
abla\phi_n=0\Rightarrow
abla^2\phi_o=T'^{\mathsf T}
abla^2\phi_nT'.\)

notation.meaning: Reduced objectives in the old and new coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Compatibility Across Feasible Charts
Chart Transition Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlapping feasible charts are switched while preserving the represented point and objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let old and new admissible charts be \(\chi_o:U_o\to\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\chi_n:U_n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(\chi_o(u)=(h_o(u),u)\), \(\chi_n(v)=(h_n(v),v)\), and a common feasible point \(x_k\) in both chart images. Initialize \(v_k\) by extracting from \(x_k\) the variables designated independent in the new partition, and verify that \(\chi_n(v_k)=x_k\) to the prescribed feasibility tolerance. On an overlap, define the transition map \(T=\chi_n^{-1}\circ\chi_o\), transfer coordinates by \(v=T(u)\), and transform first derivatives by \[\nabla_u(\phi_n\circ T)(u)=T'(u)^\mathsf{T}\nabla_v\phi_n(T(u)).\] Reject the switch if the new dependent Jacobian fails the prescribed conditioning test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a common feasible point, initialize the new chart from its independent-variable components, verify that it represents the same point, transfer coordinates through the overlap map, apply the chain rule to derivatives, and reject a poorly conditioned chart.
assumptions_latex: \(\chi_o\) and \(\chi_n\) are admissible charts on neighborhoods whose images contain \(x_k\).
The two chart images overlap at \(x_k\).
Feasibility and conditioning tolerances are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted transition satisfies \(\chi_o(u_k)=\chi_n(v_k)=x_k\), preserves objective values and feasibility at the represented point, and transfers first derivatives by the chain rule.

notation.meaning: Old and new feasible chart maps.
Coordinate transition map on the chart overlap.
Coordinates in the old and new charts, respectively.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate compatibility of reduced curvature on an overlap of two regular feasible charts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\chi_o\) and \(\chi_n\) be \(C^2\) feasible charts with transition map \(T=\chi_n^{-1}\circ\chi_o\), and let \(\phi_o=\phi_n\circ T\). Then
\[
abla^2\phi_o(u)=T'(u)^{\mathsf T}
abla^2\phi_n(T(u))T'(u)+\sum_j \partial_j\phi_n(T(u))
abla^2T_j(u).\]
At a stationary point of either reduced representation, the second term vanishes. Hence the two reduced Hessians are congruent and have the same inertia.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across overlapping charts, reduced Hessians obey the second-order chain rule; at stationarity they are congruent and give the same curvature classification.
assumptions_latex: The old and new charts are twice continuously differentiable diffeomorphisms onto overlapping feasible neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At reduced stationarity, \(\nabla^2\phi_o=T'^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2\phi_nT'\), so inertia is chart-independent.

notation.meaning: Transition map from old to new coordinates.
Reduced objectives in the two charts.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Transformation Across Feasible Charts

children.title: Repartitioning Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity limits affecting reliable partition replacement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Perturbation Radius of a Selected Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-norm stability margin for retaining invertibility after repartitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\) be nonsingular. If \(\|B^{-1}E\|_2<1\), then \(B+E\) is nonsingular and
\[\|(B+E)^{-1}\|_2\le\frac{\|B^{-1}\|_2}{1-\|B^{-1}E\|_2}.\]
In particular, \(\|E\|_2<\sigma_{\min}(B)\) guarantees nonsingularity. The radius is sharp in the worst case: some \(E\) with \(\|E\|_2=\sigma_{\min}(B)\) makes \(B+E\) singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturbations smaller than the smallest singular value preserve invertibility, and a worst-case perturbation at that radius can cause singularity.
assumptions_latex: The spectral operator norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|E\|_2<\sigma_{\min}(B)\Rightarrow B+E\text{ is nonsingular}\), with a sharp worst-case boundary.

notation.meaning: Smallest singular value and spectral distance to singularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Perturbation Radius of a Selected Block

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct coupling criterion for stability of a family of replacement partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a family of admissible partitions \(J=[B\;N]\), the chart derivative is \(Dh=-B^{-1}N\). Uniform first-order chart sensitivity is therefore exactly the boundedness of \(\|B^{-1}N\|\). Uniform bounds on \(\|B^{-1}\|\) and \(\|N\|\) are sufficient but not necessary, because cancellation can keep \(B^{-1}N\) bounded even when \(\|B^{-1}\|\) grows. If \(\|N\|\) is bounded and \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\ge\gamma>0\), then \(\|Dh\|\le\|N\|/\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The actual stability quantity is the coupled product of the inverse dependent block with the free block; separate factor bounds are sufficient but not necessary.
assumptions_latex: A fixed compatible operator norm and fixed scaling are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup\|Dh\|<\infty\iff\sup\|B^{-1}N\|<\infty\); separate bounds on \(B^{-1}\) and \(N\) imply this condition.

notation.meaning: Derivative of the dependent-variable chart map.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Chart-Sensitivity Boundary
Repartitioning Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies breakdown of an implicit coordinate chart as its selected dependent-variable Jacobian approaches singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(c(x)=0\), and partition \(x=(y,z)\) so that \(J(x)=\nabla c(x)=[B(x)\;N(x)]\), where \(B(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\). Whenever \(B(x)\) is nonsingular, the local implicit chart satisfies \(D y(z)=-B(x)^{-1}N(x)\) and
\[\|D y(z)\|\leq \frac{\|N(x)\|}{\sigma_{\min}(B(x))}.\]
Thus a family of partitions is uniformly stable only if \(\sigma_{\min}(B(x))\geq\gamma>0\) and \(\|N(x)\|\) remains bounded. The boundary \(\sigma_{\min}(B(x))=0\) is a chart-breakdown boundary: the dependent variables cease to be locally determined by that partition, although another nonsingular partition may remain available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit partition becomes ill-conditioned as its basic Jacobian approaches singularity and breaks down when that Jacobian is singular, even if another partition remains valid.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable near the feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|D y(z)\|\leq \|N(x)\|/\sigma_{\min}(B(x))\), with chart breakdown at \(\sigma_{\min}(B(x))=0\).

notation.meaning: Jacobian block associated with dependent variables
Jacobian block associated with independent variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but no evidence is supplied. Singularity of the selected block invalidates the differentiable implicit-chart guarantee; it does not by itself prove that the dependent variables cease to be locally determined. The asserted necessary condition for uniform stability also requires a specified operator norm and more careful qualification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Perturbation Radius for a Selected Dependent Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-specified stability margin for retaining invertibility after repartitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular and use the spectral norm. If a perturbation \(E\) satisfies \(\|B^{-1}E\|_2<1\), then \(B+E\) is nonsingular and
\[\|(B+E)^{-1}\|_2\le \frac{\|B^{-1}\|_2}{1-\|B^{-1}E\|_2}.\]
In particular, \(\|E\|_2<\sigma_{\min}(B)\) guarantees nonsingularity. This radius is sharp as a normwise worst-case boundary: there exists an \(E\) with \(\|E\|_2=\sigma_{\min}(B)\) for which \(B+E\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected block remains invertible under perturbations smaller than its smallest singular value; at that radius a worst-case perturbation can make it singular.
assumptions_latex: The spectral operator norm is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|E\|_2<\sigma_{\min}(B)\Rightarrow B+E\text{ nonsingular}\), and the worst-case radius is sharp.

notation.meaning: Perturbation of the selected dependent Jacobian block.
Smallest singular value and spectral distance to singularity.

children.title: Generalized Reduced-Gradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Partition-based feasible-direction methods combining reduced descent with dependent-variable correction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f,c\in C^1\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and a feasible iterate \(x_k\) at which \(A_k=Dc(x_k)=[B_k\;N_k]\) has nonsingular \(B_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained GRG with a fixed valid partition during one iteration and exact restoration of feasibility for accepted iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generalized reduced-gradient iteration chooses the coordinate null-space matrix \[Z_k=\begin{pmatrix}-B_k^{-1}N_k\\I\end{pmatrix},\qquad g_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k),\] selects a reduced descent direction \(p_k^R\) satisfying \((g_k^R)^Tp_k^R<0\), and forms a tangent trial displacement \(Z_kp_k^R\). For a trial scalar \(\alpha>0\), the independent variables are displaced according to \(x_{N,k}(\alpha)=x_{N,k}+\alpha p_k^R\), while the dependent variables are determined by a nonlinear correction so that \[c(x_{B,k}(\alpha),x_{N,k}(\alpha))=0.\] An accepted step satisfies both feasibility and a prescribed sufficient-decrease condition for \(f\). The resulting curve \(x_k(\alpha)\) is a feasible arc with \(x_k(0)=x_k\) and \(x_k'(0)=Z_kp_k^R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A GRG method partitions the variables into dependent and independent blocks. It computes the reduced gradient \(g_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\), takes a descent step in the independent variables, and iteratively adjusts the dependent variables until the nonlinear equalities are restored. A trial is accepted only when it is feasible and sufficiently decreases the objective. Thus the method combines reduced-space descent with dependent-variable correction along a feasible arc.
assumptions_latex: The nonlinear restoration equations have a solution for the trial step under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate \(x_{k+1}=x_k(\alpha_k)\) satisfies \(c(x_{k+1})=0\), decreases \(f\) according to the acceptance rule, and has initial arc tangent \(x_k'(0)=Z_kp_k^R\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: GRG is the variable-reduction form of a reduced-gradient-type method with \(Z_k=(-B_k^{-1}N_k,I)^T\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(p_k^R=-g_k^R\) gives the basic reduced-steepest-gradient variant.
For linear equalities, the dependent correction is affine and no nonlinear restoration iteration is required.
immediate_consequences_latex: The search computation has \(n-m\) reduced degrees of freedom.
The accepted iterates remain on the equality manifold when restoration is solved exactly.
boundary_notes: The tangent trial \(x_k+\alpha Z_kp_k^R\) is generally not feasible for nonlinear constraints.
The restoration subproblem may fail or force a smaller \(\alpha\); feasibility is not guaranteed for arbitrary trial lengths.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Executable acceptance rule for a fixed-partition reduced-gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=Y(z)\) be the current implicit feasible branch, \(\psi(z)=f(Y(z),z)\), and let \(s\) satisfy \(\nabla\psi(z)^\mathsf Ts<0\). Given \(\alpha_0>0\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), choose the first \(\alpha=\alpha_0\beta^j\) for which \(Y(z+\alpha s)\) is defined and \[\psi(z+\alpha s)\leq\psi(z)+\eta\alpha\nabla\psi(z)^\mathsf Ts.\] If \(Y\) and \(\psi\) are continuously differentiable near \(z\), backtracking eventually finds such an \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking accepts the first restorable feasible trial satisfying Armijo decrease along the current implicit branch.
assumptions_latex: The fixed partition defines a continuously differentiable implicit map \(Y\) near \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backtracking terminates locally and returns a feasible point with strict objective decrease.

notation.meaning: Dependent-variable map on the current feasible branch.
Objective reduced to the free variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Curve Armijo Line Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outcome when a trial leaves the domain of the current implicit feasible chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed dependent-variable block \(B=\nabla_yc\), local feasibility restoration is guaranteed only while \(B\) remains nonsingular and the trial free variable stays in the domain of the same implicit branch. A failed dependent-variable solve invalidates that trial and requires step reduction. If restoration fails for all sufficiently small trials, or \(B\) is singular at the current point, the fixed-partition method has no local chart guarantee and must terminate or invoke a repartitioning method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failed restoration rejects the trial; singularity of the fixed basic block is the boundary of the fixed-partition method.
assumptions_latex: Feasibility is restored by solving \(c(y,z)=0\) for a fixed dependent-variable block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent local restoration failure or singularity of \(B\) invalidates the fixed partition.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian with respect to the fixed dependent variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Partition Restoration Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between a free-coordinate direction and its lifted tangent directional derivative under a fixed partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=[B\;N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular, partition \(\nabla f=(f_y,f_z)\), and define \(r=f_z-N^{\mathsf T}B^{-\mathsf T}f_y\). For any free-coordinate direction \(s\), set \(d=(-B^{-1}Ns,s)\). Then \[Jd=0,\qquad \nabla f^{\mathsf T}d=r^{\mathsf T}s.\] Hence \(r^{\mathsf T}s<0\) gives a strict first-order feasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced directional derivative equals the full objective derivative along the lifted tangent direction.
assumptions_latex: The objective gradient is partitioned conformably.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Jd=0\) and \(\nabla f^{\mathsf T}d=r^{\mathsf T}s\).

notation.meaning: Full-space tangent lift of the reduced direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Gradient Descent Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical first-order direction choice inside a valid fixed implicit chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With fixed-partition reduced gradient \(r\), choose \(s=-r\) and lift it to \(d=(B^{-1}Nr,-r)\), where \(J=[B\;N]\) and \(B\) is nonsingular. Then \(Jd=0\) and \(\nabla f^{\mathsf T}d=-\|r\|^2\). Among all reduced directions with \(\|s\|\le1\), \(s=-r/\|r\|\) minimizes the first-order reduced directional derivative when \(r\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative reduced gradient is the steepest Euclidean descent direction in the current free coordinates and lifts to a tangent descent direction.
assumptions_latex: Reduced coordinates use the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Jd=0,\qquad \nabla f^{\mathsf T}d=-\|r\|^2.

notation.meaning: Full-space tangent lift of the negative reduced gradient.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\) be feasible for \(c(x)=0\), let \(A_k=Dc(x_k)\) have full row rank, and let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) be the coordinate basis induced by a valid elimination partition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order, deterministic, smooth equality-constrained descent in explicit local reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A basic reduced-gradient method is a GRG method whose reduced search direction is the negative reduced gradient, \[p_k^R=-g_k^R=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k).\] Its ambient tangent direction is therefore \[d_k=Z_kp_k^R=-Z_kZ_k^T\nabla f(x_k),\qquad A_kd_k=0.\] For each trial \(\alpha>0\), the method changes the independent coordinates by \(\alpha p_k^R\), restores the dependent coordinates to obtain a feasible point \(x_k(\alpha)\), and accepts a step satisfying a sufficient-decrease condition. If \(Z_k\) has orthonormal columns, then \(Z_kZ_k^T\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A_k\); otherwise the direction is steepest only in the chosen reduced-coordinate metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basic reduced-gradient method uses the negative reduced gradient \(-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\) as its reduced direction. The corresponding ambient direction \(-Z_kZ_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\) is tangent to the equality manifold. After moving the independent variables, the dependent variables are corrected to restore feasibility, and a sufficiently decreasing feasible trial is accepted. Orthogonal \(Z_k\) gives intrinsic Euclidean projected steepest descent; a coordinate elimination basis gives steepest descent in its reduced coordinates.

abla f(x_k)\), and \(

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-gradient algorithm for linear equality constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed-null-space quasi-Newton procedure for minimizing a twice-differentiable objective subject to full-row-rank linear equalities; the extract states no convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min F(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), choose a feasible \(x_0\), set \(\lambda_0=0\), choose \(B_0\succ0\), and choose basis matrices \(Y\) and \(Z\) for \(\mathcal R(A^T)\) and \(\mathcal N(A)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), set \(g_k=\nabla F(x_k)\); solve \(Z^TB_kZ\,\bar z=-Z^Tg_k\) and set \(p_k=Z\bar z\); solve \(Y^TA^T\lambda_{k+1}=Y^Tg_k+Y^TB_kp_k\); choose a line-search step \(s>0\) such that \(x_{k+1}=x_k+sp_k\) and \(F(x_{k+1})<F(x_k)\); and obtain \(B_{k+1}\) by a quasi-Newton update. Terminate when \(\lVert Z^Tg_k\rVert\) is below the specified tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible point, solve a reduced quasi-Newton system in null-space coordinates, recover a multiplier estimate through the range-space equations, take a decreasing line-search step, update the Hessian approximation, and stop when the reduced-gradient norm is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: Z^TB_kZ\text{ is nonsingular and the stated line search and update are well defined at each executed iteration}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k=Z\bar z,\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+sp_k,\quad F(x_{k+1})<F(x_k),\quad \text{terminate when }\lVert Z^T\nabla F(x_k)\rVert<\varepsilon.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic reduced-gradient iteration for linear equalities and nonnegative variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible reduced-gradient iteration with a nonsingular basic partition, bound-aware reduced direction, exact feasible line search, basis exchange, and a direction-norm stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(x\ge 0\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable, \(A=[B\ C]\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(m\le n\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. Partition \(x=(x^B,x^N)\), eliminate \(x^B=B^{-1}b-B^{-1}Cx^N\), and compute \(r=\nabla_{x^N}f-(B^{-1}C)^T\nabla_{x^B}f\). At a feasible iterate having \(x^B>0\), define \(z_i^N=0\) if \(x_i^N=0\) and \(r_i>0\), and \(z_i^N=-r_i\) otherwise, then set \(z^B=-B^{-1}Cz^N\). Choose \(\alpha^*\) to minimize \(f(x+\alpha z)\) over \(0\le\alpha\le\min\{\bar\alpha_B,\bar\alpha_N\}\), where \(\bar\alpha_B=\sup\{\alpha:x^B+\alpha z^B\ge0\}\) and \(\bar\alpha_N=\sup\{\alpha:x^N+\alpha z^N\ge0\}\). If \(\alpha^*<\bar\alpha_B\), set \(x^+=x+\alpha^*z\); if the basic-variable limit is attained, exchange a basic variable that reaches zero with a positive nonbasic variable. Stop when \(\|z\|\le\varepsilon\), for a prescribed \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a nonsingular basic block, eliminate the basic variables, and compute the gradient in the resulting independent coordinates. Suppress descent components that would violate an active nonnegativity bound, recover the basic-variable direction so that the equality constraints are preserved, and minimize the objective over the feasible step interval. Exchange the basis when the basic-variable step limit is attained. The stated termination test is that the direction norm does not exceed the prescribed positive tolerance; no convergence guarantee is asserted by the extract.
assumptions_latex: A=[B\ C]\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\quad m\le n
x^B>0\text{ at the current feasible iterate}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Az=0\text{ and the restricted line search gives a feasible accepted update; basis exchange is performed when the basic-variable limit is attained, and }\|z\|\le\varepsilon\text{ is the stopping rule.}

children.title: Changing-Partition Reduced-Gradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Reduced-gradient methods that update dependent-variable selections as geometry changes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-defined handling of partition-dependent state after changing dependent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After replacing \(JQ=[B\;N]\) by \(J\widetilde Q=[\widetilde B\;\widetilde N]\) at the same feasible full-space iterate, recompute all partitioned derivatives and the reduced gradient. Any search direction, scaling, or curvature state defined only in the old free-variable coordinates must either be transformed by a specified nonsingular coordinate-change map or discarded and reinitialized. Restarting such state leaves the primal iterate and its feasibility unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After switching partitions, recompute reduced quantities and restart any state lacking an explicit coordinate transformation.
assumptions_latex: Both old and new basic blocks are nonsingular at the same feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recomputation and restart produce valid new reduced state without changing the feasible primal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Restart after Repartitioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence Boundary for a New Basic Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank condition for restoring valid dependent coordinates by repartitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), an \(m\)-column nonsingular submatrix can be selected if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}J=m\). Therefore, if \(J\) loses row rank, no variable permutation can produce a valid dependent-variable block, and repartitioning must report rank failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular dependent block exists exactly when the full constraint Jacobian has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists B\text{ formed from }m\text{ columns of }J:\det B\neq0\iff\operatorname{rank}J=m\).
knowledge_statements.title: Existence Boundary for a New Basic Block

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete exact-arithmetic rule for selecting a new dependent-variable block after repartitioning is triggered.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a full-row-rank Jacobian \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), compute a column-pivoted QR factorization \[J\Pi=Q[\,R_{11}\;R_{12}\,],\] where \(R_{11}\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\). Select as the new dependent variables the first \(m\) columns identified by \(\Pi\), so \(B=Q R_{11}\). In exact arithmetic \(R_{11}\) and \(B\) are nonsingular. In finite precision, accept the block only if a prescribed rank or reciprocal-condition test passes; otherwise report that this selection did not produce an admissible block and try another rank-revealing selection or terminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column-pivoted QR supplies a concrete replacement block; a numerical rank or conditioning test decides whether it is usable.
assumptions_latex: A column-pivoted QR factorization is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det R_{11}\ne0\) and \(\det B\ne0\) in exact arithmetic; finite-precision acceptance is conditional on the stated stability test.

notation.meaning: Column permutation produced by rank-revealing pivoting.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Replacement-Block Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covariance of Reduced Gradients under Repartitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation law for valid changes of dependent-variable partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T,\widetilde T\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) be full-column-rank tangent-lift matrices generated by two nonsingular partitions of the same full-row-rank Jacobian \(J\). Then \(\operatorname{range}T=\operatorname{range}\widetilde T=\ker J\), so \(\widetilde T=TR\) for some nonsingular \(R\). If \(r=T^{\mathsf T}\nabla f\) and \(\widetilde r=\widetilde T^{\mathsf T}\nabla f\), then \[\widetilde r=R^{\mathsf T}r.\] Thus \(r=0\) if and only if \(\widetilde r=0\), and corresponding reduced directions represent the same full tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing a valid partition applies an invertible coordinate transformation and preserves the tangent space and reduced stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Both partitions select nonsingular basic blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde T=TR\) and \(\widetilde r=R^{\mathsf T}r\) for some nonsingular \(R\).

notation.meaning: Reduced gradients in the two partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Covariance of Reduced Gradients under Repartitioning
Changing-Partition Reduced-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-gradient iteration with rank-aware reselection of dependent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible iterate \(x_k\), choose a permutation \(Q_k\) such that \(J_kQ_k=[B_k\;N_k]\) and \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) satisfies \(\sigma_{\min}(B_k)\geq\gamma_k>0\). In the associated coordinates \((y,z)\), compute
\[r_k=f_{z,k}-N_k^{\mathsf T}B_k^{-\mathsf T}f_{y,k}.\]
Take a reduced descent step in \(z\), then restore \(c(x)=0\) by solving for \(y\). Before the next step, retain the partition if its conditioning test passes; otherwise select a new admissible \(Q_{k+1}\), transform the iterate and any reduced state to the new coordinates, and recompute the reduced gradient. Stop on reduced-stationarity and feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method monitors the current basic Jacobian and changes dependent variables when conditioning deteriorates, then recomputes all partition-dependent reduced quantities.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)\) has full row rank at accepted iterates.
Each accepted partition has a nonsingular basic block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm maintains a valid local reduced coordinate system whenever an admissible partition is found.

notation.meaning: variable permutation defining the current partition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced Gradient with Dynamic Elimination Bases
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider smooth equality-constrained optimization with feasible iterates \(x_k\), full-row-rank Jacobians \(A_k=Dc(x_k)\), and iteration-dependent partitions \((B_k,N_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order reduced-gradient methods that may change the dependent-variable selection between iterations to retain rank and numerical stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A changing-partition reduced-gradient method is a GRG method in which each iteration selects an elimination pair \((B_k,N_k)\) satisfying \[\det A_{B_k}(x_k)\ne0,\qquad Z_k=\begin{pmatrix}-A_{B_k}(x_k)^{-1}A_{N_k}(x_k)\\I\end{pmatrix},\] and may replace it by \((B_{k+1},N_{k+1})\) when the current block is singular, inadequately conditioned, or fails a prescribed pivot-quality test. The method computes \(g_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\), chooses a reduced descent direction, restores feasibility using the current dependent block, and transports any retained reduced vector or matrix to the new basis before reuse. If \(Z_k\) and \(Z_{k+1}\) span the same tangent space at a transition point, the coordinate-change matrix \(T_k\) satisfies \(Z_k=Z_{k+1}T_k\); reduced covectors and quadratic models are transformed by \(g_R^{k+1}=T_k^Tg_R^k\) and \(M_{k+1}=T_k^TM_kT_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This method is a reduced-gradient scheme whose dependent and independent variables are allowed to change. At every iterate it chooses an invertible constraint-Jacobian basis, computes descent and feasibility correction with that basis, and changes the partition when rank or conditioning deteriorates. Stored reduced gradients, directions, or curvature models must be converted through the basis-change matrix before they are reused.
assumptions_latex: At least one acceptable nonsingular \(m\)-column block is available whenever a partition change is made.
Feasibility restoration is carried out with the currently selected dependent variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence may use \(Z_k\ne Z_{k+1}\), but every \(Z_k\) satisfies \(A_kZ_k=0\), and retained reduced objects are transformed consistently when their coordinate basis changes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method is GRG with dynamic pivoting of the variable-reduction basis.
special_cases_latex: If one partition remains acceptable for all iterations, the method reduces to a fixed-partition GRG method.
immediate_consequences_latex: Dynamic partitioning can preserve a valid local elimination chart after the original dependent block becomes nearly singular.
boundary_notes: Full Jacobian rank loss cannot be repaired by column exchanges alone.
Changing a partition without transforming a stored reduced Hessian changes the quadratic model represented by its entries.

children.top_down_role: Reduced-gradient implementations emphasizing sparse bases and structured corrections.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of adjoint and tangent solve residuals into reduced-gradient and tangency errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be nonsingular, \(w=B^{-\mathsf T}f_y\), and \(r=f_z-N^\mathsf Tw\). If \(e_a=B^\mathsf T\widehat w-f_y\), then \[\widehat r-r=-N^\mathsf TB^{-\mathsf T}e_a,\qquad \|\widehat r-r\|\leq\|N^\mathsf TB^{-\mathsf T}\|\,\|e_a\|.\] If \(e_t=B\widehat t+Ns\), then \[J(\widehat t,s)=e_t,\qquad \|\widehat t+B^{-1}Ns\|\leq\|B^{-1}\|\,\|e_t\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoint and tangent solve residuals give explicit bounds on reduced-gradient error and linearized infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual-to-error identities and norm bounds hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Solve Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure-dependent work and storage for sparse reduced-gradient evaluation and tangent correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the sparse factors of the selected \(m\times m\) block \(B\) contain \(F\) stored nonzeros and cost \(C_{\mathrm{fac}}(B)\) operations to form. One triangular solve with \(B\) or \(B^\mathsf T\) then costs \(O(F)\). One adjoint solve, one tangent solve, and sparse products with \(N\) cost \(O(F+\operatorname{nnz}(N))\) beyond derivative evaluation when the factors are reused, and \(C_{\mathrm{fac}}(B)+O(F+\operatorname{nnz}(N))\) when refactorization is required; factor storage is \(O(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse reduced-gradient cost is governed by factor fill and sparse products, with factorization cost paid upon refactorization.
assumptions_latex: A sparse direct factorization of \(B\) is used.
One adjoint and one tangent solve are counted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{reuse}}=O(F+\operatorname{nnz}(N)),\quad W_{\mathrm{refactor}}=C_{\mathrm{fac}}(B)+O(F+\operatorname{nnz}(N)),\quad S=O(F).

notation.meaning: Number of stored nonzeros in the sparse factors.
Arithmetic cost of factoring the current basic block.

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Dependent Sparse Iteration Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical outcomes invalidating the current sparse basic-block representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The current sparse basic-block representation is unusable if factorization detects structural or numerical singularity, if a prescribed pivot-growth or inverse-condition estimate fails, or if factor fill exceeds the available work or storage budget. The method must reject that representation and try another admissible partition or solver. If none passes the rank, stability, and resource tests, it must terminate with an explicit factorization or resource-failure status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singularity, numerical instability, or prohibitive fill requires basis replacement or explicit failure.
assumptions_latex: Sparse factors of the selected basic block define the reduced quantities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of a prescribed rank, stability, or resource test forbids accepting a step computed from that representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Basic-Factorization Failure Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Symbolic and Numeric Factorization Reuse Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes safe sparsity-pattern reuse from reuse of obsolete numerical factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If successive basic blocks \(B_k\) have the same sparsity pattern, an ordering and symbolic factorization may be reused. Numerical triangular factors may be reused without changing the defining linear systems only when they still factor the current matrix \(B_k\) to the prescribed backward-error tolerance. Otherwise the current block must be numerically refactorized or handled by a controlled update whose residual passes the solve-accuracy tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stable sparsity pattern permits symbolic reuse, but changed numerical values generally require refactorization or a verified factor update.
assumptions_latex: Sparse direct solves are used for the basic block.
Reuse is judged by a prescribed backward-error tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|B_k-\widehat L_k\widehat U_k\|\text{ above tolerance forbids treating }\widehat L_k\widehat U_k\text{ as current factors}.

notation.meaning: Reused or updated numerical factors proposed for the current basic block.

Sparse Large-Scale Reduced-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse reduced-gradient computation without forming dense inverses or null-space matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For sparse \(J_k=[B_k\;N_k]\) with nonsingular \(B_k\), compute the adjoint variable \(w_k\) from the sparse linear solve
\[B_k^{\mathsf T}w_k=f_{y,k},\qquad r_k=f_{z,k}-N_k^{\mathsf T}w_k.\]
Choose \(s_k\) satisfying \(r_k^{\mathsf T}s_k<0\). Obtain the associated first-order dependent-variable correction \(t_k\) from \(B_kt_k=-N_ks_k\), globalize the combined direction, and restore nonlinear feasibility by a structured correction using the same or an updated sparse factorization of \(B_k\). Never form \(B_k^{-1}\) explicitly. Terminate when reduced stationarity, feasibility, and linear-solve residual tolerances are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse factorizations and adjoint solves produce reduced gradients and feasibility corrections without forming dense inverses or an explicit null-space basis.
assumptions_latex: The selected sparse block \(B_k\) is nonsingular.
Sparse solves attain the prescribed residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed combined direction satisfies \(J_k(t_k,s_k)=0\) and is reduced-descent whenever \(r_k^{\mathsf T}s_k<0\).

notation.meaning: adjoint variable used in reduced-gradient evaluation
dependent and independent components of the tangent direction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and sparse adjoint equations match the leaf, but the large-scale factorization reuse, structured correction, and globalization claims require a specific sparse-GRG source.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(n\) and \(m\) be large, let \(A_k=Dc(x_k)=[B_k\;N_k]\) be sparse with a sparse nonsingular basis block \(B_k\), and let \(x_k\) be feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale smooth equality-constrained reduced-gradient implementation emphasizing sparse factorizations and operator application rather than dense null-space storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse large-scale reduced-gradient method is a GRG method that represents the coordinate null-space action \[Z_kv=\begin{pmatrix}-B_k^{-1}N_kv\\v\end{pmatrix}\quad\text{and}\quad Z_k^Tw=-N_k^TB_k^{-T}w_B+w_N\] through sparse solves with a maintained factorization of \(B_k\), without forming dense \(B_k^{-1}\) or \(Z_k\). It computes the reduced gradient \(g_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\), obtains a reduced direction by a storage-compatible model or iterative solve, and restores feasibility through structured dependent-variable corrections. Basis selection, updates, and refactorization are chosen to control fill-in and conditioning. If a reduced curvature model is used, it is stored only when its dimension is manageable or applied through products such as \(v\mapsto Z_k^TH_kZ_kv\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse large-scale reduced-gradient method implements GRG using sparse basis factorizations. It never forms the inverse basis or a dense null-space matrix. Instead it applies \(Z_k\) and \(Z_k^T\) by sparse solves with \(B_k\), computes the reduced gradient, obtains a reduced direction with limited storage, and performs a structured feasibility correction. Pivoting and periodic refactorization control fill-in and numerical conditioning.
assumptions_latex: The Jacobian and selected basis admit a sparse factorization or structured linear solver.
Products with the chosen reduced curvature model can be computed within the available storage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The GRG quantities \(Z_kv\), \(Z_k^Tw\), and \(g_k^R\) are computed by sparse basis solves without explicitly storing \(B_k^{-1}\) or a dense \(Z_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: This is an implicit variable-reduction null-space method based on the operator \(Z_k=(-B_k^{-1}N_k,I)^T\).
special_cases_latex: When the number of reduced variables is small, a dense reduced Hessian factorization may be stored while the ambient basis operations remain sparse.
When the reduced dimension is large, an iterative method may use products \(Z_k^TH_kZ_kv\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage depends primarily on sparse factors, Jacobian nonzeros, and reduced-model data rather than on an \(n\times(n-m)\) dense basis.
boundary_notes: A sparse Jacobian does not ensure sparse factors; fill-in can dominate cost.
An ill-conditioned basis can spoil reduced-gradient scaling even when its factorization remains sparse.

children.title: Projected-Gradient Equality Methods
children.top_down_role: First-order methods using tangent projections followed by a return toward the nonlinear feasible set.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f,c\in C^1\), and let \(x_k\) be feasible with full-row-rank \(A_k=Dc(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional first-order methods using the Euclidean tangent projection and a nonlinear return to the equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the orthogonal tangent projector \[P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k.\] A projected-gradient equality method forms the tangent descent direction \[d_k=-P_k\nabla f(x_k),\qquad A_kd_k=0,\] and, for a trial \(\alpha>0\), applies a feasibility-return map \(\Pi_k\) to obtain \[x_k(\alpha)=\Pi_k(x_k+\alpha d_k),\qquad c(x_k(\alpha))=0,\quad x_k(0)=x_k,\quad x_k'(0)=d_k.\] It accepts a trial satisfying a prescribed decrease condition for \(f\) along this feasible arc. The return can be an orthogonal projection, a range-space correction, or another locally defined smooth feasibility map; the defining feature is the tangent projected-gradient direction followed by nonlinear feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method projects the negative objective gradient onto the tangent space \(\ker Dc(x_k)\), obtaining \(d_k=-P_k\nabla f(x_k)\). Because a straight tangent step is generally infeasible for nonlinear equalities, the method maps each trial back to the feasible set and searches along the resulting feasible arc. The accepted iterate is feasible and decreases the objective according to the selected acceptance rule.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) has full row rank, so \(A_kA_k^T\) is invertible.
A local feasibility-return map exists for sufficiently small tangent steps.
\(P_k\nabla f(x_k)\ne0\) when a nonzero step is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(d_k=-P_k
abla f(x_k)\in\ker A_k\), \(
abla f(x_k)^Td_k=-\|P_k
abla f(x_k)\|^2<0\), and accepted iterates satisfy \(c(x_{k+1})=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(Z_k\) is an orthonormal basis of \(\ker A_k\), then \(P_k=Z_kZ_k^T\) and \(d_k=-Z_kZ_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For affine equalities, \(x_k+\alpha d_k\) is already feasible and the return map may be the identity.
immediate_consequences_latex: The direction vanishes exactly at first-order equality-constrained stationarity.
boundary_notes: Projection onto the tangent space is not projection onto the nonlinear feasible set.
The definition excludes methods that accept the uncorrected linearized trial without restoring feasibility.

notation.meaning: Euclidean orthogonal projector onto the tangent space

children.title: Exact Feasible-Projection Methods
children.top_down_role: Projected methods whose accepted iterates lie on the nonlinear feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent expansion for a projected-gradient trial returned by nearest-point projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a \(C^2\) embedded equality manifold, \(x\in M\), \(g=P_x\nabla f(x)\), and let \(\Pi_M\) be the single-valued nearest-point projection in a tubular neighborhood of \(x\). As \(\alpha\downarrow0\), \[\Pi_M(x-\alpha g)=x-\alpha g+O(\alpha^2),\qquad f(\Pi_M(x-\alpha g))=f(x)-\alpha\|g\|^2+O(\alpha^2).\] Consequently, if \(g\ne0\), every Armijo parameter \(\sigma\in(0,1)\) is satisfied for all sufficiently small \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearest-point projection changes a tangent gradient step only at second order, so sufficiently short projected steps decrease the objective.
assumptions_latex: The nearest-point projection is single-valued near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\Pi_M(x-\alpha g))\le f(x)-\sigma\alpha\|g\|^2\) for all sufficiently small \(\alpha>0\).

notation.meaning: local nearest-point projection onto the feasible manifold

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Descent Through Exact Projection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity convergence for exact nearest-point projection with backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the iterates remain in a compact subset of a regular \(C^2\) equality manifold on which \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz, and suppose projection neighborhoods and backtracking parameters are uniform. If \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_M(x_k-\alpha_k g_k)\), where \(g_k=P_{x_k}\nabla f(x_k)\), and Armijo backtracking is used, then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|g_k\|^2<\infty,\qquad \|g_k\|\to0.\] Every accumulation point is first-order stationary on \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under uniform regularity and compactness, Armijo nearest-point-projection gradient descent drives the projected gradient to zero.
assumptions_latex: Accepted iterates lie in a compact regular portion of \(M\).
The nearest-point projection is uniformly single-valued for accepted trial radii.
\(f\) is bounded below on the level set and has Lipschitz gradient there.
Standard Armijo backtracking parameters are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|P_{x_k}\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\), and every accumulation point is stationary.

notation.meaning: projected gradient at the current feasible iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Armijo Projected-Gradient Stationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined feasibility and first-order termination test for an exact feasible-projection method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=\{x:c(x)=0\}\), suppose \(J(x)=
abla c(x)\) has full row rank, and define \[P_x=I-J(x)^{\mathsf T}(J(x)J(x)^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J(x).\] A point \(x\) is an \((\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\)-certificate when \[\|c(x)\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad \|P_x
abla f(x)\|\le\varepsilon_g.\] For an exactly projected accepted iterate, \(\varepsilon_c=0\). If also \(\varepsilon_g=0\), the unique multiplier \(\lambda=-(J J^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J
abla f(x)\) satisfies \(
abla f(x)+J(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination requires feasibility and a small tangent component of the objective gradient; at zero tolerances this is equality-constrained KKT stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_c=\varepsilon_g=0\) certifies equality feasibility and first-order stationarity.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the constraint tangent space

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Projected-Gradient Termination Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonunique Nearest Projection Outside a Tubular Neighborhood
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of single-valued Euclidean projection onto a nonlinear feasible manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x\|_2=1\}\) and \(z=(0,0)\). Then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in M}\|z-y\|_2=M.\] Hence the nearest-point projection of \(z\) onto \(M\) is set-valued, although \(M\) is a smooth compact equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point of the unit circle is a nearest point to its center, so exact projection need not be unique outside a tubular neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_M(z)\) is not single-valued.

notation.meaning: trial point at the center of the circle

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Nearest Projection Outside a Tubular Neighborhood
Exact Feasible-Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-gradient descent whose accepted points satisfy the nonlinear equalities exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c(x)=0\}\), start from \(x_0\in M\), and suppose \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)\) has full row rank. Form
\[P_k=I-J_k^{\mathsf T}(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J_k,\qquad d_k=-P_k\nabla f(x_k).\]
If \(\|d_k\|\) is below tolerance, stop. Otherwise choose \(\alpha_k>0\) and compute an exact local projection \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_M(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\), accepting only a point satisfying \(c(x_{k+1})=0\) and the prescribed decrease test. If the local projection is nonexistent or nonunique, reject the trial or reduce \(\alpha_k\). The output is the last accepted feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent projected-gradient step is followed by exact projection onto the nonlinear feasible set, so every accepted iterate remains feasible.
assumptions_latex: The local projection \(\Pi_M\) is single-valued for accepted trials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted \(x_{k+1}\) satisfies \(c(x_{k+1})=0\), and \(d_k\) is tangent to \(M\) at \(x_k\).

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the tangent space
exact local projection onto the feasible set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits exact feasible-projection methods, and the tangent projector formula is standard. A source is still required for the exact local projection selection, its existence and uniqueness conditions, and the stated rejection procedure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Return to the Nonlinear Feasible Set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M=\{x\in U:c(x)=0\}\) be a regular level set of a \(C^1\) map \(c:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \(x_k\in M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally exact feasibility restoration for smooth nonlinear equalities; numerical stopping tolerances are not treated as exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact feasible-projection method chooses a tangent trial \(v_k\in T_{x_k}M=\ker Dc(x_k)\), a step length \(\alpha_k\), and a locally defined return operator \(\Pi_k\) such that \[x_{k+1}=\Pi_k(x_k+[0malpha_kv_k)\in M,\qquad c(x_{k+1})=0.\] In a range-space realization, \(x_{k+1}=x_k+[0malpha_kv_k+Y_ku_k\), where \(Y_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) has \(Dc(x_k)Y_k\) nonsingular and \(u_k\) solves \[c(x_k+[0malpha_kv_k+Y_ku_k)=0.\] The word exact means that the accepted mathematical iterate satisfies the nonlinear equations, not merely their linearization. The return direction may depend on the method and need not be the shortest Euclidean correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact feasible-projection method first proposes a tangent displacement and then solves nonlinear correction equations so that every accepted iterate lies on \(M=\{c=0\}\). A common form adds a range-space correction \(Y_ku_k\) and solves \(c(x_k+[0malpha_kv_k+Y_ku_k)=0\). Exactness refers to satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, not just the tangent equations.
assumptions_latex: The nonlinear correction equation has a local solution for the accepted step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate satisfies \(c(x_{k+1})=0\) exactly and therefore remains on the nonlinear feasible set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In elimination coordinates, exact projection fixes the new independent variables and solves the original equalities for the dependent variables.
special_cases_latex: If \(\Pi_k\) is the nearest-point map in a tubular neighborhood, the return is orthogonal Euclidean projection.
For affine constraints, a single linear correction is exact.
immediate_consequences_latex: Merit-function constraint penalties are unnecessary merely to measure accepted-iterate feasibility, although they may still be used for globalization.
boundary_notes: The nonlinear correction may be undefined for a large tangent trial.
Terminating an inner solve at nonzero residual produces an inexact, not exact, projection method.

children.title: Linearized-Projection Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods projecting onto local linearized equality models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent Projection Does Not Preserve a Curved Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example separating linearized feasibility from exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:x_1^2+x_2^2-1=0\}\), take \(x=(1,0)\) and \(d=(0,t)\) with \(t\ne0\). Since \(J(x)=(2,0)\), \(J(x)d=0\), but \[c(x+d)=t^2>0.\] Thus the tangent trial point is infeasible for every nonzero \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero tangent step on the unit circle leaves the nonlinear feasible set with quadratic constraint error.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Projection Does Not Preserve a Curved Equality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy of a step satisfying the affine linearized equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\) have Lipschitz Jacobian with constant \(L_c\) near \(x\). If \(d\) satisfies \(c(x)+J(x)d=0\), then \[\|c(x+d)\|\le\frac{L_c}{2}\|d\|^2.\] Thus a linearized-projection step is second-order feasible locally but is not generally exactly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving the affine linearized equalities leaves a nonlinear constraint residual of quadratic order in the step.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable and its Jacobian is locally Lipschitz.

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz constant for the constraint Jacobian

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Nonlinear-Feasibility Residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic separating affine feasibility, nonlinear feasibility, and tangent stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a trial step \(d\) at \(x\), define \[r_{\mathrm{lin}}=c(x)+J(x)d,\qquad r_{\mathrm{nl}}=c(x+d),\qquad g_T=P_x\nabla f(x),\] where \(P_x\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J(x)\). An \((\varepsilon_{\mathrm{lin}},\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\)-diagnostic requires \[\|r_{\mathrm{lin}}\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{lin}},\qquad \|r_{\mathrm{nl}}\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad \|g_T\|\le\varepsilon_g.\] The first inequality alone does not certify nonlinear feasibility; under a Lipschitz Jacobian, an exact affine solve implies only \(\|r_{\mathrm{nl}}\|=O(\|d\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized-projection diagnostic separately reports affine residual, actual nonlinear residual, and current tangent stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(J(x)\) has full row rank when the inverse-based orthogonal projector is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Small linearized residual alone is not an exact nonlinear-feasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: actual nonlinear-constraint residual at the trial point
tangent projected gradient at the current point

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized-Projection Residual Diagnostic

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solvability of the Affine Linearized Projection Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-deficient solvability and pseudoinverse form of the locally owned affine projection step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), consider \[\min_d\; g^{\mathsf T}d+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|d\|^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Jd=-c.\] The constraint is feasible exactly when \(-c\in\operatorname{range}(J)\). Whenever it is feasible, strict convexity gives the unique primal solution \[d=-\alpha(I-J^\dagger J)g-J^\dagger c.\] If \(-c\notin\operatorname{range}(J)\), the subproblem has no feasible solution. Multipliers may be nonunique when \(J\) lacks full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine projection step exists exactly when the linearized constraint equation is consistent; its primal solution remains unique even for a rank-deficient Jacobian, although its multiplier need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -c\in\operatorname{range}(J)\iff\text{the subproblem is feasible},\qquad d=-\alpha(I-J^\dagger J)g-J^\dagger c.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the constraint Jacobian
orthogonal projector onto the null space of J

knowledge_statements.title: Solvability of the Affine Linearized Projection Subproblem

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Descent Identity for a Feasible Linearized-Projection Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective descent supplied by the regularized affine projection subproblem at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(x)=0\), \(g=\nabla f(x)\), \(P=I-J^\dagger J\), and \(\alpha>0\). The unique solution of \[\min_d\;g^{\mathsf T}d+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|d\|^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad Jd=0\] is \(d=-\alpha Pg\), and \[g^{\mathsf T}d=-\alpha\|Pg\|^2.\] Thus the step is a strict first-order descent direction exactly when \(Pg\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, the regularized linearized-projection step is the negative projected gradient and has negative objective slope unless tangent stationarity holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d=-\alpha Pg,\qquad \nabla f(x)^{\mathsf T}d=-\alpha\|P\nabla f(x)\|^2.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the feasible current point.
Orthogonal projector onto the linearized tangent space.

knowledge_statements.title: Descent Identity for a Feasible Linearized-Projection Step
Linearized-Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient projection onto the affine linearization of nonlinear equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and \(\alpha_k>0\), compute the unique solution of
\[d_k=\mathop{\arg\min}_{d\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\|d\|^2:J_kd=-c(x_k)\right\}.\]
When \(J_k\) has full row rank,
\[d_k=-\alpha_kP_k\nabla f(x_k)-J_k^{\mathsf T}(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(x_k),\]
where \(P_k=I-J_k^{\mathsf T}(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J_k\). Set a trial point to \(x_k+d_k\), optionally apply a feasibility correction, and accept it under the chosen merit or filter test. Without correction, nonlinear feasibility is only first-order accurate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The step minimizes a regularized linear objective over the affine linearized constraints; it generally does not satisfy the nonlinear constraints exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step satisfies \(J_kd_k=-c(x_k)\), but generally \(c(x_k+d_k)\neq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection onto the Linearized Equality Model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be \(C^1\), let \(A_k=Dc(x_k)\) have full row rank, and define the affine linearized feasible set \(L_k=\{x_k+s:c(x_k)+A_ks=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order methods enforcing the local affine equality model; accepted points need not satisfy the original nonlinear equalities exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A linearized-projection method computes a trial by projecting a proposed displacement \(q_k\) onto \(L_k\). In the Euclidean metric its correction is \[s_k=q_k-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}(c(x_k)+A_kq_k),\] so that \[c(x_k)+A_ks_k=0.\] For the gradient proposal \(q_k=-[0malpha_k
abla f(x_k)\), the trial is \(x_{k+1}^{\mathrm{trial}}=x_k+s_k\). If \(x_k\) is feasible, this reduces to the tangent projected-gradient step \(s_k=-[0malpha_kP_k
abla f(x_k)\), with \(P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k\). The defining constraint is the linearized equation; generally \(c(x_k+s_k)
e0\) for nonlinear \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized-projection method projects a proposed step onto the affine space defined by the first-order constraint model \(c(x_k)+A_ks=0\). The Euclidean formula subtracts the minimum-norm normal correction. From a feasible point and a negative-gradient proposal, it produces the tangent projected-gradient step. Unlike exact feasible projection, it does not require the resulting trial to satisfy the original nonlinear equations.
assumptions_latex: Projection is taken in the Euclidean metric for the stated closed form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected step satisfies \(c(x_k)+A_ks_k=0\); exact nonlinear feasibility \(c(x_k+s_k)=0\) is not part of the definition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(s_k\) is the unique minimizer of \(\frac12\|s-q_k\|^2\) subject to \(c(x_k)+A_ks=0\).
special_cases_latex: For affine \(c\), linearized feasibility and exact feasibility coincide.
At a feasible \(x_k\), \(L_k=x_k+\ker A_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(C^2\) constraints and bounded \(s_k\), the nonlinear residual is locally of second order in \(\|s_k\|\).
boundary_notes: This definition does not include a subsequent exact nonlinear correction; adding one yields an exact feasible-projection method.
Rank-deficient \(A_k\) requires a pseudoinverse and a consistency qualification not covered here.

notation.meaning: projection of the proposal onto the linearized model

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a trial step \(d\) at \(x\), define \[r_{\mathrm{lin}}=c(x)+J(x)d,\qquad r_{\mathrm{nl}}=c(x+d),\qquad g_T=P_x\nabla f(x),\] where \(P_x\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J(x)\). An \((\varepsilon_{\mathrm{lin}},\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\)-certificate requires \[\|r_{\mathrm{lin}}\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{lin}},\qquad \|r_{\mathrm{nl}}\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad \|g_T\|\le\varepsilon_g.\] The first inequality alone does not certify nonlinear feasibility; under a Lipschitz Jacobian, an exact affine solve only implies \(\|r_{\mathrm{nl}}\|=O(\|d\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized-projection diagnostic must separately report affine residual, actual nonlinear residual, and projected-gradient stationarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order descent identity for a tangent projected-gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a retraction on a smooth embedded manifold \(M\), let \(g=\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)\), and define \(\phi(\alpha)=f(R_x(-\alpha g))\). Then \[\phi'(0)=-\|g\|^2.\] Hence \(-g\) is a strict descent direction for the retraction pullback whenever \(g\ne0\), and sufficiently small positive steps satisfy an Armijo decrease condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order consistency of a retraction makes the negative manifold gradient a descent direction for the pullback objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{d}{d\alpha}f(R_x(-\alpha g))|_{\alpha=0}=-\|g\|^2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Retraction Pullback Descent Derivative

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global first-order stationarity for retraction gradient descent on a compact level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the retraction pullbacks \(f\circ R_x\) satisfy a uniform local descent lemma on the compact level set containing the iterates. For \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(-\alpha_k g_k)\), where \(g_k=\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k)\) and \(\alpha_k\) is chosen by Armijo backtracking, \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k\|g_k\|^2<\infty,
\qquad \|g_k\|\to0.\] Every accumulation point is Riemannian stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uniform pullback smoothness and Armijo backtracking, retraction gradient descent drives the manifold gradient to zero.
assumptions_latex: The relevant level set is compact.
Retraction pullbacks obey a uniform local descent lemma.
\(f\) is bounded below on the level set.
Standard Armijo backtracking parameters are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k)\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Armijo Retraction-Gradient Stationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and first-order stationarity test for a retraction-based feasible iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\{x:c(x)=0\}\) be a regular embedded equality manifold and let \(g(x)=\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)=P_x\nabla f(x)\). A feasible iterate \(x\in M\) is an \(\varepsilon_g\)-stationarity certificate when \[c(x)=0,\qquad \|g(x)\|\le\varepsilon_g.\] At \(\varepsilon_g=0\), this is equivalent to equality-constrained first-order KKT stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retraction method terminates at a feasible point whose manifold gradient is below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a regular embedded equality manifold.
The metric is induced by the ambient Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x)=0\) and \(\|\operatorname{grad}_M f(x)\|\le\varepsilon_g\) certify feasible approximate first-order stationarity.

notation.meaning: Riemannian gradient of the restricted objective

knowledge_statements.title: Retraction-Gradient Termination Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted-step complexity under uniform Armijo decrease and a positive step-length lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\sigma\alpha_k\|g_k\|^2,\qquad \alpha_k\ge\underline\alpha>0,\]
where \(g_k=\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k)\), \(\sigma>0\), and \(f(x_k)\ge f_{\inf}\). Then for every \(N\ge1\),
\[\min_{0\le k<N}\|g_k\|^2\le\frac{f(x_0)-f_{\inf}}{\sigma\underline\alpha N}.\]
Thus an iterate with \(\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon\) occurs within at most \(\left\lceil(f(x_0)-f_{\inf})/(\sigma\underline\alpha\varepsilon^2)\right\rceil\) accepted steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded accepted Armijo steps give an inverse-square accepted-iteration bound for finding a small manifold gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{0\le k<N}\|\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k)\|^2\le(f(x_0)-f_{\inf})/(\sigma\underline\alpha N)\).

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on accepted step lengths
objective lower bound on the iterate set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Undefined Step Outside a Local Retraction Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete example showing why a retraction-domain safeguard is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(M=\mathbb R\) and the local retraction \(R_x(\eta)=x+\eta\), defined only when \(|\eta|<(1+|x|)^{-1}\). It satisfies \(R_x(0)=x\) and \(D R_x(0)=1\). At \(x=1\), for \(f(x)=x\), the trial \(\eta=-\operatorname{grad}_M f(1)=-1\) lies outside the required domain \(|\eta|<1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid local retraction can have a restricted domain, making an unsafeguarded gradient trial undefined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_1(-1)\text{ is undefined although }-\operatorname{grad}_M f(1)=-1\text{ is a descent direction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Undefined Step Outside a Local Retraction Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions needed for retraction-gradient steps and uniform Armijo guarantees to remain well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a retraction be defined on an open neighborhood \(\mathcal D\subset TM\) of the zero section. The update \(R_x(-\alpha\operatorname{grad}_M f(x))\) is defined only when \((x,-\alpha\operatorname{grad}_M f(x))\in\mathcal D\). Pointwise smoothness does not by itself supply a uniform domain radius or uniform pullback descent constant on a noncompact iterate set. Without such uniformity or an explicit domain safeguard, a positive iteration-independent lower bound on accepted Armijo step lengths, and hence the stated \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) accepted-step bound, does not follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local retraction smoothness alone does not guarantee uniformly valid or uniformly bounded Armijo steps.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a local retraction with domain \(\mathcal D\subset TM\).
No compactness, uniform domain radius, or uniform pullback descent lemma is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_k\alpha_k>0\) and the associated \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) bound require additional uniform assumptions or safeguards.

notation.meaning: Domain of the local retraction in the tangent bundle.

knowledge_statements.title: Retraction-Domain and Uniform-Smoothness Boundary
Retraction-Based Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Riemannian gradient descent on the regular equality manifold using a smooth retraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=\{x:c(x)=0\}\) be a smooth embedded manifold, start from \(x_0\in M\), and define \(P_x\) as the orthogonal projector onto \(T_xM=\ker\nabla c(x)\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(g_k=P_{x_k}\nabla f(x_k)\). If \(\|g_k\|\) is below tolerance, stop; otherwise select \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(\eta_k=-\alpha_kg_k\), and update
\[x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k).\]
Here \(R_x:T_xM\to M\) satisfies \(R_x(0)=x\) and \(D R_x(0)\) equal to the identity on \(T_xM\). Choose \(\alpha_k\) by a decrease test applied to \(f\circ R_{x_k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method descends in the tangent space and returns to the feasible manifold through a first-order-consistent smooth retraction.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth embedded equality manifold.
\(R\) is a smooth retraction defined for accepted steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All iterates lie in \(M\), and \(-g_k\) is a feasible tangent descent direction when \(g_k\neq0\).

notation.meaning: tangent space of the feasible manifold at x
retraction from the tangent space to the manifold
