knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent Descent Composed with a Retraction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:c(x)=0\}\) be a smooth embedded manifold determined by a \(C^1\) map with full-row-rank Jacobian on \(M\), and let \(T_xM=\ker Dc(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional manifold formulation; the formal retraction axioms are stated, but no supplied source was found that supports this exact terminology and scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A retraction on \(M\) is a smooth map \(R\) defined on an open neighborhood of the zero section in the tangent bundle \(TM\), with fibers \(R_x:T_xM\supseteq U_x\to M\), such that for every \(x\in M\), \[R_x(0_x)=x,\qquad DR_x(0_x)[v]=v\quad\text{for all }v\in T_xM.\] A retraction-based equality method chooses a tangent direction \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}M\), commonly \(\eta_k=-\operatorname{grad}_M f(x_k)=-P_k\nabla f(x_k)\), selects \(\alpha_k>0\), and sets \[x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}([0malpha_k\eta_k).\] Thus every accepted iterate lies on \(M\), and the retracted curve has initial velocity \(\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retraction is a smooth tangent-to-manifold return map satisfying \(R_x(0)=x\) and having identity derivative at zero. A retraction-based method computes a tangent descent direction, scales it, and uses \(R_x\) to obtain the next feasible point. The return is first-order consistent with the tangent step and need not be the nearest-point projection.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth embedded equality manifold.
\(R_x\) is defined at the chosen tangent step.
The selected search direction lies in \(T_{x_k}M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}([0malpha_k\eta_k)\in M\), with \(\frac{d}{d\alpha}R_{x_k}([0malpha\eta_k)|_{\alpha=0}=\eta_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The map \(\alpha\mapsto R_x([0malpha\eta)\) is a feasible curve agreeing to first order with the ambient tangent line \(x+[0malpha\eta\).
special_cases_latex: A locally defined nearest-point projection onto \(M\), restricted to tangent trials near zero, is a retraction.
On an affine subspace, \(R_x([0meta)=x+[0meta\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Retraction-based updates preserve equality feasibility by construction.
boundary_notes: A general feasibility-restoration map is not a retraction unless it satisfies the identity-derivative axiom.
The definition is local; a retraction need not be defined for arbitrarily large tangent vectors.

notation.meaning: tangent bundle of the equality manifold
Riemannian gradient for the induced Euclidean metric

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Step in Local Feasible Coordinates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f,c\in C^2\), let \(x_k\) be feasible for \(c(x)=0\), let \(A_k=Dc(x_k)\) have full row rank, and let \(Z_k\) be a full-column-rank basis of \(\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order smooth equality-constrained methods using the Lagrangian Hessian restricted to the tangent space and a nonlinear feasibility return.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear reduced-Newton method forms a multiplier estimate \(\lambda_k\), the Lagrangian Hessian \[W_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k),\qquad L(x,[0mlambda)=f(x)-[0mlambda^Tc(x),\] and solves the reduced Newton equation \[Z_k^TW_kZ_kp_k^R=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k).\] The ambient tangent step is \(d_k=Z_kp_k^R\). A trial step is mapped to a feasible point by a local chart, exact projection, or equivalent nonlinear correction, giving \[x_{k+1}=R_k([0malpha_kd_k),\qquad c(x_{k+1})=0.\] The method is reduced because the Newton equation has dimension \(n-m\), and nonlinear because feasibility is maintained on the original curved equality set rather than only on its affine tangent model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear reduced-Newton method restricts the Lagrangian Hessian to the tangent space, solves \(Z_k^TW_kZ_kp_k^R=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\), lifts the reduced solution to \(d_k=Z_kp_k^R\), and applies a nonlinear feasibility return. It therefore uses second-order curvature in local tangent coordinates while keeping accepted iterates on the original equality manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
The reduced Hessian \(Z_k^TW_kZ_k\) is nonsingular for an unregularized Newton step.
The feasibility-return map is defined at the accepted trial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced step solves \(Z_k^TW_kZ_kp_k^R=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\), its lift satisfies \(A_kd_k=0\), and the accepted iterate satisfies \(c(x_{k+1})=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reduced equation is Newton's equation for the local reduced objective in feasible coordinates.
When \(Z_k\) is orthonormal, \(Z_k^TW_kZ_k\) is the matrix of the tangent-restricted Lagrangian Hessian.
special_cases_latex: With \(W_k=I\), the direction reduces to projected steepest descent.
For affine equalities, no nonlinear return is required.
immediate_consequences_latex: If the reduced Hessian is positive definite and the reduced gradient is nonzero, the full reduced Newton step is a tangent descent direction.
boundary_notes: An indefinite or singular reduced Hessian requires regularization, a trust region, or negative-curvature handling.
Using \(Z_k^T\nabla^2f(x_k)Z_k\) alone generally omits constraint curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit-Basis Reduced Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton iteration formed in an explicit basis of the equality-constraint tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^m\), with \(m<n\), be twice continuously differentiable, and consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\). Define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). At a feasible iterate \(x_k\), choose \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb{R}^m\), set \(J_k=
abla c(x_k)\) and \(H_k=
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\), and construct \(Z_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes(n-m)}\) with full column rank such that \(J_kZ_k=0\). Compute \(s_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\) and \(p_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) from
\[(Z_k^{\mathsf T}H_kZ_k)s_k=-Z_k^{\mathsf T}
abla f(x_k),\qquad p_k=Z_ks_k.\]
Choose a step length and restore exact feasibility by a local implicit solve or a retraction applied to the tangent step. Stop when feasibility and \(\|Z_k^{\mathsf T}
abla f(x_k)\|\) meet prescribed tolerances. If the reduced Hessian is singular or unsuitable for descent, apply a stated regularization or curvature-handling step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit basis of the constraint tangent space converts the equality-constrained Newton equation into a reduced-Hessian system, after which nonlinear feasibility is restored.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) are twice continuously differentiable, with \(m<n\).
\(x_k\) is feasible and \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)\) has full row rank.
The reduced Newton system is solvable after any stated regularization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The direction \(p_k\) satisfies \(J_kp_k=0\) and the reduced Newton equation in the basis \(Z_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Invariance of the Explicit-Basis Newton Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independence of the reconstructed tangent Newton vector from the chosen explicit basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z=ZR\) be full-column-rank bases of the same tangent space, with \(R\) nonsingular. If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\) is nonsingular and
\[(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)s=-Z^{\mathsf T}g,\qquad(\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}H\widehat Z)\widehat s=-\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}g,\]
then \(\widehat s=R^{-1}s\) and \(\widehat Z\widehat s=Zs\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the explicit tangent basis changes reduced coordinates but not the reconstructed tangent Newton direction.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) and \(\widehat Z\) span the same tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat Z\widehat s=Zs.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Quadratic Convergence of Exact Feasible Reduced Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rate for the exact explicit-basis method, excluding inexact and negative-curvature variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_*\) be a regular equality-constrained stationary point. Suppose a \(C^2\) feasible chart \(\chi\) exists near \(x_*\), its reduced objective \(\phi=f\circ\chi\) has a locally Lipschitz Hessian, and \(\nabla^2\phi\) is nonsingular at the solution. If each explicit-basis system uses the chart-consistent Lagrangian Hessian, is solved exactly, and the new iterate is obtained by the same exact chart or equivalent exact feasibility map, then all sufficiently close feasible initial points generate well-defined iterates satisfying
\[\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\le C\|x_k-x_*\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact explicit-basis reduced Newton is ordinary Newton in feasible coordinates and converges quadratically near a regular nondegenerate stationary point.
assumptions_latex: A regular twice-continuously-differentiable feasible chart exists near \(x_*\).
The reduced-objective Hessian is nonsingular at \(x_*\) and locally Lipschitz.
The multiplier used in the Lagrangian Hessian is chart-consistent.
Reduced systems and feasibility restoration are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x_*\|\le C\|x_k-x_*\|^2\) for sufficiently close feasible iterates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced Newton with a Formed Tangent Basis
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\) be a regular feasible point, let \(A_k=Dc(x_k)\), and let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) be an explicitly stored full-column-rank matrix satisfying \(A_kZ_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order reduced Newton that explicitly forms and stores a tangent-space basis and its reduced curvature matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit-basis reduced Newton method constructs \(Z_k\), forms \[g_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k),\qquad H_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,[0mlambda_k)Z_k,\] solves \[H_k^Rp_k^R=-g_k^R,\] and lifts the result as \(d_k=Z_kp_k^R\). The basis may be obtained by coordinate elimination, QR factorization, or another null-space factorization, but it is materially available for matrix products and storage. The method then uses a nonlinear feasible-arc or return calculation to produce an accepted feasible iterate. If \(Z_k^TZ_k=I\), the reduced gradient and Hessian are Euclidean tangent-coordinate representations; for a nonorthogonal basis, they represent the pullback under that coordinate map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This variant explicitly constructs a matrix \(Z_k\) spanning the tangent null space. It forms the reduced gradient and reduced Lagrangian Hessian, solves the \((n-m)\)-dimensional Newton system, lifts the solution with \(Z_k\), and restores nonlinear feasibility. Its distinguishing feature is the explicit tangent basis and explicitly assembled reduced curvature model.
assumptions_latex: \(H_k^R\) is nonsingular unless a regularized solve is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method explicitly forms \(g_k^R=Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(H_k^R=Z_k^TW_kZ_k\), solves \(H_k^Rp_k^R=-g_k^R\), and obtains \(d_k=Z_kp_k^R\in\ker A_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: This is Newton's method applied to the local reduced objective represented in the coordinates generated by \(Z_k\).
special_cases_latex: Coordinate elimination gives \(Z_k=(-B_k^{-1}N_k,I)^T\).
Orthogonal factorization gives an orthonormal \(Z_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced linear system has order \(n-m\).
An orthonormal basis avoids coordinate scaling in the Euclidean tangent metric.
boundary_notes: Explicit storage can be prohibitive when both \(n\) and \(n-m\) are large.
A changing basis requires consistent transport or reconstruction of stored reduced curvature information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krylov convergence for a positive-definite implicit tangent operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\mu\|v\|^2\le v^{\mathsf T}Hv\le L\|v\|^2\) for every \(v\in\ker J\), where \(0<\mu\le L\). Conjugate gradients applied on \(\ker J\) to \(PHPp=-Pg\), from a tangent initial vector, satisfies in exact arithmetic \[\|p_t-p_*\|_{PHP}\le2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^t\|p_0-p_*\|_{PHP},\qquad \kappa=L/\mu,\] and terminates in at most \(n-m\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive tangent curvature makes the projected operator positive definite on the tangent space, yielding the standard CG rate and finite termination bound.
assumptions_latex: \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(H\) is symmetric and positive definite on \(\ker J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restriction of \(PHP\) to \(\ker J\) is positive definite and satisfies the displayed CG bound.

notation.meaning: condition number of the tangent-restricted operator

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Conjugate-Gradient Rate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-free characterization of the implicit tangent Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, \(P=I-J^{\mathsf T}(JJ^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J\), and \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\). For \(p\in\ker J\), \[PHPp=-Pg\] if and only if there exists \(\nu\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \[Hp+g+J^{\mathsf T}\nu=0,\qquad Jp=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected tangent equation is equivalent to the primal equations of a KKT system without constructing a null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(PHPp=-Pg\iff\exists\nu:(Hp+g+J^{\mathsf T}\nu=0,\ Jp=0)\) for \(p\in\ker J\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Equation–KKT Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness and Descent of the Projected Newton Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of positive tangent curvature for the implicit projected equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J\), let \(H=H^\mathsf T\), and suppose \(v^\mathsf THv>0\) for every nonzero \(v\in\ker J\). Then \(PHPp=-Pg\) has a unique solution \(p\in\ker J\), and \[g^\mathsf Tp=-p^\mathsf THp.\] Hence \(p=0\) exactly when \(Pg=0\); otherwise \(g^\mathsf Tp<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive tangent curvature makes the projected Newton step unique and strictly descending unless projected stationarity already holds.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J\).
\(H\) is symmetric and positive definite on \(\ker J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) is unique, \(p=0\iff Pg=0\), and \(p\neq0\Rightarrow g^\mathsf Tp=-p^\mathsf THp<0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness and Descent of the Projected Newton Step

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori error bound for an approximate implicitly projected Newton direction under positive tangent curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J\), and suppose \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv\ge\mu\|v\|^2\) for all \(v\in\ker J\), with \(\mu>0\). Let \(p_*\in\ker J\) solve \(PHPp_*=-Pg\), and let \(p\in\ker J\) have residual \(q=P(Hp+g)\). Then \[\|p-p_*\|\le \mu^{-1}\|q\|,\qquad \|p-p_*\|_{PHP}\le \mu^{-1/2}\|q\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under positive tangent curvature, the projected-equation residual bounds the error in an approximate implicit Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J\).
\(H\) is symmetric and has tangent lower-curvature bound \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Newton Residual Certificate
Implicit-Projection Reduced Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent Newton iteration expressed with projected operators rather than an explicit null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible \(x_k\), let \(J_k=
abla c(x_k)\) have full row rank and define \(P_k=I-J_k^{\mathsf T}(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J_k\). With \(H_k=
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\), compute \(p_k\in\operatorname{range}(P_k)\) from the projected equation
\[P_kH_kP_kp_k=-P_k
abla f(x_k).\]
The equation may be solved by a Krylov method whose operator application uses solves with \(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T}\), without constructing a basis for \(\ker J_k\). Globalize the tangent step and restore feasibility by a local correction or retraction. Stop when projected stationarity, feasibility, and linear-solve residual tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected Hessian-vector products solve the tangent Newton equation without constructing an explicit null-space basis, after which feasibility is restored.
assumptions_latex: The projected Hessian equation is solvable on \(\operatorname{range}(P_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed direction satisfies \(J_kp_k=0\) and the Newton equation projected onto the tangent space.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the tangent space
Lagrangian Hessian or its Newton model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order equality-constrained Newton computation using projected operators and tangent-constrained solves without explicitly storing a null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An implicit-projection reduced Newton method computes a tangent step \(d_k\in\operatorname{range}P_k\) satisfying the projected Newton equation \[P_kW_kP_kd_k=-P_k
abla f(x_k),\qquad P_kd_k=d_k,\] or equivalently the saddle system \[ egin{pmatrix}W_k&A_k^T\A_k&0\end{pmatrix} egin{pmatrix}d_k\[0mmu_k\end{pmatrix}=- egin{pmatrix}
abla f(x_k)\0\end{pmatrix}.\] The method applies \(P_k\), \(W_k\), and the relevant linear solvers as operators and does not form an explicit \(n	imes(n-m)\) matrix \(Z_k\). After computing \(d_k\), it uses a nonlinear feasibility-return map for the accepted step. Whenever \(Z_k\) is any orthonormal tangent basis, the implicit equation is equivalent to \((Z_k^TW_kZ_k)p=-Z_k^T
abla f(x_k)\) with \(d_k=Z_kp\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This reduced-Newton variant avoids forming a tangent basis. It solves for a tangent vector using the projected Lagrangian-Hessian operator or an equivalent KKT system. Projection and curvature are applied implicitly. The computed step is mathematically equivalent to an explicit reduced Newton step, but no null-space matrix is stored; a nonlinear return then restores feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The tangent restriction of \(W_k\) is nonsingular.
The operator or saddle system is solved to the accuracy required by the method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed \(d_k\) satisfies \(A_kd_k=0\) and the tangent-restricted Newton equation, without explicit construction of a tangent basis.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For orthonormal \(Z_k\), the projected and explicit reduced systems yield the same ambient step \(d_k=Z_kp_k^R\).
special_cases_latex: Matrix-free Krylov iteration can use products with \(P_kW_kP_k\).
For affine constraints, the subsequent nonlinear return is unnecessary.
immediate_consequences_latex: Avoiding explicit \(Z_k\) can reduce storage when the tangent dimension is large.
boundary_notes: The projected operator is singular on the full ambient space unless the tangent constraint \(P_kd_k=d_k\) is imposed.
A poorly conditioned constraint solve can make applications of \(P_k\) inaccurate.

children.title: Inexact Reduced Newton
children.top_down_role: Reduced Newton methods using approximate tangent and feasibility solves.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a residual condition that permits an uninformative step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(z_k)\ne0\), the bound \[\|F'(z_k)s_k+F(z_k)\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|\] alone gives no contraction when \(\eta_k\ge1\), because \(s_k=0\) satisfies it. Thus a forcing bound below one, together with local regularity and step acceptance, is essential for the usual contraction conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At forcing tolerance one or larger, the zero step is admissible, so the residual test alone cannot ensure progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k=0\) is admissible, so convergence does not follow from the residual inequality alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncontractive Forcing Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rate classification by the forcing sequence for a regular reduced nonlinear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^r\to\mathbb R^r\) be continuously differentiable near a root \(z_*\), with \(F'(z_*)\) nonsingular and \(F'\) Lipschitz near \(z_*\). Suppose \[F'(z_k)s_k=-F(z_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\] and full steps \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k\) are taken sufficiently near \(z_*\). A sufficiently small uniform bound \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) gives local q-linear convergence; \(\eta_k\to0\) gives q-superlinear convergence; and \(\eta_k=O(\|F(z_k)\|)\) gives q-quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed forcing yields local linear convergence, vanishing forcing yields superlinear convergence, and residual-proportional forcing recovers quadratic convergence.
assumptions_latex: Reduced coordinates and feasibility restoration preserve the asserted residual order.
The initial point is sufficiently close to \(z_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three forcing regimes imply q-linear, q-superlinear, and q-quadratic convergence, respectively.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Reduced-Newton Local Rates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-error control from the residual of an inexact reduced Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_ks_k^*=-g_k\) with \(A_k\) nonsingular, and let \(A_ks_k=-g_k+r_k\). Then \[s_k-s_k^*=A_k^{-1}r_k,\qquad \|s_k-s_k^*\|\leq\|A_k^{-1}\|\,\|r_k\|.\] If \(\|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|\) and \(s_k^*\neq0\), then \[\frac{\|s_k-s_k^*\|}{\|s_k^*\|}\leq\kappa(A_k)\eta_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact reduced-system residual bounds the step error after amplification by the inverse reduced matrix and its condition number.
assumptions_latex: The vector and matrix norms are subordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|s_k-s_k^*\|\leq\|A_k^{-1}\|\|r_k\|\), with relative error at most \(\kappa(A_k)\eta_k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Linear-Solve Residual Error Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational report combining nonlinear feasibility, reduced stationarity, tangency, and the last reduced Newton-equation residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an iterate \(x_k\), let \(P_k\) project orthogonally onto \(\ker J_k\), let \(H_k\) be the current Hessian model, and let \(p_k\) be the computed trial direction. For tolerances \(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_t,\varepsilon_N\ge0\), report \[\|c(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon_c,\quad \|P_k\nabla f(x_k)\|\le\varepsilon_g,\quad \|J_kp_k\|\le\varepsilon_t,\quad \|P_k(H_kp_k+\nabla f(x_k))\|\le\varepsilon_N.\] The first two residuals certify approximate primal feasibility and first-order stationarity; the last two certify the tangency and equation accuracy of the reported inexact step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A termination report should distinguish nonlinear feasibility, projected stationarity, tangency error, and projected Newton residual.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k\) has full row rank so \(P_k\) is defined.
All residuals use the same iterate, model, and norm convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The four bounds jointly report approximate feasibility, first-order stationarity, tangency, and reduced-solve accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Inexact Reduced-Newton Termination Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A forcing condition guaranteeing descent for an inexact positive-definite reduced Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and let \(As=-g+r\). If \(\|r\|_{A^{-1}}\le\eta\|g\|_{A^{-1}}\) for some \(0\le\eta<1\), then \[g^{\mathsf T}s=-g^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}g+g^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}r\le-(1-\eta)\|g\|_{A^{-1}}^2<0\] whenever \(g\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual smaller than the right-hand side in the inverse-energy norm preserves strict descent of an inexact positive-definite reduced Newton step.

notation.meaning: Residual of the inexact reduced Newton equation.

knowledge_statements.title: Energy-Norm Forcing Condition for Descent
Inexact Reduced Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual conditions defining an inexact tangent-space Newton and feasibility correction step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a feasible \(x_k\), let \(P_k\) project onto \(\ker J_k\), let \(g_k=P_k\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(H_k\) be a Lagrangian Hessian model. A tangent step \(p_k\) is an inexact reduced Newton step with forcing parameters \(\eta_k,\tau_k\geq0\) if
\[\|P_k(H_kp_k+\nabla f(x_k))\|\leq\eta_k\|g_k\|,\qquad \|J_kp_k\|\leq\tau_k\|g_k\|.\]
After a feasibility restoration producing \(x_{k+1}\), require \(\|c(x_{k+1})\|\leq\delta_k\). For local superlinear behavior, the defining accuracy regime is \(\eta_k\to0\), \(\tau_k\to0\), and \(\delta_k=o(\|p_k\|)\), together with the usual regularity and nonsingularity hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact reduced Newton step controls projected Newton residual, tangency error, and post-restoration constraint residual through forcing tolerances that tighten near a solution.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed residual inequalities define the permitted inexactness of tangent and feasibility solves.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact reduced-Newton method computes \(p_k^R\) satisfying \[H_k^Rp_k^R=-g_k^R+r_k^R,\qquad \|r_k^R\|\le[0meta_k\|g_k^R\|,\qquad 0\le[0meta_k<1,\] rather than solving the reduced Newton equation exactly. The residual must obey a forcing condition such as \(\|r_k^R\|\le[0meta_k\|g_k^R\|\). The method may also tolerate explicitly bounded errors in tangent construction or feasibility restoration. These tolerances are declared components of the algorithm rather than unrecorded numerical artifacts.

\(H_k^R\) is nonsingular on the local regime in which a Newton interpretation is intended.

A fixed \([0meta_k\le\bar[0meta<1\) gives uniformly relative-accurate reduced solves; a vanishing forcing sequence requests progressively more accurate solves.

children.title: Negative-Curvature Reduced Newton
children.top_down_role: Reduced Newton variants detecting or exploiting tangent-space negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Reduced Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-space direction certifying failure of the second-order necessary condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, and define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(c(x)=0\), and suppose there is \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \(
abla f(x)+
abla c(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\). Set \(J=
abla c(x)\) and \(H=
abla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)\), and assume \(J\) has full row rank. Any nonzero \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[Jd=0,\qquad d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0\]
is a reduced negative-curvature certificate. It shows that \(H\) is not positive semidefinite on \(\ker J\), so \(x\) fails the second-order necessary condition for a local minimizer of the equality-constrained problem. A reduced-Newton method may use such a tangent direction in a curvature-handling step followed by globalization and feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero tangent vector with negative Lagrangian curvature certifies failure of the equality-constrained second-order necessary condition and can be used by a reduced-Newton curvature-handling step.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is feasible and satisfies first-order stationarity with multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditions \(Jd=0\), \(d\neq0\), and \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd<0\) certify that the Lagrangian Hessian is not positive semidefinite on the tangent space \(\ker J\).

notation.meaning: equality-constrained Lagrangian defined by f(x) plus lambda transposed times c(x)
Lagrangian Hessian at the stationary primal-dual point
constraint Jacobian at the feasible point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection and exploitation of reduced negative curvature during an iterative Newton solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker J\), set \(B=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\), and apply conjugate gradients to \(Bu=-Z^{\mathsf T}g\). If a nonzero search direction \(q\) satisfies \(q^{\mathsf T}Bq\le0\), terminate the Newton solve and return \(d=Zq\), choosing its sign so that \(g^{\mathsf T}d\le0\). Then \(Jd=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd\le0\). When the inequality is strict, a trust-region or suitably globalized curvature step may use \(d\) instead of an indefinite Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated CG stops on nonpositive reduced curvature and lifts the detected direction to a tangent curvature-handling step; strict negativity supplies the escape direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=Zq\) is tangent and has the same nonpositive curvature as \(q\) in reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Truncated-CG Curvature Step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Curvature Is Not a Negative-Curvature Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between strict negative curvature and semidefinite degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonzero tangent vector satisfying \(Jd=0\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd=0\) does not certify failure of the second-order necessary condition, which requires only \(v^{\mathsf T}Hv\ge0\) for all tangent \(v\). A zero Rayleigh quotient may indicate degeneracy but cannot by itself justify a negative-curvature escape conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero tangent curvature signals possible degeneracy, not failure of second-order necessity.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is the Lagrangian Hessian at a first-order stationary feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{\mathsf T}Hd=0\) alone is not a negative-curvature certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Curvature Is Not a Negative-Curvature Certificate

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), with \(m<n\), be twice continuously differentiable, and consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\). At an iterate \(x_k\), write \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\), assume \(\operatorname{rank}A_k=m\), and let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) satisfy \(A_kZ_k=0\) and \(Z_k^TZ_k=I\). Let \(W_k\) be the Lagrangian Hessian or a symmetric approximation and \(H_k^R=Z_k^TW_kZ_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth equality-constrained optimization with a full-row-rank constraint Jacobian. The definition concerns reduced-space step computation and permits an indefinite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A negative-curvature reduced Newton step is a vector \(p_k=v_k+Z_ku_k\), where the normal component \(v_k\) satisfies or approximately minimizes the linearized feasibility residual \(\|A_kv+c(x_k)\|\), and the reduced component is computed from the quadratic model \[q_k(u)=g_k^{R\,T}u+\tfrac12u^TH_k^Ru,\qquad g_k^R=Z_k^T(\nabla f(x_k)+W_kv_k).\] The reduced solver must test curvature. If it encounters \(d\ne0\) with \(d^TH_k^Rd\le0\), it terminates or truncates along \(d\), choosing its sign so that \(g_k^{R\,T}d\le0\), and selects a permitted length, typically to a reduced trust-region boundary. If no such direction is encountered, \(u_k\) is an exact or inexact solution of \(H_k^Ru=-g_k^R\). Thus negative curvature is exploited entirely in the tangent space, while \(v_k\) manages linearized feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-curvature reduced Newton method splits a trial step into a normal feasibility correction and a tangent-space Newton correction. It forms the reduced Hessian by restricting the Lagrangian Hessian, or a symmetric approximation, to the null space of the constraint Jacobian. The reduced linear or trust-region solver explicitly tests quadratic curvature. When it finds a nonzero reduced direction with nonpositive reduced-Hessian quadratic form, it truncates or follows that direction with a sign that is nonascending for the reduced linear model, usually until a trust-region boundary is reached. Otherwise it computes an exact or inexact reduced Newton solution. The lifted tangent step does not alter the linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_k=v_k+Z_ku_k,\qquad A_kZ_ku_k=0,\qquad d^TH_k^Rd\le0\ \Longrightarrow\ g_k^{R\,T}d\le0\text{ after a possible sign change}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With the orthogonal projector \(P_k=Z_kZ_k^T\), a lifted negative-curvature direction \(s_k=Z_kd\) satisfies \(A_ks_k=0\) and \(s_k^TW_ks_k=d^TH_k^Rd\le0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H_k^R\succ0\), the definition reduces to the ordinary reduced Newton equation \(H_k^Ru_k=-g_k^R\).
For a feasible iterate, one may take \(v_k=0\), so the entire trial step is tangent to the equality manifold to first order.
immediate_consequences_latex: A detected direction with \(d^TH_k^Rd<0\) certifies that the reduced quadratic model is nonconvex.
The lifted reduced component always satisfies the homogeneous linearized constraints.
boundary_notes: Nonpositive curvature of the full Hessian outside \(\ker A_k\) is irrelevant to this reduced test.
The definition does not prescribe a line search, trust-region update, or nonlinear feasibility restoration after the trial step.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian in row orientation, \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\).

children.title: Varying-Tangent Quasi-Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Reduced curvature approximations maintained as nonlinear tangent spaces and coordinates change.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with twice continuously differentiable data and full-row-rank \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\). For each iteration choose \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) with \(A_kZ_k=0\) and full column rank. Let \(M_k\in\mathbb S^{n-m}\) approximate \(Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality constraints. Tangent spaces and their coordinate bases may change between iterations; the definition does not require the iterates themselves to be exactly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A varying-tangent quasi-Newton method is an iteration that computes \[p_k=Y_kp_k^Y+Z_kp_k^Z,\qquad (A_kY_k)p_k^Y=-c(x_k),\] and determines the tangential coordinates from a reduced model using \(M_k\), for example \[M_kp_k^Z=-Z_k^T
abla f(x_k).\] After accepting \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), it forms a reduced displacement \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k^Z\) and a reduced Lagrangian-gradient difference expressed in a specified tangent coordinate system, such as \[y_k=Z_k^T igl(
abla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-
abla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1}) igr).\] A symmetric quasi-Newton rule produces an intermediate matrix satisfying the secant relation \(M_{k+1}^{(k)}s_k=y_k\). Because \(Z_{k+1}\) generally differs from \(Z_k\), the method must also specify how the intermediate curvature model is represented in the new tangent coordinates before it is used at iteration \(k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A varying-tangent quasi-Newton method maintains an approximation to Lagrangian curvature only on the current null space of the equality-constraint Jacobian. Each step has a normal coordinate component that addresses the linearized constraints and a tangent coordinate component obtained from the reduced quasi-Newton model. Following an accepted step, the method constructs a reduced displacement and a reduced difference of Lagrangian gradients, imposes a reduced secant equation, and explicitly accounts for the fact that the next null-space basis can differ from the current one. The representation-change mechanism is part of the method; without it, matrices from successive reduced coordinate systems cannot be identified canonically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A_kZ_k=0,\qquad M_{k+1}^{(k)}s_k=y_k,\qquad M_{k+1}\text{ is the specified representation of }M_{k+1}^{(k)}\text{ in the }Z_{k+1}\text{ coordinates}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method may be described intrinsically as maintaining a symmetric bilinear form on each tangent space and supplying an identification of consecutive tangent spaces.
special_cases_latex: If \(Z_{k+1}=Z_k\), no coordinate conversion is required and the method becomes an ordinary reduced BFGS, DFP, or SR1 update.
If \(c\) is affine, the tangent space is constant, so only optional basis changes remain.
immediate_consequences_latex: The stored matrix dimension is \((n-m)\times(n-m)\), not \(n\times n\).
The lifted tangential step \(Z_kp_k^Z\) satisfies \(A_kZ_kp_k^Z=0\).
boundary_notes: A secant pair whose two vectors are silently expressed in different tangent bases does not define a valid reduced update.
Positive definiteness is preserved only when the chosen update, curvature condition, and coordinate conversion provide that property.

notation.meaning: Reduced quasi-Newton approximation in the current tangent coordinates.
Complementary basis used for the normal coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Definiteness Preservation under Invertible Tangent Transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive definiteness before and after coordinate transport and BFGS updating.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0 and P_k is invertible, then \widetilde B_k=P_k^{-\mathsf T}B_kP_k^{-1}\succ0. A BFGS update of \widetilde B_k using a new-space pair (s_k,y_k) with s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0 also produces B_{k+1}\succ0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible congruence transport preserves positive definiteness, as does a subsequent positive-curvature BFGS update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde B_k\succ0\quad\text{and}\quad B_{k+1}\succ0.

notation.meaning: Updated reduced Hessian approximation in the new coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Transport of a Reduced Curvature Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact transfer of a reduced bilinear form between successive tangent-coordinate systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let u^+=P_ku with P_k\in\mathbb R^{r\times r} invertible. If the old reduced bilinear form is u^{\mathsf T}B_ku, its representation in the new coordinates is \widetilde B_k=P_k^{-\mathsf T}B_kP_k^{-1}, and (u^+)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde B_ku^+=u^{\mathsf T}B_ku. If P_k is orthogonal, \widetilde B_k=P_kB_kP_k^{\mathsf T}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible tangent-coordinate transport moves a reduced Hessian by inverse congruence and preserves its bilinear form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde B_k=P_k^{-\mathsf T}B_kP_k^{-1},\qquad (u^+)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde B_ku^+=u^{\mathsf T}B_ku.

notation.meaning: Coordinate transport between successive tangent-coordinate systems.
Old curvature form represented in the new coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Transport of a Reduced Curvature Form
Transported Reduced Quasi-Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasi-Newton updating after curvature pairs are transferred into a common tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be the regular equality manifold, let \(R\) be a retraction, and let \(\mathcal{T}_{\eta_k}:T_{x_k}M\to T_{x_{k+1}}M\) be a vector transport, where \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\). Define
\[s_k=\mathcal{T}_{\eta_k}(\eta_k),\qquad y_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1})-\mathcal{T}_{\eta_k}(\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)).\]
Transport the current reduced Hessian approximation to \(T_{x_{k+1}}M\), then apply a quasi-Newton update satisfying the transported secant equation \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). For a BFGS update, accept or damp the pair so that \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle>0\). Compute the next tangent direction from \(B_{k+1}\eta=-\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1})\), globalize it, and retract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature pairs and Hessian approximations are transported between successive tangent spaces before enforcing a reduced secant equation and computing the next direction.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth equality manifold and \(f\) is continuously differentiable on it.
\(R\) is a retraction and \(\mathcal{T}\) is a compatible vector transport.
Accepted BFGS pairs satisfy positive transported curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updated operator acts on the new tangent space and satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\).

notation.meaning: vector transport between successive tangent spaces
reduced Hessian approximation on the new tangent space

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal M=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:c(x)=0\}\) be a regular equality manifold and \(T_x\mathcal M=\ker \nabla c(x)^T\). At consecutive feasible iterates \(x_k,x_{k+1}\), let \(B_k:T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) be self-adjoint and let \(\mathcal T_k:T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\) be a specified linear transport.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic finite-dimensional formulation on a smooth regular equality manifold. The transport need not be parallel transport, but it must be explicitly defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transported reduced quasi-Newton method first transfers the old curvature operator to the new tangent space and then applies a secant update there. If \(\mathcal T_k\) is invertible, the transported operator is \[\widetilde B_k=\mathcal T_k^{-*}B_k\mathcal T_k^{-1}:T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\to T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M,\] where \(\mathcal T_k^{-*}=(\mathcal T_k^{-1})^*\). It then constructs \(s_k,y_k\in T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\), with \(s_k\ne0\), and defines \(B_{k+1}\) by a symmetric quasi-Newton update of \(\widetilde B_k\) satisfying \[B_{k+1}s_k=y_k.\] In orthonormal bases \(Z_k,Z_{k+1}\), an isometric transport has matrix \(Q_k=Z_{k+1}^T\mathcal T_kZ_k\) and transfers the reduced matrix by \(\widetilde M_k=Q_kM_kQ_k^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transported reduced quasi-Newton method treats reduced curvature as an operator attached to the current tangent space. Before imposing a new secant equation, it moves the previous operator into the next tangent space using a declared linear transport and the corresponding congruence transformation. Both vectors in the new secant pair then belong to the new tangent space, and a symmetric quasi-Newton update creates the next curvature operator. With orthonormal tangent bases and an isometric transport, the coordinate matrix is carried forward by orthogonal congruence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widetilde B_k=\mathcal T_k^{-*}B_k\mathcal T_k^{-1},\qquad B_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\qquad s_k,y_k\in T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For orthonormal coordinate bases and orthogonal \(Q_k\), transport is the matrix congruence \(M_k\mapsto Q_kM_kQ_k^T\).
special_cases_latex: If consecutive tangent spaces coincide and \(\mathcal T_k\) is the identity, the construction is an ordinary reduced quasi-Newton update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Self-adjointness is preserved by the congruence transport.
An isometric transport preserves eigenvalues and positive definiteness of the old reduced model before the new update.
boundary_notes: Projection alone may be noninvertible and therefore does not automatically define the congruence used here.
A precise authoritative source supporting this exact transported-operator definition was not located among the supplied hints.

children.title: Memory-Efficient Reduced Curvature Family
children.top_down_role: Storage-limited reduced curvature models for large nonlinear equality problems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\) of a smooth equality-constrained method, let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), \(r=n-m\), span the null space of the full-row-rank constraint Jacobian. Let \((s_i,y_i)\in\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^r\) be reduced secant pairs represented in a common current coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large finite-dimensional equality-constrained problems for which a dense \(r\times r\) reduced Hessian is too costly. The memory parameter \(\ell\) is fixed or much smaller than \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A memory-efficient reduced curvature model is a symmetric reduced quasi-Newton approximation \(M_k\) represented implicitly from a simple base matrix \(M_k^0\) and at most \(\ell\) recent reduced secant pairs, \[S_k=[s_{k-q},\ldots,s_{k-1}],\qquad Y_k=[y_{k-q},\ldots,y_{k-1}],\qquad q\le\ell\ll r.\] It permits products \(M_kv\), inverse products \(M_k^{-1}v\), or reduced subproblem solves without storing a dense \(r\times r\) matrix. An admissible compact form is \[M_k=M_k^0+U_kC_kU_k^T,\qquad U_k\in\mathbb R^{r\times O(\ell)},\] where \(U_k,C_k\) are determined by the retained pairs and the selected update, such as limited-memory BFGS or SR1. When tangent coordinates vary, all retained pairs must first be transported or re-expressed in the current coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A memory-efficient reduced curvature method approximates the Lagrangian Hessian only in the null-space coordinates and stores a bounded number of recent reduced secant pairs instead of a dense reduced matrix. A simple base matrix plus a low-rank compact representation supplies matrix-vector products, inverse products, or reduced subproblem operations. Old pairs are discarded as new pairs arrive. If the tangent basis changes, stored vectors must be converted to one common current coordinate system before the compact model is formed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\#\{(s_i,y_i)\text{ retained at iteration }k\}\le\ell,
\qquad M_k=M_k^0+U_kC_kU_k^T,
\qquad \operatorname{cols}(U_k)=O(\ell).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: An inverse limited-memory model may instead be applied by a two-loop recursion using the same retained pair set.
special_cases_latex: For \(\ell=0\), the model is the base matrix \(M_k^0\).
If \(r\) is small enough to retain all independent pairs, the construction may coincide with a full-memory reduced update.
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage is \(O(r\ell)\), compared with \(O(r^2)\) for a dense reduced matrix.
The model acts only on tangent coordinates and lifts to the ambient space through \(Z_k\).
boundary_notes: The BFGS curvature condition \(s_i^Ty_i>0\) is required when positive definiteness is claimed.
Discarding pairs changes the quasi-Newton model and generally forfeits full-memory superlinear behavior without additional assumptions.

notation.meaning: Maximum number of retained reduced secant pairs.
Simple initial or scaling matrix for the compact update.

children.title: Compact Reduced Curvature Representations
children.top_down_role: Low-storage representations of reduced quasi-Newton curvature information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage and matrix-vector cost of the compact reduced SR1 form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For reduced dimension \(r\) and \(q\) retained pairs, after factoring the \(q\times q\) matrix \(M\), one product \(B_qv\) requires one application of \(B_0\), \(O(rq)\) vector work, and \(O(q^2)\) dense triangular-solve work. Storing \(S\), \(Y\), and the small factorization requires \(O(rq+q^2)\) words instead of \(O(r^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact SR1 replaces a dense reduced matrix by pair storage and a small dense solve.
assumptions_latex: The compact SR1 representation is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{storage}=O(rq+q^2)\) and \(\operatorname{work}(B_qv)=\operatorname{work}(B_0v)+O(rq+q^2)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Compact SR1 Product Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact representation of successive symmetric-rank-one updates in fixed reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=[s_0,\ldots,s_{q-1}]\), \(Y=[y_0,\ldots,y_{q-1}]\), and \(B_0=B_0^{\mathsf T}\). Write \(S^{\mathsf T}Y=L+D+U\), where \(L,D,U\) are its strictly lower, diagonal, and strictly upper parts. If \[M=D+L+L^{\mathsf T}-S^{\mathsf T}B_0S\] is nonsingular, the matrix obtained from the corresponding non-skipped SR1 updates satisfies \[B_q=B_0+(Y-B_0S)M^{-1}(Y-B_0S)^{\mathsf T}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of reduced SR1 updates is represented by secant-pair blocks and one small symmetric matrix.
assumptions_latex: All pairs use one fixed reduced coordinate space.
The compact inner matrix \(M\) is nonsingular; skipped or dependent updates are removed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_q-B_0\) has rank at most \(q\) and has the displayed compact representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Reduced SR1 Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orthogonal Coordinate Covariance of Compact Curvature Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covariance of compact reduced quasi-Newton representations under an orthogonal change of fixed tangent coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) be orthogonal and set \[B_0'=Q^{\mathsf T}B_0Q,\qquad S'=Q^{\mathsf T}S,\qquad Y'=Q^{\mathsf T}Y.\] Then \(S'^{\mathsf T}Y'=S^{\mathsf T}Y\) and \(S'^{\mathsf T}B_0'S'=S^{\mathsf T}B_0S\). Consequently, the compact BFGS and SR1 inner matrices are unchanged and \[B_q'=Q^{\mathsf T}B_qQ.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rotating an orthonormal basis of a fixed tangent space rotates the represented curvature matrix while preserving the compact inner systems.
assumptions_latex: All secant pairs belong to one fixed reduced tangent space.
The relevant compact inner matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compact representation commutes with orthogonal coordinate changes: \(B_q'=Q^{\mathsf T}B_qQ\).
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonal Coordinate Covariance of Compact Curvature Forms

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular Compact SR1 Inner Matrix from a Skippable Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal example realizing breakdown of the unfiltered compact SR1 inverse formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r=q=1\), \(B_0=[1]\), and \(s_0=y_0=[1]\). Then \(Y-B_0S=0\) and the compact SR1 inner matrix is \[M=s_0^{\mathsf T}y_0-s_0^{\mathsf T}B_0s_0=0.\] Thus \(M^{-1}\) does not exist; this zero-correction pair must be omitted before the compact inverse formula is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pair already satisfying the secant equation can make the one-pair compact SR1 inner system singular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M=[0]\text{ is singular, so the unfiltered compact inverse formula is undefined}.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Compact SR1 Inner Matrix from a Skippable Pair
Compact Reduced Curvature Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact direct BFGS representation on a fixed reduced tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=[s_0,\ldots,s_{q-1}]\) and \(Y=[y_0,\ldots,y_{q-1}]\) contain reduced secant pairs satisfying \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i>0\), and let \(B_0\succ0\). Define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i)\) and the strictly lower-triangular matrix \(L\) by \(L_{ij}=s_i^{\mathsf T}y_j\) for \(i>j\). The matrix obtained by applying the corresponding BFGS updates admits the compact representation
\[
B_q=B_0-[B_0S,\,Y]\begin{bmatrix}S^{\mathsf T}B_0S&L\\L^{\mathsf T}&-D\end{bmatrix}^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}S^{\mathsf T}B_0\\Y^{\mathsf T}\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Thus reduced curvature products require only the stored pairs, the action of \(B_0\), and a dense system of order \(2q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of reduced BFGS updates is represented by stored secant pairs and a small dense matrix, avoiding storage of the full reduced Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(B_0\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(S,Y\in\mathbb R^{r\times q}\) and \(s_i^{\mathsf T}y_i>0\) for every retained pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_q=B_0-[B_0S,Y]\begin{bmatrix}S^{\mathsf T}B_0S&L\\L^{\mathsf T}&-D\end{bmatrix}^{-1}[S^{\mathsf T}B_0;Y^{\mathsf T}]\).

notation.meaning: Matrices of retained reduced steps and gradient differences.
Diagonal and strictly lower pair-product matrices.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Definiteness of the Limited-Memory Reduced Metric
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definiteness and descent for the implicit reduced inverse-BFGS operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H_0=H_0^{\mathsf T}\succ0. After any finite sequence of inverse-BFGS updates using reduced pairs (s_i,y_i) with y_i^{\mathsf T}s_i>0, the resulting implicit operator H_j is symmetric positive definite. Hence, for every g\ne0, p=-H_jg satisfies g^{\mathsf T}p<0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive initialization and positive-curvature pairs preserve a positive-definite limited-memory inverse metric and produce a strict reduced descent direction.
assumptions_latex: y_i^{\mathsf T}s_i>0\text{ for every applied pair}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_j\succ0\quad\text{and}\quad g^{\mathsf T}(-H_jg)<0.

notation.meaning: Implicit inverse reduced-curvature approximation after the retained updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Definiteness of the Limited-Memory Reduced Metric
Limited-Memory Reduced Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limited-memory inverse-BFGS recursion in reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reduced gradient \(g_k\in\mathbb R^r\), an initial inverse-curvature scaling \(H_k^0=\gamma_k I\) with \(\gamma_k>0\), and at most \(q\) pairs \((s_i,y_i)\) satisfying \(y_i^{\mathsf T}s_i>0\), set \(v=g_k\). In reverse storage order compute \(\alpha_i=\rho_i s_i^{\mathsf T}v\) and \(v\leftarrow v-\alpha_i y_i\), where \(\rho_i=(y_i^{\mathsf T}s_i)^{-1}\). Set \(w=H_k^0v\). In forward order compute \(\beta_i=\rho_i y_i^{\mathsf T}w\) and \(w\leftarrow w+s_i(\alpha_i-\beta_i)\). Output the reduced search direction \(p_k=-w\), discarding the oldest pair when a new accepted pair exceeds the memory limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced inverse-BFGS action is computed by a two-loop recursion using only a fixed number of accepted tangent-space secant pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k=-H_kg_k\), computed without explicitly forming \(H_k\).

children.title: Storage-Accuracy Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Effects of memory limits on reduced curvature fidelity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Low-Rank Reach of Retained Curvature Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise subspace limitation of a compact reduced-curvature correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If B=B_0+\Psi M\Psi^{\mathsf T} with \Psi\in\mathbb R^{r\times t} and t\le2q, then \operatorname{rank}(B-B_0)\le2q. Moreover, every z\in\ker(\Psi^{\mathsf T}) satisfies Bz=B_0z. For compact BFGS, \Psi generally depends on both retained gradient differences and B_0S, so this unchanged subspace cannot in general be characterized merely as the complement of \operatorname{span}(S,Y).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A q-pair compact correction has rank at most 2q and leaves the base operator unchanged on the null space of its compact right factor; that subspace generally depends on the base-scaled steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(B-B_0)\le2q,\qquad \Psi^{\mathsf T}z=0\Longrightarrow Bz=B_0z.

notation.meaning: Right factor in the compact curvature correction.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Reach of Retained Curvature Information
Storage-Accuracy Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank and resource consequences of retaining only finitely many reduced secant pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a reduced dimension \(r\) and memory limit \(q\), a compact BFGS matrix based on \(q\) retained pairs satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(B_q-B_0)\le 2q\). Storing the pair matrices costs \(O(rq)\) scalars, and a limited-memory two-loop inverse product costs \(O(rq)\) arithmetic operations. Increasing \(q\) preserves curvature information from more recent updates but does not, without additional assumptions on the Hessian sequence or pair selection, guarantee a monotone decrease in model error. When \(q\ll r\), curvature outside the span generated by the retained steps and gradient differences is governed by the initial scaling rather than independently learned secant data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Memory q gives linear storage and product cost, but captures only a low-rank curvature correction and does not ensure monotone model accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(B_q\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) has a compact BFGS representation using at most \(q\) pairs.
Arithmetic cost counts dense reduced vector operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(B_q-B_0)\le 2q\), with storage and inverse-product cost \(O(rq)\).

children.title: Large-Scale Tangent Updates
children.top_down_role: Storage-conscious curvature maintenance in changing tangent spaces.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete Pair Loss Under Orthogonal Tangent Change
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-dimensional example showing failure of naive projected transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let the old one-dimensional tangent basis be \(Z=e_1\) and the new basis be \(\widehat Z=e_2\). Then \(T=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Z=0\). The valid old reduced pair \(s=y=1\), with \(s^{\mathsf T}y=1>0\), is transported to \(Ts=Ty=0\), so all stored curvature information is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal old and new tangent lines turn a strictly positive secant pair into the zero pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive old curvature does not prevent complete loss under cross-tangent projection.

notation.meaning: standard coordinate vectors in two dimensions

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Pair Loss Under Orthogonal Tangent Change

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information loss when old tangent vectors are projected into a different tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) and \(\widehat Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times\widehat r}\) be orthonormal tangent bases and set \(T=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Z\). Its singular values are the cosines of the principal angles between the tangent spaces. Thus \(\|Ts\|\le\|s\|\), and an old direction is annihilated when its ambient vector is orthogonal to the new tangent space. Moreover, \[(Ts)^{\mathsf T}(Ty)=s^{\mathsf T}Z^{\mathsf T}\widehat Z\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Zy\] need not equal \(s^{\mathsf T}y\). Positivity and secant quality must therefore be rechecked after projected transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection between different tangent spaces can shrink or erase pairs and can alter their secant curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cross-tangent projection is generally contractive rather than isometric and does not preserve secant curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Principal-Angle Loss Under Tangent Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Transport Under a Basis Rotation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lossless reduced-pair transport when only orthonormal coordinates change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Z,\widehat Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) are orthonormal bases of the same tangent subspace. Then \(Q=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Z\) is orthogonal, and an ambient tangent vector \(v=Zs\) has new coordinates \(\widehat s=Qs\). For any reduced pair \((s,y)\), \[(Qs)^{\mathsf T}(Qy)=s^{\mathsf T}y,\qquad \|Qs\|=\|s\|.\] Hence simultaneous transport by \(Q\) preserves norms, secant curvature, and positive-curvature acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the tangent subspace is unchanged, the cross-basis matrix is an orthogonal coordinate rotation and transports curvature pairs without loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Z\) is orthogonal and preserves reduced inner products.

notation.meaning: coordinate-change matrix between bases of the same tangent subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Transport Under a Basis Rotation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic for norm loss, secant curvature, and dependence after projected transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Z\), \(\widehat s_i=Ts_i\), and \(\widehat y_i=Ty_i\). For prescribed \(\tau_s,\tau_y,\tau_c,\tau_G>0\), retain only pairs satisfying
\[\|\widehat s_i\|\ge\tau_s\|s_i\|,\quad \|\widehat y_i\|\ge\tau_y\|y_i\|,\quad \widehat s_i^{\mathsf T}\widehat y_i\ge\tau_c\|\widehat s_i\|\|\widehat y_i\|.\]
After rejecting zero transported steps, let \(G\) be the Gram matrix of their normalized vectors. The additional test \(\lambda_{\min}(G)\ge\tau_G\) certifies the declared numerical-independence threshold. Failure identifies excessive norm loss, inadequate relative curvature, or dependence but does not prescribe repair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Post-transport tests can detect pair shrinkage, poor curvature, and numerical dependence without selecting a repair policy.
assumptions_latex: Zero transported steps are rejected before normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Passing certifies the declared lower bounds on norm retention, relative curvature, and normalized-step independence.

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of normalized transported step vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Tangent Pair-Retention Diagnostic

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and storage cost when consecutive tangent bases are explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), \(\widehat Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times\widehat r}\), and \(q\) retained pairs, forming \(T=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Z\) costs \(O(nr\widehat r)\) arithmetic and \(O(r\widehat r)\) storage. Transporting both vectors of all pairs costs \(O(qr\widehat r)\) arithmetic and stores \(O(q\widehat r)\) reduced coordinates. Retaining both explicit bases requires \(O(n(r+\widehat r))\) words.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit cross-tangent transport is dominated by the cross-basis product and its application to the retained archive.
assumptions_latex: Both tangent bases are stored explicitly and densely.
Basis construction and diagnostic Gram-matrix costs are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{work}=O(nr\widehat r+qr\widehat r)\), with incremental transport storage \(O(r\widehat r+q\widehat r)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Cross-Basis Transport Cost

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and storage for retaining old tangent pairs as ambient vectors and projecting them into a new explicit tangent basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(q\) old tangent pairs are retained as ambient vectors \((\bar s_i,\bar y_i)\in\mathbb R^n\), and the new tangent basis \(\widehat Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times\widehat r}\) is explicit. Forming \(\widehat s_i=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}\bar s_i\) and \(\widehat y_i=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}\bar y_i\) for all pairs costs \(O(qn\widehat r)\) dense arithmetic. The pair archive uses \(O(qn)\) storage and the new basis uses \(O(n\widehat r)\); neither the old basis nor an explicit cross-basis matrix is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ambient pair storage avoids an explicit cross-basis matrix but uses ambient-size archive storage.
assumptions_latex: The new tangent basis is stored explicitly and densely.
Both vectors of every retained pair are stored in ambient coordinates.
Basis construction and filtering costs are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{work}=O(qn\widehat r),\qquad \operatorname{storage}=O(qn+n\widehat r).

notation.meaning: Ambient representations of retained tangent secant pairs.
Dimension of the new tangent basis.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambient-Vector Archive Reprojection Cost
Large-Scale Tangent Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transport and filtering of limited-memory pairs when the tangent basis changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_k}\) and \(Z_{k+1}\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_{k+1}}\) have orthonormal columns spanning consecutive tangent spaces. For each retained reduced pair \((s_i,y_i)\), form transported pairs \(\widehat s_i=T_ks_i\) and \(\widehat y_i=T_ky_i\), where \(T_k=Z_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}Z_k\). Discard a transported pair if its norm is negligible or if \(\widehat s_i^{\mathsf T}\widehat y_i\le\eta\lVert\widehat s_i\rVert\lVert\widehat y_i\rVert\) for a prescribed \(\eta>0\). Append the newly measured pair in the current basis, retain at most \(q\) pairs, and apply the limited-memory recursion in \(\mathbb R^{r_{k+1}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Old reduced pairs are projected into the new tangent basis, filtered for curvature quality, and combined with the newest pair under a memory limit.
assumptions_latex: All retained pairs are represented in the coordinates of \(Z_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((s_i,y_i)\mapsto(T_ks_i,T_ky_i)\), followed by curvature filtering and truncation to at most \(q\) pairs.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis of the current tangent space.
Coordinate transport between consecutive tangent bases.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, but no evidence is supplied for transporting both secant vectors by Z_{k+1}^{T}Z_k, especially when tangent dimensions or subspaces change. Such projection can lose secant information and curvature, so the transport and filtering rule requires an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let the old one-dimensional tangent basis be \(Z=e_1\) and the new basis be \(\widehat Z=e_2\). Then \(T=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}Z=0\). The valid old reduced pair \(s=y=1\), with \(s^{\mathsf T}y=1>0\), is transported to \(Ts=Ty=0\), so all stored curvature information is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal old and new tangent lines turn a strictly positive secant pair into the zero pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive old curvature does not prevent complete loss under cross-tangent projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Pair Loss After a Tangent Rotation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and storage for a matrix-free cross-tangent archive that retains ambient vectors instead of an explicit cross-basis matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(q\) old tangent pairs are retained as ambient vectors \((\bar s_i,\bar y_i)\in\mathbb R^n\), and the new tangent basis \(\widehat Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times\widehat r}\) is explicit. Forming new reduced coordinates \(\widehat s_i=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}\bar s_i\) and \(\widehat y_i=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}\bar y_i\) for all pairs costs \(O(qn\widehat r)\) dense arithmetic. The archive requires \(O(qn)\) storage, the new basis requires \(O(n\widehat r)\), and no \(r\times\widehat r\) cross-basis matrix or old explicit basis is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping secant vectors in ambient coordinates avoids forming the cross-basis matrix, at the cost of ambient-size pair storage.
assumptions_latex: The new tangent basis is stored explicitly and densely.
Both vectors of each retained pair are stored in ambient coordinates.
Basis construction and filtering costs are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{work}=O(qn\widehat r),\qquad \operatorname{storage}=O(qn+n\widehat r).

children.title: Feasibility Management for Reduced Methods
children.top_down_role: Feasible-start requirements, nonlinear feasibility restoration, and local safeguards intrinsic to reduced-space methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define the violation measure \(h(x)=\|c(x)\|\). A reduced method proposes tangential or reduced-coordinate trial moves that satisfy the constraints only to first order unless a separate correction is applied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear equality constraints. Both feasible-start and infeasible-start reduced methods are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility-management mechanism is a collection \((\mathcal I,\mathcal N,\mathcal R,\mathcal S)\) consisting of: an initialization rule \(\mathcal I\) producing \(x_0\) with \(h(x_0)\le\varepsilon_0\); a normal-step rule \(\mathcal N\) producing \(v_k\) that reduces or minimizes \(\|c(x_k)+A_kv\|\); a restoration rule \(\mathcal R\), invoked when prescribed acceptance or compatibility tests fail, that returns \(x_k^R\) with \(h(x_k^R)\le\eta_Rh(x_k)\) for a stated \(\eta_R<1\), or terminates at a stationary point of the chosen violation problem; and safeguards \(\mathcal S\) that bound corrections and reject steps outside the regular neighborhood. In a feasibility-preserving variant, \(\varepsilon_0=0\) and every accepted iterate satisfies \(c(x_k)=0\). In an infeasible variant, the mechanism instead controls a declared sequence of violation tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility management for a reduced method is the explicit part of the method responsible for producing an admissible starting point, computing normal corrections to the linearized equalities, invoking restoration when a reduced trial move cannot be accepted, and enforcing safeguards that keep corrections inside a region where the constraint model is reliable. A feasible method requires every accepted iterate to satisfy the nonlinear equalities. An infeasible method declares tolerances and sufficient-reduction conditions for the constraint residual. Restoration either reaches the required reduction or reports stationarity for the selected feasibility problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h(x_0)\le\varepsilon_0,\qquad v_k\approx\arg\min_v\|c(x_k)+A_kv\|,\qquad h(x_k^R)\le\eta_Rh(x_k)\ \text{when restoration succeeds}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Feasibility management may be expressed through a normal–tangential decomposition in which only the normal component is charged with reducing the linearized residual.
special_cases_latex: Exact feasible reduction uses \(\varepsilon_0=0\) and a manifold return map after every tangential trial move.
Filter methods may trigger restoration after repeated rejection or an excessively small trial step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced objective step and the feasibility correction have separate mathematical acceptance obligations.
boundary_notes: This definition does not require restoration to find a feasible point when the equality system is inconsistent.
Merit-function or filter globalization beyond feasibility management is not fixed here.

notation.meaning: Selected norm of the equality residual.

children.title: Feasible-Point Initialization
children.top_down_role: Routes for obtaining a starting point compatible with feasibility-preserving reduced methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuous and define \(\mathcal M=\{x\in\mathcal D:c(x)=0\}\). Let \(\bar x\in\mathcal D\) be supplied data and let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization for equality-constrained reduced methods. Exact initialization uses zero tolerance; approximate initialization is included only when the downstream method explicitly permits it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible-point initialization rule is a possibly partial map \[\mathcal I:(c,\bar x,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}})\mapsto(x_0,\sigma_0)\] whose successful status \(\sigma_0=\mathrm{success}\) certifies \[x_0\in\mathcal D,\qquad \|c(x_0)\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}.\] For a feasibility-preserving reduced method, the defining requirement is \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}=0\). The rule may construct \(x_0\) directly for affine constraints, solve the nonlinear equations \(c(x)=0\), minimize a residual merit function such as \(\tfrac12\|c(x)\|^2\), or correct a transferred near-feasible state. A failure status must not be interpreted as a feasible initialization. If residual minimization terminates with positive residual, it supplies an approximate initial point only when that residual meets the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible-point initializer accepts the equality mapping, a supplied estimate, and a feasibility tolerance. On success it returns a point in the domain together with a certificate that the equality residual is at most that tolerance. A method that preserves feasibility exactly requires zero tolerance. The initializer can use a direct affine solve, a nonlinear-equation solve, residual minimization, or correction of a nearby state, but merely stopping a feasibility solver does not establish success. A positive-residual stationary point is admissible only for a downstream algorithm that explicitly accepts that residual level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sigma_0=\mathrm{success}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_0\in\mathcal D\ \text{and}\ \|c(x_0)\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact initialization is the selection of an element \(x_0\in\mathcal M\).
Approximate initialization is selection from the residual tube \(\mathcal M_\varepsilon=\{x:\|c(x)\|\le\varepsilon\}\).
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints \(c(x)=Ax-b\), initialization reduces to solving \(Ax_0=b\).
For a square nonlinear system with nonsingular Jacobian near a root, Newton corrections are a local initialization route.
immediate_consequences_latex: An exactly feasible initial point allows tangent-space methods to begin on the equality manifold.
boundary_notes: Residual minimization can terminate at a positive-residual stationary point and therefore is not itself a feasibility certificate.
The definition does not claim that \(\mathcal M\) is nonempty.
