children.title: Affine Feasible-Point Construction
children.top_down_role: Direct and least-norm initialization for affine equality systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Feasible-Point Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct and minimum-norm solutions of a consistent affine equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the affine constraints \(Ax=b\), with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). The system is feasible exactly when \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). In that case every feasible point has the representation \(x=A^{\dagger}b+z\), where \(z\in\ker(A)\), and the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm feasible point is \(x_{\min}=A^{\dagger}b\). If \(A\) has full row rank, then \(A^{\dagger}=A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\), so \(x_{\min}=A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}b\). A prescribed reference point \(x_r\) may instead be projected to feasibility by \(x_0=x_r-A^{\dagger}(Ax_r-b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent affine system is initialized using its pseudoinverse; this gives either the minimum-norm solution or the feasible projection of a reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax=b\}=A^{\dagger}b+\ker(A)\), and \(x_{\min}=A^{\dagger}b\).

notation.meaning: Reference point to be projected onto the affine set.

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Linear Least-Squares Problems p. 106

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Linear Least-Squares Problems p. 106

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVD construction and consistency test for an affine equality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\mathsf T}\) be the compact exact SVD formed from the nonzero singular values of \(A\). Define \(x_0=V_r\Sigma_r^{-1}U_r^{\mathsf T}b\) and \(r_b=(I-U_rU_r^{\mathsf T})b\). Then \(r_b=0\) if and only if \(Ax=b\) is consistent; upon consistency, \(x_0=A^\dagger b\) is the minimum-norm feasible point. A finite-precision implementation must separately declare rank and residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SVD tests affine consistency and constructs the minimum-norm feasible point.
assumptions_latex: The exact statement uses the nonzero singular values of \(A\).
Finite-precision use declares rank and consistency tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_b=0\iff b\in\operatorname{range}(A),\qquad r_b=0\Rightarrow x_0=A^\dagger b.

notation.meaning: Component of the right-hand side orthogonal to the range of A.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Revealing Feasible Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact left-null-space certificate for inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), the system \(Ax=b\) is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left-null-space vector having nonzero inner product with the right-hand side certifies affine infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax=b\text{ is infeasible}\iff\exists y:\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y\ne0.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Infeasibility Alternative

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-change affine initialization in a positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\succ0\), let \(A\) have full row rank, and let \(x_r\) be prescribed. The unique minimizer of \(\tfrac12\|x-x_r\|_W^2\) subject to \(Ax=b\) is \(x_0=x_r-W^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}(AW^{-1}A^{\mathsf T})^{-1}(Ax_r-b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reference point can be projected onto the affine feasible set in a positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}\tfrac12\|x-x_r\|_W^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Projection to Affine Feasibility

children.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Solve
children.top_down_role: Initialization through a nonlinear-equation or residual-minimization phase.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Feasibility Solve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-minimization initialization for smooth nonlinear equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For smooth constraints \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), choose \(x_0\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\ge0\). At iteration \(j\), let \(J_j=\nabla c(x_j)\) and compute a regularized Gauss–Newton correction
\[
d_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert c(x_j)+J_jd\rVert^2+\tfrac{\mu_j}{2}\lVert d\rVert^2,
\]
where \(\mu_j\ge0\). Choose a step length \(\alpha_j\in(0,1]\) that decreases \(\tfrac12\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\), and set \(x_{j+1}=x_j+\alpha_jd_j\). Stop with a feasible initializer when \(\lVert c(x_j)\rVert\le\varepsilon_c\); otherwise report failure when the prescribed iteration or safeguarding limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialization minimizes the squared constraint residual with safeguarded Gauss–Newton steps until the required feasibility tolerance is met or failure is declared.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert c(x_j)\rVert\le\varepsilon_c\) on successful termination.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the current feasibility iterate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of residual stationarity to certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x)=x^2+1\), let \(\phi(x)=\tfrac12(x^2+1)^2\). Then \(\phi'(0)=0\) while \(c(0)=1\), and the equality \(c(x)=0\) has no real solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual minimization can stop at a stationary point with positive residual, including when the equality system is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi'(0)=0\quad\text{and}\quad \phi(0)=\tfrac12>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Stationary Residual Point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative structure of the nonlinear feasibility objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\phi(x)=	frac12\|c(x)\|^2\), \(
abla\phi(x)=J(x)^{\mathsf T}c(x)\). If \(c\) is twice continuously differentiable, then \(
abla^2\phi(x)=J(x)^{\mathsf T}J(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(x)
abla^2c_i(x)\). Moreover, \(\phi(x)=0\) if and only if \(c(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear feasibility is a nonnegative residual-minimization problem whose Gauss–Newton curvature is the Jacobian Gram matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable; the Hessian formula additionally requires twice continuous differentiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla\phi=J^{\mathsf T}c,\qquad \phi=0\iff c=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Squared-Residual Feasibility Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local residual rate for the unregularized minimum-norm feasibility phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(c(x_*)=0\), \(J(x_*)\) has full row rank, and \(J\) is locally Lipschitz. If \(x_j\) is sufficiently near \(x_*\) and the feasibility phase uses the full unregularized minimum-norm correction \(d_j=-J_j^{\mathsf T}(J_jJ_j^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(x_j)\), then \(\|c(x_j+d_j)\|=O(\|c(x_j)\|^2)\). This rate is not asserted for a regularization sequence bounded away from zero or for persistently damped steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full unregularized Gauss–Newton feasibility corrections have quadratic local residual reduction near a regular zero; persistent damping or regularization can change the rate.
assumptions_latex: \(J(x_*)\) has full row rank and \(J\) is locally Lipschitz.
The displayed full unregularized step is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Full-Step Gauss–Newton Residual Rate

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable. The initialization target is a point in \(\mathcal M=\{x\in\mathcal D:c(x)=0\}\), or a point meeting a declared residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear equality initialization. Square Newton steps and rectangular least-squares steps are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear feasibility solve is an auxiliary computation whose primary problem is \[c(x)=0,\] or, when a root method is unavailable or globalization is required, the residual problem \[\min_{x\in\mathcal D}\ \psi(x)=\tfrac12\|c(x)\|_2^2.\] At an iterate \(z_j\), a Newton correction satisfies \(A_jp_j=-c(z_j)\) when this system has an appropriate solution. A Gauss–Newton or least-squares correction minimizes \(\|A_jp+c(z_j)\|_2\), possibly subject to a trust region. The solve is successful for initialization only if its returned point \(x_0\) satisfies \(\|c(x_0)\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\); stationarity \(A(x_0)^Tc(x_0)=0\) with positive residual is not equivalent to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear feasibility solve treats the equality constraints as a nonlinear system or minimizes their squared residual. Newton steps solve the linearized equality equations, while Gauss–Newton or trust-region variants minimize the linearized residual when a direct correction is unsuitable. The output becomes a valid initial point only after its nonlinear equality residual meets the declared tolerance. A stationary point of the residual objective can have nonzero residual and therefore does not certify feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\psi(x)=\tfrac12\|c(x)\|_2^2,\qquad \nabla\psi(x)=A(x)^Tc(x),\qquad \mathrm{success}\Longrightarrow\|c(x_0)\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}.\]

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c(\cdot;\theta):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be a parameterized equality mapping. Suppose \(\hat x\) is available from a nearby parameter \(\hat\theta\), and a target problem uses \(\theta_0\). Let \(\mathcal P_{\hat\theta\to\theta_0}\) be a declared transfer map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start initialization for related smooth equality-constrained problems. It covers parameter continuation and transferred states but does not presume that transfer preserves feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transferred near-feasible initialization consists of a predictor \[x_0^{\mathrm{pred}}=\mathcal P_{\hat\theta\to\theta_0}(\hat x)\] satisfying a declared neighborhood and residual test \[\|c(x_0^{\mathrm{pred}};\theta_0)\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pred}},\] followed, when required, by a correction map \(\mathcal C_{\theta_0}\) giving \[x_0=\mathcal C_{\theta_0}(x_0^{\mathrm{pred}}),\qquad \|c(x_0;\theta_0)\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}.\] A first-order corrector may solve \(A_0p=-c(x_0^{\mathrm{pred}};\theta_0)\) and set \(x_0=x_0^{\mathrm{pred}}+p\), possibly iterating or globalizing this correction. The initializer is exact only when the final residual is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transferred near-feasible initialization reuses a state from a related problem. A declared transfer map predicts a target-problem state, the target equality residual is tested, and a correction phase is applied if the residual exceeds the method's initialization tolerance. A typical correction solves the target linearized equalities. Transfer alone is not a feasibility certificate; the final target residual determines whether initialization succeeded and whether it is exact or approximate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_0^{\mathrm{pred}}=\mathcal P_{\hat\theta\to\theta_0}(\hat x),\qquad x_0=\mathcal C_{\theta_0}(x_0^{\mathrm{pred}}),\qquad \|c(x_0;\theta_0)\|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In continuation form, \(\mathcal P\) is a parameter predictor and \(\mathcal C\) is a nonlinear-equation corrector.
special_cases_latex: If \(c(\hat x;\theta_0)=0\), the identity correction is admissible.
If the problems differ only slightly, the transferred state may already meet a positive feasibility tolerance.
immediate_consequences_latex: Warm-start quality is measured against the target constraints, not the source constraints.
boundary_notes: No authoritative locator supporting this exact family definition was located among the supplied hints.
Closeness in Euclidean distance does not by itself imply a small constraint residual without regularity bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a previous solution at \(\theta^-\), form either the zero-order predictor \(x_p=x(\theta^-)\) or an available sensitivity predictor for \(\theta^+\). Apply a local feasibility corrector to \(c(x,\theta^+)=0\), and return the corrected point to the receiving reduced method only if that method's declared initialization test succeeds. If correction or admission fails, return a fallback status for full feasibility initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start predicts from the previous problem, corrects feasibility locally, and either passes the receiving method's admission test or falls back to full initialization.

The receiving method declares its admission test and fallback status.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of a nearby parameterized solution followed by a normal feasibility correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the parameterized problem \(c(x,\theta)=0\), suppose a previously computed point \(x^-\) corresponds to \(\theta^-\), and a new parameter \(\theta^+\) is given. Initialize \(\widetilde x_0=x^-\), or use an available predictor for \(x(\theta^+)\). With \(J_0=\nabla_xc(\widetilde x_0,\theta^+)\), compute
\[
n_0=-J_0^{\mathsf T}(J_0J_0^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(\widetilde x_0,\theta^+)
\]
when \(J_0\) has full row rank, and set \(x_0=\widetilde x_0+n_0\). Accept \(x_0\) as a warm start only if its residual meets the initialization tolerance; otherwise invoke a full nonlinear feasibility solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearby previous solution is transferred to the new problem, corrected in the normal space, and accepted only after a residual test.
assumptions_latex: \(J_0\) has full row rank when the displayed correction is used.
\(x^-\) solves or approximately solves the nearby problem at \(\theta^-\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-parameterized admission of a small-residual regular initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable with \(m\le n\), and let the receiving reduced method declare a norm, a residual tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\ge0\), and, when regular-manifold reduction is required, a Jacobian margin \(\sigma_*>0\). The point \(x_0\) passes that method's near-feasible admission test when \(\|c(x_0)\|\le\varepsilon_c\) and, if required, \(\sigma_{\min}(J(x_0))\ge\sigma_*\). These are declared algorithmic thresholds, not universal mathematical constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A receiving method may admit a near-feasible point using its declared residual, scaling, and regularity thresholds.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable and \(m\le n\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local relation between equality residual and distance to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\{x:c(x)=0\}\). If \(c\) is continuously differentiable, \(\bar x\in M\), and \(J(\bar x)\) has full row rank, then there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa>0\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,M)\le\kappa\|c(x)\|\) for every \(x\in U\).

assumptions_latex: \(c(\bar x)=0\) and \(J(\bar x)\) has full row rank.

Near-Feasible Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and regularity test for admitting an inexact initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable and let \(J(x)=\nabla c(x)\). For prescribed tolerances \(\varepsilon_c\ge0\) and \(\sigma_*>0\), a point \(x_0\) is an admissible near-feasible initializer when
\[
\lVert c(x_0)\rVert\le\varepsilon_c
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sigma_{
min}(J(x_0))\ge\sigma_*.
\]
The first inequality bounds initial constraint violation; the second excludes an initially rank-deficient equality linearization. If either test fails, initialization must be restored, regularized, or rejected rather than treated as locally feasible. The norm and tolerances are fixed by the algorithm and scaling convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A near-feasible point must satisfy both a constraint-residual tolerance and a lower bound on the smallest singular value of the constraint Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: The norm, \(\varepsilon_c\), and \(\sigma_*\) are prescribed consistently with constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\lVert c(x_0)\rVert\le\varepsilon_c\) and \(\sigma_{
min}(J(x_0))\ge\sigma_*\).

children.title: Transferred Multiplier Initialization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-squares correction of a transferred equality multiplier at a new primal initializer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Lagrangian convention \(L=f+\lambda^{\mathsf T}c\), let \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(J_0=\nabla c(x_0)\). If \(J_0\) has full row rank, the unique multiplier minimizing \(\|g_0+J_0^{\mathsf T}\lambda\|\) is \(\lambda_{\mathrm{ls}}=-(J_0J_0^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J_0g_0\). A transferred multiplier may be retained only if it passes the receiving method's declared stationarity-residual test; otherwise \(\lambda_{\mathrm{ls}}\) provides the unregularized corrected initializer.

Then \(\|\lambda(\theta^+)-\lambda(\theta^-)\|=O(\|\theta^+-\theta^-\|)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer and stationarity-based correction of equality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_x f(x,\theta)\) subject to \(c(x,	heta)=0\), transfer a previous multiplier \(\lambda^-\) to obtain a candidate \(\widetilde\lambda_0\) for the new parameter. At the new primal initializer \(x_0\), let \(g_0=\nabla_x f(x_0,	heta^+)\) and \(J_0=\nabla_x c(x_0,	heta^+)\). If \(J_0\) has full row rank, replace or correct the transferred value by the least-squares stationarity estimate
\[
\lambda_0=-(J_0J_0^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J_0g_0,
\]
which uniquely minimizes \(\lVert g_0+J_0^{\mathsf T}\lambda\rVert\). When transfer is trusted, the same estimate may be regularized toward \(\widetilde\lambda_0\); the chosen \(\lambda_0\) is retained only if its stationarity residual passes the initialization test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previous multiplier may be transferred, but it is checked or replaced by the least-squares multiplier minimizing the new stationarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(J_0\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_0=-(J_0J_0^{\mathsf T})^{-1}J_0g_0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lambda}\lVert g_0+J_0^{\mathsf T}\lambda\rVert\).

children.title: Initialization Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Perturbation and conditioning limits governing useful transfer from nearby states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a transferable feasible branch at a singular equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x,\theta)=x^2-\theta\), the branch \(x(\theta)=\sqrt\theta\) exists for \(\theta>0\), but \(D_xc(0,0)=0\), \(dx/d\theta=1/(2\sqrt\theta)\) diverges as \(\theta\downarrow0\), and no real feasible point exists for \(\theta<0\). Thus arbitrarily small parameter changes do not ensure a valid or well-conditioned transfer across the fold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fold, a feasible branch becomes singular and may disappear under an arbitrarily small parameter change.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_xc(0,0)=0,\qquad \theta<0\Rightarrow\{x:c(x,\theta)=0\}=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Fold Boundary for Solution Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local existence and sensitivity of a transferable primal-dual KKT branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(z,\theta)=0\) be the parameterized equality-constrained KKT equations, with \(z=(x,\lambda)\). If \(F\) is continuously differentiable, \(F(z_*,\theta_*)=0\), and \(D_zF(z_*,\theta_*)\) is nonsingular, then there are neighborhoods in which a unique continuously differentiable solution branch \(z(\theta)\) exists. Consequently \(\|z(\theta)-z_*\|=O(\|\theta-\theta_*\|)\). This guarantee does not extend beyond the local branch or through loss of KKT-Jacobian nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nearby primal-dual solution is transferable within a neighborhood supporting a unique smooth KKT branch; branch exit or singularity ends the guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,z(\theta)\text{ locally},\qquad \|z(\theta)-z_*\|=O(\|\theta-\theta_*\|).
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Transfer Neighborhood
Initialization Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which transferred primal-dual initialization loses local validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A transferred primal-dual pair \((x^-,\lambda^-)\) is not certified as a valid local initializer for a new equality-constrained problem merely because the parameter change is small. Local transfer requires the new constraint residual and stationarity residual to lie within prescribed tolerances and the new Jacobian to retain full row rank. In particular, validity fails whenever
\[
\lVert c(x^-,\theta^+)\rVert>\varepsilon_c,
\quad
\lVert\nabla_x f(x^-,\theta^+)+J(x^-,\theta^+)^{\mathsf T}\lambda^-\rVert>\varepsilon_s,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\sigma_{
min}(J(x^-,\theta^+))<\sigma_*.
\]
Rank loss, branch switching, or a parameter jump outside the local regularity neighborhood therefore requires restoration or reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred solution becomes invalid when feasibility, stationarity, or Jacobian-regularity tests fail; branch changes and rank loss require reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\lVert c\rVert>\varepsilon_c\) or \(\lVert\nabla_x f+J^{\mathsf T}\lambda^-\rVert>\varepsilon_s\) or \(\sigma_{
min}(J)<\sigma_*\) invalidates local transfer acceptance.

children.title: Feasibility-Restoration Maps
children.top_down_role: Return mechanisms used after a tangent or reduced-coordinate trial move.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(h(x)=\|c(x)\|\), and let \(U\subseteq\mathcal D\) be a neighborhood in which feasibility corrections are attempted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local or algorithmic restoration for smooth nonlinear equalities. The map may restore exact feasibility or only produce a prescribed residual contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility-restoration map is a possibly partial map \(R:U\to\mathcal D\) equipped with a success test such that, whenever it succeeds at \(z\in U\), \[h(R(z))\le\tau_R h(z),\qquad 0\le\tau_R<1.\] An exact restoration map additionally satisfies \[c(R(z))=0\quad\text{and}\quad R(x)=x\ \text{for every feasible }x\in U.\] In a reduced method, \(z\) is typically a point obtained after a tangent or reduced-coordinate trial move. An iterative restoration routine defines such a map by its returned point, provided the routine's stopping rule certifies the stated reduction. If restoration terminates at a stationary point of \(h\) without the required reduction, the map is undefined or reports failure at that input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-restoration map takes a trial point and, on success, returns a point whose equality residual is reduced by a declared strict factor. An exact restoration map returns a feasible point and fixes every already feasible point. An iterative feasibility phase counts as a map through its output only when its stopping test certifies the required reduction. Termination at an infeasible stationary point is a failure unless the residual already meets the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[h(R(z))\le\tau_Rh(z),\quad \tau_R<1;\qquad \text{exact restoration: }c(R(z))=0\text{ and }R|_{\mathcal M}=\operatorname{id}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact restoration is a local retraction onto the feasible set in the set-theoretic sense \(R(U)\subseteq\mathcal M\) and \(R|_{\mathcal M}=\operatorname{id}\).
special_cases_latex: One or more Newton feasibility corrections can implement a local restoration map.
A restoration phase minimizing \(h\) implements an inexact map when it reaches the specified contraction.
immediate_consequences_latex: Applying an exact restoration after each accepted tangent move yields feasible accepted iterates.
boundary_notes: A contraction map need not land exactly on the equality manifold.
The source supports restoration by minimizing violation but does not canonically name the resulting input-output procedure a restoration map.

children.title: Newton Feasibility Corrections
children.top_down_role: Local nonlinear-equation corrections toward the equality manifold.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton Feasibility Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-norm Newton correction toward a regular equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable and let \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)\) have full row rank. Compute the minimum-norm Newton correction as the solution of
\[
J_kd_k=-c(x_k),
\qquad
d_k=-J_k^{\mathsf T}(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(x_k).
\]
Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by a residual-decrease safeguard and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Stop when \(\lVert c(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon_c\). If \(J_k\) is rank deficient or the full Newton correction does not provide adequate residual reduction, the displayed map is not used without regularization, damping, or a least-squares restoration step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum-norm solution of the linearized equality equations supplies a damped Newton correction toward the feasible manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(J_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
A residual-decrease safeguard and tolerance \(\varepsilon_c\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-J_k^{\mathsf T}(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(x_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric characterization of the minimum-norm Newton feasibility correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, the unique minimum-norm solution of \(Jd=-c\) is \(d=-J^{\mathsf T}(JJ^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c\). It lies in \(\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})=\ker(J)^\perp\), and every solution is \(d+z\) with \(z\in\ker(J)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum-norm Newton feasibility correction is orthogonal to the linearized tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T}),\qquad \{v:Jv=-c\}=d+\ker(J).
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Space Characterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local residual estimate for an undamped minimum-norm Newton feasibility correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) have a locally Lipschitz Jacobian, let \(c(x_*)=0\), and suppose \(J(x_*)\) has full row rank. For \(x\) sufficiently near \(x_*\), set \(d=-J(x)^{\mathsf T}(J(x)J(x)^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(x)\). Then \(\|d\|=O(\|c(x)\|)\) and \(\|c(x+d)\|=O(\|c(x)\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular feasible point, a full minimum-norm Newton correction leaves a quadratically small constraint residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Quadratic Residual Reduction

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable and let \(A(z)=\nabla c(z)^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). A current point \(z\in\mathcal D\) need not be feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth nonlinear equality correction. Square Newton systems and underdetermined full-row-rank systems are both covered through a selected solution of the linearized equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Newton feasibility correction at \(z\) is any vector \(p_N\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying the linearized equality equations \[A(z)p_N=-c(z).\] The corrected point is \(z^+=z+p_N\), or \(z^+=z+\alpha p_N\) in a damped variant with \(0<\alpha\le1\). If \(m=n\) and \(A(z)\) is nonsingular, the correction is uniquely \(p_N=-A(z)^{-1}c(z)\). If \(m<n\) and \(A(z)\) has full row rank, the minimum-norm Newton correction is \[p_N=-A(z)^T\bigl(A(z)A(z)^T\bigr)^{-1}c(z).\] Repeating this construction defines a local nonlinear-equation correction process toward \(c(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Newton feasibility correction solves the linearized equality constraints at the current point and adds that solution to the point, possibly with damping. For a square nonsingular Jacobian the correction is unique. For an underdetermined full-row-rank Jacobian, the canonical normal correction is the minimum-Euclidean-norm solution obtained with the right pseudoinverse. The correction enforces the linearized equations exactly, although the corrected point generally retains a higher-order nonlinear residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A(z)p_N=-c(z),\qquad z^+=z+p_N,\qquad p_N^{\min}=-A(z)^T(A(z)A(z)^T)^{-1}c(z).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The minimum-norm correction solves \(\min_p\tfrac12\|p\|_2^2\) subject to \(A(z)p=-c(z)\).
special_cases_latex: At a feasible point, \(p_N=0\) is the minimum-norm correction.
For affine \(c(x)=Ax-b\), a full Newton correction produces an exactly feasible point.
immediate_consequences_latex: The minimum-norm correction belongs to \(\operatorname{range}(A(z)^T)\), the linearized normal space.
boundary_notes: The linearized equations may be inconsistent when the Jacobian is rank deficient.
A full Newton correction need not reduce the nonlinear residual far from the feasible manifold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence of undamped minimum-norm Newton corrections to a regular equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) have a locally Lipschitz Jacobian, and suppose \(c(x_*)=0\) and \(J(x_*)\) has full row rank. For \(x_k\) sufficiently near \(x_*\), define \(d_k=-J_k^{\mathsf T}(J_kJ_k^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(x_k)\). Then \(J_kd_k=-c(x_k)\), \(\|d_k\|=O(\|c(x_k)\|)\), and \(\|c(x_k+d_k)\|=O(\|c(x_k)\|^2)\). Consequently, full corrections reduce the feasibility residual quadratically while the iterates remain in the regular neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular feasible point, a full minimum-norm Newton correction cancels the linearized residual and leaves a quadratically small nonlinear residual.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz Jacobian.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the current point.

children.top_down_role: Normal-space corrections for ill-conditioned or locally inconsistent linearizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Normal Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized normal-space correction for inconsistent or ill-conditioned linearized equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a point \(x_k\), let \(r_k=c(x_k)\) and \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)\). For \(\mu_k>0\), compute
\[
d_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\lVert J_kd+r_k\rVert^2+\tfrac{\mu_k}{2}\lVert d\rVert^2,
\]
 equivalently by \((J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k+\mu_kI)d_k=-J_k^{\mathsf T}r_k\). The solution lies in \(\operatorname{range}(J_k^{\mathsf T})\) and is therefore a normal-space correction. Choose a safeguarded step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and accept the correction only when the nonlinear residual decreases sufficiently. Positive regularization makes the subproblem uniquely solvable even when \(J_k\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized least-squares solve produces a unique normal correction even when the linearized constraints are inconsistent or the Jacobian is rank deficient.
assumptions_latex: The step is accepted through a nonlinear residual-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k+\mu_kI)d_k=-J_k^{\mathsf T}c(x_k)\) with \(d_k\in\operatorname{range}(J_k^{\mathsf T})\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for the least-squares normal-correction subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mu>0\), a vector \(d\) is the unique minimizer of
\[
\phi(d)=\tfrac12\|Jd+r_0\|^2+\tfrac\mu2\|d\|^2
\]
if and only if
\[
J^{\mathsf T}(Jd+r_0)+\mu d=0.
\]
At this minimizer, \(\phi(d)\le\phi(0)=\tfrac12\|r_0\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing regularized normal-equation residual exactly certifies the unique correction, whose model value cannot exceed the zero-step value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\) is optimal iff \(J^{\mathsf T}(Jd+r_0)+\mu d=0\), and then \(\phi(d)\le\phi(0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Normal-Equation Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic and storage cost of the seed algorithm when implemented by dense formation and Cholesky factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dense \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), explicitly forming \(J^{\mathsf T}J+\mu I\) costs \(O(mn^2)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(n^2)\) storage. Because \(\mu>0\), the matrix is positive definite; a dense Cholesky factorization costs \(O(n^3)\), followed by \(O(n^2)\) triangular solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct dense primal normal-equation implementation costs O(m n squared plus n cubed) work and O(n squared) storage.
assumptions_latex: \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is treated as dense.
The shifted primal normal equations are formed explicitly and solved by dense Cholesky factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{work}=O(mn^2+n^3)\) and \(\text{storage}=O(n^2)\).
review_flags: The bound is implementation-specific and does not cover sparse, matrix-free, dual, QR, or SVD solvers.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Shifted-Normal-Equation Cost

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model Decrease Does Not Guarantee Nonlinear Residual Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance boundary separating the regularized subproblem from nonlinear feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Even when \(d_\mu\) uniquely minimizes the regularized linear model, a full step need not reduce \(\|c(x)\|\), since
\[
c(x+d_\mu)=c(x)+J(x)d_\mu+O(\|d_\mu\|^2).
\]
For example, with \(c(t)=1+t+4t^2\), \(x=0\), and \(\mu=1\), the regularized scalar step is \(d_\mu=-1/2\), but
\[
|c(-1/2)|=3/2>|c(0)|=1.
\]
Thus regularization guarantees model solvability, not nonlinear feasibility improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint curvature can make a model-optimal full correction increase the actual residual, so damping or an explicit decrease test is required.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) has a locally Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x\).
\(d_\mu\) solves the regularized linearized least-squares problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model optimality alone does not imply \(\|c(x+d_\mu)\|<\|c(x)\|\).
knowledge_statements.title: Model Decrease Does Not Guarantee Nonlinear Residual Decrease

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular-Value Filtering of the Regularized Normal Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral representation and limiting behavior of the Tikhonov correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) have positive singular values \(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r\). The unique regularized correction is
\[
d_\mu=-\sum_{i=1}^r\frac{\sigma_i}{\sigma_i^2+\mu}(u_i^{\mathsf T}r_0)v_i.
\]
Consequently, \(d_\mu\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\), small-singular-value components are damped,
\[
d_\mu\to-J^\dagger r_0\quad(\mu\downarrow0),
\qquad d_\mu\to0\quad(\mu\to\infty).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization filters poorly determined singular-vector components and interpolates between the pseudoinverse correction and the zero step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_\mu=-\sum_{i=1}^r\sigma_i(\sigma_i^2+\mu)^{-1}(u_i^{\mathsf T}r_0)v_i\), with the stated limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Filtering of the Regularized Normal Correction

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\), and let \(\Delta_k>0\) be an optional correction radius.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear equalities when the linearized system may be inconsistent, ill-conditioned, rank deficient, or deliberately solved only approximately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A least-squares normal correction is a solution or admissible approximate solution of \[\min_{v\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12\|A_kv+c(x_k)\|_2^2\quad\text{subject, optionally, to }\|v\|_2\le\zeta\Delta_k,\] where \(0<\zeta<1\) reserves room for a later tangential step. In the unconstrained-radius case, every minimizer satisfies \[A_k^T(A_kv+c(x_k))=0.\] If minimizers are nonunique, the normal correction is canonically selected as the minimum-norm minimizer. Its linearized residual \(r_k=A_kv_k+c(x_k)\) is retained as the attainable residual for the subsequent tangential subproblem. When \(A_k\) has full row rank and the radius is inactive, \(r_k=0\) and the minimum-norm correction equals \(-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-squares normal correction minimizes the norm of the linearized equality residual, optionally inside a fraction of the current trust region. It remains defined when the linearized equations cannot be solved exactly. The residual at the selected correction records the amount of linearized infeasibility that remains and can be imposed in the later tangential subproblem. If the Jacobian has full row rank and the radius does not bind, the construction reduces to the minimum-norm exact normal correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[v_k\in\arg\min_{\|v\|\le\zeta\Delta_k}\|A_kv+c_k\|_2^2,
\qquad r_k=A_kv_k+c_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Without the trust-region bound, the optimality condition is \(A_k^Tr_k=0\).
The bounded problem is a linear least-squares trust-region subproblem.
special_cases_latex: If \(A_k=0\), the minimum-norm correction is \(v_k=0\) and the entire residual remains.
If \(c(x_k)=0\), \(v_k=0\) is optimal.
immediate_consequences_latex: The least-squares residual is orthogonal to \(\operatorname{range}(A_k)\) when the radius is inactive.
The trust-region fraction prevents the normal correction from consuming the whole step budget.
boundary_notes: The correction minimizes a linearized residual, not necessarily the nonlinear residual \(\|c(x_k+v)\|\).
Rank deficiency can make the minimizer nonunique unless a minimum-norm convention is imposed.

notation.meaning: Fraction of the trust-region radius allocated to the normal step.
Residual of the linearized constraints after the normal correction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linearized Decrease Does Not Guarantee Nonlinear Residual Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance boundary separating the regularized subproblem from nonlinear feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Even when \(d_\mu\) uniquely minimizes the regularized linear model, a full step need not reduce \(\|c(x)\|\), because
\[
c(x+d_\mu)=c(x)+J(x)d_\mu+O(\|d_\mu\|^2).
\]
Therefore nonlinear residual decrease requires a sufficiently small accepted step or an explicit merit decrease test. Rank regularization guarantees solvability of the model but does not by itself guarantee nonlinear feasibility improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization makes the linear subproblem well posed, but curvature can make a full correction increase the true constraint residual.

\(d_\mu\) solves the regularized linearized least-squares problem.

children.title: Feasible-Manifold Return Map Family
children.top_down_role: Geometric maps returning trial points to or toward the feasible manifold.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal M=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:c(x)=0\}\) be a regular embedded manifold, with \(c\) continuously differentiable and \(\nabla c(x)^T\) full row rank on a neighborhood of \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometric return of tangent trial moves to the exact feasible manifold. This is stronger than mere residual reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible-manifold return-map family is a collection of local maps \[R_x:V_x\subseteq T_x\mathcal M\to\mathcal M,\qquad x\in\mathcal M,\] satisfying \[R_x(0)=x,\qquad DR_x(0)[\xi]=\xi\quad\text{for every }\xi\in T_x\mathcal M.\] Thus a tangent trial vector \(\xi\) is converted into the feasible point \(x^+=R_x(\xi)\), and \[c(x^+)=0,\qquad R_x(\xi)=x+\xi+o(\|\xi\|).\] A second-order return family additionally satisfies \(R_x(\xi)=x+\xi+O(\|\xi\|^2)\) uniformly in a stated neighborhood. The map may be implemented by local projection, dependent-variable elimination, or a converged nonlinear feasibility correction, provided these defining identities hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible-manifold return map assigns to each feasible base point a local mapping from its tangent space back to the equality manifold. It fixes the zero tangent vector and has the identity as its derivative at zero, so it preserves the intended tangent direction to first order. Every returned point is exactly feasible. Projection, local elimination, and converged nonlinear correction are implementations only when they satisfy these identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R_x(0)=x,\qquad DR_x(0)=\operatorname{id}_{T_x\mathcal M},\qquad c(R_x(\xi))=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The family is a retraction on the regular equality manifold.
In ambient coordinates, \(R_x(\xi)=x+\xi+o(\|\xi\|)\) with image contained in \(\mathcal M\).
special_cases_latex: For affine \(\mathcal M\), \(R_x(\xi)=x+\xi\) is an exact global return map.
A locally unique nearest-point projection defines a return map on a sufficiently small tubular neighborhood.
immediate_consequences_latex: Accepted points generated through \(R_x\) satisfy the nonlinear equalities exactly.
The return map does not alter the tangent trial direction to first order.
boundary_notes: A single damped Newton correction generally reduces infeasibility but need not map exactly onto \(\mathcal M\).
No precise authoritative locator for this retraction-style definition was found among the supplied sources.

notation.meaning: Local return map based at the feasible point \(x\).

review_flags: Needs a differential-geometric or reduced-optimization source explicitly supporting the return-map identities.

children.title: Feasible-Set Projection Maps
children.top_down_role: Maps selecting nearby points on the equality-feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Set Projection Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Euclidean projection onto a regular equality-constraint manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(\mathcal M=\{x:c(x)=0\}\), and suppose \(J(x)=Dc(x)\) has full row rank near \(\bar x\in\mathcal M\). On a neighborhood \(U\) where the nearest point is unique, the feasible-set projection is \[P(y)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathcal M}\frac12\|z-y\|^2.\] It satisfies \(P(y)\in\mathcal M\), \(P(x)=x\) for \(x\in U\cap\mathcal M\), and \[DP(x)=I-J(x)^{\mathsf T}\bigl(J(x)J(x)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)^{-1}J(x),\qquad x\in U\cap\mathcal M.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local feasible-set projection sends nearby points to their unique nearest feasible points and has the tangent-space orthogonal projector as its derivative on the manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(c(\bar x)=0\) and \(J(\bar x)\) has full row rank.
The nearest feasible point is unique on \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(U)\subseteq\mathcal M\), \(P|_{U\cap\mathcal M}=\operatorname{id}\), and \(DP(x)\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normality and Idempotence of Local Nearest-Point Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characteristic local properties of Euclidean projection onto a regular equality manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P(y)\) be the unique local Euclidean projection of \(y\) onto the regular manifold \(\mathcal M=\{z:c(z)=0\}\). Then
\[
P(P(y))=P(y),\qquad y-P(y)\in N_{P(y)}\mathcal M=\operatorname{range}(J(P(y))^{\mathsf T}).
\]
Because \(J(P(y))\) has full row rank, there is a unique \(\lambda(y)\) satisfying
\[
y-P(y)=J(P(y))^{\mathsf T}\lambda(y),\qquad c(P(y))=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearest-point projection is locally idempotent, and its displacement is normal to the manifold with a unique projection multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M=c^{-1}(0)\) is a regular embedded manifold locally.
The nearest feasible point \(P(y)\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^2=P\) locally and \(y-P(y)=J(P(y))^{\mathsf T}\lambda(y)\) for a unique \(\lambda(y)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Normality and Idempotence of Local Nearest-Point Projection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection as a First-Order Tangent Return Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local expansion of nearest-point projection along a tangent displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathcal M\), let \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\), and suppose the local nearest-point projection \(P\) is \(C^2\) near \(x\). Then
\[
P(x+v)=x+v+O(\|v\|^2)
\]
as \(v\to0\). Hence \(R_x(v):=P(x+v)\) is a local first-order retraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a small tangent trial point changes it only by second order and therefore induces a local retraction.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection as a First-Order Tangent Return Map

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection as a Second-Order Tangent Return Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local expansion of nearest-point projection along a tangent displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathcal M\), let \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\), and suppose the local nearest-point projection \(P\) is \(C^2\). Then, as \(v\to0\),
\[
P(x+v)=x+v+O(\|v\|^2).
\]
Thus \(R_x(v):=P(x+v)\) is a first-order retraction on its local domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting a small tangent trial point changes it only by second order, so nearest-point projection induces a local retraction.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is \(C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(x\in\mathcal M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Manifold Retraction Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order retractions used to return tangent steps to the feasible manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a smooth embedded manifold with tangent bundle \(T\mathcal M\). A manifold retraction is a smooth map \(R\) defined on a neighborhood of the zero section of \(T\mathcal M\) such that, for every \(x\in\mathcal M\), \[R_x(0)=x,\qquad DR_x(0)[v]=v\quad\text{for every }v\in T_x\mathcal M.\] Thus \(R_x(v)\in\mathcal M\), and in ambient coordinates \(R_x(v)=x+v+O(\|v\|^2)\) as \(v\to0\) within \(T_x\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retraction smoothly maps a tangent step back to the manifold, fixes the base point, and agrees with tangent displacement to first order.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is a smooth embedded manifold.
\(R\) is smooth near the zero section of \(T\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_x(v)\in\mathcal M\) and \(R_x(v)=x+v+O(\|v\|^2)\) for tangent \(v\to0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Diffeomorphism Property of a Retraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertibility of a retraction in tangent coordinates near the zero vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be a smooth retraction on \(\mathcal M\). For each \(x\in\mathcal M\),
\[
DR_x(0)=I_{T_x\mathcal M}.
\]
Consequently, there are neighborhoods \(V\subset T_x\mathcal M\) of \(0\) and \(U\subset\mathcal M\) of \(x\) such that \(R_x:V\to U\) is a diffeomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every smooth retraction is locally invertible in tangent coordinates around the zero step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_x\) is a local diffeomorphism at \(0\in T_x\mathcal M\).

notation.meaning: Neighborhood of zero in the tangent space.
Neighborhood of the base point on the manifold.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Projection Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-based local approximation to exact feasible-manifold projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathcal M=\{z:c(z)=0\}\), and let \(s\in\ker J(x)\) be sufficiently small. A map \(Q_x\) is an approximate projection of order \(p\ge1\) if \[Q_x(0)=x,\qquad Q_x(s)=x+s+O(\|s\|^2),\qquad \|c(Q_x(s))\|=O(\|s\|^{p+1}).\] The constants in the order bounds are uniform for \(x\) in the stated local neighborhood. Unlike an exact projection, \(Q_x(s)\) need not lie in \(\mathcal M\); its defining guarantee is the prescribed residual order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate projection preserves a tangent step to first order while reducing the resulting equality residual to a specified asymptotic order.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is sufficiently smooth for the asserted order.
The order constants are locally uniform.

children.title: Map Validity Neighborhoods

knowledge_statements.title: Map Validity Neighborhoods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local conditions under which a specified feasible-manifold return map is well-defined and uniformly regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(\mathcal M=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c(x)=0\}\), let \(\bar x\in\mathcal M\), and set \(J(x)=Dc(x)\). For a specified return map \(R:\mathcal D\to\mathbb{R}^n\), a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) is a validity neighborhood if there are constants \(\gamma,L_R>0\) such that \[\sigma_{\min}(J(x))\ge\gamma\qquad(x\in U),\] the restricted map \(R|_{\mathcal D_U}\) is single-valued, satisfies \(R(\mathcal D_U)\subseteq U\), and obeys \[\|R(u)-R(v)\|\le L_R\|u-v\|\qquad(u,v\in\mathcal D_U),\] where \(\mathcal D_U\subseteq\mathcal D\) is the stated local domain. Any residual-order estimate assigned to \(R\) must additionally hold on \(\mathcal D_U\) with constants uniform over that domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validity neighborhood is a local region where the specified return map is single-valued, remains local, is uniformly Lipschitz, preserves constraint regularity, and satisfies its claimed residual estimates uniformly.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\in\mathcal M\).
\(R:\mathcal D\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is a specified projection, retraction, or correction map with a stated local domain \(\mathcal D_U\).
The displayed rank, locality, single-valuedness, Lipschitz, and applicable residual conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is a neighborhood on which the specified return map is locally valid with uniform regularity and residual constants.

local domain of the specified return map associated with U

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct breakdown mechanisms for the constraint-based projection guarantee and for projection single-valuedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nearest-point map onto \(\mathcal M=c^{-1}(0)\), two distinct events invalidate the stated regular local guarantee. If
\[
\sigma_{\min}(J(P(y)))=0,
\]
the full-row-rank constraint representation and its Jacobian-inverse formulas cease to be justified, although the set itself may still possess a smooth projection under another representation. Independently, if distinct \(z_1,z_2\in\mathcal M\) satisfy
\[
\|y-z_1\|=\|y-z_2\|=\operatorname{dist}(y,\mathcal M),
\]
nearest-point projection is not single-valued. The latter failure can occur while both nearest points are regular; for example, the center of a circle has every point on the circle as a nearest point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank loss invalidates the stated constraint-based projection formulas, while multiple nearest points invalidate the projection map itself; these failures must not be conflated.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M=c^{-1}(0)\) is considered with Euclidean nearest-point projection.
The claims concern loss of a previously stated local guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Jacobian rank loss ends the representation-based guarantee, whereas nearest-point nonuniqueness ends single-valuedness of the projection.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from y to the feasible set.

review_flags: Corrected the builder claim: rank loss need not destroy an intrinsically smooth projection when the chosen equality representation is singular or redundant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp geometric events that terminate a local nearest-point projection guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A local nearest-point projection remains a single-valued smooth return map only while the projected point stays regular and the nearest feasible point is unique. Its validity guarantee ends upon either
\[
\sigma_{\min}(J(P(y)))=0
\]
or the existence of distinct \(z_1,z_2\in\mathcal M\) with
\[
\|y-z_1\|=\|y-z_2\|=\operatorname{dist}(y,\mathcal M).
\]
Rank loss destroys the regular-manifold formula, while nonunique nearest points destroy single-valuedness even if both projected points are regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection neighborhood fails at constraint-rank loss or at the medial set where a point has multiple nearest feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M=c^{-1}(0)\) is considered with Euclidean nearest-point projection.
The statement concerns the boundary of a previously valid local projection neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rank loss or nearest-point nonuniqueness invalidates the corresponding local smooth single-valued projection guarantee.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from y to the feasible manifold.

children.title: Normal–Tangential Step Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of a trial correction into feasibility and reduced-objective components.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal–Tangential Decomposition of an Equality Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Let \(Z_k\) span \(\ker A_k\), and let \(Y_k\) be a complementary basis such that \([Y_k\mid Z_k]\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained step models. Orthogonality is optional unless explicitly imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A normal–tangential decomposition of a trial step is \[p_k=v_k+t_k=Y_kp_k^Y+Z_kp_k^Z,\] where the normal component is responsible for the linearized equality residual and the tangential component satisfies \[A_kt_k=0.\] For an exact linearized-feasibility step, \[A_kv_k=-c(x_k),\qquad A_kp_k+c(x_k)=0.\] For a relaxed or least-squares normal step, set \(r_k=A_kv_k+c(x_k)\) and require the full step to preserve that residual, \[A_kp_k+c(x_k)=r_k.\] The tangential coordinates are then selected to improve a reduced objective or Lagrangian model subject to any remaining step restrictions. If \(Y_k\) spans \(\operatorname{range}(A_k^T)\) and both bases are orthonormal, the two components are orthogonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal–tangential step writes the trial correction as a feasibility component plus a component in the null space of the constraint Jacobian. The normal component solves or approximately solves the linearized equalities. The tangential component leaves the achieved linearized residual unchanged and is chosen to improve the objective model. With orthogonal range-space and null-space bases, the decomposition is orthogonal and unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[p_k=v_k+t_k,\qquad A_kt_k=0,\qquad A_kp_k+c_k=A_kv_k+c_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In complementary coordinates, \(p_k=Y_kp_k^Y+Z_kp_k^Z\).
With the orthogonal projector \(P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k\), one may write \(t_k=P_kw_k\).
special_cases_latex: At a feasible point, the minimum-norm normal component is zero and a first-order feasible step is purely tangential.
For affine equalities, every tangential displacement preserves exact feasibility once the normal component reaches the affine set.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing \(t_k\) cannot change the linearized residual achieved by \(v_k\).
If the decomposition is orthogonal, \(\|p_k\|_2^2=\|v_k\|_2^2+\|t_k\|_2^2\).
boundary_notes: A tangent step preserves nonlinear feasibility only to first order for nonlinear constraints.
Without a specified complementary subspace, the normal component need not be unique.

notation.meaning: Linearized residual left by the normal component.

The components need not be orthogonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite step is the sum of a feasibility-oriented normal component and a model-reducing tangential component that maintains the normal step's feasibility gains. The components need not be orthogonal.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Feasibility Component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Least-norm normal-space step for reducing the linearized equality residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable, let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(c_x=c(x)\) and \(J=Dc(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and choose \(\Delta_n>0\). Compute \[n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T}),\ \|v\|\le\Delta_n}\frac12\|c_x+Jv\|^2.\] If \(J\) has full row rank and the radius constraint is inactive at the solution, then the unique minimizer in \(\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\) is \[n=-J^{\mathsf T}(JJ^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c_x,\] and it satisfies \(c_x+Jn=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal component minimizes the linearized equality residual over the Jacobian normal space and a prescribed normal-step radius; with full row rank and an inactive radius, it is the displayed least-norm exact correction.
assumptions_latex: Full row rank and an inactive radius are required only for the displayed closed form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(n\) minimizes \(\|c(x)+Jv\|\) over \(v\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\) with \(\|v\|\le\Delta_n\).

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the current point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for the Euclidean radius-constrained normal least-squares component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Delta_n>0\), a vector \(n\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\) solves \[\min_{v\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T}),\ \|v\|\le\Delta_n}\frac12\|c_x+Jv\|^2\] if and only if there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \[J^{\mathsf T}(c_x+Jn)+\lambda n=0,\qquad \|n\|\le\Delta_n,\qquad \lambda(\|n\|^2-\Delta_n^2)=0.\] Thus \(\lambda=0\) gives the unrestricted normal-space least-squares certificate, while \(\lambda>0\) certifies an active normal-step boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radius-constrained normal step is optimal exactly when its least-squares gradient is balanced by a nonnegative radius multiplier and primal feasibility and complementarity hold.
assumptions_latex: The norm and normal space are Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda\ge0:\ J^{\mathsf T}(c_x+Jn)+\lambda n=0,\ \|n\|\le\Delta_n,\ \lambda(\|n\|^2-\Delta_n^2)=0.

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the normal-step radius constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Radius-Constrained Normal-Step Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained least-norm normal correction and residual characterization without a full-row-rank assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c_x\in\mathbb R^m\), and consider \[\min_{v\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})}\frac12\|c_x+Jv\|^2.\] The unique minimizer is \[n_*=-J^\dagger c_x.\] Its residual is \[r_*=c_x+Jn_*=(I-JJ^\dagger)c_x=P_{\ker J^{\mathsf T}}c_x,\] and satisfies \(J^{\mathsf T}r_*=0\). Exact linearized feasibility is attainable precisely when \(c_x\in\operatorname{range}(J)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rank-deficient Jacobian, the unrestricted normal-space least-squares problem has the unique pseudoinverse correction, while the unrecoverable residual is the projection onto the left null space.
assumptions_latex: No active normal-step radius is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n_*=-J^\dagger c_x,\quad r_*=P_{\ker J^{\mathsf T}}c_x,\quad J^{\mathsf T}r_*=0.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the constraint Jacobian.
Orthogonal projector onto the left null space.

children.title: Tangential Optimization Component
children.top_down_role: The component devoted to objective improvement within the tangent model.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangential Optimization Component
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-model improvement within the linearized equality-feasible tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable at \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Given a normal component \(n\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g=\nabla f(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(J=Dc(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), choose a symmetric matrix \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and a radius \(\Delta>0\), and compute \[t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ Ju=0,\ \|n+u\|\le\Delta}\left[g^{\mathsf T}(n+u)+\frac12(n+u)^{\mathsf T}B(n+u)\right].\] Output the combined trial step \(s=n+t\). Because \(Jt=0\), the tangential component does not change the linearized equality residual produced by \(n\): \(c(x)+J(n+t)=c(x)+Jn\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangential component minimizes the quadratic objective model over tangent directions that keep the combined step within its radius and leave the normal component's linearized equality residual unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The tangential feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(Jt=0\), \(\|n+t\|\le\Delta\), and minimizes the stated quadratic model over the tangential feasible set.

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the current point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient trust-region optimality conditions in orthonormal null-space coordinates, including the zero-radius boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_R=Z^\mathsf{T}BZ\), \(g_R=Z^\mathsf{T}(g+Bn)\), and \(\delta^2=\Delta^2-\|n\|^2\ge0\). If \(\delta=0\), the sole feasible reduced vector \(p_\star=0\) is globally optimal. If \(\delta>0\), a vector \(p_\star\) globally minimizes \[g_R^\mathsf{T}p+\tfrac12p^\mathsf{T}H_Rp\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|p\|\le\delta\] if and only if there exists \(\sigma\ge0\) such that \[(H_R+\sigma I)p_\star=-g_R,\qquad H_R+\sigma I\succeq0,\qquad \|p_\star\|\le\delta,\qquad \sigma(\|p_\star\|-\delta)=0.\] Then \(t_\star=Zp_\star\) is a globally optimal tangential component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero remaining radius forces the zero tangential step; otherwise shifted positive semidefiniteness, stationarity, radius feasibility, and complementarity certify global tangential optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_\star=Zp_\star\) globally solves the tangential quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangential Quadratic Global-Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space-coordinate representation of the tangential quadratic optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}\) form a basis of \(\ker J\). Every tangential vector has the unique form \(t=Zp\). For \(q(s)=g^\mathsf{T}s+\tfrac12s^\mathsf{T}Bs\), the tangential subproblem with fixed normal component \(n\) is equivalent, up to the constant \(q(n)\), to \[\min_{p\in\mathbb{R}^d}\ \bigl(Z^\mathsf{T}(g+Bn)\bigr)^\mathsf{T}p+\tfrac12p^\mathsf{T}(Z^\mathsf{T}BZ)p\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|n+Zp\|\le\Delta.\] If \(Z\) is orthonormal and \(n\in\operatorname{range}(J^\mathsf{T})\), the radius constraint becomes \(\|p\|^2\le\Delta^2-\|n\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space basis converts tangential optimization into a reduced quadratic problem; under Euclidean orthogonality, the remaining radius is explicit.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker J\).
For the simplified radius formula, \(Z^\mathsf{T}Z=I\) and \(n\in\operatorname{range}(J^\mathsf{T})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t=Zp,\qquad H_R=Z^\mathsf{T}BZ,\qquad g_R=Z^\mathsf{T}(g+Bn).\)

notation.meaning: Null-space basis for the constraint Jacobian.

children.title: Normal-Tangential Compatibility Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where feasibility and objective components conflict or require coupled control.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal–Tangential Compatibility Boundary for a Composite Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be smooth, let \(A_k=Jc(x_k)\), and let \(\Delta>0\) be a trust-region radius. A composite step is written \(p=v+u\), where \(v\in\operatorname{Range}(A_k^T)\) is a normal feasibility step and \(u\in\operatorname{Null}(A_k)\) is a tangential optimization step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality constraints with a Euclidean trust region and a normal–tangential decomposition at one iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a prescribed normal-step fraction \(\zeta\in(0,1)\), define \(V_k(\Delta)=\{v:\|v\|_2\leq\zeta\Delta\}\) and \(T_k(v,\Delta)=\{u:A_ku=0,\ \|v+u\|_2\leq\Delta\}\). The normal–tangential compatibility boundary is \[\mathcal B_k=\{(v,\Delta):v\in V_k(\Delta),\ T_k(v,\Delta)\neq\varnothing,\ \sup_{u\in T_k(v,\Delta)}\|u\|_2=0\}.\] More generally, its quantitative \(\tau\)-boundary is \(\mathcal B_k(\tau)=\{(v,\Delta):\sup_{u\in T_k(v,\Delta)}\|u\|_2=\tau\Delta\}\). A pair lies on the strict compatibility side when this supremum exceeds \(\tau\Delta\), and on the conflict side when it is smaller.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an equality-constrained iterate, a normal step consumes part of the available trust-region radius to reduce the linearized constraint residual, while a tangential step must remain in the null space of the constraint Jacobian and keep the composite step inside the trust region. The compatibility boundary consists of the normal-step and radius pairs for which the remaining admissible tangential motion has exactly a prescribed size. At the zero-size boundary, the normal component leaves no nonzero tangential step available. Thus the definition identifies precisely where feasibility control and objective reduction cease to have independent room within the same step budget.
assumptions_latex: The composite step is constrained by \(\|v+u\|_2\leq\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B_k(\tau)=\{(v,\Delta):\sup\{\|u\|_2:A_ku=0,\ \|v+u\|_2\leq\Delta\}=\tau\Delta\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(v\perp\operatorname{Null}(A_k)\), compatibility is measured explicitly by \(\sup_{u\in T_k(v,\Delta)}\|u\|_2=(\Delta^2-\|v\|_2^2)^{1/2}\).
For orthogonal normal and tangential spaces, \((v,\Delta)\in\mathcal B_k(\tau)\) iff \(\|v\|_2=\Delta\sqrt{1-\tau^2}\).
special_cases_latex: The common restriction \(\|v\|_2\leq0.8\Delta\) guarantees residual tangential radius at least \(0.6\Delta\) when the decomposition is orthogonal.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\|v\|_2=\Delta\), only \(u=0\) is compatible under orthogonality.
Bounding the normal step by a strict fraction of \(\Delta\) prevents complete consumption of the composite-step budget.
boundary_notes: This definition concerns geometric compatibility of the two components, not acceptance of the resulting trial point by a merit function or filter.
For non-Euclidean norms or oblique decompositions, the square-root formula need not hold, although the set-valued definition remains applicable.

children.title: Normal-Component Interference
children.top_down_role: Effects of feasibility corrections on intended tangential progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Component Interference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region and quadratic-model effects introduced by the normal component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(n\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\), let \(t\in\ker J\), and suppose \(\|n+t\|\le\Delta\) for \(\Delta>0\). Then \[n^{\mathsf T}t=0,\qquad \|n+t\|^2=\|n\|^2+\|t\|^2,\qquad \|t\|\le\sqrt{\Delta^2-\|n\|^2}.\] Hence \(\|n\|=\Delta\) permits no nonzero tangential component. For a quadratic model \(q(p)=g^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}Bp\), where \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, the normal component also contributes \(g^{\mathsf T}n\), \(\tfrac12n^{\mathsf T}Bn\), and \(n^{\mathsf T}Bt\) to \(q(n+t)\); these terms can oppose model decrease while the normal component improves feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal component consumes part of the shared step radius and contributes its own linear, quadratic, and interaction terms to the objective model, which can limit tangential model improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric for the stated quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|t\|\le\sqrt{\Delta^2-\|n\|^2}\), and the normal component contributes explicit terms that can reduce attainable quadratic-model decrease.

children.title: Tangential-Component Interference
children.top_down_role: Effects of optimization motion on constraint restoration.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangential-Component Interference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear feasibility error generated by a linearly tangent component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and set \(J=Dc(x)\). Suppose \(n,t\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(c(x)+Jn=r\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(Jt=0\). With \(s=n+t\), as \(s\to0\), \[c(x+s)=r+\frac12D^2c(x)[s,s]+o(\|s\|^2).\] Thus the tangential component leaves the linearized residual unchanged but generally contributes the curvature terms \(D^2c(x)[n,t]\) and \(\tfrac12D^2c(x)[t,t]\). Consequently, a tangential component can increase nonlinear equality violation even though it is tangent to the linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangential component preserves the normal component's linearized residual but can create second-order equality violation through constraint curvature and normal-tangential interaction.
assumptions_latex: The combined step \(s=n+t\) tends to zero.

notation.meaning: residual after the normal linearized correction

knowledge_statements.title: Component Compatibility Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic and radius conditions for a compatible normal-tangential decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable at \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(J=Dc(x)\), and let \(\Delta>0\) and \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\). A normal component \(n\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and a tangential component \(t\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are compatible with radius \(\Delta\) and residual target \(r\) when \[n\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T}),\qquad c(x)+Jn=r,\qquad Jt=0,\qquad \|n+t\|\le\Delta.\] Because \(\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\) is orthogonal to \(\ker J\), the radius condition is equivalently \(\|n\|^2+\|t\|^2\le\Delta^2\). The combined step preserves the target residual: \(c(x)+J(n+t)=r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible normal and tangential components achieve the selected linearized residual, keep the tangential component in the Jacobian null space, and satisfy the shared step radius.
assumptions_latex: The displayed normal-space, residual, tangency, and radius conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x)+J(n+t)=r\) and \(\|n+t\|\le\Delta\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Control Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the shared Euclidean radius for orthogonal normal and tangential components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(n\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\), let \(t\in\ker J\), and choose \(\Delta>0\). Since \(n^{\mathsf T}t=0\), the admissible coupled-control set is \[\mathcal C_\Delta=\{(n,t)\in\operatorname{range}(J^{\mathsf T})\times\ker J:\ \|n\|^2+\|t\|^2\le\Delta^2\}.\] Its active boundary satisfies \(\|n\|^2+\|t\|^2=\Delta^2\). For fixed \(n\) with \(\|n\|\le\Delta\), the exact remaining tangential allowance is \[\Delta_t(n)=\sqrt{\Delta^2-\|n\|^2}.\] No admissible pair with that fixed normal component exists when \(\|n\|>\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The shared Euclidean radius couples the orthogonal components: increasing the normal norm decreases the exact remaining tangential allowance, and a normal component outside the radius is inadmissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\|n\|\le\Delta\), admissibility is equivalent to \(\|t\|\le\sqrt{\Delta^2-\|n\|^2}\), with equality on the active boundary.

children.title: Second-Order Feasibility Corrections
children.top_down_role: Corrections accounting for mismatch between tangent models and nonlinear equality curvature.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) continuously differentiable. At \(x_k\), write \(A_k=Jc(x_k)\) and suppose a primary step \(p_k\) satisfies the linearized constraints \(A_kp_k+c(x_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional equality-constrained methods; the correction repairs nonlinear feasibility after a primary linearly feasible step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A_k\) has full row rank, the second-order feasibility correction associated with \(p_k\) is the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm vector \[\widehat p_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{w\in\mathbb R^n}\{\|w\|_2:A_kw+c(x_k+p_k)=0\}=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k+p_k).\] The corrected trial point is \(x_k^+=x_k+p_k+\widehat p_k\). The term “second-order” refers to the regime in which \(p_k\) is linearly feasible, so \(c(x_k+p_k)\) is generated by nonlinear constraint curvature and is of order \(\|p_k\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order feasibility correction is the smallest normal-space displacement that cancels the constraint residual observed after taking a primary step that satisfies the first-order constraint model. It is computed by solving the linear equation formed with the current constraint Jacobian and the nonlinear residual at the uncorrected trial point. Full row rank makes the displayed pseudoinverse formula well defined and selects the unique minimum-norm correction. The corrected point adds this displacement to the primary step; the correction changes feasibility while avoiding an unnecessary tangential component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat p_k=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k+p_k)\) and \(A_k\widehat p_k+c(x_k+p_k)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\widehat p_k=-A_k^\dagger c(x_k+p_k)\), where \(A_k^\dagger=A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}\).
\(\widehat p_k\in\operatorname{Range}(A_k^T)\) and it is orthogonal to \(\operatorname{Null}(A_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For one equality \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(\widehat p_k=-c(x_k+p_k)\nabla c(x_k)/\|\nabla c(x_k)\|_2^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(c(x_k+p_k)=0\), then \(\widehat p_k=0\).
Under standard local smoothness and a linearly feasible primary step, the correction is smaller in order than \(p_k\).
boundary_notes: The formula uses the Jacobian at \(x_k\); variants may relinearize at \(x_k+p_k\).
The definition does not itself assert acceptance by a merit function, filter, or trust-region test.
If \(A_k\) is rank deficient, a specified generalized inverse or regularized solve is required.

notation.meaning: Minimum-norm right pseudoinverse of the full-row-rank Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.title: Curved-Constraint Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order normal correction for curvature-induced equality residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be twice continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(J=Dc(x)\), and suppose \(J\) has full row rank. Given a sufficiently small trial step \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(c(x)+Js=0\), compute \[d=-J^{\mathsf T}(JJ^{\mathsf T})^{-1}c(x+s).\] Accept the curvature correction only when its prescribed safeguard holds, for example \(\|d\|\le\kappa\|s\|^2\) with \(\kappa>0\), and then output \(s+d\). For the untruncated correction, \(c(x+s)=O(\|s\|^2)\), \(d=O(\|s\|^2)\), and \[c(x+s+d)=O(\|s\|^3)\qquad(s\to0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted second-order normal correction cancels the leading curvature residual of a linearized-feasible step and improves its local equality residual from second to third order.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is twice continuously differentiable and has a locally Lipschitz Jacobian near \(x\).
\(c(x)+Js=0\), \(s\to0\), and the untruncated correction satisfies the selected acceptance safeguard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the accepted untruncated correction, \(d=O(\|s\|^2)\) and \(c(x+s+d)=O(\|s\|^3)\).

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the base point
