knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank and Conditioning Boundary for Normal Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability and sensitivity of the minimum-norm curvature correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For full-row-rank \(J\) and residual \(r=c(x+s)\), the minimum-Euclidean-norm solution of \(Jd=-r\) is \(d=-J^{\mathsf T}(JJ^{\mathsf T})^{-1}r=-J^\dagger r\), and \(\|d\|_2\le \|r\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(J)\). Thus an \(O(\|s\|^2)\) residual yields a uniformly \(O(\|s\|^2)\) correction only if \(\sigma_{\min}(J)\) remains bounded away from zero. At rank loss the inverse formula is undefined; near rank loss the correction can violate its size safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal correction is minimum norm, but small Jacobian singular values amplify it; rank loss invalidates the inverse formula.
assumptions_latex: \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(r=c(x+s)\) is the residual to be corrected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d=-J^\dagger r\) and \(\|d\|_2\le \|r\|_2/\sigma_{\min}(J)\).

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose inverse of the constraint Jacobian
smallest singular value of the constraint Jacobian

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correction of the Curvature Residual of Nonlinear Equalities
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(A_k=Jc(x_k)\) have full row rank, and let \(p_k\) satisfy \(c(x_k)+A_kp_k=0\). Define the nonlinear curvature residual \(r_k^{\mathrm{curv}}=c(x_k+p_k)-c(x_k)-A_kp_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear equalities and primary steps satisfying the first-order constraint model; unlike a generic feasibility correction, the defining right-hand side isolates constraint curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A curved-constraint correction is a vector \(w_k\in\operatorname{Range}(A_k^T)\) satisfying \[A_kw_k=-r_k^{\mathrm{curv}}.\] Its canonical minimum-norm realization is \[w_k=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}r_k^{\mathrm{curv}}.\] Because \(c(x_k)+A_kp_k=0\), one has \(r_k^{\mathrm{curv}}=c(x_k+p_k)\), so this definition specializes to the standard second-order correction while explicitly identifying the quantity being repaired as the mismatch between the curved constraint and its tangent model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The curved-constraint correction repairs only the residual that remains because a nonlinear equality manifold bends away from its tangent affine space. The residual is defined as the actual constraint value after the primary step minus the value predicted by first-order linearization. A correction is normal to the linearized tangent space and maps through the current Jacobian to the negative of this residual. The canonical choice is the minimum-norm solution. When the primary step exactly satisfies the linearized equality, the curvature residual equals the full trial-point constraint violation, but retaining the residual definition distinguishes curvature repair from correction of pre-existing linearized infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(c\in C^2\) on a neighborhood containing the segment from \(x_k\) to \(x_k+p_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For component Hessians, \(r_k^{\mathrm{curv}}=\frac12( p_k^T\nabla^2c_i(x_k+\theta_i p_k)p_k)_{i=1}^m\) for suitable \(\theta_i\in(0,1)\).
The correction is the solution of \(\min_w\frac12\|w\|_2^2\) subject to \(A_kw=-r_k^{\mathrm{curv}}\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c\) is affine, then \(r_k^{\mathrm{curv}}=0\) and \(w_k=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Locally, \(\|w_k\|_2=O(\|p_k\|_2^2)\) when the Jacobian pseudoinverse remains bounded.
The correction has no component in \(\operatorname{Null}(A_k)\).
boundary_notes: This definition excludes corrections for rank loss or inaccurate solution of the first-order feasibility equation.
Using \(Jc(x_k+p_k)\) instead of \(A_k\) defines a relinearized variant, not the canonical fixed-Jacobian correction stated here.

notation.meaning: Mismatch between the nonlinear equality and its first-order tangent model.

children.title: Maratos-Effect Boundary
children.top_down_role: The local acceptance failure motivating second-order feasibility repair.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent geometric source of Maratos-type full-step rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c\in C^2\), \(c(x)=0\), and let \(s\to0\) satisfy \(Dc(x)s=0\). Then \[c(x+s)=\tfrac12D^2c(x)[s,s]+o(\|s\|^2).\] Thus a linearly feasible step generally retains a second-order nonlinear constraint residual. A residual \(o(\|s\|^2)\) requires the leading curvature term to vanish asymptotically along the step sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearized feasibility generally leaves a second-order nonlinear residual, which is the geometric mismatch behind Maratos-type rejection.

notation.meaning: vector of constraint second directional derivatives

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Feasibility-Mismatch Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine-Constraint Exclusion of the Curvature Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence boundary for the geometric mechanism underlying Maratos-type rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(c(x)=Ax-b\), \(c(x)=0\), and \(As=0\), then \(c(x+s)=0\). Thus \(D^2c\equiv0\), so the second-order nonlinear feasibility mismatch vanishes identically; rejection of such a step cannot be attributed to the curvature-driven Maratos mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine equalities eliminate the second-order nonlinear residual responsible for Maratos-type rejection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x+s)=0\) and \(D^2c\equiv0\).

notation.meaning: Step feasible for the linearized equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Constraint Exclusion of the Curvature Mismatch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit curvature-driven rejection of a tangent step near a constrained minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=-x_1\), \(c(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2-1\), and \(\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho|c(x)|\). For \(\theta>0\), set \(x_\theta=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), \(q_\theta=(-\sin\theta,\cos\theta)\), and \(s_\theta=-\theta q_\theta\). Then \(c(x_\theta)=0\), \(Dc(x_\theta)s_\theta=0\), \(c(x_\theta+s_\theta)=\theta^2\), and \(\nabla f(x_\theta)^{\mathsf T}s_\theta=-\theta\sin\theta\). Hence the test \[\phi_\rho(x_\theta+s_\theta)\leq\phi_\rho(x_\theta)+\eta\nabla f(x_\theta)^{\mathsf T}s_\theta\] fails for all sufficiently small \(\theta>0\) whenever \(0<\eta<1\) and \(\rho>1-\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the unit circle, a tangent descent step leaves a quadratic constraint residual whose exact-penalty cost can force asymptotic Armijo rejection.
assumptions_latex: The displayed exact-penalty merit function and Armijo convention are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi_\rho(x_\theta+s_\theta)>\phi_\rho(x_\theta)+\eta\nabla f(x_\theta)^{\mathsf T}s_\theta\quad\text{for all sufficiently small }\theta>0.

notation.meaning: Unit tangent to the circle at the feasible point.
Exact-penalty merit function used by the acceptance test.

knowledge_statements.title: Circle Constraint Merit-Test Rejection
Maratos-Effect Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local full-step rejection caused by second-order constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) be feasible, let \(s\) satisfy \(J(x)s=0\), and use the exact-penalty merit function \(\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\|c(x)\|\). For \(s\to0\), \[\phi_\rho(x+s)-\phi_\rho(x)=g^{\mathsf T}s+\frac12s^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)s+\frac{\rho}{2}\|D^2c(x)[s,s]\|+o(\|s\|^2).\] With Armijo parameter \(\eta\in(0,1)\), the full step is asymptotically rejected whenever the right-hand side exceeds \(\eta g^{\mathsf T}s\), despite the SQP step being locally fast. This curvature-driven acceptance failure is the Maratos-effect boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full SQP step can fail a merit-function test because its second-order constraint violation outweighs predicted descent, even near a regular solution.
assumptions_latex: The acceptance test uses \(\phi_\rho\) and Armijo parameter \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((1-\eta)g^{\mathsf T}s+\frac12s^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(x)s+\frac{\rho}{2}\|D^2c(x)[s,s]\|+o(\|s\|^2)>0\), the full step fails the Armijo test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits the Maratos-effect leaf, and the displayed expansion is plausible for the stated norm merit function. However, no citation is supplied, and the exact penalty norm, directional model, and Armijo acceptance convention materially determine the boundary formula. An authoritative Maratos-effect or SQP globalization source with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Acceptance Boundary Defining the Maratos Effect
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\) be feasible iterates for \(c(x)=0\), let \(p_k\) be steps with \(\|x_k+p_k-x^*\|=O(\|x_k-x^*\|^2)\), and let \(\mathcal A_k(p)\leq0\) denote a merit-function or filter acceptance test for the full step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth equality-constrained methods whose fast primary steps can be rejected because nonlinear constraint curvature degrades the globalization measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Maratos-effect boundary at iteration \(k\) is \[\mathcal M_k=\{p:\mathcal A_k(p)=0,\ \|x_k+p-x^*\|=O(\|x_k-x^*\|^2),\ c(x_k)+A_kp=0\}.\] The Maratos-effect region is the rejection side \(\mathcal A_k(p)>0\) containing fast local steps for which the nonlinear residual satisfies \(c(x_k+p)=O(\|p\|^2)\) but causes insufficient merit decrease or filter domination. A method exhibits the Maratos effect if such rejected full steps occur arbitrarily close to \(x^*\), thereby obstructing eventual acceptance of unit steps and potentially preventing superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Maratos-effect boundary separates fast, linearly feasible local steps that pass a globalization test from steps of the same local quality that fail it because the curved constraints create a second-order violation. Formally, the boundary is the zero level set of the chosen acceptance residual, restricted to primary steps that satisfy the tangent constraint and would produce quadratic local progress if accepted. The effect is present when rejected steps of this kind occur arbitrarily near the solution. This definition distinguishes the phenomenon from ordinary rejection of a poor direction: the rejected direction is locally excellent for solving the optimality equations, and the failure is attributable to the acceptance mechanism’s treatment of objective and feasibility changes.
assumptions_latex: The acceptance test is defined by a merit function or filter and rejects when \(\mathcal A_k(p_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The boundary is \(\mathcal M_k=\{p:\mathcal A_k(p)=0\}\) restricted to linearly feasible, fast local steps; the Maratos region is its rejected side.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an Armijo merit test, \(\mathcal A_k(p)=\phi(x_k+p;\mu)-\phi(x_k;\mu)-\eta D\phi(x_k;\mu)[p]\).
For a filter, rejection occurs when \((f(x_k+p),h(x_k+p))\) is dominated by an existing filter pair.
special_cases_latex: In Powell’s equality-constrained example, the primary step is Q-quadratic but increases both objective value and constraint violation for every nonzero nearby angular error.
immediate_consequences_latex: A second-order correction may move the same primary step from the rejected side to the accepted side.
Persistent unit-step rejection can reduce a nominally superlinear method to a slower local regime.
boundary_notes: The term does not cover rejection caused solely by an inaccurate linear solve, an indefinite reduced Hessian, or a non-descent primary step.
The numerical location of the boundary depends on the merit or filter parameters.

notation.meaning: Signed acceptance-test residual; nonpositive values are acceptable.

review_flags: The source defines the phenomenon and gives its canonical example; the zero-level boundary notation is an operational formalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ownership Boundary Between Reduced-Step Generation and Globalization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), a reduced equality method supplies a model step \(p_k=v_k+Z_ku_k\), predicted objective change \(\operatorname{pred}_k\), and predicted feasibility change. A globalization mechanism maintains state \(G_k\), such as a penalty parameter, filter, funnel bound, line-search interval, or trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An interface definition separating the mathematical responsibilities of a local equality-reduction solver from those of a line-search, trust-region, merit, filter, or restoration framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A globalization ownership boundary is a pair of maps \[S_k:(x_k,G_k)\mapsto(p_k,\operatorname{pred}_k,\operatorname{fepred}_k),\qquad \Gamma_k:(x_k,G_k,p_k,\operatorname{pred}_k,\operatorname{fepred}_k)\mapsto(a_k,G_{k+1}),\] where the step generator \(S_k\) owns satisfaction of the reduced or linearized subproblem conditions, while \(\Gamma_k\) owns trial evaluation, acceptance \(a_k\in\{0,1\}\), step scaling or radius revision, and restoration invocation. The accepted iterate is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+a_ks_k\), with \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\) for a line search or \(s_k=p_k\) for a trust-region trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The globalization ownership boundary is the formal interface between producing a locally meaningful reduced step and deciding whether that step is globally acceptable. The reduced solver is responsible for the normal and tangential equations and for predicted reductions. The globalization mechanism is responsible for evaluating the nonlinear trial point, accepting or rejecting it, changing a step length or radius, updating merit, filter, or funnel state, and invoking restoration when required. The boundary is respected when neither component silently assumes the other’s responsibilities and all quantities needed for the acceptance decision are returned explicitly.
assumptions_latex: The step generator returns a finite candidate step and model predictions.
The globalization map has access to the nonlinear values required by its acceptance test.
The state update \(G_k\mapsto G_{k+1}\) is defined for both accepted and rejected trials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k\) owns model-step conditions, whereas \(\Gamma_k\) owns nonlinear acceptance and globalization-state updates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For line search, \(G_k\) contains \(\mu_k\) and \(\Gamma_k\) chooses \(\alpha_k\) from a sufficient-decrease test.
For trust region, \(G_k\) contains \(\Delta_k\) and \(\Gamma_k\) uses \(\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\).
special_cases_latex: A feasible reduced method may use \(f\) alone as the acceptance merit because \(c(x_k)=0\) is maintained.
An infeasible method must expose a feasibility measure or model to the globalization map.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing from line search to trust region need not alter the definition of the reduced optimality equations.
A rejected step does not by itself imply failure of the reduced linear algebra.
boundary_notes: This is an interface definition, not a convergence guarantee.
Multiplier updating may be assigned to either side only if that assignment is explicitly included in the maps.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Method Line-Search Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between a reduced feasible-step generator and a scalar step-acceptance mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\). At iterate \(x_k\), the reduced solver supplies a tangent direction \(d_k\), a feasible or restored trial curve \(x_k(\alpha)\), and a predicted decrease \(\Delta m_k(\alpha)>0\). Given \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), the globalization layer tests step lengths \(\alpha\in\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\) in order and accepts the first trial satisfying \[\Phi(x_k(\alpha))\leq \Phi(x_k)-\sigma\Delta m_k(\alpha),\] where \(\Phi\) is either the reduced objective on a feasible curve or a specified merit function. If such a step \(\alpha_k\) is found, it returns \(x_{k+1}=x_k(\alpha_k)\) and acceptance metadata; otherwise it reports line-search failure and leaves the reduced iterate unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced solver proposes a direction, trial curve, and predicted decrease. The line-search layer tests a backtracking sequence and returns the first trial satisfying the declared feasible-objective or merit-function decrease test, or reports failure without changing the iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(Jc(x_k)d_k=0\), and the trial curve and acceptance function \(\Phi\) are defined at every tested step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the search succeeds, it returns an accepted \(x_{k+1}=x_k(\alpha_k)\) satisfying the declared sufficient-decrease test; otherwise it returns failure without updating \(x_k\).

notation.meaning: Reduced objective or merit function used for acceptance.
Predicted decrease supplied by the reduced model.
Accepted line-search step length, when one is found.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Merit-Based Line-Search Interface for a Reduced Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a reduced equality method return a direction \(p_k\) at \(x_k\). Let \(\phi(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|\) be an exact nonsmooth merit function with directional derivative \(D\phi(x_k;\mu)[p_k]<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained step generation coupled to a merit-function backtracking line search; feasible objective-only searches are included as a special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduced-method line-search interface consists of the tuple \((p_k,\phi_k,D\phi_k,\mathcal T_k)\), where \(\mathcal T_k\subset(0,1]\) is an ordered trial set and the accepted step length is \[\alpha_k=\max\{\alpha\in\mathcal T_k:\phi(x_k+\alpha p_k;\mu_k)\leq\phi(x_k;\mu_k)+\eta\alpha D\phi(x_k;\mu_k)[p_k]\},\qquad \eta\in(0,1).\] The interface is valid only when the reduced solver supplies a merit-descent direction and the line search owns evaluation, backtracking, and acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The line-search interface exposes a reduced direction together with the merit value and directional model needed for sufficient-decrease testing. The globalization layer selects the largest allowed trial length satisfying an Armijo-type inequality. The reduced solver must provide a descent direction for the selected merit function, while the line search controls only the scalar length and the acceptance decision. This definition accommodates both feasible reduced methods, for which the objective itself is an appropriate merit function, and infeasible methods, for which objective and equality violation must be combined.
assumptions_latex: The trial values \(f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) and \(c(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) are defined for tested \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted reduced step is \(s_k=\alpha_kp_k\), where \(\alpha_k\) satisfies the displayed sufficient-decrease condition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\phi_1(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|_1\), the condition is equation (18.28) of the cited source.
If every iterate and trial curve is feasible, set \(\phi=f\) and recover the ordinary Armijo condition.
special_cases_latex: Before backtracking, a method may test a second-order-corrected full step \(p_k+\widehat p_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of the unit step triggers correction or backtracking without changing the reduced direction.
Eventual acceptance of \(\alpha_k=1\) is required to preserve the fastest local Newton regime.
boundary_notes: A line search does not bound the direction before it is generated; that responsibility differs from a trust-region interface.
The definition does not specify a penalty-parameter update rule.

notation.meaning: Directional derivative of the merit function.

children.title: Reduced-Method Trust-Region Interface
children.top_down_role: Connection to reduced, projected, and composite trust-region frameworks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variant-independent acceptance and radius-control interface for reduced, projected, or composite trust-region trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), the reduced component returns a model coordinate \(p_k\), a trial construction \(x_k^+=T_k(p_k)\), and a positive predicted reduction \(\operatorname{pred}_k\). The trust-region layer evaluates the declared acceptance measure \(\Psi_k\), forms \[\rho_k=\frac{\Psi_k(x_k)-\Psi_k(x_k^+)}{\operatorname{pred}_k},\] applies declared acceptance thresholds, commits either \(x_k^+\) or \(x_k\), and updates the radius \(\Delta_k\) by its declared policy. The trial map, model prediction, norm constraint, and acceptance measure must describe the same feasible, projected, retracted, or composite trial semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced component supplies a radius-constrained model trial and its prediction; the trust-region layer evaluates the corresponding actual reduction, accepts or rejects, and updates the radius under a declared policy.
assumptions_latex: The trial map, model prediction, trust-region norm, and acceptance measure use consistent trial semantics.
Acceptance thresholds and the radius-update policy are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_{k+1},\Delta_{k+1})\in\{x_k,x_k^+\}\times\mathbb R_{++}\text{ is determined by the declared ratio and radius policy}.

notation.meaning: Declared feasible, projected, retracted, or composite trial map.
Acceptance measure used for actual reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Trust-Region Exchange Contract

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary consistency conditions for interpreting an actual-to-predicted reduction ratio at a reduced-method trust-region interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a reduced solver return a model step \(p_k\), a trial point \(x_k^+=T_k(p_k)\), and \(\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\). For an acceptance measure \(\Psi_k\), the ratio \[\rho_k=\frac{\Psi_k(x_k)-\Psi_k(x_k^+)}{\operatorname{pred}_k}\] is a model-agreement statistic only when \(\operatorname{pred}_k>0\), the denominator predicts the same step \(p_k\), and \(T_k\) is the trial construction assumed by that prediction and acceptance measure. If \(\operatorname{pred}_k\le0\), the usual ratio is undefined or cannot certify predicted descent; if a different projected, restored, or composite trial is evaluated without a corresponding prediction, \(\rho_k\) does not measure agreement for the supplied model step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region ratio is meaningful only when its positive prediction and actual reduction refer to the same step, trial construction, and acceptance measure.
assumptions_latex: The ratio is intended as an actual-to-predicted model-agreement statistic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{pred}_k>0\text{ and consistent pairing of }p_k,T_k,m_k,\Psi_k\text{ are necessary for the usual agreement interpretation}.

notation.meaning: Trial-point construction applied to the reduced step.
Predicted reduction for the supplied model step.

knowledge_statements.title: Model–Trial Consistency Boundary
Reduced-Method Trust-Region Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between reduced-step construction and trust-region acceptance, rejection, and radius updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), the reduced solver supplies a trial step \(p_k\) satisfying \(Jc(x_k)p_k=0\) and \(\lVert p_k\rVert\leq\Delta_k\), together with a model decrease \(\operatorname{pred}_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\). The globalization layer evaluates a feasible, projected, or composite trial point \(x_k^+\), computes \[\rho_k=\frac{\Psi(x_k)-\Psi(x_k^+)}{\operatorname{pred}_k},\] and accepts only when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\), where \(0<\eta_1<1\). It contracts \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and may enlarge it after sufficiently good agreement with an active trust-region boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced solver supplies a bounded tangent step and predicted decrease; the trust-region layer owns ratio evaluation, acceptance, and radius contraction or expansion.
assumptions_latex: The model \(m_k\) is defined on the tangent or reduced space.
The trial-point construction and the acceptance measure \(\Psi\) are specified consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns \(x_{k+1}\in\{x_k,x_k^+\}\) and an updated radius \(\Delta_{k+1}>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the interface leaf, but no source supports the particular ratio test or radius policy. Feasible, projected, and composite trial constructions are blended even though their actual-reduction measures and model predictions need not be interchangeable. An authoritative reduced or composite trust-region source with a precise algorithm or section locator is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Trust-Region Interface for Equality Reduction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(m_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), let \(A_k=Jc(x_k)\), and let \(\Delta_k>0\). A normal step \(v_k\) reduces \(\|c_k+A_kv\|\) within a fraction of the radius, and a tangential component completes \(p_k\) inside \(\|p_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained composite-step trust-region methods, including projected and reduced subproblem solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduced-method trust-region interface returns \((p_k,\operatorname{pred}_k,\operatorname{ared}_k,\rho_k)\) with \[p_k=v_k+u_k,\quad \|p_k\|\leq\Delta_k,\quad A_ku_k=0,\] \[\operatorname{pred}_k=q_{\mu_k}(0)-q_{\mu_k}(p_k)>0,\qquad \operatorname{ared}_k=\phi(x_k;\mu_k)-\phi(x_k+p_k;\mu_k),\qquad \rho_k=\frac{\operatorname{ared}_k}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.\] The globalization layer accepts when \(\rho_k\geq\eta\), enlarges or preserves \(\Delta_k\) after successful trials, and contracts it after unsuccessful trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The trust-region interface couples a reduced or projected composite step to a nonlinear agreement test. The step must obey the radius and expose predicted reduction from the local merit model. The globalization mechanism evaluates the actual merit reduction and forms their ratio. Acceptance and radius updating depend on this ratio, while the reduced solver owns the normal and tangential subproblems. Separating the normal component from the tangential component keeps the feasibility model compatible with a radius that may be too small to satisfy the full linearized constraints exactly.
assumptions_latex: The merit function and its local model use the same penalty parameter \(\mu_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k=\operatorname{ared}_k/\operatorname{pred}_k\) is the interface quantity governing acceptance and radius revision.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The relaxation formulation uses \(A_kp_k+c_k=r_k\), with \(r_k=A_kv_k+c_k\).
A null-space implementation obtains the tangential component by projected conjugate gradients without explicitly forming a reduced basis.
special_cases_latex: For the Byrd–Omojokun construction, the normal subproblem uses \(\|v\|_2\leq0.8\Delta_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A negative or small \(\rho_k\) indicates poor nonlinear agreement and causes rejection or contraction.
The radius simultaneously limits objective-model error and the amount of achievable linearized feasibility.
boundary_notes: The interface does not require the Hessian model to be positive definite.
If the normal subproblem fails to produce adequate feasibility decrease, a restoration or alternative feasibility mechanism is needed.

notation.meaning: Ratio of actual to predicted merit reduction.
Trust-region model of the merit function.

children.title: Feasibility Globalization Interface
children.top_down_role: Connection to globalization frameworks that manage feasibility and objective progress jointly.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h(x)=\|c(x)\|_1\) measure equality violation and let \(\mathcal F_k\) be a filter of mutually nondominating pairs \((f_j,h_j)\). A reduced method proposes a trial point \(x^+=x_k+p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globalization mechanisms that keep objective and feasibility progress separate and invoke restoration when ordinary step generation or acceptance stalls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility globalization interface declares \(x^+\) acceptable when, for every \((f_j,h_j)\in\mathcal F_k\), \[f(x^+)\leq f_j-\beta h_j\quad\text{or}\quad h(x^+)\leq(1-\beta)h_j,\qquad \beta\in(0,1).\] If accepted, the pair \((f(x^+),h(x^+))\) is inserted and dominated pairs are removed. If repeated rejection, an infeasible step subproblem, or a line-search length below its threshold occurs, the interface transfers control to restoration, whose subproblem is \(\min_x h(x)\) and whose return point must have sufficiently reduced violation and be compatible with the filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasibility globalization interface judges a reduced trial step by objective progress or equality-violation progress without forcing both into one scalar merit function. A filter stores mutually nondominating objective–violation pairs. The trial point is acceptable only if it improves sufficiently relative to every stored pair in at least one coordinate. Accepted pairs update the filter. When ordinary trials cannot be accepted, the interface invokes a restoration phase devoted to reducing constraint violation and returns control only at a point compatible with the filter. This makes restoration a defined globalization state transition rather than an unstructured solver failure.
assumptions_latex: No pair in \(\mathcal F_k\) dominates another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is disjunctive objective-or-feasibility improvement; failure triggers a feasibility-restoration transition.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Without margins, acceptability means that \((f(x^+),h(x^+))\) is not dominated by any filter entry.
A merit-function interface instead combines the two coordinates as \(f(x)+\mu h(x)\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m|c_i(x)|\).
A trust-region filter contracts the radius after rejection before invoking restoration.
immediate_consequences_latex: An objective-increasing trial may be accepted if it gives sufficient feasibility improvement.
A feasibility-increasing trial may be accepted if it gives sufficient objective improvement and is not excluded by the filter margins.
boundary_notes: Filter acceptability alone is not a complete global convergence scheme; safeguards and restoration are part of the interface.
Restoration seeks feasibility, not constrained optimality of the original objective.

notation.meaning: Current filter of nondominated objective–violation pairs.

source_refs.locator: §15.4, equations (15.31)–(15.33), feasibility-restoration discussion, and Algorithm 15.1, pp. 435–440

knowledge_statements.title: Filter-and-Restoration Feasibility Globalization Interface

source_witnesses.locator: §15.4, equations (15.31)–(15.33), feasibility-restoration discussion, and Algorithm 15.1, pp. 435–440

children.title: Filter Globalization Interface
children.top_down_role: Exchange of feasibility and objective-progress information with filter frameworks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filter acceptability stated relative to a declared margin convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain stored pairs \((\theta_i,f_i)\). A filter implementation must declare positive margins and its precise margin convention. Under the convention \(0<\beta<1\), \(\gamma>0\), a trial pair \((\theta^+,f^+)\) is acceptable relative to the filter when, for every \((\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), \(\theta^+\le\beta\theta_i\) or \(f^+\le f_i-\gamma\theta^+\). Other established filter conventions replace the displayed margins but must be declared rather than silently mixed. Switching and sufficient-decrease tests may impose additional conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter acceptance requires sufficient improvement in violation or objective against every stored entry under one explicitly declared margin convention.
assumptions_latex: The violation and objective values are finite.
The implementation declares one margin convention and any additional switching test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall(\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k:\quad \theta^+\le\beta\theta_i\ \lor\ f^+\le f_i-\gamma\theta^+.

notation.meaning: Margins for the displayed filter convention.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Filter-Acceptance Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order structure of an objective–violation filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For pairs \((\theta_1,f_1)\) and \((\theta_2,f_2)\), with \(\theta_i\ge0\), the first weakly dominates the second when \(\theta_1\le\theta_2\) and \(f_1\le f_2\), and strictly dominates it when at least one inequality is strict. A filter is maintained as an antichain under this componentwise order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter stores mutually nondominated objective–violation pairs.
assumptions_latex: Smaller objective and violation values are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal F\text{ is an antichain under componentwise dominance}.
knowledge_statements.title: Filter Dominance and State

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Responsibility split between reduced-step generation and filter globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduced-step generator supplies a trial point, objective value, violation measure, and any prediction or step-status data required by the selected filter scheme. The filter layer owns comparison with stored entries, additional switching or sufficient-decrease tests, acceptance or rejection, filter maintenance, and requests for restoration. It returns either an accepted next iterate or the contraction, recomputation, or restoration status prescribed by the selected globalization framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced method produces trial data, while the filter framework owns acceptance, filter maintenance, and restoration requests.
assumptions_latex: The selected filter framework declares its violation measure, margins, switching tests, and status protocol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{trial generation and filter acceptance/update have separate ownership}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Step Filter Handoff Contract
Filter Globalization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard two-criterion filter acceptance condition for objective value and equality violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta(x)=\lVert c(x)\rVert\), and let the current filter \(\mathcal F_k\) contain mutually nondominated pairs \((\theta_i,f_i)\). Given constants \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(\gamma>0\), a trial point \(x^+\) is filter-acceptable if, for every \((\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), \[\theta(x^+)\leq\beta\theta_i\quad\text{or}\quad f(x^+)\leq f_i-\gamma\theta(x^+).\] Acceptance may additionally require a switching or sufficient-decrease test near feasibility. After acceptance, the globalization layer inserts the new pair when prescribed and removes every filter entry dominated by it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial passes the filter when it sufficiently improves either constraint violation or objective relative to every stored nondominated pair; the globalization layer maintains the filter.
assumptions_latex: The objective and violation measures are finite at every compared point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed disjunction is the filter-acceptance predicate applied against every entry of \(\mathcal F_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but filter margins, the use of theta(x+) rather than a stored violation in the objective margin, switching tests, and filter updates vary among algorithms. No cited source fixes the stated convention, so the exact predicate cannot be validated.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent order structure of an objective–violation filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For pairs \((\theta_1,f_1)\) and \((\theta_2,f_2)\), with \(\theta_i\ge0\), the first weakly dominates the second when \(\theta_1\le\theta_2\) and \(f_1\le f_2\), and strictly dominates it when at least one inequality is strict. A filter is maintained as an antichain under this order: no stored entry strictly dominates another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter stores mutually nondominated objective–violation pairs under componentwise minimization.
assumptions_latex: Smaller objective and violation values are preferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is an antichain under componentwise dominance.
knowledge_statements.title: Filter Dominance and Antichain

children.title: Funnel Globalization Interface
children.top_down_role: Exchange of feasibility bounds and trial-point status with funnel frameworks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variant-independent exchange contract between a reduced-step generator and a feasibility-funnel acceptance layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta(x)\ge 0\) measure equality violation and let \(\tau_k\ge 0\) be the current funnel bound. The reduced component returns a trial \(x_k^+\) and the objective- and feasibility-progress data required by a declared predicate \(A_k\). The funnel layer may accept the trial only if \[\theta(x_k^+)\le \tau_k\quad\text{and}\quad A_k(x_k^+)=\mathrm{true}.\] It then updates \(\tau_k\) using a declared transition rule appropriate to the selected funnel variant. Funnel eligibility alone is not an acceptance certificate, and monotonicity of \(\tau_k\) may be claimed only when imposed by that transition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A funnel interface passes a trial and progress data to an acceptance layer that enforces the current feasibility bound plus a declared progress test. Bound updates and restoration resets must be specified by the chosen funnel variant.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta\) is a declared nonnegative equality-violation measure.
The acceptance predicate \(A_k\) and funnel-state transition rule are fixed before the trial is classified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k^+\text{ accepted}\Longrightarrow \theta(x_k^+)\le\tau_k\ \text{and}\ A_k(x_k^+)=\mathrm{true}.

notation.meaning: Variant-specific objective or feasibility progress predicate.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Funnel Interface Contract
Funnel Globalization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-funnel acceptance condition with an iteration-dependent upper bound on constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta(x)=\lVert c(x)\rVert\), and let \(\tau_k>0\) be the current funnel bound. A trial point \(x^+\) is eligible for acceptance only if \[\theta(x^+)\leq\tau_k.\] Within the funnel, the globalization layer accepts the trial when the designated objective-reduction test or feasibility-reduction test holds. After an accepted feasibility-oriented step it chooses \(\tau_{k+1}\) with \(\theta(x^+)\leq\tau_{k+1}\leq	au_k\); after an objective-oriented step it may retain \(\tau_{k+1}=\tau_k\). The reduced-step generator supplies trial points but does not enlarge the funnel bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A funnel admits only trials below a maintained feasibility bound, then applies objective or feasibility decrease tests; accepted feasibility steps may tighten, but do not enlarge, that bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective and feasibility decrease tests are declared before trial classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate satisfies \(\theta(x_{k+1})\leq\tau_{k+1}\leq\tau_k\), except when a separately declared restoration reset is invoked.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the objective-step, feasibility-step, bound-update, and restoration-reset rules depend on the selected funnel algorithm. No source identifies a variant supporting the stated monotonic bound and acceptance interface.

children.title: Restoration-Phase Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of control to procedures focused primarily on recovering feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variant-independent control transfer from a reduced optimality phase to a feasibility-focused restoration procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta(x)\ge0\) be the declared constraint-violation measure. When the main globalization layer invokes restoration at \(x_k\), it supplies the permitted region, termination tolerances, and a declared success test \(S_k\). Restoration searches primarily for reduced violation and returns a point \(x_k^R\), residual diagnostics, and a status. A successful return satisfies \(S_k(x_k^R)=\mathrm{true}\); an unsuccessful return leaves iterate commitment to the caller and may distinguish numerical failure from approximate stationarity of the restoration model. The caller applies its own filter, funnel, merit, or other re-entry predicate before committing \(x_k^R\). Restoration success certifies only the declared feasibility-recovery test, not optimality for the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration receives a feasibility measure, permitted region, tolerances, and success test; it returns a candidate, diagnostics, and status. The calling globalization mechanism separately decides re-entry and iterate commitment.
assumptions_latex: A nonnegative violation measure, permitted restoration region, termination tolerances, and success predicate are declared.
The caller defines the re-entry and commitment rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_k(x_k^R)=\mathrm{true}\text{ certifies declared feasibility recovery but does not by itself commit }x_k^R\text{ or certify original-problem optimality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Handoff and Return Contract
Restoration-Phase Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface for recovering acceptable equality feasibility when the main reduced iteration cannot progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the main globalization mechanism cannot produce an acceptable trial from \(x_k\), it calls restoration with the violation measure \(\theta(x)=\lVert c(x)\rVert\), a neighborhood restriction, and a target reduction. Restoration approximately solves a feasibility problem such as \[\min_x\;\tfrac12\lVert c(x)\rVert^2\] within that restriction and returns \(x_k^R\) only if \(\theta(x_k^R)\leq\kappa_R\theta(x_k)\) for a prescribed \(0<\kappa_R<1\), together with residual and termination data. The globalization layer then tests compatibility with its filter or funnel before resuming the reduced optimality phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When normal trial generation fails, restoration seeks a nearby point with smaller equality violation and returns diagnostics for filter or funnel re-entry.
assumptions_latex: The restoration subproblem and its neighborhood restriction are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful call returns \(x_k^R\) satisfying the declared feasibility reduction; otherwise it reports restoration failure without claiming an optimality step.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the restoration interface, but the fixed contraction test, neighborhood restriction, and filter-or-funnel re-entry rule are method-specific. An authoritative restoration-phase algorithm with a specific locator is needed.

children.title: Globalization Ownership Boundary
children.top_down_role: Division of responsibility between reduced-step generation and external acceptance logic.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional separation of trial generation from iterate commitment and globalization-state updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a modular reduced/globalization method, let the reduced component return a candidate \(x_k^+\), model predictions, and diagnostics, and let \(G_k\) denote the declared globalization state. If the method assigns commitment authority to the globalization component, that component evaluates its declared predicate and returns \[(x_{k+1},G_{k+1})=\begin{cases}(x_k^+,\,U_k(G_k,x_k^+)),&\text{if accepted},\\(x_k,\,R_k(G_k,x_k^+)),&\text{if rejected},\end{cases}\] where \(U_k\) and \(R_k\) are its declared state transitions. Any projection, correction, or restoration that changes the evaluated point must be included in the data presented to this predicate. This is an interface contract of the selected architecture, not a universal requirement on all implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a declared modular architecture, the reduced component proposes a trial and predictions, while globalization commits or rejects the iterate and updates its own state. Corrections must be exposed before acceptance is evaluated.
assumptions_latex: The selected method declares a modular reduced/globalization ownership contract.
The acceptance predicate and accepted- and rejected-trial state transitions are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Only the declared commitment operation changes }(x_k,G_k)\text{ to }(x_{k+1},G_{k+1}).
knowledge_statements.title: Declared Globalization Ownership Contract
Globalization Ownership Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of reduced-model responsibilities from feasibility-globalization state and acceptance decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), the reduced-method component may compute tangent coordinates, normal or tangential trial steps, model values, predicted reductions, and linear-solve diagnostics. The globalization component exclusively applies the declared acceptance predicate and updates globalization state: line-search step lengths, trust-region radii, filter entries, funnel bounds, penalty parameters, or restoration status. Thus a candidate \(x_k^+\) becomes the next iterate only through \[x_{k+1}=x_k^+\quad\text{if the globalization predicate accepts it},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k\quad\text{otherwise}.\] Any feasibility correction that changes the trial point must be reported before acceptance is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced computations propose steps and predictions; globalization alone accepts iterates and updates line-search, trust-region, filter, funnel, penalty, or restoration state.
assumptions_latex: A single declared globalization mechanism owns the iteration state.
All corrections affecting the evaluated trial point are exposed to that mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No reduced trial changes \(x_k\) or globalization state unless the owning acceptance mechanism authorizes the update.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind matches the ownership-boundary leaf, but exclusive ownership of all listed state and the mandatory ordering of feasibility correction and acceptance are architectural requirements rather than universal mathematical facts. A method or software-interface source must establish this boundary.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reliability Hierarchy for an Equality-Reduction Iterate
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(A=Jc(x)\), \(g_L=\nabla f(x)-A^T\lambda\), let \(Z\) span \(\operatorname{Null}(A)\), let \(W=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,\lambda)\), and let \(r_{\mathrm{solve}}\) denote the residual of the reduced or KKT linear solve.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A diagnostic hierarchy for smooth, regular equality-constrained reductions; it orders increasingly strong computable claims and does not identify them as logically equivalent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_\ell\geq0\), define levels \[R_0:\text{ quantities finite},\quad R_1:\|c(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_f,\quad R_2:R_1\ \text{and}\ \|g_L\|\leq\varepsilon_s,\] \[R_3:R_2\ \text{and}\ \lambda_{\min}(Z^TWZ)\geq-\varepsilon_c,\quad R_4:R_3\ \text{and}\ \|r_{\mathrm{solve}}\|\leq\varepsilon_\ell.\] The equality-reduction reliability hierarchy is the ordered family \(R_0\prec R_1\prec R_2\prec R_3\prec R_4\), with higher levels certifying feasibility, first-order optimality, tangent curvature, and numerical solve quality in succession.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reliability hierarchy assigns an equality-reduction iterate a level according to which diagnostic conditions it satisfies. The base level merely requires evaluable quantities. The next level certifies equality feasibility, followed by primal–dual stationarity, nonnegative curvature on the tangent space, and finally acceptable residual in the inner reduced or KKT solve. The order expresses increasing diagnostic strength: passing a higher level includes all lower-level requirements. It does not assert that a lower-level certificate implies a higher one or that finite tolerances establish exact optimality.
assumptions_latex: The indicated norms and smallest reduced-Hessian eigenvalue are computable or bounded.
If curvature is assessed, \(Z\) has full column rank and \(AZ=0\).
Tolerances and scaling conventions are fixed before assigning a level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_4\Rightarrow R_3\Rightarrow R_2\Rightarrow R_1\Rightarrow R_0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With orthonormal \(Z\), tangent stationarity can be recorded as \(\|Z^T\nabla f(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_s\) when \(\lambda\) is chosen by least squares.
The curvature condition is equivalent to \(d^TWd\geq-\varepsilon_c\|d\|^2\) for every \(d\in\operatorname{Null}(A)\).
special_cases_latex: Algorithm 18.4 uses the practical level-\(R_2\) stopping test \(\|c_k\|_\infty<\epsilon\) and \(\|\nabla f_k-A_k^T\widehat\lambda_k\|_\infty<\epsilon\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A small inner-solve residual cannot compensate for a failed feasibility or stationarity certificate.
Curvature diagnostics distinguish approximate KKT points that may be maxima or saddles along feasible directions.
boundary_notes: The hierarchy is diagnostic, not a convergence-rate classification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Q-Local Convergence Families for Equality-Reduction Iterates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(y_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb R^{n+m}\) be primal–dual iterates converging to a regular KKT pair \(y^*=(x^*,\lambda^*)\), and define \(e_k=\|y_k-y^*\|\) in a fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local convergence classifications for reduced-space or primal–dual equality methods after iterates enter a neighborhood of a regular solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The local convergence family of \(\{y_k\}\) is classified as follows: Q-linear if there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(K\) such that \(e_{k+1}\leq q e_k\) for all \(k\geq K\); Q-superlinear if \(\lim_{k\to\infty}e_{k+1}/e_k=0\); Q-order \(p>1\) if there exist \(M>0\) and \(K\) such that \(e_{k+1}\leq M e_k^p\) for all \(k\geq K\); and Q-quadratic when \(p=2\). The same definitions apply to reduced coordinates \(z_k\) after replacing \(e_k\) by \(\|z_k-z^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local convergence families classify how quickly equality-reduction iterates approach a fixed regular solution once they are sufficiently close. Linear convergence contracts the error by a uniform factor. Superlinear convergence makes the ratio of consecutive errors tend to zero. Order greater than one bounds the next error by a power of the current error, with quadratic convergence corresponding to power two. The classification may be applied to full primal–dual variables or to nonsingular local reduced coordinates, but the selected error variable and norm must remain fixed within a claim.
assumptions_latex: The norm is fixed and finite-dimensional.
Only indices with \(e_k>0\) are used in error quotients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is determined by the asymptotic relation between \(e_{k+1}\) and \(e_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Q-superlinear convergence is equivalent to \(e_{k+1}=o(e_k)\).
Q-order \(p\) can be written \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}e_{k+1}/e_k^p<\infty\).
special_cases_latex: Exact local SQP under standard regularity belongs to the Q-quadratic family.
Quasi-Newton equality methods satisfying an appropriate projected Dennis–Moré condition belong to a superlinear family.
immediate_consequences_latex: Q-quadratic convergence implies Q-superlinear convergence.
Q-superlinear convergence implies eventual Q-linear convergence for any fixed contraction factor sufficiently close to one.
boundary_notes: R-linear and two-step superlinear convergence are distinct, weaker classifications and must be labeled separately.
A residual sequence may have a different observed rate from the primal–dual error unless local error equivalence is available.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Gradient Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear convergence of feasible reduced-gradient descent in a regular manifold chart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(x)=0\) define a smooth manifold near a local minimizer \(x_*\), and let \(x=\psi(z)\) be a twice continuously differentiable feasible chart with \(\psi(z_*)=x_*\). Define \(\phi=f\circ\psi\). Suppose \(\phi\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(\mu I\preceq\nabla^2\phi(z)\preceq LI\) throughout a neighborhood of \(z_*\), where \(0<\mu\leq L\). Consider \[z_{k+1}=z_k-\alpha_k\nabla\phi(z_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=\psi(z_{k+1}),\] where the step lengths satisfy \(0<\alpha_{\min}\leq\alpha_k\leq\alpha_{\max}<2/L\) and an Armijo decrease condition. Then every sufficiently close initial point generates feasible primal iterates converging to \(x_*\), and the reduced-coordinate errors converge Q-linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a regular feasible chart with a uniformly positive-definite and bounded reduced Hessian, reduced-gradient steps bounded away from zero and below two over the smoothness bound converge feasibly and Q-linearly when started sufficiently near the solution.
assumptions_latex: A twice continuously differentiable feasible chart exists near \(x_*\).
The reduced Hessian satisfies \(\mu I\preceq\nabla^2\phi(z)\preceq LI\) throughout a neighborhood of \(z_*\), with \(0<\mu\leq L\).
The step lengths satisfy \(0<\alpha_{\min}\leq\alpha_k\leq\alpha_{\max}<2/L\) and the declared Armijo condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(K\) such that \(\lVert z_{k+1}-z_*\rVert\leq q\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert\) for every \(k\geq K\), and \(x_k=\psi(z_k)\) remains feasible and converges to \(x_*\).

notation.meaning: Uniform lower and upper bounds on the reduced-gradient step lengths.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Convergence of a Feasible Reduced-Gradient Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c(x)=0\) define a smooth manifold near \(x^*\), let \(x=\chi(z)\) be a regular local feasible parametrization, and set \(\varphi(z)=f(\chi(z))\). Let \(Z(z)=D\chi(z)\), so \(\nabla\varphi(z)=Z(z)^T\nabla f(\chi(z))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible first-order reduced methods in a regular local chart; the definition classifies local convergence rather than asserting it for every step-size rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible iteration \(z_{k+1}=z_k-\alpha_kH_k
abla\varphi(z_k)\), with \(x_k=\chi(z_k)\), has reduced-gradient local convergence to \(x^*=\chi(z^*)\) if \(z_k	o z^*\), \(
abla\varphi(z^*)=0\), and there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(K\) such that \[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\leq q\|z_k-z^*\|\qquad(k\geq K).\] It is a feasible method because \(c(x_k)=0\) for every \(k\); its stationarity measure is the reduced gradient \(Z(z_k)^T
abla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-gradient local convergence means that a feasible first-order iteration, expressed in local coordinates on the equality manifold, converges to a stationary reduced point with an eventual linear contraction of coordinate error. The reduced gradient is the gradient of the objective restricted to the local feasible chart. Feasibility is exact at every iterate, and the iteration uses a uniformly positive-definite scaling of that reduced gradient. The definition separates this first-order linear regime from reduced Newton and quasi-Newton regimes, which use curvature information to obtain faster rates under stronger conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(\chi\) is continuously differentiable and locally one-to-one near \(z^*\).
The scaling matrices \(H_k\) are uniformly positive definite and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reduced-gradient local convergence is Q-linear convergence of \(z_k\) together with exact feasibility and \(\nabla\varphi(z^*)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With an orthonormal tangent basis \(Z_k\), the reduced stationarity residual is \(\|Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\|\).
Local norm equivalence and a regular chart transfer Q-linear convergence between \(z_k\) and \(x_k\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(H_k=I\) gives reduced steepest descent.
For linear equalities, \(\chi(z)=x_p+Zz\) and the reduced gradient is \(Z^T\nabla f(x_p+Zz)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A vanishing reduced gradient certifies first-order stationarity along feasible directions.
Poor conditioning of the reduced Hessian can make the linear contraction factor close to one.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes infeasible iterates corrected only asymptotically.
No superlinear rate is implied without curvature approximation or a stronger iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Newton Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic local convergence of exact Newton iterations on a regular reduced coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=\psi(z)\) be a twice continuously differentiable feasible chart near a strict equality-constrained minimizer \(x_* = \psi(z_*)\), and set \(\phi=f\circ\psi\). Suppose \(\phi\) is twice continuously differentiable, \(
abla\phi(z_*)=0\), \(H_*:=
abla^2\phi(z_*)\) is positive definite, and \(
abla^2\phi\) is locally Lipschitz. Then the exact reduced-Newton iteration \[z_{k+1}=z_k-
abla^2\phi(z_k)^{-1}
abla\phi(z_k),\qquad x_{k+1}=\psi(z_{k+1}),\] is well defined for every sufficiently close \(z_0\) and converges quadratically to \(z_*\), while all primal iterates remain feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a nonsingular positive-definite reduced Hessian and local Hessian Lipschitz continuity, exact feasible reduced-Newton iterations started nearby converge quadratically.
assumptions_latex: A smooth feasible chart exists near the solution.
The reduced Hessian at \(z_*\) is positive definite.
The reduced Hessian is locally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some \(C>0\) and all sufficiently large \(k\), \(\lVert z_{k+1}-z_*\rVert\leq C\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert^2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Local Convergence of an Exact Reduced-Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x=\chi(z)\) be a twice differentiable local parametrization of \(c(x)=0\) near a regular solution \(x^*=\chi(z^*)\), and let \(\varphi=f\circ\chi\). Assume \(\nabla\varphi(z^*)=0\) and \(\nabla^2\varphi(z^*)\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, full-step Newton iteration in local feasible coordinates, or an algebraically equivalent exact Newton–KKT/SQP iteration near a regular equality-constrained minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reduced-Newton step \(s_k\) and iterate are defined by \[\nabla^2\varphi(z_k)s_k=-\nabla\varphi(z_k),\qquad z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=\chi(z_{k+1}).\] The iteration has reduced-Newton local convergence when, for all sufficiently close \(z_0\), it is well defined and there exist \(M>0\) and \(K\) such that \[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\leq M\|z_k-z^*\|^2\qquad(k\geq K).\] Thus the defining local rate is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-Newton local convergence is the quadratic convergence obtained by applying exact Newton steps to the objective restricted to a regular local representation of the equality manifold. Each step solves the exact reduced Hessian equation and is accepted with unit length. Near a solution satisfying the equality constraint qualification and positive-definite tangent curvature, the reduced Hessian is nonsingular and the error after one iteration is bounded by a constant times the square of the preceding error. The equivalent primal–dual formulation solves the Newton–KKT system for the equality optimality equations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice differentiable near \(x^*\), with locally Lipschitz second derivatives.
The Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on \(\operatorname{Null}(Jc(x^*))\).
The initial point is sufficiently close and full steps are taken.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\leq M\|z_k-z^*\|^2\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The exact Newton–KKT system is equation (18.6), and its SQP form is equations (18.7)–(18.9).
Under a regular chart, Q-quadratic convergence of \(z_k\) is equivalent to Q-quadratic convergence of the primal variables locally.
special_cases_latex: For linear equalities, the reduced Hessian is \(Z^T\nabla^2f(x)Z\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The error exponent doubles asymptotically in the quadratic regime.
A globalization mechanism must eventually accept unit steps to retain this local rate.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover singular constraint Jacobians or merely semidefinite tangent curvature.
Approximated or inexact reduced solves belong to separate convergence regimes.

notation.meaning: Exact Newton step in reduced coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Reduced-Newton Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local rate classification by reduced Newton residuals and feasibility-coordinate errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the regular-chart and reduced-Hessian assumptions of exact reduced Newton, let \(g_k=\nabla\phi(z_k)\), \(H_k=\nabla^2\phi(z_k)\), and choose \(s_k\) satisfying \(H_ks_k=-g_k+r_k\). Suppose the coordinate or feasibility solve contributes an error \(e_k\), so that \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k+e_k\), and \[\lVert r_k\rVert+\lVert e_k\rVert\leq\eta_k\lVert g_k\rVert.\] If \(\sup_k\eta_k<1\) is sufficiently small, convergence is Q-linear; if \(\eta_k\to0\), it is Q-superlinear; and if \(\eta_k=O(\lVert g_k\rVert)\) with a locally Lipschitz reduced Hessian, it is Q-quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact reduced Newton is locally linear for uniformly small forcing terms, superlinear when they vanish, and quadratic when they scale with the reduced-gradient norm.
assumptions_latex: The reduced Hessian is nonsingular near \(z_*\).
The initial reduced coordinate is sufficiently close to \(z_*\).
Residual and feasibility errors satisfy the displayed forcing inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \(z_k\to z_*\) with the linear, superlinear, or quadratic rate determined by \(\eta_k\).

notation.meaning: Residual of the reduced Newton equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forcing-Sequence Regimes for Inexact Reduced Newton
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\varphi:\mathbb R^{n-m}\to\mathbb R\) be the smooth reduced objective near a nondegenerate minimizer \(z^*\). An approximate reduced Newton step \(s_k\) has residual \(r_k=\nabla^2\varphi(z_k)s_k+\nabla\varphi(z_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local full-step reduced Newton iterations with inexact tangent or coupled feasibility solves represented by a forcing residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An inexact reduced-Newton iteration is defined by \[z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\|
abla\varphi(z_k)\|,\qquad 0\leq\eta_k<1.\] Its local convergence regime is linear when \(\eta_k\leq ar\eta<1\); superlinear when \(\eta_k	o0\); and quadratic when \(
abla^2\varphi\) is locally Lipschitz and \(\eta_k=O(\|
abla\varphi(z_k)\|)\). If feasibility is computed separately, its correction residual must be included in \(r_k\) or bounded at the same asymptotic order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact reduced-Newton local convergence is classified by the forcing sequence controlling the residual of the approximate reduced Newton equation. A forcing factor uniformly below one yields a local linear regime. If the forcing factors vanish, the linear solves become increasingly accurate relative to the reduced gradient and the regime becomes superlinear. With a Lipschitz reduced Hessian and forcing factors proportional to the reduced-gradient norm, the regime is quadratic. Approximate feasibility solves must be controlled consistently; otherwise an unrecorded normal error can dominate the reduced Newton error and invalidate the stated rate.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla^2\varphi\) is continuous near \(z^*\) and positive definite at \(z^*\).
The initial reduced iterate is sufficiently close to \(z^*\), and unit steps are taken.
The forcing inequality holds at every sufficiently large iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asymptotic behavior of \(\eta_k\) determines linear, superlinear, or quadratic local convergence as specified.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(r_k\) is the backward residual of the reduced Hessian solve.
For a primal–dual KKT solve, the same definition uses the residual of the Newton–KKT equations scaled by the current KKT residual.
special_cases_latex: A constant \(\eta_k=\eta<1\) gives an eventual linear contraction.
The choice \(\eta_k=\min\{1/2,\|\nabla\varphi(z_k)\|\}\) is in the quadratic forcing regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: Oversolving far from the solution is unnecessary for the linear regime.
A fixed positive forcing factor generally prevents superlinear convergence.
boundary_notes: The cited forcing-sequence result is stated for unconstrained Newton equations; this slot applies it to a regular reduced objective.
Globalization interference and rejected unit steps are excluded from the local classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Quasi-Newton Local Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear and Dennis–Moré superlinear regimes for full-step reduced quasi-Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi=f\circ\psi\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(z_*\), with \(
abla\phi(z_*)=0\) and positive-definite \(H_*:=
abla^2\phi(z_*)\). Consider full steps \(B_ks_k=-
abla\phi(z_k)\) and \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k\). If \(B_k\) and \(B_k^{-1}\) are uniformly bounded and the iteration is locally contractive, convergence is Q-linear. If, additionally, \[ rac{\lVert(B_k-H_*)s_kVert}{\lVert s_kVert}\longrightarrow0,\] then every sufficiently close convergent sequence is Q-superlinear. Feasible primal iterates are obtained as \(x_k=\psi(z_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable reduced quasi-Newton matrices yield a local linear regime; the Dennis–Moré directional approximation condition upgrades a convergent full-step sequence to Q-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: The reduced solution Hessian \(H_*\) is positive definite.
The quasi-Newton matrices and their inverses are uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local rate is Q-linear under contraction and Q-superlinear when the displayed Dennis–Moré condition also holds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Dennis–Moré Regime for Reduced Quasi-Newton Steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\), let \(A_k=Jc(x_k)\) have full row rank, and define the orthogonal tangent projector \(P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k\). Let \(W_*=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)\), and let \(B_k\) be a symmetric curvature approximation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equality-constrained quasi-Newton methods with stabilized active equalities and unit steps near a regular solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reduced quasi-Newton local convergence is linear when the projected models remain uniformly bounded and uniformly positive definite on \(\operatorname{Range}(P_k)\) but their relative projected error need not vanish. It is superlinear when \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|P_k(B_k-W_*)(x_{k+1}-x_k)\|}{\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|}=0.\] For a two-sided reduced-Hessian approximation \(B_k=Z_kM_kZ_k^T\), the corresponding condition with \(P_k(B_k-W_*)P_k\) yields the weaker two-step superlinear relation \(\|x_{k+2}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced quasi-Newton local convergence is governed by how accurately the curvature approximation acts on the steps in tangent directions. Uniformly positive and bounded reduced models support a local linear regime. Superlinear convergence requires the projected model error along the realized step to become negligible relative to that step, which is the equality-constrained Dennis–Moré condition. When only a two-sided reduced Hessian is approximated, the standard conclusion may weaken to two-step superlinear convergence because normal–tangential cross information is omitted.
assumptions_latex: The standard smoothness, LICQ, and second-order sufficient conditions hold at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\).
The iterates converge and unit steps are eventually taken.
The approximate reduced Hessians are nonsingular on the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing projected secant error defines the superlinear regime; bounded positive reduced models without that limit define the linear regime.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With orthonormal \(Z_k\), \(P_k=Z_kZ_k^T\).
For a full approximation, the displayed limit is the projected Dennis–Moré condition (18.63).
special_cases_latex: Full BFGS under the additional local positive-definiteness hypotheses satisfies the superlinear condition.
Reduced BFGS with smoothly varying null-space bases can yield two-step superlinear convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: Accuracy of \(B_k\) outside tangent-relevant projections is not required for the primal step.
A curvature approximation may be adequate for linear convergence yet fail the superlinear test.
boundary_notes: Two-step superlinear convergence must not be reported as ordinary Q-superlinear convergence.
Changing or discontinuous null-space bases can invalidate reduced secant comparisons unless transported consistently.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Certificate Vector for Equality Optimality and Linear Solves
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(A=Jc(x)\), \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\), let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{Null}(A)\), and let \(K\delta=b\) denote the reduced or KKT system used to compute a step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable finite-dimensional diagnostics for smooth equality-constrained points and their associated numerical step solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality optimality-solve certificate is the vector \[\mathcal C(x,\lambda,\delta)=\left(\eta_{\mathrm{feas}},\eta_{\mathrm{stat}},\eta_{\mathrm{curv}},\eta_{\mathrm{solve}}\right)\] with \[\eta_{\mathrm{feas}}=\|c(x)\|,\quad \eta_{\mathrm{stat}}=\|\nabla f(x)-A^T\lambda\|,\quad \eta_{\mathrm{curv}}=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Z^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,\lambda)Z)\},\] \[\eta_{\mathrm{solve}}=\|K\delta-b\|.\] Given tolerances \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_s,\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_\ell)\), the certificate is valid at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) precisely when every component is at most its corresponding tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The certificate system combines four distinct diagnostics: equality feasibility, primal–dual stationarity, negative curvature on the tangent space, and residual of the numerical reduced or saddle-point solve. A point-and-step pair is certified only when all four components meet their separately specified tolerances. Keeping the components separate prevents a small linear-solve residual from masking infeasibility or nonstationarity, and prevents an approximate KKT point with substantial feasible negative curvature from being labeled a second-order solution.
assumptions_latex: All norms and tolerances are fixed and consistently scaled.
\(A\) has full row rank when \(Z\) or least-squares multipliers are used.
The matrix \(K\) and right-hand side \(b\) are exactly those defining the reported numerical step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C\preceq\varepsilon\) iff feasibility, stationarity, tangent-curvature, and solve-residual tests all pass.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tangent-curvature certificate can be written \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x,\lambda)d\geq-\varepsilon_c\|d\|^2\) for all \(d\) with \(Ad=0\).
With least-squares multipliers, \(\eta_{\mathrm{stat}}=\|(I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A)\nabla f(x)\|\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-Loss Failure of Linear Residual-to-Distance Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a linear distance bound when equality regularity is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c(x)=x^2\), the feasible set is \(\{0\}\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,c^{-1}(0))=|x|\), and \(|c(x)|=x^2\). Hence no finite \(\kappa\) satisfies \(|x|\le\kappa x^2\) throughout any neighborhood of zero. The residual remains a direct feasibility diagnostic, but it supplies no local linear distance bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constraint x squared equals zero shows that rank loss can make residual violation quadratic in distance to feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists\kappa<\infty:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,c^{-1}(0))\le\kappa|c(x)|\ \text{locally at }0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local conversion of an equality residual into distance from the feasible manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, let \(c(\bar x)=0\), and suppose \(\nabla c(\bar x)\) has full row rank. Then there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(\kappa>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,c^{-1}(0))\le\kappa\|c(x)\|\qquad(x\in U).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a regular feasible point, the equality residual bounds distance to the feasible manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla c(\bar x)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(x,c^{-1}(0))\le\kappa\|c(x)\|\quad\text{locally}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based certificate for equality feasibility and quantitative restoration progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), define the primal residual \(r_p(x)=c(x)\) and violation \(\theta(x)=\lVert r_p(x)\rVert\) in a declared norm. A reported point \(x\) is \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\)-feasible precisely when \[\theta(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}.\] A restoration transition from \(x_k\) to \(x_k^R\) additionally has a contraction certificate when \(\theta(x_k^R)\leq\kappa_R\theta(x_k)\) for a declared \(0<\kappa_R<1\). Both claims are directly verifiable by reevaluating \(c\), the norm, and the stated tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint residual norms certify approximate equality feasibility; comparing residual norms before and after restoration certifies the declared feasibility contraction.
assumptions_latex: The constraint evaluation and residual norm are reproducible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities certify approximate primal feasibility and, when supplied, restoration contraction.
