knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) define the equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a specified norm on \(\mathbb R^m\), and let \(\varepsilon_f\geq0\) be an absolute feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal feasibility and restoration-progress diagnostics for finite-dimensional equality constraints; stationarity and curvature are outside this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The primal feasibility residual is \[\eta_f(x)=\|c(x)\|.\] A point \(x\) has an \(\varepsilon_f\)-primal-feasibility certificate when \(\eta_f(x)\leq\varepsilon_f\). For a restoration step from \(x_k\) to \(x^+\), define absolute progress \(\Delta_f=\eta_f(x_k)-\eta_f(x^+)\) and relative progress \[\rho_f=\frac{\eta_f(x_k)-\eta_f(x^+)}{\max\{\eta_f(x_k),\sigma\}},\qquad \sigma>0.\] The restoration trial has a \(\gamma\)-progress certificate when \(\rho_f\geq\gamma\), with \(\gamma\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal feasibility certificate is the norm of the equality residual together with a declared tolerance. The certificate passes exactly when the residual norm does not exceed that tolerance. For restoration, the same residual defines absolute and safeguarded relative progress between the current and trial points. This certificate concerns only satisfaction of the primal equalities. It makes no claim about stationarity, multipliers, tangent curvature, or optimality of the objective.
assumptions_latex: The constraint vector \(c(x)\) is evaluable at the certified point.
The norm and scaling of each equality are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is \(\varepsilon_f\)-feasible iff \(\|c(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_f\); restoration progress passes iff \(\rho_f\geq\gamma\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With the infinity norm, the certificate is \(|c_i(x)|\leq\varepsilon_f\) for every equality \(i\).
With \(h(x)=\sum_i|c_i(x)|\), the certificate is the equality-only filter violation measure.
special_cases_latex: Exact feasibility is the zero-tolerance condition \(c(x)=0\).
Algorithm 18.4 uses \(\|c_k\|_\infty<\epsilon\) as its primal part of the stopping test.
immediate_consequences_latex: A zero residual is invariant under the choice of norm.
A decrease in \(\eta_f\) certifies restoration progress but not objective improvement.
boundary_notes: Raw residual norms are sensitive to constraint scaling; scaled certificates must state the scaling matrix.

children.title: Tangent Stationarity Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Tangent-coordinate diagnostics for first-order constrained criticality.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable. At \(x\), let \(J(x)=\nabla c(x)^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker J(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality constraints under LICQ; the definition certifies first-order criticality in tangent coordinates and is not a feasibility or curvature certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For tolerances \(\varepsilon_t,\varepsilon_Z,\varepsilon_o\ge0\), a tangent stationarity certificate at \(x\) is the tuple \((Z,r_t,r_Z,r_o)\), where \(r_t=Z^T
abla f(x)\), \(r_Z=J(x)Z\), and \(r_o=Z^TZ-I\), satisfying \(\|r_t\|_2\le\varepsilon_t\), \(\|r_Z\|_2\le\varepsilon_Z\), and \(\|r_o\|_2\le\varepsilon_o\). It is exact when all three tolerances vanish. With exact \(Z\), exact tangent stationarity is \(Z^T
abla f(x)=0\), equivalently \(
abla f(x)\in\operatorname{range}J(x)^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent stationarity certificate consists of a null-space basis and three measured residuals: the objective gradient in tangent coordinates, violation of the null-space equation, and loss of basis orthonormality. The certificate is accepted when these residuals meet their stated tolerances. With an exact basis, zero tangent gradient is equivalent to the objective gradient belonging to the range of the transposed constraint Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has \(n-m\) columns; exact equivalence uses \(J(x)Z=0\) and \(Z^TZ=I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate reports whether \(\|Z^T\nabla f(x)\|_2\), \(\|J(x)Z\|_2\), and \(\|Z^TZ-I\|_2\) lie within their respective tolerances.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For exact \(Z\), \(Z^T\nabla f(x)=0\iff \exists\lambda\in\mathbb R^m:\nabla f(x)+J(x)^T\lambda=0\).
For the orthogonal tangent projector \(P_T=ZZ^T\), exact tangent stationarity is equivalent to \(P_T\nabla f(x)=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), then \(Z=I\) and the certificate reduces to \(\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon_t\).
If \(n=m\) and \(J(x)\) is nonsingular, the tangent space is \(\{0\}\), so the tangent residual is vacuous.
immediate_consequences_latex: An exact tangent certificate together with \(c(x)=0\) yields the first-order KKT equations for some multiplier \(\lambda\).
Nonzero \(r_Z\) or \(r_o\) separates basis error from the tangent-gradient residual.
boundary_notes: The definition does not certify primal feasibility, second-order conditions, or global optimality.
For rank-deficient Jacobians, a rank-revealing tangent basis and an explicitly chosen stationarity concept are required.

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian with constraint gradients as rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-independent first-order stationarity certificate obtained by orthogonally projecting the objective gradient onto the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(A=Jc(x)\in\mathbb R^{m	imes n}\) have full row rank and define the orthogonal tangent projector \[P=I-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}A.\] The quantity \(r_{\mathrm{tan}}=P
abla f(x)\) certifies \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\)-projected stationarity when \(\lVert r_{\mathrm{tan}}Vert\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\). Moreover, \[\lVert P
abla f(x)Vert=\min_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}\lVert
abla f(x)+A^{\mathsf T}\lambdaVert,\] so the certificate is independent of any chosen null-space basis and equals the least attainable Lagrangian-gradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the objective gradient onto the equality tangent space gives a basis-independent stationarity residual equal to the smallest Lagrangian-gradient residual over all multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The Jacobian \(A=Jc(x)\) has full row rank.
The vector norm is Euclidean and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\lVert P\nabla f(x)\rVert\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{stat}}\) is a verifiable projected first-order stationarity certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Stationarity Does Not Certify Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required separation between tangent criticality and equality feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The bound \(\|P\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon_s\) controls only stationarity along the linearized equality space. It does not imply \(c(x)=0\) or \(\|c(x)\|\le\varepsilon_c\); for example, a constant objective has zero projected residual at every point, including infeasible points. A constrained first-order termination certificate must therefore report feasibility separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small projected gradient alone does not certify equality feasibility; feasibility must be checked independently.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker Jc(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|P\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon_s\not\Rightarrow\|c(x)\|\le\varepsilon_c\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Stationarity Does Not Certify Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projected linearized-stationarity formulation with dependent equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(P=I-A^\dagger A\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\). For every \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \[Pg=0\iff g\in\operatorname{range}(A^T)\iff \exists\lambda:\ g+A^T\lambda=0,\qquad \|Pg\|_2=\min_\lambda\|g+A^T\lambda\|_2.\] If \(A\) lacks full row rank, the projected residual remains unique but the multiplier need not be unique. At a singular nonlinear constraint point, this is a certificate on the linearized space \(\ker A\); identifying that space with the feasible-manifold tangent space requires an appropriate regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pseudoinverse extends projected linearized stationarity to dependent equality rows; the residual remains unique, though multipliers may not and nonlinear tangent interpretation requires regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=I-A^\dagger A\) projects onto \(\ker A\) and \(\|Pg\|_2=\min_\lambda\|g+A^T\lambda\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate using an orthonormal null-space basis of the equality Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), and let \(A=
abla c(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{m	imes n}\) have full row rank. If the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes(n-m)}\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker A\), then \(ho_{\mathrm{red}}=\|Z^{T}
abla f(x)\|_2\) is a reduced stationarity residual. The pair \((x,ho_{\mathrm{red}})\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-stationarity on the linearized feasible space when \(\|c(x)\|_2\leq\varepsilon_c\) and \(ho_{\mathrm{red}}\leq\varepsilon_s\). Moreover, \(ho_{\mathrm{red}}=0\) if and only if there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \(
abla f(x)+A^T\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced gradient norm measures first-order stationarity along feasible tangent directions; it vanishes exactly when a Lagrange multiplier satisfies the stationarity equation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{red}}\leq\varepsilon_s\) certifies approximate tangent stationarity, and \(\rho_{\mathrm{red}}=0\iff \exists\lambda:\nabla f(x)+A^T\lambda=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced Stationarity with Dependent Equality Rows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of the null-space reduced certificate on the linearized equality space when equations are redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker A\). Then, for every \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \[Z^Tg=0\iff g\in\operatorname{range}(A^T)\iff \exists\lambda:\ g+A^T\lambda=0.\] Thus \(\|Z^Tg\|_2\) remains an exact linearized reduced-stationarity residual with redundant rows. It is invariant under orthogonal changes of \(Z\), although the multiplier may be nonunique. At a singular nonlinear constraint point, identifying \(\ker A\) with the feasible-manifold tangent space requires an additional regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant rows do not invalidate an orthonormal null-space residual on the linearized space, but multipliers may be nonunique and nonlinear tangent interpretation requires regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^Tg=0\iff\exists\lambda:g+A^T\lambda=0\), without a full-row-rank assumption.

children.title: Basis-Invariant Stationarity Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Comparison of reduced diagnostics across alternative tangent bases.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Invariant Stationarity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of reduced, projected, and minimum multiplier-residual diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker A\), and define \(P=ZZ^T=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\). For every \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\|Z^Tg\|_2=\|Pg\|_2=\min_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m}\|g+A^T\lambda\|_2.\] Consequently, replacing \(Z\) by any other orthonormal null-space basis leaves the reduced stationarity norm unchanged. The minimizing multiplier is \(\lambda_* =-(AA^T)^{-1}Ag\), and its residual is \(g+A^T\lambda_*=Pg\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-gradient, projected-gradient, and best multiplier-residual norms coincide, so the diagnostic is independent of the chosen orthonormal tangent basis.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Z^Tg\|_2=\|Pg\|_2=\min_{\lambda}\|g+A^T\lambda\|_2\), independently of the orthonormal basis \(Z\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Metric Normalization for Nonorthonormal Tangent Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-independent stationarity magnitude when tangent coordinates are not orthonormal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\) have full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Y)=\ker A\). Then \(P_Y=Y(Y^TY)^{-1}Y^T\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\), and \[\|P_Yg\|_2^2=(Y^Tg)^T(Y^TY)^{-1}(Y^Tg).\] The metric-normalized quantity is invariant under \(Y\mapsto YS\) for every nonsingular \(S\), whereas \(\|Y^Tg\|_2\) generally depends on basis scaling. Both vanish exactly when \(g\perp\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonorthonormal tangent basis, inverse-Gram weighting recovers the invariant projected-gradient norm; the raw coordinate norm is generally basis dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Y^Tg)^T(Y^TY)^{-1}(Y^Tg)=\|P_Yg\|_2^2\) and is invariant under nonsingular coordinate changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Certificate Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation bound for projected stationarity residuals under gradient and tangent-space errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(\widetilde P\) be orthogonal projectors in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(g,\widetilde g\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Define \(\rho=\|Pg\|_2\) and \(\widetilde\rho=\|\widetilde P\widetilde g\|_2\). Then \[|\rho-\widetilde\rho|\leq \|g-\widetilde g\|_2+\|P-\widetilde P\|_2\,\|\widetilde g\|_2.\] Thus a computed certificate \(\widetilde\rho\leq\varepsilon_s\) implies \(\rho\leq\varepsilon_s+\delta_g+\delta_P\|\widetilde g\|_2\) whenever \(\|g-\widetilde g\|_2\leq\delta_g\) and \(\|P-\widetilde P\|_2\leq\delta_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient error and tangent-projector error additively bound the discrepancy between exact and computed stationarity residuals.
assumptions_latex: The stated vector and operator norms are Euclidean induced norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\rho-\widetilde\rho|\leq\delta_g+\delta_P\|\widetilde g\|_2\) under the displayed perturbation bounds.

notation.meaning: Exact and computed projected stationarity residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform stationarity-certificate sensitivity when the equality-Jacobian rank changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon\ne0\), let \(A_\varepsilon=[\varepsilon\;0]\in\mathbb R^{1\times2}\), and let \(P_\varepsilon\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A_\varepsilon\). Then \(P_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), \(A_0=0\) and \(P_0=I\). Hence \(\|A_\varepsilon-A_0\|_2=|\varepsilon|\to0\), while \(\|P_\varepsilon-P_0\|_2=1\). No uniform projector-sensitivity bound proportional only to \(\|A-\widetilde A\|\) can therefore hold across a rank change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily small Jacobian perturbations can change the tangent projector by order one when constraint rank changes.
assumptions_latex: \(P_\varepsilon\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|A_\varepsilon-A_0\|_2\to0\) while \(\|P_\varepsilon-P_0\|_2=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual KKT Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined feasibility and stationarity residual for smooth equality-constrained optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(\min_x f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define the Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\). A pair \((x,\lambda)\) is an \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d)\)-KKT certificate when \[\|c(x)\|_2\leq\varepsilon_p,\qquad \|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|_2\leq\varepsilon_d.\] It is an exact first-order KKT certificate when both tolerances are zero. If \(x\) is a local minimizer and \(\nabla c(x)\) has full row rank, then at least one multiplier \(\lambda\) gives an exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual certificate reports both equality infeasibility and the Lagrangian-gradient residual; under full-row-rank constraints, every local minimizer admits an exact certificate.
assumptions_latex: For the necessity assertion, \(\nabla c(x)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,\lambda)\) is certified by simultaneous bounds on \(\|c(x)\|_2\) and \(\|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Qualification Failure of KKT Certificate Existence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local minimizer need not admit an exact equality KKT certificate when regularity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\) subject to \(c(x)=x^2=0\). The sole feasible point \(x=0\) is a local minimizer, but \(\nabla c(0)=0\) and \[\nabla_xL(0,\lambda)=1+2\lambda\cdot0=1\] for every \(\lambda\). Hence no multiplier yields an exact KKT certificate.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with continuously differentiable \(f\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). Write \(J(x)=\nabla c(x)^T\) and \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained optimization; this is a residual certificate for a proposed primal–dual pair, not an optimality guarantee without additional regularity and curvature assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\ge0\), a primal–dual KKT certificate is a pair \((x,\lambda)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) together with residuals \(r_p=c(x)\) and \(r_d=\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)=\nabla f(x)+J(x)^T\lambda\), such that \(\|r_p\|_2\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(\|r_d\|_2\le\varepsilon_d\). The certificate is exact when \(r_p=0\) and \(r_d=0\). A scaled certificate may instead require \(\|D_pr_p\|\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(\|D_dr_d\|\le\varepsilon_d\) for specified nonsingular scaling matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual KKT certificate is a candidate point and multiplier whose constraint residual and Lagrangian-gradient residual satisfy declared tolerances. It is exact precisely when the point is feasible and the Lagrangian gradient vanishes. Any scaling used in assessing the residuals is part of the certificate and must be stated.
assumptions_latex: The norms, tolerances, and any residual scaling are fixed before the certificate is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((x,\lambda)\) is certified to the declared accuracy exactly when \(\|c(x)\|_2\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(\|\nabla f(x)+J(x)^T\lambda\|_2\le\varepsilon_d\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(J(x)\) has full row rank and \(Z\) spans \(\ker J(x)\), exact dual stationarity is equivalent to \(Z^T\nabla f(x)=0\) with \(\lambda\) solving \(J(x)J(x)^T\lambda=-J(x)\nabla f(x)\).
The combined residual is \(F(x,\lambda)=(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda),c(x))\), and exact certification is \(F(x,lambda)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For linear constraints \(c(x)=Ax-b\), the primal residual is \(Ax-b\).
When \(m=0\), the certificate reduces to unconstrained gradient stationarity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Under LICQ, an exact certificate assigns the unique multiplier associated with \(x\).
Separate primal and dual tolerances reveal whether failure is caused by infeasibility or lack of stationarity.
boundary_notes: Small KKT residuals do not alone imply proximity to a minimizer when the KKT mapping is ill-conditioned.
Second-order sufficiency, constraint qualification, and global optimality are outside this definition.
review_flags: No inspected source supports the exact tolerance-and-scaling formulation.
The character DEL typo in one equivalent display requires verifier attention.

children.title: Tangent Curvature Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics distinguishing positive, singular, and negative tangent curvature.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the smooth equality-constrained problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\). At a primal–dual pair \((x,\lambda)\), let \(J(x)\) have full row rank and let \(Z^TZ=I\), \(J(x)Z=0\). Define the reduced Lagrangian Hessian \(R=Z^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)Z\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional twice-smooth equality constraints under LICQ; the certificate classifies curvature only on the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_Z,\varepsilon_o,\varepsilon_s\ge0\), a tangent curvature certificate consists of \((Z,R,\underline\rho,v)\) satisfying \(\|J(x)Z\|_2\le\varepsilon_Z\), \(\|Z^TZ-I\|_2\le\varepsilon_o\), \(\|R-R^T\|_2\le\varepsilon_s\), and either: positive curvature, \(\underline\rho\le\lambda_{\min}((R+R^T)/2)\) with \(\underline\rho>0\); singular or nearly singular curvature, \(|\lambda_{\min}((R+R^T)/2)|\le\tau\); or negative curvature, \(\|v\|_2=1\) and \(v^TRv\le-\gamma\) for a declared \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent curvature certificate records a tangent basis, the reduced Lagrangian Hessian, basis-quality residuals, and quantitative evidence placing tangent curvature in one of three regimes: uniformly positive, singular or nearly singular, or negative. A negative-curvature certificate also supplies a unit reduced direction attaining the declared negative threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable at \(x\).
The thresholds \(\tau\ge0\) and \(\gamma>0\) are declared as part of the classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symmetric reduced operator \((R+R^T)/2\) is certified as positive, near-singular, or negative on the computed tangent coordinates according to the stated eigenvalue or Rayleigh-quotient inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With exact \(Z\), \(R\succ0\iff d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)d>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker J(x)\).
A reduced vector \(v\) with \(v^TRv<0\) corresponds to the tangent direction \(d=Zv\) with negative Lagrangian curvature.
special_cases_latex: If \(n=m\) and \(J(x)\) is nonsingular, the tangent space is zero-dimensional and curvature classification is vacuous.
For linear constraints, \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)=\nabla^2f(x)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive tangent curvature at an exact KKT point is the curvature component of a standard second-order sufficient condition.
Certified negative tangent curvature rules out positive semidefiniteness of the Lagrangian Hessian on the tangent space.
boundary_notes: Near-zero eigenvalues require a scale-aware threshold and do not by themselves distinguish exact degeneracy from numerical error.
This definition does not address curvature along infeasible directions or inequality-constraint critical cones.
review_flags: No source was inspected for the combined positive/singular/negative certificate taxonomy.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Curvature Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order tangent-space certificate formed from the Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible KKT pair \((x,\lambda)\), let \(A=\nabla c(x)\), \(H=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)\), and let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker A\). The reduced Hessian is \(R=Z^THZ\). The inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(R)\geq0\) certifies the second-order necessary condition \(d^THd\geq0\) for every tangent direction \(d\in\ker A\). If \(\lambda_{\min}(R)>0\), then the second-order sufficient condition holds and \(x\) is a strict local minimizer on \(c(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive semidefiniteness of the reduced Hessian certifies necessary tangent curvature; positive definiteness certifies a strict constrained local minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x\).
\(A\) has full row rank and \(Z\) orthonormally spans \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\succeq0\) certifies necessary tangent curvature, while \(R\succ0\) certifies strict constrained local minimality.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Inertia Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inertia test relating the bordered KKT matrix to reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(Z\) orthonormally span \(\ker A\). Define \(R=Z^THZ\) and \[K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}.\] With inertia ordered as positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts, \[\operatorname{inertia}(K)=\operatorname{inertia}(R)+(m,m,0).\] Hence \(R\succ0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\). A symmetric-indefinite factorization revealing this inertia therefore certifies positive reduced curvature without explicitly constructing \(Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT matrix has inertia equal to reduced-Hessian inertia plus one positive and one negative eigenvalue per independent equality constraint.
assumptions_latex: The columns of \(Z\) orthonormally span \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\succ0\iff\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\).

notation.meaning: Triple of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-Deficiency Boundary for KKT Inertia Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the regular bordered-inertia target when equality rows are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), where \(H=H^T\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), then \(\operatorname{nullity}(K)\ge m-\operatorname{rank}(A)>0\). Thus \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\) is impossible, and its interpretation as a positive-reduced-curvature certificate requires an independently established full-row-rank condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependent equality rows force the KKT matrix to be singular, so the regular target inertia cannot be interpreted without a rank check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nullity}(K)\ge m-\operatorname{rank}(A)>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Curvature Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-vector certificate for degeneracy of the tangent-restricted Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be symmetric, let \(A\) have full row rank, let \(Z\) orthonormally span \(\ker A\), and put \(R=Z^THZ\) and \(P=ZZ^T\). Reduced curvature is singular if and only if there exists \(p\neq0\) such that \(Rp=0\). Equivalently, there exists a nonzero tangent vector \(d=Zp\) satisfying \(Ad=0\) and \(PHd=0\). Numerically, a unit vector \(p\) with \(\|Rp\|_2\leq\varepsilon\) certifies near-singularity, and \(\sigma_{\min}(R)\leq\varepsilon\). The scalar equality \(d^THd=0\) alone does not certify singularity when \(R\) is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-Hessian null vector certifies singular tangent curvature; a zero curvature scalar alone is insufficient for an indefinite reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\) is singular exactly when a nonzero tangent direction \(d\) satisfies \(PHd=0\).

Nevertheless, \(t=0\) is a strict local minimizer of \(\phi_+\) and is not a local minimizer of \(\phi_0\). Thus a positive-semidefinite singular reduced Hessian does not by itself determine local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero reduced curvature can occur at either a strict minimum or a nonminimum, so singular semidefinite curvature is inconclusive without higher-order information.

The scalar variable is a feasible tangent coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\succeq0\) and \(\ker R\ne\{0\}\) neither imply nor refute local minimality.

children.title: Certificate Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of reduced-curvature and inertia-based classifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-checks among reduced-Hessian, projected-curvature, directional, and KKT-inertia certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) orthonormally span \(\ker A\), let \(P=ZZ^T\), and let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric. Define \(R=Z^THZ\) and \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\). For every \(p\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\) and \(d=Zp\), \(d^THd=p^TRp\), and the restriction of \(PHP\) to \(\operatorname{range}P\) is represented by \(R\). Consequently, \(R\succeq0\) if and only if no nonzero tangent vector \(d\in\ker A\) satisfies \(d^THd<0\). Moreover, \(R\succ0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\), where inertia is ordered as positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts. Thus positive reduced curvature implies absence of tangent negative curvature, but the converse yields only positive semidefiniteness and need not certify positive definiteness. Any violation of these exact-arithmetic consistency relations signals inconsistent inputs, rank decisions, bases, Hessians, or numerical factorizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced and projected curvature representations must agree. Absence of a tangent negative-curvature direction is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of the reduced Hessian, whereas positive definiteness is equivalent to KKT inertia with n positive, m negative, and no zero eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R\succeq0\) is equivalent to absence of tangent negative curvature, while \(R\succ0\) is equivalent to \(\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the tangent space \(\ker A\).
Symmetric Lagrangian Hessian or curvature matrix.
Triple of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singularity Consistency of Reduced and KKT Certificates

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(H=H^T\), let \(Z\) span \(\ker A\), and define \(R=Z^THZ\) and \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\). Then \(\operatorname{nullity}(K)=\operatorname{nullity}(R)\). Consequently, \(K\) is singular if and only if the tangent-restricted curvature is singular.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reliability certificate for computed tangent projections
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. The exact Euclidean tangent projector is \(P=I-J^T(JJ^T)^{-1}J\). Let \(\widehat P\) be an explicitly or implicitly computed approximation, and let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\) be the vector being projected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Euclidean projections associated with full-row-rank equality Jacobians; the definition covers computed actions and does not require formation of the exact projector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerances \(\varepsilon_r,\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_o\ge0\), a projection-solve reliability certificate for \(\widehat p=\widehat Pg\) consists of a computed multiplier \(\widehat y\) and residuals \(r_s=JJ^T\widehat y-Jg\), \(r_a=\widehat p-(g-J^T\widehat y)\), and \(r_c=J\widehat p\), satisfying \(\|r_s\|_2\le\varepsilon_r\), \(\|r_a\|_2\le\varepsilon_r\), and \(\|r_c\|_2\le\varepsilon_c\). If \(\widehat P\) is available as an operator, the certificate additionally records \(\|\widehat P^2-\widehat P\|_2\le\varepsilon_o\) and \(\|\widehat P-\widehat P^T\|_2\le\varepsilon_o\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection-solve reliability certificate measures the residual of the multiplier-space solve, consistency between that solve and the reported projected vector, preservation of the linearized constraints, and, when an approximate projector is explicitly available, loss of idempotence and symmetry.
assumptions_latex: All residual norms and tolerances are specified.
Operator-level tests are required only when \(\widehat P\) can be applied sufficiently to estimate them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed projection is reliable to the declared tolerances when the solve, action-consistency, constraint-preservation, idempotence, and symmetry residuals required by the certificate are bounded.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For zero tolerances, \(\widehat p=Pg\), \(J\widehat p=0\), and \(g-\widehat p\in\operatorname{range}J^T\).
An exact orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J\) is characterized by \(P^2=P\), \(P^T=P\), and \(JP=0\) with \(\operatorname{rank}P=n-m\).
special_cases_latex: For an orthonormal null-space basis \(Z\), the exact projector is \(P=ZZ^T\).
With a weighted inner product induced by \(W\succ0\), the corresponding projector is \(I-W^{-1}J^T(JW^{-1}J^T)^{-1}J\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The residual decomposition distinguishes an inaccurate inner solve from loss of constraint preservation.
A small normal-equation residual need not imply a small projection error when \(JJ^T\) is ill-conditioned.
boundary_notes: The Euclidean and weighted projectors must not be interchanged.
The displayed DEL characters mark transcription defects requiring correction during verification.
review_flags: No inspected source supports this complete residual system.
Transcription defects are present in several LaTeX expressions.

children.title: Projection Residual Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and forward-error certificate for null-space projection via normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(P=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\). To project \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) onto \(\ker A\), suppose \(y\) approximately solves \((AA^T)y=Av\), and set \(p=v-A^Ty\) and \(r=Av-AA^Ty\). Then \[Ap=r,\qquad p-Pv=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}r.\] Hence \(\|r\|_2\leq\varepsilon\) certifies both approximate tangency and the forward-error bound \(\|p-Pv\|_2\leq\|A^T(AA^T)^{-1}\|_2\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal-equation residual equals the projected vector’s constraint residual and yields an explicit forward-error bound for the projection.
assumptions_latex: Euclidean vector norms and their induced matrix norms are used.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small absolute projection residual need not imply uniformly small projection error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A_\epsilon=[\epsilon]\), \(v=1\), and \(y=0\), where \(\epsilon>0\), the projector onto \(\ker A_\epsilon=\{0\}\) is \(P=0\). The computed vector is \(p=1\) and its residual is \(r=A_\epsilon p=\epsilon\), yet \(|p-Pv|=1\). Thus \(|r|\to0\) while the projection error remains one as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As the nonzero singular value approaches zero, a projection residual can vanish while projection error remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |r|=\epsilon\to0\quad\text{while}\quad|p-Pv|=1.

children.title: Projection Orthogonality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Orthogonality diagnostics for projected quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Orthogonality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal decomposition certificate characterizing the exact tangent projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\). A vector \(p\) equals the orthogonal projection \(Pv\) if and only if \(Ap=0\) and \(P(v-p)=0\); equivalently, \(p\in\ker A\) and \(v-p\in\operatorname{range}(A^T)\). For an approximate projection, the error has the orthogonal decomposition \[\|p-Pv\|_2^2=\|(I-P)p\|_2^2+\|P(v-p)\|_2^2.\] Thus the tangency residual \((I-P)p\) and the orthogonality residual \(P(v-p)\) jointly provide an exact a posteriori projection-error certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A correct projection is tangent while its correction is normal; the squared projection error equals the sum of squared tangency and orthogonality residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the Euclidean orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=Pv\iff Ap=0\) and \(P(v-p)=0\), with the displayed exact error decomposition.

children.title: Constraint-Preservation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics for preservation of equality constraints during projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Preservation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearized and nonlinear equality-preservation bounds for an approximate tangent step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) have an \(L_c\)-Lipschitz Jacobian near the segment from \(x\) to \(x+\alpha p\), and set \(A=\nabla c(x)\). Then \[\|c(x+\alpha p)-c(x)-\alpha Ap\|_2\leq \frac{L_c}{2}\alpha^2\|p\|_2^2.\] Consequently, if \(\|c(x)\|_2\leq\varepsilon_c\) and \(\|Ap\|_2\leq\varepsilon_t\), then \[\|c(x+\alpha p)\|_2\leq\varepsilon_c+|\alpha|\varepsilon_t+\frac{L_c}{2}\alpha^2\|p\|_2^2.\] The displayed bound certifies constraint preservation to first order and quantifies nonlinear drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initial infeasibility, tangent residual, and quadratic nonlinear drift together bound equality violation after a projected step.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable on the step segment.
The entire segment \(x+t\alpha p\), \(0\leq t\leq1\), lies in that neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|c(x+\alpha p)\|_2\leq\varepsilon_c+|\alpha|\varepsilon_t+(L_c/2)\alpha^2\|p\|_2^2\).

notation.meaning: Constraint Jacobian at the current point.
Lipschitz constant of the constraint Jacobian.

children.title: Linear-Solve Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual-based assessment of inner linear solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Solve Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise residual certificate for an approximate equality-reduction linear solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and let \(\widehat z\) approximate a solution of \(Mz=b\). Define \(r=b-M\widehat z\) and \[\eta_{\mathrm{res}}=\frac{\lVert r\rVert_2}{\lVert M\rVert_2\lVert\widehat z\rVert_2+\lVert b\rVert_2},\] with \(\eta_{\mathrm{res}}=0\) when numerator and denominator both vanish. The inequality \(\eta_{\mathrm{res}}\leq\tau\) is a scale-invariant residual certificate at tolerance \(\tau\). It is directly verifiable using a matrix-vector product and norm evaluations, and it certifies \(M\widehat z=b-r\) with a residual small relative to the data and computed solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized linear-system residual below tolerance certifies that the computed vector satisfies the required solve to the declared relative accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{\mathrm{res}}\leq\tau\) certifies the normalized residual accuracy of \(\widehat z\).

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Scaled Residual with Large Forward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioning boundary of residual-only certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_\epsilon=\operatorname{diag}(\epsilon,1)\), \(b_\epsilon=(\epsilon,1)^T\), \(z=(1,1)^T\), and \(\widehat z=(0,1)^T\). Then \(r=b_\epsilon-M_\epsilon\widehat z=(\epsilon,0)^T\), so the accepted normalized residual tends to zero as \(\epsilon\downarrow0\), whereas \(\|z-\widehat z\|_2/\|z\|_2=1/\sqrt2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ill-conditioned diagonal system can have a vanishing normalized residual while relative solution error remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_{\rm res}\to0\quad\text{but}\quad\|z-\widehat z\|_2/\|z\|_2=1/\sqrt2.
knowledge_statements.title: Small Scaled Residual with Large Forward Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning requirement for converting a solve residual into solution accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(M\) is nonsingular, \(z=M^{-1}b\), and \(r=b-M\widehat z\), then \[z-\widehat z=M^{-1}r,\qquad \|z-\widehat z\|\le\|M^{-1}\|\,\|r\|.\] When \(b\ne0\), \[\frac{\|z-\widehat z\|}{\|z\|}\le\kappa(M)\frac{\|r\|}{\|b\|},\qquad \kappa(M)=\|M\|\|M^{-1}\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual bounds solution error through the inverse norm, so forward accuracy additionally requires conditioning information.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is subordinate to the declared vector norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Forward-Error Conversion

children.title: Linear-Solve Backward-Error Certificates
children.top_down_role: Backward-error assessment of computed linear-system solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Solve Backward-Error Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise backward-error interpretation of an equality-reduction linear solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times p}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and computed \(\widehat z\), let \(r=b-M\widehat z\). In the Euclidean and induced matrix norms, define \[\eta_{\mathrm{bw}}=\frac{\lVert r\rVert_2}{\lVert M\rVert_2\lVert\widehat z\rVert_2+\lVert b\rVert_2}.\] When the denominator is positive, \(\eta_{\mathrm{bw}}\) equals the smallest \(\epsilon\geq0\) for which perturbations \(\Delta M,\Delta b\) exist satisfying \((M+\Delta M)\widehat z=b+\Delta b\), \(\lVert\Delta M\rVert_2\leq\epsilon\lVert M\rVert_2\), and \(\lVert\Delta b\rVert_2\leq\epsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\). Thus \(\eta_{\mathrm{bw}}\leq\tau\) certifies normwise backward stability at tolerance \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized residual is the smallest relative data perturbation making the computed vector an exact solution, thereby providing a backward-error certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_{\mathrm{bw}}\leq\tau\) certifies an exact solve of a normwise \(\tau\)-relative perturbation of the stated system.

notation.meaning: backward perturbations to matrix and right-hand side

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise counterpart of the accepted normwise backward-error certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r=b-M\widehat z\), define \(d=|M||\widehat z|+|b|\) componentwise and \[\eta_{\rm cw}=\max_i\frac{|r_i|}{d_i},\] using \(0/0=0\) and interpreting a positive numerator over a zero denominator as \(+\infty\). Then \(\eta_{\rm cw}\) is the smallest \(\epsilon\ge0\) for which perturbations exist satisfying \((M+\Delta M)\widehat z=b+\Delta b\), \(|\Delta M|\le\epsilon|M|\), and \(|\Delta b|\le\epsilon|b|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A componentwise-scaled residual equals the smallest componentwise relative data perturbation making the computed vector an exact solution.
assumptions_latex: Absolute values and inequalities are interpreted componentwise.
The stated zero-denominator conventions are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_{\rm cw}\le\tau\iff\exists(\Delta M,\Delta b)\ \text{satisfying the displayed componentwise }\tau\text{-relative bounds}.
knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Linear-System Backward Error

children.title: Reduced-Coordinate Conditioning Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical limits arising from the constraint Jacobian and explicit reduced-coordinate bases.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be a full-row-rank constraint Jacobian, \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) a computed null-space basis, and \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) a symmetric model Hessian. Put \(R=Z^THZ\). Fix positive, scale-aware thresholds \(\tau_J,\tau_Z,\tau_R\) and residual thresholds \(\eta_Z,\eta_o\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical conditioning of explicit reduced-coordinate representations; the boundary is relative to declared scaling, norms, and thresholds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reduced-coordinate conditioning boundary is the set of triples \((J,Z,H)\) for which at least one declared reliability condition fails: \(\sigma_{\min}(J)\ge\tau_J\), \(\kappa_2(Z)\le\tau_Z\), \(\|JZ\|_2\le\eta_Z\), \(\|Z^TZ-I\|_2\le\eta_o\), or, when inversion of the reduced operator is required, \(\kappa_2(R)\le\tau_R\). Equivalently, the boundary set is the union of \(\{\sigma_{\min}(J)<\tau_J\}\), \(\{\kappa_2(Z)>\tau_Z\}\), \(\{\|JZ\|_2>\eta_Z\}\), \(\{\|Z^TZ-I\|_2>\eta_o\}\), and \(\{\kappa_2(R)>\tau_R\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced-coordinate conditioning boundary is the union of regimes where the constraint Jacobian is nearly rank deficient, the explicit null-space basis is poorly conditioned or inaccurate, or a reduced operator that must be solved is ill-conditioned. The boundary depends on declared scales and tolerances rather than on a universal numerical constant.
assumptions_latex: Matrix norms and condition numbers use a declared scaling.
The reduced-operator condition is included only when \(R\) is intended to be nonsingular and solved.
Thresholds are fixed independently of the observed residuals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A triple lies inside the reliable region precisely when every applicable conditioning and basis-quality inequality holds; it lies beyond the boundary when at least one fails.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reliable region is the intersection of the five applicable threshold sets, while the boundary/failure region is their complementary union.
For orthonormal exact \(Z\), the basis terms satisfy \(\kappa_2(Z)=1\), \(JZ=0\), and \(Z^TZ=I\).
special_cases_latex: An implicit orthogonal projector can avoid explicit \(\kappa_2(Z)\), but its solve and projector residuals remain relevant.
If \(R\) is deliberately singular, \(\kappa_2(R)\) is replaced by a spectral-gap or pseudoinverse condition measure.
immediate_consequences_latex: Passing the Jacobian test does not imply that a computed basis or reduced operator is reliable.
Every threshold must be interpreted relative to units and matrix scaling.
boundary_notes: This is a diagnostic boundary, not a convergence theorem.
Sparsity loss and factorization growth are separate computational boundaries.
review_flags: The union-of-thresholds definition is a synthesized diagnostic not tied to an inspected source.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-coordinate conditioning boundary set

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Constraint Jacobians
children.top_down_role: Near rank deficiency causing sensitive tangent spaces and multiplier estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Constraint Jacobians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Near-rank-deficiency boundary for tangent projections and multiplier recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and define the tangent projector \(P=I-A^{\mathsf T}(AA^{\mathsf T})^{-1}A\). If \(A\) is perturbed by \(E\), first-order changes in its row space and null space scale as \(O(\lVert E\rVert_2/\sigma_{\min}(A))\), while solving multiplier normal equations involving \(AA^{\mathsf T}\) has condition number \(\kappa_2(A)^2\). Consequently, when \(\lVert E\rVert_2\) is comparable to \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\), neither the computed tangent space nor multiplier estimates are reliably determined by the supplied data; at \(\sigma_{\min}(A)=0\), the stated projector formula is undefined without a generalized inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As the smallest Jacobian singular value approaches perturbation size, tangent spaces and multipliers become highly sensitive; exact rank deficiency invalidates the inverse-based reduction.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank before perturbation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert E\rVert_2\gtrsim\sigma_{\min}(A)\) marks loss of reliable tangent-space and multiplier identification.

notation.meaning: smallest singular value of the constraint Jacobian
orthogonal projector onto the Jacobian null space

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint Scaling Is Not Geometric Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates representation-dependent Jacobian conditioning from invariant feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank with \(m\geq2\), and let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular. The systems \(Ax=b\) and \(DAx=Db\) have the same feasible set and \(\ker(DA)=\ker(A)\), so their exact orthogonal tangent projectors coincide. Suitable nonsingular diagonal row scalings \(D\) can nevertheless make \(\kappa_2(DA)\) arbitrarily large. Under the stationarity convention \(\nabla f+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda=0\), the multiplier for the scaled representation is \(\widetilde\lambda=D^{-\mathsf T}\lambda\). Thus raw Jacobian conditioning and multiplier magnitude depend on constraint scaling and, without a scaling convention and perturbation model, do not certify intrinsically ill-determined feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent row scaling can make a constraint Jacobian arbitrarily ill-conditioned and rescale its multipliers while leaving the feasible set and tangent projector unchanged.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\text{ has full row rank and }m\geq2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker(DA)=\ker(A)\text{ and }P_{\ker(DA)}=P_{\ker(A)},\text{ although suitable }D\text{ make }\kappa_2(DA)\text{ arbitrarily large}.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the constraint tangent space.
Multiplier in the scaled constraint representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Scaling Is Not Geometric Ill-Conditioning

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable and let \(J(x)=\nabla c(x)^T\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), with \(m\le n\). Let \(D_c\) and \(D_x\) be specified nonsingular row and column scalings and define \(\widetilde J=D_cJ(x)D_x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equalities; ill-conditioning is defined for a chosen norm, scaling, and numerical threshold and includes near rank deficiency but not exact rank deficiency unless stated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a threshold \(\tau\ge1\), the constraint Jacobian is \(\tau\)-ill-conditioned at \(x\) when \(\widetilde J\) has full row rank but \(\kappa_2(\widetilde J)=\sigma_{\max}(\widetilde J)/\sigma_{\min}(\widetilde J)\ge\tau\). For an absolute threshold \(\delta>0\), it is \(\delta\)-nearly rank deficient when \(\sigma_{\min}(\widetilde J)\le\delta\). It is rank deficient when \(\sigma_{\min}(\widetilde J)=0\). The scaling matrices, threshold, and singular-value convention are part of the classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint Jacobian is ill-conditioned when its scaled largest-to-smallest nonzero singular-value ratio exceeds a declared threshold. It is nearly rank deficient when its smallest singular value falls below an absolute threshold, and exactly rank deficient when that singular value is zero.
assumptions_latex: The matrix norm is the spectral norm.
Row and column scalings are fixed and reported.
The relative condition number is used only while \(J(x)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The classification is determined by \(\kappa_2(D_cJ(x)D_x)\) and \(\sigma_{\min}(D_cJ(x)D_x)\) relative to the declared thresholds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For full row rank \(\widetilde J\), \(\kappa_2(\widetilde J)=\|\widetilde J\|_2\|\widetilde J^\dagger\|_2\).
The normal matrix satisfies \(\kappa_2(\widetilde J\widetilde J^T)=\kappa_2(\widetilde J)^2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=1\), the relative spectral condition number equals one for every nonzero row, so absolute scaling and row norm carry the useful degeneracy information.
Without scaling, variables or constraints with disparate units can produce a misleading condition number.
immediate_consequences_latex: Near rank deficiency indicates sensitivity of multiplier estimates and computed tangent spaces.
Normal-equation formulations amplify the spectral condition number by squaring it.
boundary_notes: No universal value of \(\tau\) separates well-conditioned from ill-conditioned matrices.
Exact rank deficiency changes the applicable constraint qualification and is not merely a large finite condition number.
review_flags: Standard matrix-conditioning definition, but no exact scholarly locator was inspected.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-conditioned equality-constraint Jacobian

children.title: Null-Space Basis Degradation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Numerical degradation of explicit null-space representations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(\widehat Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) be a computed explicit basis intended to represent \(\ker J\). Define \(e_N=\|J\widehat Z\|_2\), \(e_O=\|\widehat Z^T\widehat Z-I\|_2\), and \(\kappa_Z=\kappa_2(\widehat Z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical quality of explicit null-space bases in Euclidean coordinates; all thresholds are scaling-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For declared thresholds \(\eta_N,\eta_O\ge0\) and \(\tau_Z\ge1\), the null-space basis is reliable when \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat Z)=n-m\), \(e_N\le\eta_N\), \(e_O\le\eta_O\), and \(\kappa_Z\le\tau_Z\). The null-space basis degradation boundary is the union of cases in which rank is lost or one of these three inequalities is violated. If orthonormality is not an intended property, replace \(e_O\) by the Gram-matrix condition \(\kappa_2(\widehat Z^T\widehat Z)\le\tau_G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit null-space basis crosses its degradation boundary when it loses column rank, fails to annihilate the constraint Jacobian accurately, loses the required orthonormality, or becomes too ill-conditioned according to declared thresholds. For a deliberately nonorthogonal basis, conditioning of its Gram matrix replaces the orthogonality residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat Z\) has the intended number \(n-m\) of columns.
The matrix scaling, norm, and thresholds are stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reliability holds exactly when the intended rank and all applicable null-space, orthogonality, and conditioning tests pass.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For exact orthonormal \(Z\), \(JZ=0\), \(Z^TZ=I\), and \(ZZ^T\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker J\).
For full-column-rank \(\widehat Z\), \(\kappa_2(\widehat Z^T\widehat Z)=\kappa_2(\widehat Z)^2\).
special_cases_latex: An orthogonal-factorization basis ideally has \(\kappa_Z=1\).
A fundamental basis produced by variable elimination may satisfy \(JZ=0\) accurately while still having a large \(\kappa_Z\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Basis degradation can distort reduced gradients and reduced Hessians even when their ambient quantities are accurate.
The separate residuals distinguish loss of null-space membership from loss of coordinate quality.
boundary_notes: This definition does not assess the condition of \(J\) itself.
Implicit projectors require operator residuals rather than an explicit basis condition number.

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number of the computed basis.

review_flags: No inspected source supports the precise degradation-threshold union.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-space basis degradation boundary

children.title: Explicit Basis Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity and numerical degradation in explicit null-space bases.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Basis Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of null-space bases constructed through an explicit dependent-variable inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a full-row-rank constraint Jacobian as \(A=[B\ N]\), where \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. The explicit null-space basis \[Z=\begin{bmatrix}-B^{-1}N\\ I\end{bmatrix}\] satisfies \(AZ=0\) in exact arithmetic. Forming or applying \(B^{-1}N\) through an inexact solve introduces an error whose relative size may be amplified by \(\kappa_2(B)\); moreover, \(\lVert Z\rVert_2\geq\lVert B^{-1}N\rVert_2\). Hence a partition with \(u\kappa_2(B)\not\ll1\), where \(u\) is unit roundoff, lies beyond the reliable explicit-basis regime even when \(A\) itself retains full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit null-space basis built from a nearly singular dependent block can have large entries and roundoff-amplified errors despite full Jacobian rank.
assumptions_latex: \(A=[B\ N]\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\kappa_2(B)\not\ll1\) is a reliability boundary for the explicit basis \(Z\).

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1. Linear Equality Constraints p. 68

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1. Linear Equality Constraints p. 68

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-Conditioned Jacobian with an Unbounded Explicit Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that partition-induced basis growth can occur without intrinsic full-Jacobian ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), let \(A_\varepsilon=[\,\varepsilon\ \ 1\,]\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times2}\), choose \(B_\varepsilon=[\varepsilon]\), and set \(N=[1]\). Using the ratio of nonzero singular values, \(\kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)=1\) and \(\kappa_2(B_\varepsilon)=1\), but \(\lVert B_\varepsilon^{-1}\rVert_2=\varepsilon^{-1}\). The explicit null-space vector \(Z_\varepsilon=(-\varepsilon^{-1},1)^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(A_\varepsilon Z_\varepsilon=0\) and \(\lVert Z_\varepsilon\rVert_2=\sqrt{1+\varepsilon^{-2}}\to\infty\). Thus relative condition numbers alone do not detect scaling-induced growth of an inverse-based explicit basis; inverse norm, block scaling, or the resulting basis norm must also be monitored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relatively well-conditioned full Jacobian and scalar dependent block can still produce an unbounded explicit null-space basis because their scaling makes the block inverse large.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)=\kappa_2(B_\varepsilon)=1,\qquad\lVert Z_\varepsilon\rVert_2=\sqrt{1+\varepsilon^{-2}}\to\infty.

notation.meaning: Explicit null-space basis vector produced by the partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Conditioned Jacobian with an Unbounded Explicit Basis

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-Conditioned Jacobian with an Unstable Explicit Partition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that partition-induced explicit-basis instability can occur without intrinsic Jacobian ill-conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), let \(A_\varepsilon=[\,\varepsilon\ \ 1\,]\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times2}\), choose the dependent block \(B_\varepsilon=[\varepsilon]\), and let \(N=[1]\). Since \(A_\varepsilon\) has only one nonzero singular value, \(\kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)=1\), whereas \(\kappa_2(B_\varepsilon)=1\) but solving with \(B_\varepsilon\) has absolute inverse norm \(\lVert B_\varepsilon^{-1}\rVert_2=\varepsilon^{-1}\). The explicit null-space vector \(Z_\varepsilon=(-\varepsilon^{-1},1)^{\mathsf T}\) therefore has \(\lVert Z_\varepsilon\rVert_2\to\infty\). Thus a full Jacobian can be perfectly conditioned in relative spectral condition number while a poor dependent-variable choice produces an unbounded explicit basis; monitoring only \(\kappa_2(B)\) is insufficient when block scaling is not normalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A well-conditioned full Jacobian can yield an unbounded explicit null-space basis when the chosen dependent block is badly scaled, even though that scalar block has condition number one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)=1\quad\text{but}\quad\lVert Z_\varepsilon\rVert_2=\sqrt{1+\varepsilon^{-2}}\to\infty.

notation.meaning: Explicit null-space basis vector produced by the partition.

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Conditioned Jacobian with an Unstable Explicit Partition

children.title: Loss of Basis Orthogonality
children.top_down_role: Deterioration of orthogonality in computed reduced-coordinate bases.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Basis Orthogonality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric distortion caused by a numerically nonorthogonal null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) be a computed null-space basis and set \(E=Z^{\mathsf T}Z-I_q\). If \(\delta=\lVert E\rVert_2<1\), then every reduced vector \(s\in\mathbb{R}^q\) satisfies \[(1-\delta)\lVert s\rVert_2^2\leq\lVert Zs\rVert_2^2\leq(1+\delta)\lVert s\rVert_2^2,\] and \(\kappa_2(Z)\leq\sqrt{(1+\delta)/(1-\delta)}\). As \(\delta\uparrow1\), reduced-coordinate lengths become arbitrarily distorted; for \(\delta\geq1\), this certificate supplies no positive lower bound and cannot certify that the columns remain numerically independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orthogonality defect bounds distortion between reduced and full-space lengths; as the defect approaches one, the basis may become numerically rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta<1\) bounds metric distortion, whereas \(\delta\geq1\) crosses the certificate's independence boundary.

notation.meaning: spectral norm of the orthogonality defect

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Nullness Does Not Ensure Basis Orthogonality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates null-space accuracy from metric quality of a computed basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=(1,0,0)\) and, for \(0<\varepsilon<1\), let \(Z_\varepsilon=[z_1,z_2]\), where \(z_1=(0,1,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(z_2=(0,1,\varepsilon)^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(AZ_\varepsilon=0\), but \(\sigma_{\min}(Z_\varepsilon)\to0\), \(\kappa_2(Z_\varepsilon)\to\infty\), and \(\lVert Z_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}Z_\varepsilon-I\rVert_2\to1\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Thus an exact null-space residual does not certify orthogonality or numerical independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact null-space basis can become arbitrarily ill conditioned as its columns become parallel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AZ_\varepsilon=0\) while \(\kappa_2(Z_\varepsilon)\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Exact but increasingly nonorthogonal null-space basis family.

children.title: Reduced-Coordinate Contamination
children.top_down_role: Propagation of basis defects into reduced coordinates and operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Coordinate Contamination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of null-space residuals into nominally feasible reduced steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) be the constraint Jacobian and let the computed basis \(\widehat Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) have null-space residual \(F=A\widehat Z\). For any reduced coordinate \(s\in\mathbb{R}^q\), the lifted step \(p=\widehat Zs\) obeys \[Ap=Fs,\qquad \lVert Ap\rVert_2\leq\lVert F\rVert_2\lVert s\rVert_2.\] Thus a basis error that appears small in isolation can produce material linearized-constraint violation when multiplied by a large reduced step. A tolerance \(\lVert F\rVert_2\lVert s\rVert_2\leq\tau_c\) certifies that this contamination remains below the prescribed feasibility budget \(\tau_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space residual contaminates a lifted reduced step in direct proportion to the reduced-step norm, yielding a computable feasibility-error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert A\widehat Z\rVert_2\lVert s\rVert_2\leq\tau_c\) certifies bounded reduced-coordinate contamination.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1. Linear Equality Constraints p. 68

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of a basis perturbation into reduced first-order data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be an exact tangent basis, \(\widehat Z=Z+\Delta Z\), and \(g\in\mathbb R^n\). For \(g_R=Z^{\mathsf T}g\) and \(\widehat g_R=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}g\), \[\widehat g_R-g_R=\Delta Z^{\mathsf T}g,\qquad \lVert\widehat g_R-g_R\rVert_2\leq\lVert\Delta Z\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis error perturbs the reduced gradient by the transpose of that error applied to the ambient gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\widehat g_R-g_R\rVert_2\leq\lVert\Delta Z\rVert_2\lVert g\rVert_2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Gradient Perturbation from Basis Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of a basis perturbation through congruence reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(\widehat Z=Z+\Delta Z\), \(R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\), and \(\widehat R=\widehat Z^{\mathsf T}H\widehat Z\). Then \[\widehat R-R=\Delta Z^{\mathsf T}HZ+Z^{\mathsf T}H\Delta Z+\Delta Z^{\mathsf T}H\Delta Z,\] and \[\lVert\widehat R-R\rVert_2\leq\lVert H\rVert_2\bigl(2\lVert Z\rVert_2\lVert\Delta Z\rVert_2+\lVert\Delta Z\rVert_2^2\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis error contaminates a reduced operator through two first-order cross terms and one quadratic term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\widehat R-R\rVert_2\leq\lVert H\rVert_2(2\lVert Z\rVert_2\lVert\Delta Z\rVert_2+\lVert\Delta Z\rVert_2^2)\).

children.title: Basis Reorthogonalization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where maintaining basis quality becomes numerically or computationally difficult.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Reorthogonalization Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance and reorthogonalization thresholds for a computed null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed basis \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) of the intended null space of \(A\), define \(\delta_o=\lVert Z^{\mathsf T}Z-I_q\rVert_2\) and \(\delta_n=\lVert AZ\rVert_2/(\lVert A\rVert_2\lVert Z\rVert_2)\), with a zero ratio when its numerator and denominator vanish. Given tolerances \(0<\tau_o<1\) and \(\tau_n\geq0\), accept the basis only if \(\delta_o\leq\tau_o\) and \(\delta_n\leq\tau_n\). If only \(\delta_o>\tau_o\), orthogonal re-factorization is indicated; if \(\delta_n>\tau_n\), reorthogonalization alone is insufficient and the null-space construction or underlying solve must be recomputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reorthogonalize when orthogonality fails but the null-space residual remains acceptable; reconstruct the basis when the null-space residual itself exceeds tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_o>\tau_o\) triggers reorthogonalization, while \(\delta_n>\tau_n\) triggers basis reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits reorthogonalization to bases whose orthogonality defect still certifies numerical full rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta_o=\lVert Z^{\mathsf T}Z-I\rVert_2\). If \(\delta_o<1\), then \(Z\) has full column rank and \(1-\delta_o\leq\sigma_i(Z)^2\leq1+\delta_o\). For a thin QR factorization \(Z=QR\), \[\lVert AQ\rVert_2\leq\frac{\lVert AZ\rVert_2}{\sqrt{1-\delta_o}}.\] Hence reorthogonalization preserves an acceptable null-space residual only while the basis remains sufficiently far from rank loss. If \(\delta_o\geq1\), the defect supplies no positive lower singular-value bound, and reorthogonalization alone is not certified; rank-revealing reconstruction may be required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reorthogonalization is justified only while the computed basis remains numerically full rank; once the orthogonality defect reaches one, reconstruction may be necessary.
assumptions_latex: Z=QR\text{ is a thin QR factorization when }Z\text{ has full column rank}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_o<1\Rightarrow\sigma_{\min}(Z)\geq\sqrt{1-\delta_o},\quad\delta_o\geq1\text{ gives no rank certificate}.

notation.meaning: Triangular coordinate transformation from the original basis.

children.title: Poor Variable Partitions
children.top_down_role: Unstable dependent-variable choices in variable-reduction methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Poor Variable Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for dependent-variable elimination in equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\geq m\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\), \(N\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(n-m)}\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(d_D\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(d_I\in\mathbb{R}^{n-m}\). For the linearized equality equation \(Bd_D+Nd_I=-c\), variable reduction gives \[d_D=-B^{-1}(c+Nd_I)\] when \(B\) is nonsingular. This representation exists uniquely for every \(c\) and \(d_I\) only when \(B\) is nonsingular. Absolute sensitivity is governed by \(\lVert B^{-1}\rVert_2\), while relative sensitivity of a backward-stable solve is governed by \(\kappa_2(B)\). A partition is numerically poor when \(B\) is singular or when \(u\kappa_2(B)\not\ll1\), where \(u\) is unit roundoff; in that regime dependent steps can be highly inaccurate and can grow without bound along sequences for which \(B\) approaches singularity, even though another column partition of the full Jacobian may be well conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable elimination is unreliable when the selected dependent-variable Jacobian block is singular or too ill conditioned, even if the full constraint Jacobian admits a better partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) singular or \(u\kappa_2(B)\not\ll1\) marks a poor variable partition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Bad Minor in a Well-Conditioned Jacobian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that full-Jacobian row regularity does not guarantee a stable selected partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), let \(J_\varepsilon=(\varepsilon,1)=[B_\varepsilon\ N]\). Its sole nonzero singular value is \(\sqrt{1+\varepsilon^2}\), so it remains uniformly full row rank. Choosing the first variable as dependent gives \(B_\varepsilon=[\varepsilon]\) and \(d_D=-\varepsilon^{-1}(c+d_I)\), which is unbounded for fixed \(c+d_I\ne0\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Choosing the second variable as dependent gives the block \([1]\) and avoids this amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly regular full Jacobian can contain a selected dependent block whose inverse causes arbitrarily large elimination amplification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\min}(J_\varepsilon)\geq1\) while \(\lvert B_\varepsilon^{-1}\rvert=\varepsilon^{-1}\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: A Bad Minor in a Well-Conditioned Jacobian

The associated fundamental null-space basis is \(Z_F=(-J_D^{-1}J_I,I)^T\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For thresholds \(\delta_D>0\), \(\tau_D\ge1\), and \(\tau_F\ge1\), a variable partition is poor when \(J_D\) is singular, \(\sigma_{\min}(J_D)\le\delta_D\), \(\kappa_2(J_D)\ge\tau_D\), or \(\|J_D^{-1}J_I\|_2\ge\tau_F\). The scaling and ordering defining \(J_D\) and \(J_I\) are part of the partition.

The classification can change under variable scaling or column permutation.

children.title: Dense Reduced-Operator Fill
children.top_down_role: Loss of exploitable sparsity after mathematically valid elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Reduced-Operator Fill
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparsity-loss boundary under null-space congruence reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be a sparse symmetric operator and \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times q}\) a null-space basis. The reduced operator is \(H_R=Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\), with entries \[(H_R)_{\alpha\beta}=\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{j=1}^n Z_{i\alpha}H_{ij}Z_{j\beta}.\] Sparsity of \(H\) alone imposes no sparsity on \(H_R\). For diagonal \(H\) with generic unequal diagonal entries and a generic dense \(Z\), every entry of \(H_R\) is nonzero, so \(\operatorname{nnz}(H_R)=q^2\). Thus mathematically valid elimination can cross from sparse full-space computation to quadratic reduced storage and dense-factorization cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense null-space basis can turn even a diagonal full-space operator into a fully dense reduced operator, destroying sparse storage and factorization advantages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Generic dense \(Z\) permits \(\operatorname{nnz}(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)=q^2\) even for diagonal \(H\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense fill in a reduced operator
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be a sparse symmetric operator and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\) a null-space basis, where \(q=n-m\). The reduced operator is \(R=Z^THZ\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\). For a structural sparsity pattern, write \(\operatorname{nnz}(M)\) for its number of stored nonzeros and \(\rho(M)=\operatorname{nnz}(M)/(\text{number of entries of }M)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural or thresholded numerical sparsity of explicitly formed reduced operators; conditioning is not part of this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a density threshold \(\rho_{\max}\in(0,1]\) or fill-ratio threshold \(\phi_{\max}\ge1\), dense reduced-operator fill occurs when \(\rho(R)\ge\rho_{\max}\) or when \(\phi_R=\operatorname{nnz}(R)/\max\{1,\operatorname{nnz}(H)\}\ge\phi_{\max}\), according to the declared convention. If numerical sparsity is used, an entry is counted only when \(|R_{ij}|>\tau_{ij}\) for specified thresholds. The classification is attached to the representation \((H,Z)\), since a different valid basis may induce a different pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense reduced-operator fill occurs when explicitly projecting a sparse ambient operator through a null-space basis produces a reduced matrix whose density or nonzero fill ratio exceeds a declared threshold. The basis, ordering, and rule for treating small numerical entries as zero are part of the classification.
assumptions_latex: \(R=Z^THZ\) is explicitly formed or its structural pattern is available.
The nonzero convention and any numerical dropping thresholds are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representation crosses the fill boundary precisely when its reduced density or declared fill ratio reaches the prescribed threshold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Structural fill is \(\operatorname{pattern}(R)\setminus\operatorname{pattern}(H_{\mathrm{reference}})\) when a compatible reduced reference pattern is supplied.
A dense \(Z\) can make \(R=Z^THZ\) structurally dense even when \(H\) is sparse.
special_cases_latex: If \(Z\) is a coordinate-selection matrix, \(R\) is a principal submatrix and introduces no projection-induced arithmetic fill.
Implicit products \(v\mapsto Z^TH(Zv)\) can avoid storing a dense \(R\) although the induced operator remains dense.
immediate_consequences_latex: Dense fill can increase storage and factorization cost without invalidating the mathematical reduction.
Basis selection affects sparsity independently of tangent-space correctness.

This definition does not imply ill-conditioning.
