knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accuracy boundary for KKT-based projection computations
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&J^T\\J&0\end{pmatrix}\). A computed pair \((\widehat p,\widehat\lambda)\) is intended to solve \(K(p,\lambda)^T=(b,d)^T\) or to realize a projection through an equivalent Schur-complement or normal-equation reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coupled KKT, Schur-complement, and implicit-projection computations; thresholds are relative to scaling and the chosen formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For declared backward-error tolerance \(\eta_K\), constraint tolerance \(\eta_c\), and projection tolerance \(\eta_P\), the computation is inside the KKT-projection accuracy region when \(\|b-H\widehat p-J^T\widehat\lambda\|\le\eta_K\), \(\|d-J\widehat p\|\le\eta_c\), and every required projector test—such as \(\|J\widehat Pg\|\le\eta_P\), \(\|\widehat P^2g-\widehat Pg\|\le\eta_P\), or \(|u^T\widehat Pv-v^T\widehat Pu|\le\eta_P\|u\|\|v\|\)—passes for the declared test vectors. The accuracy boundary is the union of failures of these inequalities or failure of the inner solve to terminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT-projection accuracy boundary separates computations whose coupled residual, constraint residual, and required projection invariants meet declared tolerances from computations where at least one test fails or the inner solve does not terminate. It applies whether the projection is obtained from the full KKT system, a Schur complement, or an implicit operator.
assumptions_latex: The KKT right-hand side, scaling, norms, and stopping tolerances are specified.
Only projector properties required by the intended projection are tested.
Test-vector certificates are distinguished from full operator-norm certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A computation crosses the boundary when any required coupled-solve, constraint-preservation, or projection-invariant test exceeds its tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The first two residuals combine as \(r_K=(b,d)^T-K(\widehat p,\widehat\lambda)^T\).
For an exact Euclidean tangent projector, \(JP=0\), \(P^2=P\), and \(P^T=P\).
special_cases_latex: When \(H=I\) and \(d=0\), the KKT system computes the Euclidean projection of \(b\) onto \(\ker J\).
A Schur-complement solve can have a small internal residual but fail the reconstructed full-KKT residual.
immediate_consequences_latex: Reporting formulation-specific and reconstructed residuals helps localize accuracy loss.
Passing finitely many test vectors does not establish an operator-norm bound unless the testing protocol supplies such a guarantee.
boundary_notes: Several displays contain DEL transcription artifacts and require correction.
This definition does not prescribe a factorization or iterative solver.
review_flags: No inspected source supports the combined boundary definition.

children.title: Schur-Complement Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity and accuracy loss in multiplier-space reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Ill-Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning limits of multiplier-space Schur-complement reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the equality-constrained KKT matrix with \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) symmetric positive definite and full-row-rank \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Its multiplier Schur complement is \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), and \[\frac{\sigma_{\min}(A)^2}{\lambda_{\max}(H)}\leq\lambda_{\min}(S)\leq\lambda_{\max}(S)\leq\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)^2}{\lambda_{\min}(H)}.\] Consequently, \(\kappa_2(S)\leq\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(A)^2\), while small \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\) or severe anisotropy in \(H\) can make multiplier recovery highly sensitive. If \(A\) loses row rank, \(S\) becomes singular and the inverse-based multiplier reduction fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The multiplier Schur complement can inherit squared Jacobian sensitivity and Hessian anisotropy; it becomes singular when the constraint Jacobian loses row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(S)\leq\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(A)^2\), and rank loss of \(A\) makes \(S\) singular.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full-Row-Rank Failure for an Indefinite Primal Block
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that full row rank alone does not keep an indefinite-primal-block Schur complement nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)\) and \(A=[1\;1]\). Then \(H\) is symmetric and nonsingular and \(A\) has full row rank, but \[AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}=[1\;1]\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1\\1\end{bmatrix}=0.\] Thus invertibility of \(H\) and full row rank of \(A\) do not ensure a nonsingular multiplier Schur complement when \(H\) is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With an indefinite primal block, a full-row-rank constraint Jacobian can still produce a singular Schur complement.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is eliminated through its exact inverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Invertibility of \(H\) and full row rank of \(A\) do not imply invertibility of \(AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) for indefinite \(H\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ill-conditioning of a multiplier-space Schur complement
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and \(J\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Eliminating the primal variable from the KKT matrix produces the multiplier-space Schur complement \(S=JH^{-1}J^T\), up to a sign convention. Let \(D_S\) be a declared nonsingular scaling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space reductions with nonsingular primal block; the spectral characterization applies directly when the scaled Schur complement is symmetric positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau_S\ge1\), the Schur complement is \(\tau_S\)-ill-conditioned when it is nonsingular and \(\kappa_2(D_SSD_S^T)\ge\tau_S\). It is \(\delta_S\)-nearly singular when \(\sigma_{\min}(D_SSD_S^T)\le\delta_S\), and singular when that smallest singular value is zero. If \(H\succ0\) and \(J\) has full row rank, then \(S\succ0\) and the condition number equals \(\lambda_{\max}(D_SSD_S^T)/\lambda_{\min}(D_SSD_S^T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier-space Schur complement is ill-conditioned when the condition number of its declared scaling exceeds a threshold, nearly singular when its smallest singular value is sufficiently small, and singular when that value vanishes. For a positive-definite primal block and full-row-rank constraints, eigenvalue ratios provide the same classification.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is nonsingular so that \(S\) is defined.
The eigenvalue formulation additionally assumes positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier-space reduction crosses its conditioning boundary according to the scaled Schur complement's condition number or smallest singular value.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonsingular \(S\), \(\kappa_2(S)=\|S\|_2\|S^{-1}\|_2\).
special_cases_latex: If \(H=I\), then \(S=JJ^T\) and \(\kappa_2(S)=\kappa_2(J)^2\) for full-row-rank \(J\).
For indefinite \(H\), \(S\) may be indefinite or singular even when both \(H\) and \(J\) have their nominal ranks.
immediate_consequences_latex: Large \(\kappa_2(S)\) indicates sensitivity in multiplier-space solves.
Primal and multiplier scaling can materially change the measured conditioning.
boundary_notes: Forming \(S\) explicitly may introduce rounding error and fill not represented by its exact condition number.
A sign change in the Schur-complement convention does not change its spectral condition number.

children.title: Normal-Equation Condition Amplification
children.top_down_role: Accuracy loss in range-space and projection calculations.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Condition Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared-condition-number accuracy boundary in range-space normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. The nonzero singular values of \(A\) are the square roots of the eigenvalues of \(AA^{\mathsf T}\); therefore \[\kappa_2(AA^{\mathsf T})=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(AA^{\mathsf T})}{\lambda_{\min}(AA^{\mathsf T})}=\left(\frac{\sigma_{\max}(A)}{\sigma_{\min}(A)}\right)^2=\kappa_2(A)^2.\] Thus forming and solving range-space normal equations squares the spectral condition number. Under standard backward-stable arithmetic, forward-error bounds consequently contain a factor of order \(u\kappa_2(A)^2\), so useful accuracy cannot generally be guaranteed when that quantity is not small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Range-space normal equations square the Jacobian's spectral condition number, potentially turning moderate Jacobian conditioning into severe accuracy loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(AA^{\mathsf T})=\kappa_2(A)^2\), with an accuracy boundary near \(u\kappa_2(A)^2\not\ll1\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, with singular values \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_m>0\). A range-space or projection computation may replace an equation involving \(A\) by the normal matrix \(N=AA^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral two-norm conditioning in exact arithmetic; finite-precision formation error is a related but distinct effect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normal-equation condition amplification is the transformation from \(A\) to \(N=AA^T\), for which \(\lambda_i(N)=\sigma_i(A)^2\) and therefore \(\kappa_2(N)=\kappa_2(A)^2\). For a reliability threshold \(\tau_N\), the normal-equation boundary is crossed when \(\kappa_2(A)^2\ge\tau_N\), equivalently \(\kappa_2(N)\ge\tau_N\). If \(A\) is rank deficient, \(N\) is singular and both condition numbers are infinite under the standard convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal equations square every singular value of the underlying matrix and consequently square its spectral condition number. The condition-amplification boundary is crossed when that squared condition number exceeds a declared threshold; rank deficiency makes the normal matrix singular.

\(A\) has full row rank for finite condition numbers.
The same compatible scaling is used when comparing \(A\) and \(AA^T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normal matrix has condition number \(\kappa_2(AA^T)=\kappa_2(A)^2\), so the declared accuracy boundary is determined by the squared condition measure.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\lambda_{\max}(AA^T)=\sigma_{\max}(A)^2\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(AA^T)=\sigma_{\min}(A)^2\).
For \(A=J\), solving \(JJ^Ty=Jg\) underlies the Euclidean range-space correction.
special_cases_latex: If \(A\) has orthonormal rows, then \(AA^T=I\) and no condition amplification occurs.
If \(\kappa_2(A)=10^q\), then \(\kappa_2(AA^T)=10^{2q}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical boundary for indefinite KKT factorization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K=K^T=\begin{pmatrix}H&J^T\\J&0\end{pmatrix}\) be a sparse symmetric indefinite KKT matrix. A computed pivoted factorization has the form \(P^TKP\approx LDL^T\), where \(P\) is a permutation, \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and \(D\) has permitted \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision sparse symmetric-indefinite direct factorization; the boundary depends on pivoting, scaling, storage, and declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given thresholds \(\eta_b,\gamma_{\max},\phi_{\max},M_{\max}\), an indefinite KKT factorization is inside the reliability region when the normalized backward error \(\|P^TKP-LDL^T\|/(\|K\|+\|L\|^2\|D\|)\le\eta_b\), the declared element-growth measure \(\gamma\le\gamma_{\max}\), the factor fill ratio \(\phi=(\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(D))/\max\{1,\operatorname{nnz}(K)\}\le\phi_{\max}\), and required memory \(M\le M_{\max}\). The factorization boundary is crossed if any test fails, a stable pivot cannot be selected, or storage is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite KKT factorization crosses its numerical boundary when its normalized backward error, pivot-growth measure, fill ratio, or memory demand exceeds a declared limit, or when the pivoting strategy cannot continue safely. Numerical stability and storage are separate recorded components.
assumptions_latex: The factorization, scaling, permutation, and pivoting convention are specified.
The denominator in the backward-error measure is nonzero.
Structural nonzeros and memory units use declared conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization is certified only when every required stability and resource inequality holds and the pivot sequence completes.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The unpermuted residual is \(K-P LDL^TP^T\).
When the factorization completes, solve residuals for representative right-hand sides may supplement but do not replace the matrix backward-error certificate.
special_cases_latex: Quasi-definite KKT matrices may permit more structured pivot choices than general symmetric-indefinite matrices.
A numerically stable factorization can still cross the memory boundary because of fill.
immediate_consequences_latex: Separate growth, backward-error, and fill measures prevent computational failure from being conflated with algebraic singularity.
Scaling and ordering can move the same exact KKT matrix across the practical boundary.
boundary_notes: Thresholds are implementation- and architecture-dependent.
This definition does not claim that a small factorization residual implies a small forward error for ill-conditioned \(K\).
review_flags: No inspected source supports this combined stability-and-memory boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical boundary for indefinite KKT factorization

children.title: Indefinite Pivoting Stability
children.top_down_role: Numerical stability limits associated with pivot selection in full-KKT factorizations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Posteriori Backward-Error Certificate for Pivoted LDL Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation-independent backward-error diagnostic for a computed symmetric-indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\ne0\), and let computed factors \(P,L,D\) define \(\widehat K=P LD L^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}\). Set \(R=K-\widehat K\) and \(\eta_F=\|R\|/\|K\|\) in any fixed consistent matrix norm. Then \(K-R=\widehat K\), so \(\eta_F\) is an exact normwise backward-error certificate for the represented factorization. Small \(\eta_F\) certifies a nearby-matrix factorization, but does not by itself guarantee a small solution forward error when \(K\) is ill conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual of the reconstructed pivoted LDL factors directly certifies factorization backward error, independently of a particular pivot-growth theorem.
assumptions_latex: The same consistent matrix norm is used in numerator and denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_F=\|K-P LDL^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}\|/\|K\|\) is the represented factorization's relative normwise backward error.

notation.meaning: Computed permutation, triangular factor, and block-diagonal pivot factor.

knowledge_statements.title: A Posteriori Backward-Error Certificate for Pivoted LDL Factorization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Breakdown of Unpivoted Scalar LDL Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal nonsingular symmetric-indefinite example requiring a two-by-two pivot or symmetric interchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\). Then \(K\) is symmetric and nonsingular, but scalar unpivoted \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) elimination encounters the zero leading pivot and cannot form \(l_{21}=K_{21}/d_{11}\). Taking \(K\) itself as a \(2\times2\) pivot block gives the exact block factorization \(K=I K I^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingularity does not prevent scalar-pivot breakdown; two-by-two pivots or symmetric interchanges are essential.
assumptions_latex: Scalar unpivoted elimination processes the leading diagonal entry first.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonsingularity does not guarantee an unpivoted \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization using only nonzero \(1\times1\) pivots.
knowledge_statements.title: Breakdown of Unpivoted Scalar LDL Factorization
Indefinite Pivoting Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-stability condition for pivoted symmetric-indefinite KKT factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\) be a nonsingular KKT matrix, and suppose a symmetric-indefinite factorization with permutation and one-by-one or two-by-two pivots computes \(P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\). Let \(\rho\) denote the element-growth factor produced during elimination. A standard floating-point backward-error model has \[(K+E)\widehat x=b,\qquad \lVert E\rVert\leq c_nu\rho\lVert K\rVert,\] where \(u\) is unit roundoff and \(c_n\) depends polynomially on dimension and implementation details. The factorization is backward stable only when \(c_nu\rho\ll1\); unbounded or excessive growth crosses the stability boundary, regardless of a small final linear residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric-indefinite pivoting is backward stable only when pivot-induced element growth keeps the factorization perturbation small relative to the KKT matrix.
assumptions_latex: the factorization uses admissible symmetric one-by-one or two-by-two pivots
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_nu\rho\ll1\) is the backward-stability condition for the computed indefinite factorization.

notation.meaning: permutation, triangular factor, and block-diagonal pivot factor

children.title: KKT Factor Fill Growth
children.top_down_role: Expansion of factor sparsity during coupled KKT factorization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Realized Fill in a Block-LDL KKT Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-complete fill measure for a realized sparse symmetric-indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q^{\mathsf T}KQ=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) be the realized factorization after all symmetric reorderings and pivot interchanges, with unit lower-triangular \(L\) and block-diagonal \(D\). Let \(\mathcal S_-(B)=\{(i,j):i>j,\ B_{ij}\text{ is structurally present}\}\). Define
\[F_{\rm real}=|\mathcal S_-(L)\setminus\mathcal S_-(Q^{\mathsf T}KQ)|.\]
This counts strict-lower factor positions absent from the correspondingly permuted input; entries stored in \(D\), including off-diagonal entries of \(2\times2\) pivot blocks, are not counted as fill in \(L\). Total factor storage is instead measured directly by the stored entries and metadata of \(L\) and \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Realized fill counts new strict-lower positions in the final triangular factor after all numerical permutations, while pivot-block storage is counted separately.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) has a fixed structural sparsity pattern.
\(Q\) includes every symmetric permutation actually used by the factorization.
Structural presence is distinguished from numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\rm real}\) is a convention-stable fill count for realized block-\(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factors.

notation.meaning: Strict-lower structural pattern of a matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Realized Fill in a Block-LDL KKT Factorization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes predicted fill for a fixed ordering from fill realized after stability-driven pivot changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symbolic fill prediction based on an initial permutation \(P\) describes the realized factor pattern only while numerical factorization preserves the assumed elimination sequence and pivot-block structure. Delayed pivots, threshold interchanges, or other stability-driven symmetric permutations can change the elimination graph and create factor entries not present in that prediction. Therefore symbolic fill for \(P\) is not, without such invariance, an exact certificate of realized block-LDL storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical pivot changes can invalidate fixed-order symbolic fill predictions and increase realized factor storage.
assumptions_latex: The symbolic prediction is constructed for a specified initial ordering and pivot model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed-order symbolic pattern is exact for realized fill only when the numerical elimination sequence conforms to its symbolic assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic-to-Numerical Fill Boundary
KKT Factor Fill Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic fill and storage growth for sparse symmetric-indefinite KKT factorizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) be a structurally symmetric sparse KKT matrix, let \(P\) be a symmetric permutation, and suppose \(P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), where \(D\) has permitted \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks. If \(S_P\) is the lower-triangular structural pattern of \(P^{\mathsf T}KP\), define the factor fill and fill-growth ratio by
\[
F(P)=\operatorname{nnz}(L)-\operatorname{nnz}(S_P),\qquad
\rho_F(P)=\frac{\operatorname{nnz}(L)+\operatorname{nnz}(D)}{\operatorname{nnz}(S_P)}.
\]
Entries of \(L\) absent from \(S_P\) are fill entries. Thus increasing \(F(P)\) enlarges factor storage and generally increases triangular-solve and factorization work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor fill counts new nonzeros created by an ordered KKT factorization; its growth increases memory use and usually raises factorization and solve costs.
assumptions_latex: \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\) has a fixed sparse structural pattern.
\(P^{\mathsf T}KP\) admits the stated pivoted \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(P)\) and \(\rho_F(P)\) quantify the structural growth of the KKT factors relative to the permuted input matrix.

notation.meaning: Lower-triangular structural pattern of the permuted KKT matrix.
Number of fill entries in the factor for ordering P.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the formulas are convention-dependent. With 1-by-1 and 2-by-2 pivots, the treatment of diagonal and pivot-block entries, subsequent numerical permutations, and the comparison between lower-triangular input storage and nnz(L)+nnz(D) must be fixed by an authoritative sparse symmetric-indefinite factorization source before the stated fill count and ratio can be relied upon.

children.title: KKT Ordering Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of stability and fill behavior on factorization ordering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of sparse KKT factor structure and work on the symmetric elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed structurally symmetric sparse KKT matrix \(K\), symbolic fill is generally not invariant under symmetric permutation: admissible permutations \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) can produce different elimination graphs and factor patterns. Consequently, factor nonzeros, frontal sizes, arithmetic work, and peak workspace can differ even though both permutations represent the same linear system. Moreover, stability-driven delayed or threshold pivots may alter an initially selected ordering, so the symbolic prediction for that ordering need not equal the realized factorization cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different symmetric orderings of the same KKT matrix can produce different fill, work, and peak workspace, and numerical pivoting can modify the predicted ordering.
assumptions_latex: \(K=K^{\mathsf T}\) has a fixed structural sparsity pattern.
Comparisons use one fixed symbolic convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Realized sparse-factorization cost is not determined by \(\operatorname{nnz}(K)\) alone and may differ across orderings or after numerical reordering.

notation.meaning: Alternative symmetric permutations of the same KKT matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Ordering Sensitivity

children.title: Memory-Limited KKT Factorization
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes where factor storage becomes the limiting computational resource.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient pre-run or runtime tests using certified storage bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\underline S\le S_{\rm peak}\le\overline S\) are valid bounds for a specified KKT factorization and memory budget \(M\). If \(\overline S\le M\), the factorization is certified memory-feasible under the accounting model. If \(\underline S>M\), it is certified memory-infeasible. When \(\underline S\le M<\overline S\), these bounds are inconclusive; in particular, a symbolic estimate that omits delayed-pivot fill or concurrent workspaces is not an upper-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid peak-storage upper bound below the budget certifies feasibility, while a valid lower bound above it certifies failure.
assumptions_latex: The storage bounds and \(M\) use the same accounting model.
The bounds apply to the specified ordering and permitted pivot behavior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline S\le M\) certifies feasibility and \(\underline S>M\) certifies memory failure.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper bounds on peak storage.

knowledge_statements.title: Peak-Memory Feasibility Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Peak-storage boundary separating algebraic solvability from resource feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M>0\) be the memory available to a direct KKT factorization, and let \(S_{\rm peak}(K,P,\Pi)\) denote its actual peak storage under initial ordering \(P\) and numerical pivot sequence \(\Pi\), including factors, indices, permutations, pivot data, active frontal workspaces, and other simultaneously live solver storage. The specified run is memory-feasible only if \(S_{\rm peak}(K,P,\Pi)\le M\). If \(S_{\rm peak}(K,P,\Pi)>M\), it cannot complete within this memory model even when \(K\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular KKT system may be infeasible for a direct solver because its factors and live workspaces exceed available memory.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is the memory available to the specified factorization.
\(S_{\rm peak}\) counts all storage simultaneously live under the actual ordering and pivot sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\rm peak}(K,P,\Pi)>M\) is a computational resource boundary independent of algebraic nonsingularity.

notation.meaning: Actual peak simultaneously live factorization storage.
Initial ordering and realized numerical pivot sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Limited KKT Factorization

children.title: Projection Drift
children.top_down_role: Accumulated feasibility loss from inaccurate projections or reduced solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accumulated linear-feasibility error caused by inexact null-space projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(N\in\mathbb N\). For \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), suppose \(x_k,p_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\widehat P_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\widehat P_kp_k\), where \(\widehat P_k\) approximates a projector onto \(\ker A\). Defining \(r_k=Ax_k-b\), one has
\[
r_N=r_0+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}A\widehat P_kp_k,
\qquad
\|r_N\|\le \|r_0\|+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|A\widehat P_kp_k\|.
\]
Thus the constraint-space components left by inexact projected steps can accumulate as feasibility drift. If \(r_0=0\) and \(A\widehat P_kp_k=0\) for every \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), then \(r_k=0\) for every \(k=0,\ldots,N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over any finite sequence of inexact projected steps, the final linear-feasibility residual equals the initial residual plus the accumulated constraint-space components of those steps. Exact null-space steps preserve linear feasibility when the initial point is feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(N\in\mathbb N\), \(x_k,p_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\widehat P_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) for the stated index ranges.
The same vector norm is used in every term of the triangle-inequality bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(N\in\mathbb N\), \(\|r_N\|\le \|r_0\|+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|A\widehat P_kp_k\|\); exact null-space steps preserve feasibility from a feasible initial point.

notation.meaning: Inexact null-space projector at iteration k.
Unprojected trial direction at iteration k.
Linear feasibility residual at iteration k.
Finite number of projected updates under consideration.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accumulated feasibility drift from inexact tangent projections
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuously differentiable, \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). Suppose \(p_k\) is intended to be tangent but is computed inexactly. Define the linearized projection defect \(e_k=J_kp_k\) and feasibility residual \(h_k=c(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequences generated near a smooth equality manifold; the definition separates accumulated linearized projection error from nonlinear curvature of the constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a reference index \(k_0\), projection drift through iteration \(N\) is the excess feasibility residual \(d_N=h_N-h_{k_0}-\sum_{k=k_0}^{N-1}e_k\). The sequence crosses a drift tolerance \(\eta_N\) when \(\|h_N\|>\eta_N\), and it crosses a cumulative projection-defect tolerance \(\eta_E\) when \(\sum_{k=k_0}^{N-1}\|e_k\|>\eta_E\). The certificate records \((\|h_N\|,\sum\|e_k\|,\|d_N\|)\), thereby distinguishing feasibility loss attributable to inaccurate tangent solves from the nonlinear remainder.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection drift is recorded along an iterate sequence by the final feasibility residual, the cumulative norm of linearized tangent defects, and the remaining nonlinear discrepancy. A declared boundary is crossed when feasibility or cumulative projection error exceeds its tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable along the iterate path.
Every step and Jacobian use the same constraint scaling.
The reference index and tolerances are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The drift certificate is \((\|c(x_N)\|,\sum_{k=k_0}^{N-1}\|J_kp_k\|,\|d_N\|)\), with boundary crossing determined by the declared componentwise thresholds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For affine constraints \(c(x)=Ax-b\), \(d_N=0\) exactly.
A per-step feasibility increment is \(c(x_{k+1})-c(x_k)=J_kp_k+r_k\), where \(r_k\) denotes the nonlinear remainder.
special_cases_latex: Exact tangent steps have \(e_k=0\), but nonlinear constraints can still produce nonzero drift through \(d_N\).
An exact restoration or retraction satisfying \(c(x_{k+1})=0\) resets the measured feasibility residual.
immediate_consequences_latex: Monitoring only the latest tangent defect can miss accumulation across many steps.
The three-part certificate distinguishes projection error, nonlinear manifold curvature, and total feasibility loss.
boundary_notes: This is a diagnostic definition, not a bound on drift growth.
For large steps, the nonlinear discrepancy may dominate even with accurate projections.

notation.meaning: Accumulated nonlinear discrepancy after subtracting linearized defects.

review_flags: No inspected source supports this exact cumulative drift decomposition.

children.title: Chapter-External Guarantee Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Guarantee families whose full treatment belongs to globalization, SQP, or general constrained-complexity chapters.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary between reduction-local and framework-dependent guarantees
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal A_R\) denote assumptions local to equality reduction, such as smoothness near a solution, a constraint qualification, accurate local solves, and reduced-Hessian regularity. Let \(\mathcal A_G\) denote additional assumptions specifying a globalization, SQP, restoration, merit, filter, funnel, or complexity framework. Let \(G\) be a quantified guarantee about a generated sequence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal ownership boundary for guarantees, not a convergence theorem; its meaning is relative to explicitly enumerated assumption classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A guarantee \(G\) is chapter-external relative to \((\mathcal A_R,\mathcal A_G)\) when the valid statement has the form \((\mathcal A_R\wedge\mathcal A_G)\Rightarrow G\), while \(\mathcal A_R\) alone neither specifies the algorithmic objects quantified by \(G\) nor supplies all hypotheses required to assert \(G\). The chapter-external boundary is the set \(\mathfrak B_{\mathrm{ext}}=\{G: G\text{ quantifies global convergence, worst-case evaluation complexity, or composite-step SQP behavior and requires at least one hypothesis in }\mathcal A_G\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A guarantee is chapter-external when it becomes a valid mathematical assertion only after adding assumptions that define a globalization, complexity, or SQP framework, whereas local equality-reduction assumptions alone do not even specify all algorithmic objects or hypotheses in the guarantee. The boundary is the class of such framework-dependent guarantees.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_R\) and \(\mathcal A_G\) are explicitly listed rather than inferred from chapter labels.
\(G\) is a quantified proposition about specified iterates, residuals, or evaluation counts.
Externality concerns missing hypotheses or objects, not merely where a result is printed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\in\mathfrak B_{\mathrm{ext}}\) exactly when its valid formulation requires framework assumptions outside \(\mathcal A_R\) in one of the declared external guarantee families.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The internal guarantee class is \(\mathfrak G_R=\{G:\mathcal A_R\Rightarrow G\text{ is well-formed and valid}\}\); the external boundary contains declared guarantees outside \(\mathfrak G_R\).
special_cases_latex: A local rate theorem derived from reduced Newton regularity may be internal even when the algorithm also has a globalization.
A statement that every accumulation point is stationary is external when it relies on acceptance rules and global model-decrease safeguards.
immediate_consequences_latex: Local reduction identities cannot by themselves establish an evaluation-complexity bound.
The definition prevents importing unspecified merit, filter, trust-region, or restoration assumptions into a local reduction claim.
boundary_notes: Failure of \(\mathcal A_R\Rightarrow G\) must not be asserted as a counterexample unless one is available; externality may instead follow because \(G\) is not well-formed without \(\mathcal A_G\).
The boundary class depends on the declared scope of the chapter.
review_flags: This is a synthesized scope-boundary definition without an inspected authoritative locator.

children.title: Global Convergence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Global criticality results owned by the corresponding line-search, trust-region, merit, filter, or funnel framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Convergence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates local equality-reduction equations from framework-level global convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an equality-constrained method whose reduction step only computes directions satisfying a linearized constraint equation and a reduced first-order or Newton equation. These local equations alone do not imply that every accumulation point is first-order critical. Such a conclusion requires a specified globalization mechanism—such as a merit-function line search, filter, funnel, or trust region—together with its acceptance rule, restoration or feasibility safeguards, regularity assumptions, and boundedness conditions. Therefore no global criticality conclusion follows solely from solvability or local accuracy of the equality-reduced subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accurate equality-reduced steps alone do not establish global convergence; that guarantee belongs to a complete globalization framework with acceptance and safeguard rules.
assumptions_latex: The method specification contains only local equality-reduction and step equations.
No globalization acceptance or restoration mechanism is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local reduced-step conditions are insufficient, by themselves, to guarantee convergence to a first-order critical point.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal M_R\) be a local equality-reduction step map defined only in a neighborhood of a regular KKT point. Let \(\mathcal F\) be a complete algorithmic framework that defines iterates from an admissible initial set \(X_0\) using acceptance, step-control, restoration, and termination rules. Let \(R(x)\) be a declared first-order criticality residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between local reduction analysis and global criticality results owned by line-search, trust-region, merit, filter, or funnel frameworks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A global convergence claim has the quantified form \(\forall x_0\in X_0\), every sequence \(\{x_k\}\) generated by \(\mathcal F\) is well defined and satisfies a declared conclusion such as \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|R(x_k)\|=0\), \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|R(x_k)\|=0\), or “every accumulation point is first-order stationary.” Such a claim lies beyond the local-reduction boundary when \(\mathcal M_R\) alone does not define iterates for all \(x_0\in X_0\) or when its local hypotheses do not include the framework's global acceptance, boundedness, model-agreement, and feasibility-control assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global convergence claim quantifies over every admissible starting point and every sequence produced by a complete algorithmic framework, and concludes a specified asymptotic criticality property. It is beyond the local reduction boundary whenever the local step map does not globally define those sequences or lacks the acceptance, boundedness, model-quality, and feasibility-control hypotheses needed by the framework.
assumptions_latex: The initial set \(X_0\), generated-sequence relation, and residual \(R\) are explicitly defined.
The chosen globalization framework and its hypotheses are named.
The precise conclusion distinguishes limit inferior, full residual convergence, and stationary accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The guarantee is classified as global-framework-owned when its quantifiers or required hypotheses are not supplied by the locally defined equality-reduction map.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A stationary-accumulation-point claim is \(x_{k_j}\to x_*\Rightarrow R(x_*)=0\) for every convergent subsequence.
A full criticality claim \(\|R(x_k)\|\to0\) is stronger than \(\liminf_k\|R(x_k)\|=0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(X_0\) is restricted to a local attraction neighborhood and the step map remains there, the result is a local convergence claim rather than a global one.
A restoration or funnel mechanism may be required to make iterates well defined when the starting point is infeasible.
immediate_consequences_latex: A local quadratic-rate result does not imply global convergence from arbitrary admissible starts.
Different globalization frameworks can share the same local reduction step while requiring different global hypotheses.
boundary_notes: Global convergence does not mean convergence to a global minimizer; it commonly means convergence toward first-order criticality.
The definition states an ownership boundary and supplies no global convergence theorem.
review_flags: No supplied global-convergence source was inspected for this formal boundary definition.
A precise locator supporting the distinction among global conclusions is required.

children.title: Evaluation-Complexity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates inner equality-reduction accuracy from worst-case constrained evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an equality-reduction routine returns steps satisfying prescribed linearized-feasibility and reduced-stationarity tolerances. These conditions alone do not bound the objective, constraint, derivative, or model evaluations required to obtain \[\|c(x)\|\le\varepsilon_c,\qquad \|\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\|\le\varepsilon_g.\] A worst-case evaluation bound additionally requires a complete outer algorithm, a declared oracle and cost model, smoothness constants, acceptance and update rules, and an explicit stopping convention. Therefore no evaluation-complexity rate is attributable to equality reduction alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Per-step reduction accuracy does not imply a worst-case evaluation count without a complete outer algorithm and oracle model.
assumptions_latex: Only the inner equality-reduction routine is specified.
Feasibility and Lagrangian-stationarity tolerances are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No bound in }\varepsilon_c\text{ and }\varepsilon_g\text{ follows from inner reduction accuracy alone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-Complexity Specification Boundary
Evaluation-Complexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates linear-algebra reduction accuracy from worst-case constrained evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an equality-reduction routine return a step satisfying prescribed linearized-feasibility and reduced-stationarity tolerances. Those per-step conditions do not determine the number of objective, constraint, derivative, or model evaluations needed to obtain an iterate with
\[
\|c(x)\|\le\varepsilon_c,
\qquad
\|\nabla_x L(x,\lambda)\|\le\varepsilon_g.
\]
A worst-case evaluation bound additionally requires a complete outer algorithm, an oracle model, smoothness constants, an acceptance and radius or step-size update rule, and an explicit termination convention. Consequently, no evaluation-complexity rate is attributable to equality reduction alone.

Only the inner equality-reduction routine is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No bound in \(\varepsilon_c\) and \(\varepsilon_g\) follows without a fully specified outer constrained-optimization framework.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Worst-Case Evaluation-Complexity Boundary for Equality-Constrained Optimization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a class of finite-dimensional problems \(P:\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). Let an algorithm \(\mathcal A\) access each problem through an oracle returning a prescribed collection of values among \(f(x)\), \(c(x)\), \(\nabla f(x)\), and \(J_c(x)\). For a primal-dual pair \((x,\lambda)\), define \(\theta_P(x)=\|c(x)\|\) and \(\chi_P(x,\lambda)=\|\nabla f(x)+J_c(x)^T\lambda\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This candidate fixes a deterministic, finite-dimensional, first-order equality-constrained regime. It defines the boundary separating uniform oracle-evaluation bounds from local reduction, asymptotic convergence, and per-iteration linear-algebra analyses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For tolerances \(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g>0\), define the evaluation count of \(\mathcal A\) on \(P\) by
\[
N_{\mathcal A}(P;\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)
=\inf\left\{N\in\mathbb N_0:\text{after at most }N\text{ oracle evaluations, }\mathcal A\text{ has produced }(x,\lambda)\text{ with }\theta_P(x)\leq\varepsilon_c\text{ and }\chi_P(x,\lambda)\leq\varepsilon_g\right\},
\]
with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Its worst-case evaluation complexity on \(\mathcal P\) is
\[
\mathcal C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal P}(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)
=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}N_{\mathcal A}(P;\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g).
\]
A result lies beyond the equality-reduction evaluation-complexity boundary when it asserts a finite, uniform bound \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal P}(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\leq B(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\) under explicitly stated regularity and oracle assumptions. Claims concerning only one problem, iteration counts without bounded evaluations per iteration, or asymptotic convergence do not constitute such a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a class of smooth equality-constrained problems and a fixed oracle model, count how many oracle evaluations an algorithm needs before producing a point whose constraint violation is at most the feasibility tolerance and whose Lagrangian-gradient norm is at most the stationarity tolerance. The count is infinite if no such point is produced. The worst-case evaluation complexity is the supremum of this count over every problem in the declared class. A guarantee crosses the evaluation-complexity boundary only when it supplies a finite bound, uniform over that class, as an explicit function of the tolerances. Local convergence, asymptotic convergence, and iteration bounds that do not control evaluations per iteration remain outside this definition.
assumptions_latex: The problem class \(\mathcal P\), starting-data convention, oracle outputs, norm, and evaluation-counting convention are fixed before the supremum is taken.
For every \(P\in\mathcal P\), the functions and derivatives appearing in \(\theta_P\), \(\chi_P\), and the selected oracle are defined at every evaluated point.
The multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) may be generated by the algorithm or recovered by a procedure whose oracle cost is included in \(N_{\mathcal A}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal P}(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}N_{\mathcal A}(P;\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\), and an evaluation-complexity guarantee is precisely a uniform finite upper bound on this quantity for the declared problem and oracle class.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a one-parameter tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), one may set \(\varepsilon_c=\varepsilon_g=\varepsilon\) and write \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal P}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\inf\{N:\max(\theta_P(x_N),\chi_P(x_N,\lambda_N))\leq\varepsilon\}\).

A bound \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal P}(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\leq B(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\) is equivalent to requiring that every \(P\in\mathcal P\) admit a qualifying output within at most \(B(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\) counted oracle calls.
special_cases_latex: If every iteration makes at most \(q\) counted oracle calls and termination occurs within \(K(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\) iterations, then \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal P}(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)\leq qK(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)+N_0\), where \(N_0\) counts initialization calls.

For feasibility alone, omit the stationarity test and define \(N^{\mathrm{feas}}_{\mathcal A}(P;\varepsilon_c)=\inf\{N:\theta_P(x)
\leq\varepsilon_c\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If some \(P\in\mathcal P\) never yields a qualifying pair, then \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal A,\mathcal P}(\varepsilon_c,\varepsilon_g)=+\infty\).
Changing the oracle—for example, counting joint evaluations of \((f,c,\nabla f,J_c)\) rather than each component separately—changes the complexity object and must be declared explicitly.
boundary_notes: The definition does not itself assert any rate such as \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\); such a rate requires algorithm-specific assumptions and evidence.
Second-order complexity requires an additional criticality condition and a correspondingly richer oracle, so it is outside this first-order slot.

The supplied source hints do not contain a locator supporting this exact constrained worst-case definition; the formulation is retained as a standard-field candidate requiring an authoritative complexity source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\). At iterate \(x_k\), write \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=J_c(x_k)\), let \(H_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let \(\Delta_k>0\). Define the quadratic SQP model \(q_k(s)=g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers deterministic, smooth, finite-dimensional equality-constrained trust-region SQP steps. It identifies the structural boundary of the composite-step family, not a particular acceptance rule, penalty update, filter, global convergence theorem, or evaluation-complexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A vector \(s_k\in\mathbb R^n\) is a composite-step trust-region SQP step if it is explicitly decomposed as
\[
s_k=n_k+t_k,
\]
where the normal component \(n_k\) targets linearized feasibility and the tangential component \(t_k\) preserves the achieved linearized residual while reducing the quadratic model. A precise admissibility form is
\[
\|n_k\|\leq \xi^{N}\Delta_k,
\qquad
\|c(x_k)+A_kn_k\|\leq\|c(x_k)\|,
\]
for some \(0<\xi^{N}<1\), together with
\[
A_kt_k=0,
\qquad
\|n_k+t_k\|\leq\Delta_k,
\qquad
q_k(n_k+t_k)\leq q_k(n_k).
\]
The equality \(A_kt_k=0\) gives
\[
c(x_k)+A_ks_k=c(x_k)+A_kn_k,
\]
so the tangential component does not undo the normal component's linearized feasibility improvement. The canonical exact Byrd–Omojokun realization chooses \(n_k\) to minimize \(\|c(x_k)+A_kn\|\) over \(\|n\|\leq\xi^{N}\Delta_k\), then chooses \(t_k\) to minimize \(\tfrac12t^TH_kt+(g_k+H_kn_k)^Tt\) subject to \(A_kt=0\) and \(\|n_k+t\|\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth equality-constrained problem, a composite-step trust-region SQP step is explicitly written as the sum of a normal step and a tangential step. The normal step lies in a contracted trust region and decreases, or at least does not increase, the norm of the linearized constraint residual. The tangential step lies in the null space of the constraint Jacobian, keeps the complete step in the trust region, and decreases, or at least does not increase, the quadratic SQP model relative to the normal step alone. Because the tangential step is annihilated by the constraint Jacobian, it preserves the linearized feasibility gained by the normal step. The exact Byrd–Omojokun version obtains the two components by sequential constrained minimizations; practical algorithms may instead require prescribed fractions of the corresponding model decreases.
assumptions_latex: The functions \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable at \(x_k\), so \(g_k\) and \(A_k\) exist.
The matrix \(H_k\) is a symmetric approximation to the Hessian of the Lagrangian, and \(\Delta_k>0\).
The normal-step contraction satisfies \(0<\xi^{N}<1\), leaving trust-region capacity for a tangential component.
At least one of the feasibility or model inequalities is strict unless the associated subproblem is already stationary at its initial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining relations \(s_k=n_k+t_k\) and \(A_kt_k=0\) imply \(c(x_k)+A_ks_k=c(x_k)+A_kn_k\), while \(q_k(s_k)\leq q_k(n_k)\) and \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\); hence feasibility restoration and tangential model reduction are separated within one trust-region SQP step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tangential subproblem may equivalently be written in the complete-step variable \(s\): minimize \(q_k(s)\) subject to \(A_ks=A_kn_k\) and \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\), with \(t=s-n_k\).
If an orthonormal basis \(Z_k\) of \(\ker A_k\) is available, every tangential step has the form \(t_k=Z_kp_k\), reducing the tangential subproblem to the null-space coordinates \(p_k\).
special_cases_latex: For full-row-rank \(A_k\), a Vardi-like normal component may be \(n_k=\alpha_k n_k^C\), where \(n_k^C=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k)\) and \(0<\alpha_k\leq\min\{1,\Delta_k/\|n_k^C\|\}\).
If \(c(x_k)=0\), one may take \(n_k=0\); the composite step then reduces to a tangential trust-region SQP step satisfying \(A_kt_k=0\) and \(\|t_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The tangential subproblem is always feasible because \(t=0\) satisfies \(A_kt=0\) and \(\|n_k+t\|\leq\Delta_k\) whenever \(\|n_k\|\leq\xi^{N}\Delta_k<\Delta_k\).
Normal and tangential are functional descriptions: the definition does not require \(n_k^Tt_k=0\).
boundary_notes: Approximate normal and tangential solves require explicit sufficient-decrease conditions; merely labeling two arbitrary vectors normal and tangential is insufficient.

The definition alone supplies no global convergence, local rate, or worst-case evaluation bound. Those guarantees require algorithm-specific acceptance, radius-update, merit or filter, boundedness, and regularity assumptions.
Inequality constraints, active-set changes, restoration phases, and filter globalization lie outside this equality-constrained structural definition.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At an iterate \(x_k\), let \(g_k=Gx_k+c\), let \(A_{W_k}\) collect the working-constraint rows, and let \(q_k(p)=\tfrac12p^TGp+g_k^Tp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The mathematical input-output contract of a working-set subproblem, independent of its direct or iterative linear-algebra implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A working-set subproblem interface is the relation that maps \((G,g_k,A_{W_k})\) to one of the following valid outputs: (i) a stationary pair \((p_k,\lambda_k)\) satisfying \[Gp_k+g_k-A_{W_k}^T\lambda_k=0,
\qquad A_{W_k}p_k=0;\] (ii) a nonzero reduced negative-curvature direction \(d_k\in\ker A_{W_k}\) with \(d_k^TGd_k<0\); or (iii) a declared rank-deficiency or inconsistency status. When \(A_{W_k}\) has full row rank and \(Z_k^TGZ_k\succ0\) for a null-space basis \(Z_k\), output (i) is unique in \(p_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The working-set subproblem interface takes the quadratic model, its gradient, and the working-constraint matrix. It returns either a stationary step and multipliers satisfying the equality-constrained KKT equations, a feasible direction of negative reduced curvature, or an explicit rank/inconsistency status. If the working rows are independent and the reduced Hessian is positive definite, the returned step is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal S(G,g_k,A_{W_k})\in\{(p_k,\lambda_k),\ d_k,\ \mathrm{rank\_failure}\},\] with each output satisfying its stated algebraic certificate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a full-row-rank working matrix, the stationary output solves the saddle-point system \(\begin{bmatrix}G&-A_W^T\\A_W&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\0\end{bmatrix}\).
With \(p=Zz\), the stationary output solves \(Z^TGZz=-Z^Tg\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal W_k=\varnothing\), the interface reduces to an unconstrained quadratic subproblem.
If \(p_k=0\), the returned multipliers support the working-set optimality or release test.
immediate_consequences_latex: The outer working-set manager can be specified without selecting a factorization method.
Negative curvature is an explicit alternative output rather than a failed positive-definite solve.
boundary_notes: The interface does not determine the step length against nonworking inequalities.
Rank-deficient working sets require dependency handling not encoded by the ordinary KKT solve.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained Subproblem Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic working-set subproblem obtained by treating selected inequalities as equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k\) be a symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian model, and let \(W_k\) index inequalities treated as active. The equality-constrained step interface is
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;g_k^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
h(x_k)+J_h(x_k)p=0,\qquad
c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^\top p=0\ \ (i\in W_k).
\]
The interface returns a primal step \(p_k\), associated equality multipliers, and either a success status, an inconsistency status, or a direction of negative curvature when the quadratic model is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The current working inequalities are imposed as equalities in a quadratic model, which returns a step, multipliers, or a structured failure or negative-curvature status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equality-constrained quadratic program is the local subproblem associated with \(W_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The system \(Ap=r\) is inconsistent if and only if there exists \(y\) such that \(A^\top y=0\) and \(y^\top r\ne0\). Such a vector separates \(r\) from \(\operatorname{range}(A)\) and certifies the inconsistency status returned by the interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A left-null-space vector having nonzero inner product with the equality right-hand side certifies inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ap=r\text{ is inconsistent}\iff\exists y:\ A^\top y=0,\ y^\top r\ne0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality classification of a feasible stationary point of an equality-constrained quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(Ap=r\) is consistent, let \(Z\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\), and let \(p^*\) satisfy the KKT equations. Then \(p^*\) is a global minimizer if and only if \(Z^\top BZ\succeq0\), and it is the unique global minimizer if and only if \(Z^\top BZ\succ0\). If \(A\) has full row rank, the bordered KKT matrix is nonsingular exactly when \(Z^\top BZ\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced semidefiniteness certifies global minimality, reduced positive definiteness certifies uniqueness, and reduced nonsingularity characterizes KKT nonsingularity under full row rank.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*\in\arg\min_{Ap=r}q(p)\iff Z^\top BZ\succeq0,\qquad p^*\text{ is the unique minimizer}\iff Z^\top BZ\succ0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrange dual of the equality-constrained quadratic when the full Hessian is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(B\succ0\), the Lagrange dual of
\[\min_p\;g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\quad\text{subject to }Ap=r\]
is
\[\max_\lambda\;-\tfrac12(g+A^\top\lambda)^\top B^{-1}(g+A^\top\lambda)-r^\top\lambda.\]
When \(Ap=r\) is consistent, the primal and dual optima are attained with equal values, and \(p=-B^{-1}(g+A^\top\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive-definite curvature, eliminating the primal step gives a concave multiplier dual with no duality gap when the equalities are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{Ap=r}q(p)=\max_\lambda\left[-\tfrac12(g+A^\top\lambda)^\top B^{-1}(g+A^\top\lambda)-r^\top\lambda\right].
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Equality-QP Dual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual system for the working-set equality QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Writing the working equalities as \(Ap=r\), a pair \((p,\lambda)\) is stationary for \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\) subject to \(Ap=r\) exactly when
\[\begin{bmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\r\end{bmatrix}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-constrained quadratic step and its multipliers satisfy a bordered KKT system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bp+g+A^\top\lambda=0\quad\text{and}\quad Ap=r.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min_p\tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\) subject to \(Ap=h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained quadratic subproblems, including the homogeneous tangent subproblems used by active-set methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality-constrained subproblem interface associates the data \((H,g,A,h)\) with a primal-dual pair \((p,\lambda)\) satisfying \[Hp+g-A^T\lambda=0,
\qquad Ap=h.\] Equivalently, \((p,\lambda)\) solves \[\begin{bmatrix}H&-A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p\\\lambda\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g\\h\end{bmatrix}.\] The interface is regular when \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z^THZ\succ0\) for a basis \(Z\) of \(\ker A\); under these conditions the KKT matrix is nonsingular and the subproblem has a unique primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained quadratic subproblem maps its Hessian, gradient, constraint matrix, and right-hand side to a step and multiplier satisfying stationarity and the equality constraints. These conditions form the KKT saddle-point system. The interface is regular when the constraint matrix has independent rows and the Hessian is positive definite on its null space; then the KKT matrix is nonsingular and the primal solution is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal E(H,g,A,h)=\{(p,\lambda):Hp+g-A^T\lambda=0,\ Ap=h\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\), with \([Y\ Z]\) nonsingular and \(AZ=0\), then \(AYp_Y=h\) and \(Z^THZp_Z=-Z^T(g+HYp_Y)\).
special_cases_latex: For an active-set tangent step, \(h=0\).
For \(A=0\) and nonsingular \(H\), the solution is \(p=-H^{-1}g\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(Z^THZ\) is the relevant second-order condition; full positive definiteness of \(H\) is unnecessary.
The multiplier output supplies the constraint-release test.
boundary_notes: If \(Z^THZ\) is indefinite, a stationary solution can be a saddle point rather than a minimizer.
Dependent equality rows require a rank-revealing representation or removal of redundancy.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P=\{x:A_{[0m\mathcal E}x=b_{[0m\mathcal E},\ A_{[0m\mathcal I}x\ge b_{[0m\mathcal I}\}\) be a polyhedron, let \(x\in P\), and let \(\mathcal E\subseteq W\subseteq\mathcal A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine faces of polyhedral feasible sets and the null-space reduction used in active-set subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The face associated with the working set \(W\) is \[F_W=P\cap\{z:a_i^Tz=b_i\ \text{for every }i\in W\}.\] Its affine tangent space at \(x\in F_W\) is \[T_W=\{p:A_Wp=0\}=\ker A_W.\] If \(Z_W\) has full-column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z_W)=\ker A_W\), then every tangent displacement has a unique reduced coordinate \(u\) with \(p=Z_Wu\). Consequently, restricting a quadratic model \(\tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\) to the working face corresponds exactly to the reduced model \(\tfrac12u^TZ_W^THZ_Wu+(Z_W^Tg)^Tu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The working set defines the portion of the feasible polyhedron on which all working constraints are equalities. The tangent displacements along this face are exactly the null space of the working-constraint matrix. Choosing a basis \(Z_W\) for that null space gives a one-to-one representation \(p=Z_Wu\), and the quadratic model restricted to the face becomes a quadratic model with reduced Hessian \(Z_W^THZ_W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[T_W=\ker A_W=\operatorname{range}(Z_W),\qquad q(Z_Wu)=\tfrac12u^TZ_W^THZ_Wu+(Z_W^Tg)^Tu.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(A_W\) has full row rank, \(\dim T_W=n-|W|\).
The face-restricted stationarity condition is \(Z_W^T(HP+g)=0\) for the relevant displacement \(p\).
special_cases_latex: At a vertex with \(\operatorname{rank}A_W=n\), the reduced space is \(\{0\}\).
With no working constraints, \(Z_W\) may be the identity and the reduced model is the original model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(Z_W^THZ_W\) characterizes strict convexity along the working face.
Adding an independent working constraint reduces the tangent-space dimension by one.
boundary_notes: If working rows are dependent, \(n-|W|\) is not the reduced dimension; rank must replace cardinality.
The affine face includes feasibility restrictions from nonworking constraints, while its tangent space records only working equalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Restricted Subproblem Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic model restricted to the affine face determined by a working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\}\), let \(x_k\in P\), and let \(W\subseteq\{i:a_i^\top x_k=b_i\}\). The affine face model is \(F_W=\{x\in P:a_i^\top x=b_i\text{ for all }i\in W\}\). For a quadratic step model \(q_k(p)=g_k^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp\), the face-restricted interface solves
\[
\min_p q_k(p)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_k+p\in F_W,
\]
and returns a minimizing step, a boundary-blocking event, an unboundedness or negative-curvature certificate, or an inconsistency status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subproblem minimizes the local quadratic model while the trial point remains on the polyhedral face fixed by the working constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible trial points remain in \(F_W\), with all indices in \(W\) fixed at equality.

source_refs.locator: 10.3 Active Set Methods p. 236

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational certificate for minimizing a differentiable model over the selected polyhedral face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y^*=x_k+p^*\in F_W\). The step \(p^*\) is first-order stationary for minimizing differentiable \(q_k\) over \(F_W\) exactly when
\[\nabla q_k(p^*)^\top d\ge0\quad\text{for every }d\in T_{F_W}(y^*),\]
equivalently \(-\nabla q_k(p^*)\in N_{F_W}(y^*)\). If \(q_k\) is convex, this condition is sufficient for global optimality on \(F_W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationarity on the selected face is equivalent to a tangent-cone variational inequality or normal-cone inclusion; for a convex model it certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\nabla q_k(p^*)\in N_{F_W}(x_k+p^*),\text{ with global sufficiency when }q_k\text{ is convex.}

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Subproblem Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space reduction of a working-set equality-constrained quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the working-set equalities be \(A_Wp=r_W\), let \(p_0\) satisfy \(A_Wp_0=r_W\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A_W\). Every feasible step has the form \(p=p_0+Zz\). With \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\), the exact reduced representation is
\[
\min_{A_Wp=r_W} q(p)
\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
\min_z\; q(p_0)+(Z^\top(g+Bp_0))^\top z+\tfrac12z^\top(Z^\top BZ)z.
\]
The reduced-space interface returns \(z\) and reconstructs \(p=p_0+Zz\), together with a singularity or negative-curvature status when appropriate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible particular step plus a null-space basis converts the equality-constrained quadratic problem into an unconstrained reduced-coordinate problem with exactly the same objective values under reconstruction.
assumptions_latex: \(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full and reduced problems have corresponding feasible points and identical objective values under \(p=p_0+Zz\).

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1. Linear Equality Constraints p. 68

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1. Linear Equality Constraints p. 68

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, optimality, uniqueness, and unboundedness tests in reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_R=Z^\top BZ\) and \(g_R=Z^\top(g+Bp_0)\). The reduced quadratic \(g_R^\top z+\tfrac12z^\top H_Rz\) has a global minimizer if and only if \(H_R\succeq0\) and \(g_R\in\operatorname{range}(H_R)\). Its minimizers are exactly the solutions of \(H_Rz=-g_R\), and the minimizer is unique if and only if \(H_R\succ0\). If \(H_R\succeq0\) but \(g_R\notin\operatorname{range}(H_R)\), the model is unbounded below along one orientation of a zero-curvature direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced quadratic is solvable exactly when its Hessian is positive semidefinite and its linear coefficient lies in the Hessian range; positive definiteness gives uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \arg\min_z\left(g_R^\top z+\tfrac12z^\top H_Rz\right)\ne\varnothing\iff H_R\succeq0\text{ and }g_R\in\operatorname{range}(H_R).

knowledge_statements.title: Face-to-Reduced-Space Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine bijection between a working face and its null-space coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{p\in\mathbb R^n:A_Wp=r_W\}\) be nonempty, choose \(p_0\in F\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\), where \(r=\operatorname{rank}(A_W)\). Then the map \(\phi:\mathbb R^{n-r}\to F\) defined by \(\phi(z)=p_0+Zz\) is bijective. Moreover, for \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\), minimizing \(q\) on \(F\) is equivalent to minimizing \(q\circ\phi\) on \(\mathbb R^{n-r}\); local and global minimizers correspond through \(\phi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A particular face point and null-space basis give unique reduced coordinates for every point on the affine face, preserving quadratic minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(z)=p_0+Zz\) is a bijection, and \(\arg\min_{p\in F}q(p)=\phi\bigl(\arg\min_z q(\phi(z))\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced feasible direction certifying nonconvexity of a working-set quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained quadratic model \(q(p)=g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\) with homogeneous feasible directions \(A_Wd=0\), a nonzero vector \(d\) satisfying
\[
A_Wd=0,\qquad d^\top Bd<0
\]
is a negative-curvature certificate. It is directly verifiable by matrix-vector products. For every feasible \(p_0\), both \(p_0+td\) and \(p_0-td\) satisfy the working equalities, and at least one sign of \(d\) is a descent direction whenever \(\nabla q(p_0)^\top d\ne0\). Without additional bounds or inequalities, \(q(p_0+td)\to-\infty\) as \(|t|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction with negative quadratic curvature certifies nonconvexity; absent other restrictions, the quadratic model is unbounded below along that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(d\) certifies negative curvature on the working-set tangent space and unboundedness of the equality-only quadratic model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of negative curvature in null-space coordinates and feasible full-space directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) have full column rank with \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A_W\). There exists a nonzero \(d\) satisfying \(A_Wd=0\) and \(d^\top Bd<0\) if and only if there exists \(v\ne0\) satisfying \(v^\top(Z^\top BZ)v<0\). The directions correspond through \(d=Zv\). Thus feasible negative curvature exists exactly when the reduced Hessian has a negative eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible full-space negative curvature exists exactly when the reduced Hessian has a negative direction, with lifting through the null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists d\ne0:\ A_Wd=0,\ d^\top Bd<0\iff\lambda_{\min}(Z^\top BZ)<0.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced and Full-Space Negative-Curvature Equivalence

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=\tfrac12p^THp+g^Tp\), let \(A_Wp=0\) define the working tangent space, and let \(Z\) span \(\ker A_W\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indefinite equality-constrained quadratic models arising inside active-set methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A negative-curvature interface returns a nonzero reduced direction \(s\) and its full-space image \(d=Zs\) satisfying \[A_Wd=0,
\qquad d^THd=s^TZ^THZs<0.\] Its sign is oriented so that \(g^Td\le0\). The outer method may then choose the largest admissible step along \(d\) until a nonworking constraint blocks the motion. If no such finite blocking step exists, the quadratic model is unbounded below along the working-feasible ray because \(q(p+\alpha d)\to-\infty\) as \(\alpha\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative-curvature interface returns a nonzero direction tangent to all working constraints whose quadratic curvature is negative. The sign is chosen to make the direction nonascending to first order. The outer active-set method follows it until a nonworking constraint blocks the step. If no finite blocker exists, the quadratic model tends to minus infinity along that feasible ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d\in\ker A_W\setminus\{0\},\quad d^THd<0,\quad g^Td\le0;\qquad \alpha_{\max}=\infty\Rightarrow q(p+\alpha d)\to-\infty.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Negative reduced curvature is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\min}(Z^THZ)<0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Z^THZ\succeq0\), the interface reports that no strict negative-curvature direction exists.
In inertia-controlling methods, a release is arranged so that the reduced Hessian has at most one negative eigenvalue.
immediate_consequences_latex: A stationary point of the working subproblem with negative reduced curvature is not a local minimizer on the working face.
A finite blocker supplies an index that can be admitted to shrink the negative-curvature subspace.
boundary_notes: Zero curvature \(d^THd=0\) is not strict negative curvature and needs a separate recession test.
The definition concerns the model Hessian, not necessarily the exact NLP Lagrangian Hessian.
